3 - Service was definitely good, considering the business of 7pm dinner on a Thursday night. Waiters were on hand to refill your drinks, even if they did appear to be ready to escort you out quickly once your bowl is close to empty.

Lastly, too pricey for what it was.A $10 ramen bowl would be more acceptable.

I've been here twice. The first time I tried the meatballs which were surprisingly moist and tasty. I had a taste of the ramen and it was okay not bad. 

That prompted a second visit and I ordered my own Garlic Mazeman and it was soooo freaking salty. I think I downed like 3 glasses of water. To the point where the waiter just brought me the whole jug... The noodles weren't soggy which was good I guess. Didn't even finish it though. Figured I had enough sodium for a month. I also had a taste of the Spicy red chili ramen. Someone said it tasted like ma po tofu in a noodle soup. I think that described it well.

I loved the slurp shop too, but this makes it look like cup o noodles. The ramen here is just amazing. The noodles are perfection and the broth is heavenly ambrosia. The wait can be long, unless you go on a hot summer day when no when is in thy mood for ramen. The meatballs were awesome and almost more like a dumpling in consistency. Loved the garlic kick. The spicy ramen is not a joke, bring a handkerchief for the mixed tears of pain and ecstasy. I eagerly awaited slurping the last bit of broth with all the spice at the bottom with fear and excitement.  The garlic mazeman was super tasty as well and a bit more tame but also on the tangy side. The beer choices are great and a perfect way to wash it all down and put out the burn. Great staff too who knows the dishes and even which beers work well with them.

Fantastic! The food is amazing and the waitstaff is so friendly and helpful. We had the Coney Island tofu, red chilli ramen, shoyu ramen. Everything was delicious and they were so accommodating about removing certain ingredients. I can't wait to go back and try more.

The one thing I blurted out after we finished our meal and stepped outside: "Why do I have to pay $5 extra to have the same ingredients as a standard bowl of ramen anywhere else?!!!"

Make no mistake-it was a solid bowl of ramen with good flavors. 

I had the shio ramen, NOT "fully loaded" (I didn't even realize there would be no egg, fish cake, veggies...usually you charge extra for EXTRA portions of meat, noodles, etc so it didn't even register I'd need to pay $5 just to have those standard ingredients there), and was not impressed for the $16.49 (including tax and 18% tip) price of this experience. 

The one thing that shined was the rye noodles which made it unique from other ramen. The pork chashu was too big. When a slow eater who is usually satisfied with half portions slurps up the last drop of soup and is still hungry...methinks there is a quantity issue.

I looked at the bowl I ate and my mind just kept saying it shouldn't be that much $....my stomach grumbled in agreement.

got the tokyo shio ramen fully loaded. the noodles itself had great texture. the egg was good, a golden soft boil but not runny. the broth had flavor but too salty to just quickly slurp down. i have no particular feelings about the chashu, but it may be a bit too fatty for some. the roasted tomato did absolutely nothing for me.

the price though. 13 dollars before any toppings besides green onions. +5 for "fully loaded" + tax + tip. not worth it

Came here for lunch on a random Saturday and it was pretty easy to get some seating, so that's definitely the time to come if you want to avoid any type of wait.  

Started off with the 1000 year old deviled egg which was good, but not necessarily something I'd feel a strong urge to try again.  Next up were the pork meatballs which were good, worth getting in the future.

Had the spicy red chili for my ramen and it's definitely got a good kick if that's what you're looking for.  Also really liked the texture of the noodles.  My only complaint is I wish they would've put some more meat in there...but hey, what do you expect for a trendy ramen spot right?

Worth trying, though I'm not sure if the price tag justifies me coming back often.

Ivan Ramen
NY: Manhattan: LSE
2pm Sunday 3rd August 2014
Three Stars

This ramen shop has a cool look and feel:  Japanese Pop-art, Sleek Modern Tables, and nice outdoor patio.  I sat at the bar in front of the kitchen.  I ordered the Masubi ($6) and Spicy Miso Ramen ($14) with an extra egg ($2). I wanted the Garlic Mazemen but it is only available on their dinner menu.  The Masubi was delicious. The Roasted Tomato was the dominant flavor of this dish.  The Toasted Nori was still warm.  The Roasted Pork was salty and fat.  The complete combination made for a delicious bite. The Ramen was very spicy (Asian spicy, spicy enough for me to not ask for any togarashi, chili oil, sriracha, etc.). The Broth kicks you in the face with its upfront flavor.   The Rye Noodles held its own against the boldness of the dish. The Soft Egg was perfectly cooked: firm whites and silky yolk.  Plus you get some smashed up eggs (presumably the less than perfect looking ones).  I enjoyed the flavor but it was hard to eat the entire bowl because that one flavor was very intense and there was nowhere else to go.  The service was good but he didn't offer to refill my glass at the end of the meal.  Overall it was good but not my favorite ramen place.

Walking up, this place is slightly discreet without much of a sign outside. The inside is white and quite modern. 

For $14, I ordered the Shio Ramen. Delicious thin noodles with a bit of a snap. The broth was medium bodied with a good balance of fat, pork flavor, and saltiness. However, it only came with two small pieces of pork and some scallion.

There is also a good craft beer selection and cocktails.

Not really what you expect considering the reviews, but it was flavorful and technically solid. Not traditional flavors and the Tonkatsu taste more like a chicken stock and dashi broth that pork, but I would go back.

Recommend.

Quoted 45 minute on a Friday night and it was closer to 25. I ordered the Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen. It was decadent and exactly as described. A pork overload that is tempered slightly by the garlic. I would get it again, although i am not the biggest fan of the Mazemen style. Fiancée got the shoyu ramen. It was very good, although not worth the trouble to come back for. Service at the bar was LES surly.

bar
sorachi ace, good beer.

lancaster okonomiyaki
interesting, surprising, very delicious. not much offal taste. maple kewpie set it off.

triple pork triple garlic mazeman
superb noodle (whole wheat). pork chasu, okay. tonkotsu broth, rich. combination, perfect.

tokyo shoyu ramen
superb noodle (rye). no discernible chicken taste but good, salty broth.

"did the tango with my kidneys." -action bronson

Holy freaking smokes!!
おいしいですよですよ (So delicious)!
These guys are the only one in town that make their ramen with the real Japanese dashi base. Dashi is a broth made of seaweed and bonito (dried fish essentially) flakes. Super savory and wonderful, it's the base of much traditional Japanese cooking.

We sat at the bar pretty late on a weekday night and we didn't get any dirty looks from the cooks, and the bar tender was great! Through his brilliant suggestion I have now been rehabilitated from my dislike of sake. I obviously had bad sake before, and he knew exactly what to give me to show me the error of my ways.

Wish I could go here all the time!

Went yesterday for first time.... As big Toto and Ippudo fan this place just doesn't compete. I was prepared for something 'less traditional' which was clear by the three guys making the food..one black, one white and one latin...but nothing I had wowed me. The Shoyu Ramen was heavy on the soy and not much else was like eating liquid Lo Mein from some 80's UES chinese take out. The spicy cold noodle ramen was certainly spicy but was a one note wonder too...couldnt taste the noodles or cucumbers bc of overwhelming heat. Anyway I'd try again in winter but not encouraged :(

Go by yourself, sit at the bar, and hope that Jen is there. Not only is she delightful company she has great recommendations. The spicy chili Ramen is not for the faint of heart but a treat for heat enthusiasts. Jen strongly recommended the salmon rice bowl which I'm going to try next time. They also have a nice selection of beers on tap including some new sour beers. Perfect for summer

Ramen, for me, should be in a very small and crowded place, with the chef cooking right in front of you. The house should be filled with the steam of the noodle pot and with way too much "irashai". After you eat the noodle and drink all the soup, you are a bit sweaty but very satisfied and you would rub your belly saying "argh~"

Ivan Ramen is nothing like that. It's nice and well established restaurant with great waiters. The ramen is a bit westernized which is fine but I just have a thing for authentic Japanese ramen.

Layered Ramen! Cold garnishes on top and fried pork. Then noodles. Soft pork. Then finally, a shot of hot broth at the bottom. It's like deconstructed ramen.  

Once combined, the dish wasn't very hot.

It ate almost like lo-mein. The flavors are rich, but the "triple garlic" is kinda muddled into the taste of pure roasted garlic. 

The portion is small. $23 after tip for one small bowl. No drink. Wasn't full walking out the door.

Came here on my lunch hour after reading Pete Wells's NYT review. I ordered exactly what the article recommended I order - the roast pork musubi and the red-hot cold mazemen - and both were out of this world incredible. Don't know what this spot looks like at night, but lunchtime had no lines or waiting whatsoever. Superb.

Wow. Overrated. Started off with a 15 minute wait for their one unisex bathroom (seriously this place must seat nearly 100 people it's ridiculous to have one john). The shaved daikon starter is tasty, covered in pork crackling with some chili oil pumping up the jam on an otherwise pretty standard ingredient. The fried tofu and pork balls also bode well, light and fluffy with the traditional sweet and sesame sauce accompaniment. But the ramen SUCKED. Like get this at any low end nothing special kind of place. This is what Ramen in Kansas must be like. First off most of their ramen doesn't come with an egg. Whaaaaa? Also the spicy chili shio ramen I had would have been even more miserable had I not ordered the pork belly as an extra side. The broth was ok but came out lukewarm and ultimately was so thick it was literally more of a chili or stew than soup. No slurp for you! The guy working the front door could clearly hear when I said the broth was lukewarm but couldn't be bothered to look up from his phone to do anything about it. 

Ivan Ramen? More like Ivan Nah,man!

Had the spicy redi chili ramen for luch.  The broth was very rich and thick and flavorful.  It is spicy, but enjoyable spicy--not blazing hot.

The buckwheat noodles were very nice.  Had a great texture and tasted very fresh.

Only complaint was that the bowl did not come out hot.  More like warm.  I am not sure if ramen is traditionally supposed to be served this way.

I also saw a customer come to the bar with a piece of wire mesh that was found in his bowl.  It was lucky he found it and didn't ingest it.  I really hope management swaps out ALL the noodle mesh cookers, from which the wire came from to something more industrial.  Seems kind of dangerous.

Not that impressed with the service or the food.  

We weren't allowed to sit until our entire party got there even though half the seats were empty. The server was condescending when we asked to describe mazemen and still didn't actually explain it. 

The food was good, but nothing to write home about.

However, I did love the retro Japanese decor. It made me very nostalgic.

3 instead of 4 because of the poor waiting estimate.  We arrived at a busy time, and were told a 45-minute wait. We go walk part of the Williamsburg Bridge and come back 45 minutes later, and are then told the wait would be extended 30 minutes. We leave to grab a drink at the subpar tapas bar on the corner. 5 minutes later, Ivan Ramen calls us to tell us our table is ready - after we've ordered drinks and a plate of tapas. We wait for our tapas to come, ask them to box it, and chug our drinks before heading back. 

I do love the food. The appetizers and ramen are good. I wish the experience were better.

So good.  Celebrated my anniversary here and it was fun and delicious.  We had the pickled daikon (delicious) and the pork meat balls (fluffy and came out piping hot).  We also had a triple pork ramen (hearty and full, no broth), and a Tokyo Shio ramen with an added egg (tasty, light).  I want to come back and try more!

Fantastic place! 

We went a little bit early to ensure that we got a seat - we were let in no problem around 630PM, friday. 

We got tofu coney island as an app and i got trip pork trip garlic mazemen (mazemen is like ramen but with minimal broth). They were both fantastic!! Not usually a huge vegetarian guy but tofu coney island was a very interesting and unique. Same goes for the mazemen main dish - it was very inventive and you could tell that they put a lot of time perfecting the dish. It had so much flavor but not in an overwhelming way. 

A little side note, we saw Ivan himself walking around the restaurant throughout the dinner hours to say hi to his customers/share his infinite ramen knowledge! It's always nice to be at a place where you can tell the owner truly cares about the place and the product it sells. We got to say hi to Ivan on our way out which I thought was a special treat. 

Overall, I would definitely make this my regular place whenever I'm downtown!

we hit traffic on the way down for lunch but a parking spot 1/2 block from this renowned place made it worth it.  +we got a table for 3 without any wait at all.

service was super, very nice wait person.

iced barley tea, also very very good.

duck heart skewers and meatballs were delicious.

my wife, son and i each had different ramens, all excellent.  

i know the place and ivan orkin have been hyped beyond recognition, but hey: it's a meal and a delicious one at that.

I've probably been here about 5-6 times. So yummy. The deviled eggs are different but great. I get the Tokyo shio ramen and I love it. Sometimes the broth is a bit grainy but I can look past it. It gets busy so I try and go during slower times.

not worth the hype

Sure, this is not your traditional ramen place and you wanna spice things up in your ramen world, but it's even beyond how ramen should be.

I'll give it to them that they made the place very modern and fancy...but thats pretty much it.

I tried their Triple Garlic Triple Pork ramen with their Roasted Pork musbi.

The roasted pork musbi was alright.  They gave you TWO little itty piece, literally done in one bite.  It wasn't bad and the plum tomato gave it the juice it needed but for the price for small piece...eh...i can pass

The triple garlic triple pork - FIRST OFF, there is no broth!! I wasnt aware of that and was feeling a bit disappointed by it.  You pretty much mixed everything in and first bite was overwhelming, there was so much stuff going on that you kinda miss the basic.  It was very salty, i felt llike i need to drown myself in water to balance everything else.  And i believe it was for $15 bucks....it was the size of my fist...didnt even fill me up at all!  All in it was ramen, shallot?, pork and small meek bamboo shoot...nothing in it.

I rather save my money and go elsewhere

PS...four cheese ramen? wth!?

I went there for lunch on the strength of the glowing review by NYmag's Adam Platt and was sadly underwhelmed.  The ramen was very one note and unremarkable.  The meatballs were ok. The salad was good but that's so not what I was there for. It wasn't bad but with all the excellent ramen in this city I just can't see myself going there again.

Decided to try the infamous Ivan Ramen after reading a couple of write ups.  Here's what it comes down to: "Boutique Ramen".  In other words, not much food and a lot of fanciness.  The irony is the backdrop art contains a cartoon graphic of people slurping GIANT bowls of ramen, Yeah Sure! If you went somewhere else you might be served that much!!  That was the funniest-not-so-funny thing about it.  I had the Triple Garlic Triple Pork Ramen and it was tasty and not too salty like other ramen I've had.  I would strongly advise you add the $5 option of fully loaded or you might leave still hungry.  
Don't think I'm repeating this one, but it's worth a try.

Triple pork triple garlic mazemen, fully loaded. That's all that's needed to be said. I do note this, come early to beat the dinner rush. Wait time, 0 minutes. Oh yeah, you'll need lots of water (a ton of sodium).

Coney Island Tofu, is one of the best dishes I have had in a very long time.

Ramen was great, the bottled Japanese beer even better.

Great ambiance and decor.

Seriously?  $15 for some mediocre noodles soaked in extremely salty sauce w some bean sprout and ONE piece of pork? Oh you can pay extra $2 for an egg! Why don't they just go rob a bank?! I'm willing to pay a lot of money for good food, but no thanks Ivan Ramen. Bottom line is it's nothing special or even good. If you have too much money and like to be poisoned by salt, go there. Otherwise save your money and maybe just give it to the hungry homeless people on the street. I'm sure they will have a feast.

Fooled me once, shame on you. Fooled me twice, shame on me.

I've tried the Slurp Shop and had such a poor experience with the food (and the cost) that I swore I'd never eat Ivan's ramen again. Then Pete Well's paean to this restaurant's triple pork triple garlic mazemen made me reconsider (though honestly, I didn't have to read that much farther past "triple pork" to get me psyched). Maybe the review hyped it beyond reason. But I should have known better than to give in the Orkin hype.

We got there at 5:45 for dinner, and the place was pretty empty. A number of other diners showed up and were told they wouldn't be seated until their entire party arrived. Fine, that's standard in small NY restos. Our waiter hated us. I don't know what we did wrong other than sit down and look at the menu. He seemed like he was in a rush to take our order and for us to leave. He also gave me a spoon that had a long piece of dried scallion stuck to the back. So yes, pretty sure he hated us because what server would give utensils to guests without checking their condition first? (and as I said, the place was empty so he wasn't in a rush or overworked or anything)

I had the fried chicken liver/heart crispy app and my friend got the roast pork musubi. Neither were a lot of food considering the price. The musubi was two bites for $6. They were so small that I didn't want to take one, since it was my friend's food. The chicken innards tasted like fried oysters except liver on the inside. I like chicken heart and liver, but this preparation was not my favorite. The liver chunks were a bit big too so I felt like there was too much liver in each bite and not enough crunchy exterior to make up for the overwhelming liver taste.

We both got the triple pork triple garlic mazemen. I didnt like the thick noodles, though they still had a good mouthfeel - this dish is really rich to begin with and the thick noodles made me hyper aware that I was eating a lot of carbs covered in oil on top of just eating a very fattening dish. 
The slice of pork belly in nestled in the noodles was heavenly. It was 95% fat. But it made the lard covering the noodles redundant, because it really was too much of a good thing. The thickness of the noodles, which got tangled and messy, buried the candied pieces of pork belly that were also in the dish. I didn't see how they added anything because they were in larger pieces so not every bite of noodle got some candied pork. 

The broth at the bottom was too rich to drink, and was so salty that the noodles at the bottom were acidic to taste. The dish altogether was not congruent - however hard I tried to mix it all up and kept mixing it throughout the meal, the top tasted oily but had no flavor beyond the fat, while the bottom was overly salty and sour. 

We paid $56 for the two mazemen and two apps, which is about $30 more than this meal was worth. Not going back and NOT wasting any more money on this ridiculously overhyped ramen empire.

I don't understand the hype. I got the ramen and was very disappointed by how bland and unflavorful it was. On top of that, it is pretty pricey for the small portions.

Probably not a place I will ever seek out again.
This place does not feel too Japanese, very modern. I ordered a spicy kind, and will give a four for it being truly spicy!

Awful. Came here for lunch. Guess it has a more limited menu. Got the shoyu ramen which has pretty much nothing in it and was very salty. Also got the Coney Island tofu dish which was terrible. I hate wasting food but I didn't even finish it. 

I've been to many well known ramen places like Orenchi, totto, ippudo and ramen places all over tokyo. Don't believe the hype. With other options, I would never come back here.

Was very disappointed by the Triple garlic mazeman last night at the LES location. Ramen needs to have soup coming with it. And Ivan's ramen barely had any.. How ironic for them to bring spoon for us when the most they had in the bowel was some source. In terms of flavor, I think the saltiness overpowered any other flavor, which is another unfortunate thing. Perhaps I went with too much expectation, only walking away disappointed. Comparing to Totto ramen, I think the latter is much more sophisticated in the flavor category. On the positive side, the wait time is substantially less to none vs Totto.

KenScale: 8.5/10

After opening a sort of test kitchen at Slurp Shop in Gotham West Market, Ivan Orkin, who initially carved out his name as a ramen master in Tokyo out of all places, soon opened a full-scale joint in LES. I was obviously very intrigued with the full menu featuring not just ramen dishes but other Japanese- and Asian-inspired dishes. I finally made a visit on a recent weekend, and really loved many of the dishes coming out of the kitchen.

Pickled daikon with dried shrimp and scallop chili oil, while simple-looking, had that refreshing quality whetting my appetite. I was a bit underwhelmed by JFC (double dredged chicken hearts and livers to dip in ponzu honey mustard), as I was expecting crispy bites but they came out to be mushy. On the other hand, tofu coney island, an inventive dish with miso mushroom chili, yellow mustard and scallion, was a dish with great flavor. I was also a huge fan of ankimo dirty rice with monkfish liver, lemon sofrito and scallion, a rustic dish that wasn't overly salty. The winner of the night, however, belonged to roast pork musubi with salted plum wasabi, roast tomato and toasted nori. I was absolutely blown away by the melting taste of the pieces, with awesome texture (which resembled uni) and all the ingredients working in harmony. Obviously, I had to finish the meal with a ramen dish, and I went with triple pork triple garlic mazemen (with tonkotsu broth, pork chashu and whole wheat noodle). Quickly becoming a signature dish at the restaurant (with a rave from NY Times), this soupless dish was just pure decadence, very rich in flavor (although it became a bit heavy by the end).

The restaurant doesn't accept reservations and it quickly fills up (New Yorkers are always suckers for ramen dishes), so if you plan on a dinner here, make sure to come early (the restaurant doesn't seat you unless the full party has arrived). Ivan Ramen has a full bar, with some Asian-inspired cocktails (although I found wine to surprisingly work well with the dishes I've had). I liked the vibe of the restaurant, with interesting paintings on the wall that make you feel like you're sitting at a hip ramen joint somewhere in Tokyo. I highly recommend Ivan Ramen for a lot of creative dishes that also taste great. If you're planning on a night out in LES or East Village, definitely start from here for a casual dinner.

I first heard about Ivan Ramen on a David Chang documentary so I was eying this place up for a while. 

I was expecting a hole in a wall type place like most ramen joints in and around LES/East village however it was quite the opposite and modern looking. It's very large, with plenty of seating and even an outdoor area. Overall, a pretty good looking venue.

On to the food, I had the roast pork musubi to start which was delicious. The pork was so moist and tender and full of flavor. I then had the Tokyo Shio Ramen, which is one of their goto ramens. I was kind of disappointed. I thought the broth was pretty bland and didn't have a lot of flavor. However, the poached egg, pork and ramen was perfectly cooked and delicious. For a 15+ dollar bowl of ramen and hype around this place, I expected more. 

I'll be back to try the other ramens, hopeful for a better experience but for now their ramen is average in my book.

I came here with a friend. She had the triple pork triple garlic mazemen and I had the spicy red chili ramen. The flavors of both were pretty good. At first I wanted to order what my friend had until the waiter notified me that it is broth less. Therefore I ordered the spicy ramen which has broth. It was pretty spicy but in that good way where you just want to keep eating it. By the end of the meal, my friend was still hungry but I was full, probably due to her not having broth. The staff was very nice and attentive here. They also have outdoor seating that looks nice but since today was super hot, we decided to dine inside instead but maybe next time.

The best part of the meal was the Ivan Palmer. Barley tea and yuzu lemonade - yum!

The Tokyo Shio Ramen, fully loaded, was delicious, but nothing crazy or mind blowing. I have I say that I love roasted tomatoes, but incredibly weird in the ramen. Tasty, but odd combination. Excellent chewy noodles.

I'd definitely go back for the ambiance. It was easy enough to get a seat during lunch, but unsure of the popularity during dinner.

Clean, fancier ramen that is pretty good but not quite up to its hype.

I came with two friends on a weekend for lunch around its opening time, and there wasn't much of a wait at that time, but it got busy by the time we left. We split an order of the meatballs and the roast pork musubi, the former being pretty blah but the latter being quite tasty. Although small, it had a lot of flavor, particularly the pork, and it's something I'd definitely try again. For my meal, I had the red-hot cold mazeman since I was looking for a cold noodle dish on a hot summer day. It probably wasn't the best choice since it was quite spicy (although not as spicy as the broth of a friend's spicy red chili ramen). I felt that the spice mostly overwhelmed the flavor of the other ingredients; the noodles were high quality and the ingredients themselves tasty, but probably the overall pairinng was lost on me given the spiciness. 

It's a clean place to enjoy a ramen meal, although you pay up a bit for it in prices (relative to the portion sizes, particularly for the appetizers). I'd consider coming back to try the triple pork mazeman given the reviews but would otherwise probably not go out of my way to come back.

I actually read and made the ramen from Ivan Ramen's book, so I was very curious on what I cooked compared to what the original source is like.

[coney island tofu]
Tofu squares are deep fried with a miso sauce on top.  Looks wise, it kind of oddly looks like a hot dog with the yellow from the mustard and 'red' from the miso.  Taste wise it was pretty good, but a bit heavy as expected.  It would have been nice to have some contrast like shiso, but given this was supposed to mimic a hot dog, I think it was a really nice play on the dish.

[spicy ramen]
So unlike other ramen's, Ivan Ramen uses chicken stock and dashi.  One of the things really different is the ramen broth is very fish forward.  The dashi is really really aromatic.  

The noodles are made from toasted rye noodles, but aren't as spongy as other pure flour based noodles

[vegetarian ramen]
This ramen is made from a soy sauce vegetable broth.  Oddly enough I enjoyed this more than their spicy ramen because I prefer not to have so much of a fishiness aromatic on the stock.  It was served with a roasted tomato, enoki mushrooms, and baby arugula.  Vegetarian ramen wise, this was probably the best one I've ever had.

[overall]
If you like more daishi/fish forward ramen, then this place is for you.  If you also want the best vegetarian ramen ever go here.

Personally I wish they would make their ramen a little bit more chicken forward and ease a little bit on the fish/dashi aromatics.

Usually I write really long reviews but this place doesn't really need a long one.  

Ambience: Cool
Service: Friendly and fast
Menu: good selection
Food: Tasty, but way too salty
Prices: a little pricey for what we got

It's a great place to get a casual meal with a friend and on a weekday we didn't have to wait for a table.  I think I prefer ramen a little more on the traditional side, but I do have to give this place props for trying things that are a little outside the box.

Oh, Ivan. Oh, oh Ivan. Why?  Just, why are you the way you are?  

So following my trip to the Slurp Shop in the Hell's Kitchen area, I was morbidly curious to see if things were any better at the b&m shop on Clinton. Plus a friend wanted to check this place out so the stars aligned for Ivan Ramen, round 2.

I feel I should start with the good just to show how I don't hate everything about this place. It's actually really nice inside, bordering on the cleanest ramen joint I've ever seen. The bar doesn't directly overlook the kitchen like in most ramen shops so you're not directly exposed to the ramen making process. I like that I don't have to watch out for splashing water as they fling the ramen around. The server is really friendly and informative. Keep her and keep the cleanliness. It's the only reason you're not getting a 1-star review. 

Now onto the more important bits. The food is expensive. Like the Slurp Shop, the portions are tiny and overpriced. The Tokyo Shio (which I did not reorder) is $1 more here for no good reason. All the ramen are a minimum of $13 here and what the heck, it's the same lack of topping options here. 

Onto the taste. The JFC is kinda just plain and unexciting, but not bad. I would've preferred a good old kara-age. The okonomiyaki, advertised as having been highly rated in some magazine, is not bad but a little too sweet and onion heavy. 

Now I love ramen. I search high and low for good ramen spots. How has a ramen shop with the hype this place has gotten get soooooo much wrong? The noodles were overcooked into oblivion so there was no texture. Our two ramen of choice were vegetarian and spicy red chili. The soy broth was like super, unfiltered, concentrated soy. Complete lack of complexity. The spicy red chili was a slow burn type heat which builds and builds. It wasn't the heat itself that bothered me. It was the lack of flavor profile. Cut back on the heat if you want patrons to taste anything. 

Remember guys, ramen is supposed to be a cheap meal as it was originated in Japan. The drinks were also hella expensive so total bill pre-tip for 2 apps, 2 ramen, 4 drinks was $100. For a ramen shop, this is super stupendously ridiculous when your product is literally a wet noodle. And a bad one at that. 

DO BETTER!

Got the Tokyo Shio Ramen, it was a nice clean broth. Good noodles, definitely would go again to try another ramen.
I also got the duck heart skewers which I liked the dipping sauce.

The 1000 year old deviled egg was not what I expected, it was actually the filling part that had the preserved duck egg. I was a bit sad about that, but the filling didn't have as strong of a flavor as I hoped

Not too many guys from Long Island decide they are going to open a ramen shop in Tokyo.....and end up being crazy successful!!!

So I first need to preface this review by saying ramen isn't my favorite thing. 
 Yes, I am of japanese descent.
 Yes, I am not a very good driver. 
 Yes, when I laugh hard, you can't see my eyes.

But for some reason, it is just ok for me...I love udon, but ramen, meh....I'll eat it, but I wont go out of my way for it.

....until now

THIS IS THE BEST RAMEN I HAVE EVER HAD.

We went to Ivan Ramen right when it opened for lunch and were seated near the front.  The restaurant is very modern/Japanese inside....but the front area is a little narrow.  
My wife watches my face...'Do you want to move?'.  

I say "No....I'm ok."

She says 'Babe....'

I say "No....I'm ok."

She says slowly .... 'Babe'

I say "Ok.....let's move....I want to see into the kitchen"

She smiles....

I ask the waitress to relocate us and we sit at the counter and are able to watch the food come out of the pass...much better.....ok...so I am a little stubborn...

My wife orders a yuzu lemonade and it tastes like the nectar of the gods...so delicious!  Is it wrong that my mind immediately starts to think of alcohol pairings for it?

We start with the roast pork musubi, which had salted plum wasabi, roast tomato,  and toasted seaweed on the bottom.  It came out fairly quickly.  My wife never swears or curses, but after she put it in her mouth she says 'Ohhh $#!%!'.
Yeah....it was that good.  All the combinations of flavors mixed together blended into the perfect bite of comfort.

I ended up going with a summer ramen (Cold Lemon shio ramen with sea salt, dashi broth, roast tomato, shiso, and rye noodles ) and my wife had the Tokyo Shoyu ramen with soy sauce, dashi and chicken broth, pork chashu, and rye noodles.  
Both were amazing.  The rye noodle definitely made my day.  It was toothsome, and had a lot of taste.  The broth on the cold ramen was nice and sharp.  It had lots of flavor, and the roasted tomato matched well with the sharp citrus.  The tokyo shoyu broth was amazing....I finished my wife's bowl after I was done with mine.  It had amazing depth of flavor and intensity. The fatty piece of pork floating on top didn't hurt either....

 I don't know if he has figured out a way to get the broth to stick to the noodles better or if the absorption rate is better with the rye noodle, but the broth flavor really flavored the noodle well.

I will be back here.......as soon as I can!

Avoid, run away, do not wake up and go go go.

Well, what can I say.  Having seen the hype about Jewish guy from NYC, moving back home, and opening his flagship store in America.  What a complete, utter, disaster.  The waiter was a pretentious snob, the food was awful, and the hype over this place has definitely worn down.  I'll tear these points off one at a time, in case you're interested.

1.  My dinner companions arrived and were told that it was a 20 minute wait.  It took 1.5 hours, and four visits to the host before we were seated.

2. The waiter was rude, pedantic, and saccharine.

3. The ramen.  Awful.  It was worse than the college noodle stuff you remember - so bad.  Imagine boiling a pot of water, dumping it in a Chinatown gutter, and then collecting the run-off.  You just about have the taste and smell.

4. The hype was not worth it.  A couple of TV shows about this place, and you would think that they would step up their game ro at least have a bit of consistency.  Neither was true.  Companion and I ordered the exact same thing and they looked totally different.  After finishing only a bite and setting it aside, the immature server didn't even ask how it was or if anything was wrong.  Just took it away and came back with his paws out looking for a tip.

I do not write a lot of reviews, but when I do - you should pay clear attention like the clarion call from a bell on a winter's morning.

Peace love, and good ramen (elsewhere).

Ramen is as good as the hype.
Experience is sub par. Party of 5 including 3 young children checked in and was given the automatic 20m wait answer.  50m later, after at least 2 parties of 4 or 5, including 1 group that checked in at least 20m later than us got seated, we were told for the 4th time that your table is almost ready.

Really liked it - went on a Sunday night with a good group of friends. Put our name in and then went to the bar around the corner to have some drinks until they called or texted (every single restaurant should do this....). The food is reasonably priced (no, maybe not for ramen, just for nyc), the wait staff is so terribly pleasant (they should train others), the ambiance is okay if not cool...definitely not romantic or charming, the music and room is really, really loud (please put cork on the ceiling). All-in-all, the ramen was really good, met all of our expectations. Yes, I ran there after reading the Times review, no I don't usually do that (sometimes). It was bustling yet efficient. It's worth the trip if you like ramen, was a fun and food-filled experience, don't know how else to put it.

Chinese Broc and garlic - great
Kewpie Ebi - good/great, I don't love the heads....it's a personal thing
Triple Pork Ramen - holy richness, but so delish
Spicey Ramen - eat it before it starts "blooming", tore my stomach apart, but man was it good going down, if you like spicy...dive. right. in.
Shio Ramen - good, least flavorful of the three, but I still finished the bowl

I don't see the fuss on the 'fully-loaded' aspect, but I'm not a ramen connoisseur...of course, I ordered it and didn't regret it, but I could have gone either way?

When the appetizers are better than the ramen is, and you're in a place that supposedly specializes in ramen, something is off. 

Our party of three plus one straggler was seated immediately, which was great because within minutes of sitting, a swarm of people came in and filled the remaining spots. 

For appetizers, our server Jonathan (more on him later), recommended the broccoli, the meatballs and the scrapple waffle (I don't remember the actual Japanese name.) On. Point.  The broccoli was almost cured in a ponzu soy and had a huge kick of garlic, which is never that bad of a thing. The meatballs were delicate, yet rich and doused in a ponzu mayonnaise, which really may have had some crack cocaine in it because it was just as bomb as Jonathan said it'd be. 

The scrapple waffle. Okay. For those of you who haven't been to diners outside of NYC, scrapple is basically the poor man's corned beef hash. Made with a variety of....parts, it's basically a way to blend and then flat top your leftover...parts. Obviously Ivan doesn't do scrapple as crudely but that's the premise. They cook it in an waffle iron, so it actually comes out as a waffle, which is hilarious. And you know what, it works. It really works. I don't recall how they prepared it or what sauce was drizzled on top but it worked. 

My friends ordered the triple pork triple garlic ramen and the special of the day, which was so the pork chashu/chasiew tsukemen, which was comprised of cold noodles served with a bowl of really hearty corn and bacon broth (honestly, it was straight up chowder.)  It was tasty, but is couldn't shake the feeling that I was dipping noodles into chowder. The triple pork triple garlic ramen was delicious though salty. Also, pay the extra $2 for an egg. So worth it. 

I ordered the Tokyo shoyu ramen, which came with the chashu (pork belly) as well. I got an egg because egg and ramen just go. 

I understand I ordered a soy sauce based broth. I understand that. But wow it was salty. I don't really use salt when I'm cooking for myself so this was a swift NaCl kick to the mouth. The noodles were average. Meh. 

The star was our server. Funny, genial and personable, Jonathan was pretty much the man. Attentive but not overbearing, and quick to refill your water or drink order, he knew his recommendations and suggestions. Give that man a raise!

Cash and credit, and the Cisco network is their free wifi for guests.
Ramen was ok, at best. Tiny portions for the price.  Walked out hungry and had another meal after I left.

Got the shoyu ramen, which funnily enough auto corrected on my iPhone to "shitty", which is exactly what it tasted like. The broth was reminiscent of soy sauce water. Noodles were good though. 

Not worth $18 for ramen + some tomato and egg for the fully loaded option. I'll stick to totto and ippudo for my ramen cravings.

Not quite up to the likes of Ippudo or Chuko, but Ivan Ramen has some solid offerings. I had the spicy red chili ramen, and it was solid. I had almost ordered the extra pork chasu for my dish, but the waiter assured me that I would be fine with what came standard, the shredded pork. However, the shredded pork was shredded so finely that it was all sitting at the bottom of the bowl and lacked the texture that I was really looking for in my ramen. Taste was great, texture was lacking.

Coney Island Tofu is an interesting take on a hot dog-like thing. I don't know that I would get it again, but it was interesting. A little heavy handed on the mustard.

Service was great for lunch on a Thursday!

Tasty ramen!

I went here with a couple of friends and we all agreed that this was one of the better ramen places we've had in NYC. A couple of us had the regular ramen and one tried the tsukemen style special which was pretty good too.

Its low broth style, which they tell you before you order, different but didnt alter the taste.

overall, I think its a little bit too pricey for what you get but it was still a good bowl of ramen.

I was the first person there at Noon - it was super humid inside, and there was kind of a funky smell and a fly. Then I asked to use the bathroom and it was occupied. Waited a good 10 minutes and the person didn't come out, so I left.
I'll definetely come back for their spicy chilly ramen.... 14 dollar which is worth it.... The taste was just so good....

So I first got a taste of Ivan ramen at his slurp shop in Gotham West Market. I was thoroughly unimpressed. The broth was weak and lacked character and the mazemen did not wow me the way Yuji ramen did so I honestly could not understand what the hype was about. I was ready to compare it to David Chang's pathetic ramen but I figured Ivan deserved another chance at least. So I visited his LES restaurant for lunch. I ordered the roast pork omusubi and the spicy prawn mazemen. The omusubi was OK but as soon as I had my first bite of the mazemen I immediately thought it was better than what I had at slurp shop. The flavors were bold and memorable, in fact I wasn't expecting the heat to be as strong since it was cold noodles after all. I also liked the use of the whole prawn and the intrinsic flavors of the head is always delightful. I will still say that in comparison, Yuji Ramen is better so that will still be my preference. Ivan's is also a little pricey for ramen but the portion is more than the mazemen at Yuji's Whole Foods pop-ups. All in all it's an interesting addition to New York's ramen scene.

Came here with a small group of friends (about 4 of us) on a Friday night and we were seated within 5 minutes. The place was pretty packed but the service wasn't affected. 

Loves the triple pork triple garlic mazemen and the jfc. Cocktails were a big weak but I guess that's not what you really come here for anyway. Will definitely be back for more mazemen and to try other intriguing apps.

Overall menu: Very innovative, great flavors, very interesting stuff.
Service: Great
Noodles: very springly, perfectly cooked every time, perfect perfect perfect
Sauce/ soup: TOO salty! And too greasy. Ramen is supposed to be greasy and salty yes I know, but I have to make sure I get 3x volume of noodles per soup/sauce every bite because this really is quite excessive.
Other items (salads, crispy prawn etc): Excellent.
Ramen soup was good and tasty. However, only defect was soup was too salty because took much soy sauce was used which made soup also too dark

In town from Chicago and wanted to grab some Ramen at one of the places that are well known for it. I'm surprised that Ivan has the rep that it does because our experience was great. We had the meatballs, pickled Daikon and a smoked salmon dish to start. All of which were very tasty starters. There were three of us and we all had different ramens and the flavors were great in all of them. To top it all off all of the support staff were very helpful and pleasant and our server Johnathon was great: Down to earth, knowledgeable, and always there when we needed anything. Couldn't have asked for a better NYC lunch experience. Bravo Ivan Ramen!!

We had such a great experience for lunch today at Ivan Ramen. The service was fantastic. Jonathan really took care of us and the support staff was stellar too. This was my first time having authentic ramen noodles and it was quite yummy. Definitely try the meatball from the starter section of the menu. We will definitely be going back.

I have never been to the pop-up at Whole Foods but Ivan Ramen has been more enticing, being that it is a permanent establishment. We were quoted a 15 minute wait which was quite accurate. We quickly got seated and just as quickly decided on our order, mine being the spicy chili ramen and his being the triple pork garlic mazemen.

My bowl came out looking pretty unattractive. It looked like the bowl was sloshed around before it reached me. The broth was too spicy to be enjoyed throughout the meal. I guess because I am a no-frills ramen gal, I didn't like the rye noodles or the minced meat. The meat just made the broth thicker and even harder to drink. The mazemen wasn't too shabby. The noodles were thicker and chewier than the rye noodles in mine. His chasiu pieces were depressingly small.

For the price, Ivan Ramen is just not worth it.

sadly i didnt like this place and I was really hoping I would as i need a good ramen place in LES.  It was very expensive for a very small bowl of ramen.  The Ramen it self was perfectly cooked but broth was very greasy.  The flavor was good but on the salty side and unfortunately the grease made it less enjoyable after a few bites.  the egg was perfectly executed but cost $2 ontop of the $13 ramen price.  The spicy ramen was nothing special and saw almost no meat.  The service however was great and I love the decor and atmosphere.  I would go back only if I had a really strong craving for ramen and there was no wait.  Execution was good but overly priced for too greasy broth.

Had the spicy pork ramen which I thought was good.  One pet peeve of mine is not getting a pipping hot bowl of ramen,  this ramen was just warm.   I bet they don't serve it so hot so that way it takes you a quicker time to eat it.  
Also ordered the pork meatballs,  yummy..  I would come back to try some other ones.

A 3/5. It's the noodle itself. They use the Chinese wonton noodle base which has a little Alkaline taste. For wonton noodle, u may add some vinegar, however, ramen broth didnt go well with sourness. Therefore, even the booth is good, the noodle is the main problem.

I don't get it? Why do people love this place? I couldn't find anything to like about Ivan other than the beer that I ordered. Our waiter was slow and smug. I couldn't stand the interior of the restaurant. The weird teal color of the walls and the booth padding mixed with the light-colored wood paneling and fluorescent lighting made me feel like I was in a hospital cafeteria. I hated the grooved texture of the chopsticks. I get that it makes it easier to grab food & noodles, but they really turned me off.

The 1000 year old egg was gross. I took one bite and almost spit it out. Though I will concede that its not my flavor profile and I get that maybe other people might be into it. The pork musubi appetizer was the most edible out of anything that we ordered, but the presentation was really off. The seaweed wrapper stuck to the plate so half of the filling fell off when picking it up to eat it. It was overfilled and cumbersome to eat.

We both were disappointed that the signature dish, the triple garlic pork mazeman wasn't available for lunch. We asked the waiter why it was only on the dinner menu and he said "if we had it on the lunch menu everyone would order it". Uhhh, is there some kind of alternative business strategy that I don't know about where restaurants choose not to serve things that people want and that will make them money?

The ramen was so bland. So so bland. Blandy blandy bland. I got the spicy red chili ramen, and my boyfriend got the shoyu fully loaded. I hated the texture of the shredded pork in the broth--the only way I can describe it is that it tasted like someone using a crock pot for the first time and making a mistake. The flavor was so one note. Even the egg in the dish felt sad and tasteless. I remember being at Totto ramen and never realizing that an egg could taste so good--literally the best egg I had ever tasted. I can't believe people put Ivan and Totto or Ippudo in even the same sentence together. The shoyu was equally disappointing. Also totally one note in flavor. Way too much onion. Like someone with huge hands took a heaping handful and just dumped the shredded onions on top. 

It was so bad we started laughing when the bill came because of the absurdity of it all. I can't believe that the shoyu fully loaded was $19. Really?!

Ugh.

I sat at the bar was helped my a tall African American man- he gave me the best recommendation as to which ramen dish I should get. I was not disappointed. I got the red chili bowl which was spicy but still enjoyable. The ambience of the place was quiet and it was very clean. My dish came out very quickly. It has an outside deck which is beautiful for a bigger group and the bar area seats about 10 people. I suggest the bar area because you have a small view of the kitchen. This place did not disappoint.

This new-ish Ramen joint got a lot of press buzz over the summer of 2014 so I had to come in for a peek and I'm glad I did. (This review is for visits in late August)

I'll be honest, I don't give a damn about noodles, I hit Ramen joints for the broth and this place did not disappoint. The Shio broth that I had was old...., meaning, it was brewed long enough to really get out all of the flavors from the ingredients. (Making good broth is very much akin to making good booze or beer lolz) No plastic packet into hot water broth here! The spicy broth was very thick and definitely had a kick - the only drawback is that it almost seemed too condensed if such a thing is possible.

I'm not a fan of wheat so I asked for rice instead of noodles and after some discussion, they were down with it. (Ippudo waiters don't blink an eye) The "Rye" noodles are not wheat free as I learned so if you think the rye noodles will save you from gluten, think again. This is not a neg against Ivan though - it is a noodle joint after all.

The appetizers are really awesome. The devilled egg is insanely creamy and yummy and the daikon with shrimp is a new and.... very unique taste. (I loved it.)

The decor and ambiance are par the course for a funky little LES eatery. The cartoons over the bar add a nice splash of color. The staff is friendly, efficient and have great knowledge of the menu. Ask them for their favorites! They may surprise you with their choices!

All in all, this is worth the trek to the LES if you are already not in the neighborhood. I've always arrived for early dinner or lunch and have never had to wait for a seat upon entry. Ippudites - yes, there is no-wait and line life beyond Ippudo for your Ramen needs. :-)

I went here twice for lunch over Columbus Day weekend. My first visit I had the red-hot cold mazeman, which was delicious -- cold spicy ramen noodles in a bowl with no broth. I also had the pickled daikon appetizer, which was also a winner. I came back the next day for the spicy red ramen soup fully loaded, which was disappointing. The broth was served luke-warm (inexcusable), and overall it was just OK. Definitely a let-down after my first visit. I sat at the bar, and it was not particularly crowded for lunch. Service was good, and the space is nice.

If you're hungry and expecting the ramen bowl to fill you up, think again.  This fusion ramen joint serves the portion like cup o noodles.  I ordered the triple pork ramen (or whatever the official name is), it wasn't bad, something different, but not enough to fill me up.  I finished that bowl in 5 minutes and I took my time slurping it!   Don't get what the hype is about this Ivan guy.  Because he's a LI Jew who opened a ramen joint?

First time we passed by accident,  we bumped into Ivan. The second time that we decided to try out, Ivan was in the shop too - explaining his entire menu to some customers. 
    Anyway, let me go back to the actual food review. We ordered meat balls, yuzu lemonade, Tokyo shio ramen and triple pork. We ordered ramen first and totally forgot about the appetizer. When we mentioned that to our waiter, he told the chef to hold on to the ramen order. Ivan really takes the best time of eating ramen SERIOUSLY!
     Yuzu lemonade was amazing! Refreshing! Strong yuzu flavor but I like to let the ice melt a little more while bf enjoyed it just like that.
     The deep fried meat balls were actually quite disappointing. My mom can make it better, more meaty and juicer amd I'm serious about this.  The only difference or specialty on the meat balls was the sauce. They used the sauce very similar to takoyaki. Hmm...no good...
      Tokyo shio ramen was disappointing too. The only component I liked about the ramen was the rye ramen noodle specially designed and manufactured by Sun Ramen. The broth was oily to me part of it was due to the fact that the soup was bland. Too strong on the dashi and I didn't taste any chicken broth flavor. Charsu was too fatty. I understood that they used pork belly but just too fatty. I almost wanted to cry out " did you ever try Totto ramen?" Or I should just call for the regular chicken paitan to do a direct comparison. 
      Bf got the triple pork which had bacon in there. Plus it's the only ramen with tonkatsu broth. Well, again the noodle was excellent. And the broth had much more dense flavor to it. 
       The boiled egg, my favorite thing whenever I eat ramen, was just okay. The texture of the egg yolk was perfect. I wished the eggs could be more seasoned. If the flavor didn't even stay in my shio ramen, how could you taste it if you order anything else? 
       I think I'm just a traditional ramen person than fusion.

After seeing a bunch of my friends check into this new ramen joint, I had to see what the fuss was about. Came here after work on a Friday evening and got seated immediately. About 20 minutes later, the place filled up and there seemed to be a long wait. Guess we made it in time before the dinner rush. Had the dry ramen - cheese mazemen. Pretty good. Also had the 1000 year old deviled egg.. As an Asian person, I thought i was getting the actual 1000 egg.. but it was just a typical deviled egg. Don't get it. I probably wont come back as there are many ramen joints out there to try.

To start off, this was my first Ramen experience and I now see what the hype is all about! I ordered the tokyo shoyu ramen which is one of their classic dishes and loved it! The pork was cooked perfectly and the egg was a great touch. I also liked that they used whole wheat noodles because it made me feel like what I was eating was healthy :) The broth was a little salty for my liking, but I've never been a fan of super salty foods so that's just a personal preference. We also got the meatball appetizer and it was delicious- the sauce was creamy and flavorful so I would highly recommend that! 

The reason I give this place 3*s is because of the rude hostess. One person in our party was running late and not answering her phone (later found out it was bc her subway was stuck underground). The hostess refused to seat us until our whole party was there, which is understandable, so I put my name and phone number down so we could walk around and explore the LES while we waited. We were told it was going to be about a 20-30 minute wait, and 10 minutes later I got multiple calls and annoying texts asking us if our whole party was here, then telling us we needed to come back because the table was ready. Of course, when we came back she refused to seat us again...and continued to pester us about when we would expect the other person to show up! To conclude this long review, I would probably not come back because in addition to the annoying service, there are other ramen places in the city I want to try.

Great Ramen dining experience. I ordered the vegetarian ramen option, and it is delicious. They have a roasted egg in the dish which I thought was very unique and added an amazing taste to the meal. 

Definitely worth the money.

I think the outdoor seating is absolutely adorable, and it's a great date spot, as well.

I've been there at least 4 times and am looking forward to making it back there.

Ordered the beef tongue which was good but not exceptional. I liked the spicy mustard but the tongue was a little tough by my measure. The spicy ramen though... It was really nice and the broth, albeit thick, had great flavor and embraced. Nice hear level.

I read about Ivan Ramen in Time Out magazine's cheap eats feature and it was in walking distance from my accom.  I'd never had Ramen before and it was delicious. I was seated straight away at the bar/ servery area (as a single) by the efficient if not very friendly hostesses at front of house. Here I got to sit with other singles and watch the kitchen and the handsome barman/server, while u ate my noodles and drank my beer.
A great experience for someone who us not so keen to dine alone.

Interesting ramen noodles with okay broth, but $14-15 for an okay bowl of ramen is a bit too pricey. Better off going to Ippudo if you're willing to dish out that amount of money for ramen. Or for even better ramen go to Totto in midtown (they have two locations, it's THAT good).

Flavorful food and a friendly staff.

Get the ankimo dirty rice, full of flavor and loved texture of the monkfish liver ($14).

Triple pork mazemen was good, but I prefer having soup so I would recommend the classic shoyu.

Skip the meatballs ($9), very regular.

Overall, creative dishes that are full of flavor.

I got the devil eggs- Best part of the meal. Delicious but I usually all love all type of devil eggs.

I got the Spicy Red Chili Ramen
(dashi + chicken broth, minced pork, smashed egg, rye noodle). I like the spicy broth - flavorful. My friend got the non-spicy ramen and it was really bland. There was not much meat in my bowl. I liked the noodles. It was average ramen- nothing special.

Was very excited to finally try Ivan Ramen and it did not disappoint!  All dishes were incredibly flavorful and delicious- for appetizers we shared the Roast Pork Musubi, which were compliments of the chef, and they were excellent! We also tried the Pork Meatballs and the Chinese Greens with Garlic, both dishes were outstanding and the flavor was oh so good! Ramen wise I chose to go with the Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen, which was ah-ma-zingly tasty. We had the friendliest server who was top notch. Overall we had a really great experience and I am looking forward to going back!

This was my second time coming here. I went with two other friends. It was super busy but we were able to be seated right away. I had a very pleasant experience. The waitress was very attentive and the atmosphere was very trendy and upbeat.

Popped into Ivan ramen for a very late dinner the night I arrived in NYC. I was a little apprehensive considering that no one in the restaurant looked Japanese, but I figured hey if I've had excellent French cooked by Asian chefs back home, why can't the folks at Ivan do the same for Japanese-inspired cuisine?

The unusual take on Japanese starters got my interest piqued. I ordered the cold Chinese greens and garlic, which is essentially hong kong gailan or bak choy tze char (stir fry), but the cold version. The vegetables were cooked with the right amount of crunch and firmness, but the soy sauce base was just a little too sour for me. Perhaps I'm too much of a traditionalist, but I would've preferred less tang and more flavorful garlic.

On to the ramen itself, I got the spicy red chilli ramen with extra char shu. The soup was excellent - rich with bone essence, good pork and chilli oil and just enough fire to warm my homesick belly. Noodles were springy and while I wished my egg wasn't smashed, the bits I caught were melt-in-the-mouth good. The only thing I wished was more kick ass was the char shu, which wasn't anywhere as smoky or charred as what I usually get at Bari Uma in Singapore but that's comparing a Hiroshima style of cooking to uh, Shikoku style? My point is that my gripe is probably a stylistic issue rather than any fault on the chef's part.

Glad to see some diversity of ramen offerings in the city. But then I wouldn't expect anything less in New York :p

I've tried a couple of ramen places in New York in the short time that I've been here, and personally I prefer the other places that I've been.

I ordered the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen ($14), which I heard later that most people who try this one usually leave disappointed. The chicken broth is complemented with soy sauce and dashi, and the dish comes with one piece of chasu pork, egg, and rye noodles. I think I was caught off guard by the soy sauce because even though I knew what was coming, it's not something I've had before at other ramen places, and I don't think I'll be getting that one again in the future. The pork chasu was good (I've yet to have bad pork chasu) but it was small and underwhelming considering the ramen costs $14. The rye noodles were interesting as well, thinner than what I've become accustomed too; it was good but I personally prefer thicker noodles. As for the egg, I'm glad they tried to soft-boil it (because, besides deviled eggs, it really is the best way to eat eggs), but it was way to undercooked, the yolk was hardly cooked and the egg whites were runny as well. 

I also felt like the portion size was smaller than at other places that I've been to.

Definitely one of the better ramen/noodles shops in NYC. Having followed Chef Ivan Orkin's work from Japan to stateside, I was pleasantly surprised and impressed to see how he localized the menu for this shop. 

We had the shio ramen, the triple garlic triple pork ramen, katsu, ebi, casear salad, and dirty rice. The meal was fantastic, and I'd recommend the silken tofu casear, any ramen, and the dirty rice. You can do without the katsu. I don't think they use panko, so it doesn't give it the typical fried crunch Japanese cuisine is accustomed to. 

I know Chef Orkin spends a lot of time mastering and prepping each of his dishes, but I found it particularly fun and interesting to see his Jewish/American background webbed through the menu. Whether it be an ingredient or play on a dish, you can definitely see his heritage come through while still being very respectful to Japanese cooking. 

The dirty rice is probably the best representation of that, as it's typically a southern dish with chicken liver that he substitutes with monk fish liver. The short grain rice is definitely imported from Japan, and seasoned perfectly. The small bites of monkfish liver adds an ocean-ness, but doesn't over power. It's an incredibly well balanced dish, especially when you squeeze the lemon juice over it. 

I'd come back here again without worry, and think it'll be a NYC ramen staple within a few years.

3 stars for A-OK ramen. I went during lunch and they didn't have the triple pork triple garlic mazeman that I wanted to try. I don't know why but it wasn't on the menu. I had the red-hot cold mazeman. I really liked the noodles but the flavor was fine, not anything super special.
I might go again just to ry the triple pork triple garlic one but I'm not in a rush.

While walking around the LES after dinner at Balvanera and sorbets at il Laboratorio Del Gelato, last Saturday, we noticed, "hey, no long lines outside Ivan Ramen's" so we decided to put our names down for a table.  After 20 minutes, we received a text message telling us our table was ready (actually, it wasn't.  They thought we were a table for 2 when there were 3 of us.)  So after another 10 minutes or so, we got one of the bar tables in the middle.  

Although some of the apps looked interesting, we knew we couldn't eat more than ramen noodles so we ordered the chicken paitan with eggs ($2 extra but worth it), Tokyo shoyu and Tokyo shio.  The chicken paitan was too salty, as was the Tokyo shoyu, and the shredded white meat chicken was alittle on the overcooked side.  Since I haven't noticed other Yelpers mentioning oversalting as an issue, perhaps it was just an issue with our order.  

Service was friendly and proficient and the place was clean and not too noisy so will probably go back and try the apps, too.

Really dig this place. We went one chilly/rainy afternoon and it really hit the spot. the place is really cool inside, laid back and the servers were really friendly. I really have almost zero ramen experience, so I'm no expert, but I really loved what I got (Tokyo shio) and so did my friend (who bravely got the spicy red chile and man was it hot!) We also had the Roast Pork Musubi and we both agree we could've easily ordered another of that, or two. Oh and my cocktail, which had hibiscus flower in it, went down like water. I probably could've consumed 4 of those like water!! So I recommend this place - totally dope casual place for when you're bumming around in the cold and need something comforting in your belly.

I still dream of the miso mushroom chili and shoyu broth at Ivan Ramen. Seriously. I'm salivating right now. 

Went here on a cold, rainy night a couple of weeks ago, and the timing couldn't have been better. Though we had a small party and it was fairly early on a weekday, we still had to wait 10-15 minutes to grab a table, which is a testament to the popularity of this place (especially on said cold, rainy night). 

When we finally were seated, our server came to us and explained the menu-sake, appetizers, ramen, and all. Since my friends and I are sake n00bs, we had to ask for special help in choosing what would complement our meal. Our server recommended the Oze No Yukidoke Ookarakuchi sake (had to look that one up on the menu) since it was on the dry side, and would pair well with the sweeter shoyu-base soup we were all getting. 

Since my group was vegetarian, we ordered the Tofu Coney Island appetizer and three  (identical) bowls of the vegetarian ramen, add one soft boiled egg, please. The Coney Island appetizer didn't sound too interesting, with "miso mushroom chili, yellow mustard," and "scallion," but let me tell you...this ish is OFF THE CHAIN. For those of you who want to know (and that should be all of you), it's tempura battered and fried tofu cubes, topped in this RIDICULOUS salty, creamy mushroom sauce, mustard, diced white onions, and scallions. HOLY CRAP. I honestly didn't even know what to do with myself. I thought I would have to lick the sauce off the plate in public...but luckily, our ramen came in time and I spared myself the embarrassment. 

Onto the main event: the shoyu broth...I mean, the veggie ramen. Usually, eating vegetarian ramen at restaurants is a huge disappointment, because you're given overcooked noodles and an assortment of par-cooked vegetables in a soup that's essentially watered down soy sauce. This was not the case at Ivan! The balance and depth of flavor of the broth was impressive, and the enoki mushrooms, roasted tomato, and assorted greens were perfectly tender and not too tough to chew in the broth. And then there was the (optional) soft boiled egg (although we all know it's not really optional, is it?), which leaked its runny yolk all up in the broth, and created a creamy and thick soupy substance that coated the noodles properly. I slurped up the contents of the bowl, despite my extremely distended belly and the sweat dripping down my face (from the hot broth, sake, and being seated directly underneath a heating vent).

Like I said, I'm salivating now, just thinking about this meal. If you just stick to your bowl of ramen, it's a fairly affordable and incredibly filling wintertime dining option. I will definitely be back. (PS: Props to our server for attending to Amanda Seyfried, Justin Long, and his brother, who were sitting at the table behind us the whole time, without freaking out or asking for an autograph. I was seriously tempted.)

Came here Saturday night with the boyfriend and it was just want we wanted. We were told about a 10-15 minute wait at about 8:20 pm so we went down the block for a quick drink. About 4 minutes later my phone buzzed that our table was ready. So we finished up and went back. We were seated "outside" on the covered patio. They had heaters (and I knew we were about to eat steaming bowls of soup) so it wasn't so bad, but it was cold enough that we had to keep our jackets on the whole time. So, not ideal. To start we got the sauteed Chinese greens, which I would highly recommend, and the pork meatballs. The meatballs were good but not stellar, lightly fried and topped with bonito. For our ramen bowls, I got the Tokyo Shiyo (salty) and he got the Tokyo Shoyu (sweet). The biggest differences between the two were in the broth. The delicious rye noodles and simple green onion and pork toppings were the same. I slurped the whole thing up. All in all, it was a solid meal. The boyfriend had never had anything but instant ramen so he gave this 2 thumbs way up! The decor is super fun too.

Food was great; noodles were perfect, broth was flavorful as hell. Even better, the waitstaff loves talking ramen. Our server, Nicole, was borderline geeking out on the difference in between each broth. That kind of enthusiasm is contagious, made the meal all the more memorable.
I enjoyed the ramen here so much that I bought their cookbook! We'll be back. Service was good and the price was right. The portions was on the smallish side, but very filling.

Totes disappointed on the ramen front. There is definitely ingenuity on the non-ramen dishes - Coney Island tofu, 1000 year old deviled egg, tofu caesar salad - but not enough to save this place from my ire.

The spicy chili ramen was a mess, but boring. The pork garlic mazemen was the same. I left both bowls to my friend to eat and if you know me, you know how astounding it is for me to leave a noodle dish untouched.

I used to go to Ivan Ramen in Tokyo a while ago when it was super good.  After Ivan-san left to NY, that place became non-edible ramen place (almost). 
Here in NY, I tried 3rd time and can't believe the temperature of the soup. It is [NURUI], not hot enough. All the Japanese friends complained same issue. Maybe because they are afraid to get sued like McDonald??  But this temperature issue has to be changed.

I still like Shio that he makes. Yet their Chasu is too oily, no-taste. 
Spicy ramen is good, yet the noodle is too thin, weak for the soup. 
The topping of raw Enoki is very strange. 

More we visit, more we get disappointed.

Totally underwhelming and expensive two people lunch and $60, granted we got two appetizers, one beer and two ramen bowls, but just definitely not to up to the standard I expected after all the hype about Ivan Ramen Tokyo etc.  What's worse is that the small plates outshined the ramen (in this case Shoyu Tokyo Ramen, which had two pieces of pork and one egg and literally NOTHING else besides noodles, I think this is the barest bowl of ramen I have ever experienced. I do agree the noodles were excellent.  But that's all there was excellent, service good and peppy, but in a ramen shop, its the broth and the bowl needs to stand up , not much else.

I had heard a lot about Ivan Ramen from friends, press, etc but I think it's a lot of hype. Quite overpriced and just decent. I've had much better ramen. Staff is nice and it's a clean looking place but it didn't live up to expectations. The yelp reviews are quite accurate at 3/3.5 stars.

Came here for lunch last week on a cold day (perfect ramen weather!). It was only my second time eating ramen and I definitely enjoyed it more at Ivan Ramen. I ordered the Spicy Red Chili Ramen. Key word -- spicy!! I am a big fan of spicy food and my mouth was on fire, but I still managed to enjoy it. The presentation is really nice. My bowl was a combination of red, green and white.  Noodles are good, broth was tasty. Probably not the healthiest thing in the world but it hit the spot. Probably not somewhere I would come often, but if I have a ramen craving, it's nice to know of a good spot close to home. Oh, and another thing. It's a little pricey here. ~$20 bucks during lunch for a bowl of soup. Maybe I'm missing the concept of ramen and what goes into it, but I feel like I would come back more often if it was between $10-15.

I really love this place. Whenever I come, the service is always wonderful, and the food is delicious. My boyfriend and I started coming here because my boyfriend can't eat pork, and they have a lot more options in that regard than Ippudo (which I also love). We always get the Spicy Red Chili Ramen. It is SOOOO good. The noodles are definitely different than i've had at other ramen places, but that's what I like about them...they're a little chewier, but in a good way. And the broth is AMAZING.

The other great thing about this place is that there's always a lot of people, but not SO many that you're forced to wait forever. We first tried Ivan out during the summer, when the NY Times review came out, and it was crazy then, but I guess the fanfare has died down a little since then. I come here about every 2 weeks now, because it's great ramen without having to wait 1.5 hours (ahem, Ippudo).

If I could put zero reviews, I would but then I wouldn't be able to write this review. Simply put, both service and food were terrible (and I am not biased so those two factors aren't a cause-and-effect of one another). When my friend got there, the reservations were just for the two of us and they refused to sit her (but get this--when a group of 3-4 came in and were waiting on one more, they decided to sit them first instead). So that was already a bad start. When we ordered, we noticed that basically if we wanted to add any real, typical ramen topping (e.g. bamboo shoots, eggs), we would have to pay extra (most ramen spots already come with toppings and only if we want extra toppings, we would pay extra..this place does not come with ANY toppings at all..except for seaweed?). That was pretty ridiculous as I've been to numerous other ramen spots and this was the only place with such a menu pricing. Ok, so maybe their ramen will be out of this world that they would make us pay for toppings. WRONG. It was so bland and not flavorful at all.. a homeless man on the street would be able to whip up something better. Terrible, terrible use of spices (maybe we were supposed to pay for spices on the side as well?). I will never recommend this place to anyone nor will I come back. They should at least not hire inexperienced college kids as their staff who just goofs around and not pay any attention to their customers at all (it wasn't even a busy, packed day!). Never, never again.

The food here is great but be careful when eating, peppers can easily fly into your eyes. I will be dining here again and may eventually upgrade my four stars to five. When I was eating and the pepper flew into my eye, I think it would have been nice of them to throw me a little something on the house for experiencing some of the worst pain of my life, no exaggeration, but they just said "it happens" pretty much. Next time, I'm wearing glasses. Ha

I guess we feel differently as I am often contacted by the owners in regards to good and bad reviews I have left. I'm not sure why you think responding a week later makes your customer service above average?
You apologized for the misunderstand and not for the BAD information your staff gave. 
Good luck fixing that! All the best :)

There is so much hype surrounding this place. And normally with that much hype, I would give any restaurant the cinco treatment.  The only reason why I didn't was because, I've eaten at famous ramen places, and this place is legit, but the broth was too salty.  That was my only complaint.  

However, the service was impeccable.  I could go on and on about how attentive everyone was (including, asking me if I wanted to charge my phone because they overheard that my cell was out of battery).  Now, that's some attention to detail.  Dig that! 

But, I will say, the other dishes.  Wow, now that's something to write about.  My favorite was this deep fried shrimp dished covered with this delicious Chipotle mayo, laced on top of a bed of watercress. Truly, I could have eaten a pound of those shrimps, but my belly was full from the ramen. 

Would I come back... absolutely!  But, to try the other offerings.  Shout-out to the manager, Mike, who did a phenomenal job explaining all the dishes and just being a fantastic host.

This place is a 3.5 but I really couldn't round up. 
My party of 8 was seated immediately which was great! But we were seated in outdoor seating turn inside seating (so outside seating had been closed off and several heaters were added). This was only this past weekend so it was cold! We didn't enjoy this so much. We asked if we could move to another table which was vacant but they said people were already waiting for it (nobody sat there for another 10 -15 minutes). Anyway, they brought each of us blankets to wear while we dined which was really nice of them. Plus it was great photo op :)

We ordered a few appetizers to share. I'm not a pickles fan so I didn't try the Akiko's Pickles but my friends who did try it said they were delicious. We also ordered the Warm Japanese Sweet Potatoes. We all thought they were great! The Greens were also really good! For my entree I ordered the Chicken Paitan Ramen. It was good ramen but not excellent. Definitely not $16 worth.

Everything about this place rocks.  I had the spice ramen and it was amazing.  We also had spiced pickles recommended by the waiter.  They were spicy and delicious.  The service was perfect.  My only complaint it was hard to sit on the high stools when you are a short person or a large person like my meal mate.  This place is definately worth the trip.  A little pricey for lunch but well worth every bite.

After reading a article on grubstreet "best of 2014". I decided to give this place a shot. Spicy chile ramen & Lancaster Okonomiyaki were both part of that so called best list. First the ramen at $15. I was expecting more then a egg & noodles, and that exactly what I got...seriously the biggest joke ever. Then the Lancaster Okonomiyaki....umm No. I will never trust grubstreet again. Service was diner service. Tiny cramped seating so uncomfortable. Place where I sat smelled like spilled beer that was left over from nights ago. At this price range I think it's the worst ramen in NYC. Worst $40 I ever spent.
