I had the tokoyo shoyu ramen and it was very salty. There was also only one small pork. The staffs are very nice and they serve you right away. Very cozy on a tues night. Not sure if I would be back

So I went thinking that it would be great ramen, In actuality it's ok. I mean it's good ramen. The prices are 15-17$ . I like the shoyu , I disliked the spicy ramen. the chicken one is not that good. The place is actually really cool. Cool playlist. The staff is really friendly.

I've read so much about this place as it is big in Japan.

Pros: the ramen, what else! The rye noodles are my favorite. Oh, and the pork meatballs!

Cons: Nothing. It's how a restaurant should be done!

I sat at the bar alone one evening on a cold winter night.   One a great spot to warm up from the cold.   I had a spicy pork amen, recommended by the staff and it was great.   

I usually don't go out alone, so it was so nice to have such a great bartender to talk with, his name was Everett.   When I am back in the LES I will be back!
Side dishes are better than the actual ramen, which is just OK. Not a big fan of the rye noodles either. Pretty steep price for what you get, too.

1 star for the ramen
+1 star because the service was great
+1 star because I generally enjoyed my appetizers

Ah, what a let down. A news article popped up on my feed that Ivan Ramen was finally taking reservations, so I immediately made one for dinner the following weekend. I'm a huge fan of both Ippudo and Mu Ramen, so I was pumped to try ramen that made NYMag's list of the best restaurants of 2014. 

We were seated promptly upon arrival and ordered roast pork masubi, pork meatballs, and Lancaster okonomiyaki as starters. The roast pork masubi was probably my favorite. The pork was tender and delicious; I just wish I got more than one bite. The meatballs were good, but I think they overcompensate for average meat with the breading and the sauces. The okonomiyaki was also good, but I wanted a lot more of the mayo - the pancake was a bit dry. 

For ramen, we ordered the spicy red chili and the triple pork triple garlic ("TPTG").  I knew going in that the TPTG only had a small amount of broth, but the dish was SO disappointing. The noodles were well cooked but the dish was very lacking in flavor. A few hours later, I do have garlicky dragon breath....but while eating, there wasn't nearly enough salt or umami. It was just boring. The spicy red chili ramen is spicy, but that is THE flavor. It's very one note, and the broth was also strangely thick and gritty. 

The servers were so nice and offered to bring me a new ramen when they saw I wasn't eating mine, and then comped me the Chinese greens and garlic to try and make up for the disappointing ramen. 

Unfortunately, I don't think I'll be returning here. Everything on the Ippudo menu is vastly superior, and the ramen is definitely better at Mu Ramen.

came twice and service was great both times. love the ambience and had no problems getting a table. sat in the covered backyard both times and loved it. ordered the triple garlic mazemen the first time and  really enjoyed it.  garlicky and bits of bacon on the bottom, whats not to love? its brothless, know what to expect. 

had the 1000 year old deviled eggs, greens with garlic and pork meatballs. pork meatballs were awesome but the eggs and greens were just ok, nothing special. 

second time i came, the chicken paitan ramen and mazemen were good the first few bites but both were so overpoweringly salty. all i tasted was msg and had to drink water for hours after to get the salty taste out of my mouth. ruined my meal completely. the portions are small and the paitain ramen with an added egg came out to i think 18 bucks (its RAMEN.. its supposed to be poor man's food and prices are getting outrageous for this street food.. but this is a rant for another time...)

place is not consistent, which is a big no no. would i come again?.. maybe i would give it one more try if i am in the area. but would never make a trek for this place.

We got sat right away which was a great start. Got the pork meatballs as an appetizer, they were amazing. Cant say anything wrong about them! For dinner we ordered the chicken ramen and the pork ramen, the chicken broth wasnt cutting it for me. The broth in the pork ramen was amazing definetely recommend that! Always add egg to your soup, you wont go wrong. Momofuku has better soup, and better flavor but this place was pretty good too!

Delicious chicken ramen, perfect for cold NYC night. Made reservations for party of 5 in advance. Glad I did, even though we were seated in the Garden and had to wear our coats! The wait for those without reservations was still over an hour at 7:30 on a Monday eve. Would love to go back next time I'm in town.

Very good ramen. Ivan's Dan Dan Noodle was okay. The Tokyo shio was much better.
Definitely get the beets and pork. Delicious (obviously unhealthy).
Lots of recommendations for the Roast Pork Musubi but I found it only okay.
Can get packed very quickly. Expect to wait, even for just one person.

The promo for this restaurant was crazy, the meal itself was ok. Not that the ramen wasn't good, but... it's wasn't amazeballz like I was expecting. The consequences of high expectations back fires again. 

I will say the drink I got was very tasty, and fresh, but almost felt like a meal. It tasted like a cucumber drink, I didn't really taste the alcohol, until an hour and a half later I got a little buzzed then it was gone... I quickly chugged two of those drinks down within our meal. 

I got the Triple Pork and Triple Garlic Mazemen and forgot that mazemen meant little broth and my little ramen heart sank... I was looking forward to the brothy goodness of pork and garlic, but I didn't. The noodles were very flavorful and the dish was good but again high expectation dies hard. 

Service was good the server was attentive and helpful in explaining the menu, A+. Water glasses were always full A++

But I'm sorry, I don't see myself coming back here, sorry, I think there's probably more places to explore and better places to revisit. Nothing against the establishment but like I said not amazeballz.

Great ramen in s space with chic decor.  Crowded, even for lunch. However, staff was adequately attentive and accommodated a fifth person in our party, even though our reservation for four people. Will definitely come back.

Maybe three stars is a little stingy... (when is yelp going to let us give 1/2 stars?!)
The hype around this place maybe raised my expectations, so take this with a grain of salt. 
First of all--great move for them to take reservations. I've been known to wait on lines for food (#cronut), but I'd much rather make a reservation--especially when is 20° outside! 
We were all set to order the pork meatballs to start, but were tempted by the special pork ribs. They were really good--tender and flavorful. They had a crust that i think included seaweed and sesame seeds. Sounds like they're thinking about adding them to the menu. If they do, get them! 
I had the spicy red chili ramen. It was good, but not great. Again, i had really high expectations, which may not be fair. The noodles were very good. But the broth was a little to thick and a little to salty. The smashed egg was ok, but i prefer a soft cooked egg in my ramen. And it added to the overall thickness, which isn't necessarily a good thing. The minced pork was ok, i think, but it wasn't really distinguishable in that thick broth. I would have preferred a more traditional treatment where the elements were cleaner and separate parts of the whole. This was more like a stew where the broth, noodles, egg, and pork were all melded together as if they were sitting on the stove too long. Or maybe the broth is simply to thick for my liking. 
I'd like to go again to try the meatballs and to give a different ramen a try, but with so many great ramen places in NY, not sure when that will happen amy time soon.

I'm a die-hard ramen fan, and have been to all of the best ramen-ya restaurants in NYC. I love this food so much, and I feel sorry for anyone that thinks it's just "over-priced soup".

Because of this love, I was beyond excited to FINALLY try Ivan Ramen, especially with all the hype surrounding this place.  Let me tell you, I was not impressed, and actually borderline disappointed. 

I heard there was a long wait to get in, so me and my friends came exactly at when they started serving dinner, and were able to snag a table.  I will tell you, within 10 minutes of opening, every single seat was taken.  The menu also has a good assortment of cocktails, appetizers, and ramen choices- so definitely not lacking there.  But what sadly feel short was the actual ramen. I got the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen, that came with the rye noodles. The noodles were nothing special at all. They had the right texture of a noodle, but the flavor was a little bland.  I honestly didn't know why this noodle was called rye, when it was just a plain old noodle.

Next, the broth....UGH this is where I was REALLY disappointed.  The broth is described as dashi + chicken- all I tasted was FISH.  Like a really overly Thai fish sauce seasoned broth.  It was off putting, and not what I wanted to taste in a bowl of Shoyu ramen.  I thought I was crazy and overreacting, so I let my friends taste it and they all thought the same thing.Fail.

So yea, this place is crazy packed, and the talk of the town, but I will pass. For me Totto Ramen and Ippudo are still the reigning ramen masters in NYC, and for that I am grateful.

I had read so much about this place and was not disappointed. Thankfully I used OpenTable to book my lunch time and so that I didn't have to wait 90 minutes! 
The staff was great and very welcoming. My big bowl of ramen noodles was perfect. It was very busy but the staff was very relaxed and explained the menu and made us feel welcome. I can't wait to go again!

On a cold, blustery Saturday evening, I came here with my cousin to fill that void in the belly. 

We arrived around 8pm and we luckily showed up when there was a mass exodus of people. We asked how long it would take to seat a party of 2 and we were told the wait would be about 30 minutes. And since my cousin has never been here before, we decided to stick it out. No more than 10 minutes had passed, and the host was nice enough to seat us quickly. Thank you awesome host!

The menu options are curated carefully, so don't have to worry about the paradox of choices. 

For starters, we tried the 10 year deviled eggs (2 for $3.50) and we ordered 2 servings. This was an excellent dish. Both my cousin and I have not had preserved eggs in a long time, and we both liked the creativity and taste of this dish. Then, we had the Tofu Coney Island ($11). I was a bit apprehensive about mustard and tofu, but it worked well. The tofu was fried crispy (tasted almost like French Fries) and once again, I appreciated the ingenuity of the dish. My cousin also tried the roast pork misubi ($7), but it was underwhelming for my cousin. 

As for the ramen, I had the vegetarian option ($15) and my cousin ordered the chicken paitan ramen fully loaded ($21 total). My ramen was decent, but I have had better and for cheaper. And the broth was just too salty for my liking. My cousin also wished the ramen came "scalding hot" and also noted the egg yolk wasn't fully cooked. We both didn't know if ramen is supposed to be served at this temperature or hotter, but both agreed on a day that was soo cold, something hotter would've been nice. 

I had a "Hottotodi" cocktail, which is basically a Hot Toddy but made with Junmai. I could drink this all night, but at $12 a pop, I only had one. 

Definitely a solid ramen experience, but for $47 (tip added in), I think my Piggy Bank won't allow for this on a regular basis. 

Oh and after the meal, we were both fiending for dessert, and it would've been nice if there was something to end the meal sweetly (how about some mini mochis with interesting flavors?)...

I was actually pretty pleasantly surprised by Ivan. I follow him on Instagram and ever since trying his Chicken Paitan at a Ramen Festival a few months ago, I've been meaning to check out this place when I get to make some rare trips to New York. I was a little skeptical since the Yelp reviews aren't super great, but having had such a positive experience with his food in the past, I definitely wanted to give the brick and mortar shop a try. I hear this one is supposedly better than the West Gotham one, so keep that in mind.

My friend and I went on a Sunday around 1pm and oddly enough, there was no line at all. By the time we left--around 2pm, a line was definitely forming so we got lucky I guess. I tried the smoked salmon rice and the shoyu ramen. 

Smoked salmon rice bowl--YES. So spot on. I wish Ivan would offer this in a smaller size to complement the noodles as a rice set which is pretty common amongst California ramen shops. Smoked salmon is cooked and sooo good. It also comes with a nitamago egg that is cooked quite well. There's also some salmon roe and the rice is perfectly seasoned and just flavorful enough.

Shoyu ramen--first thing I really like about Ivan is that he uses chicken broth. I'm so sick of only pork stock broth which is pretty much what everywhere else does, so chicken was a wonderful refreshing change. Upon first sip, it's really, really good. I loved the chicken flavor and the noodles are a special rye noodle that is fairly unique among the ramen industry and just as chewy and delicious, if not better than typical ramen noodle. The con though, and what makes this not a five star place for me is that once you start making ample progress through the bowl, you realize that it's actually really, really salty. It starts to get a little difficult to eat toward the end once the salty flavor hits you.  The salt overpowers the chicken flavor toward the end making it hard to slurp the whole thing down.

All in all, I think it's a solid ramen shop and I really loved it. I wish I went with more friends since I actually think his non ramen dishes are all really interesting and from what I see on his instagram, they're all super stunning. Would def recommend you try an appetizer or two if you head over! It is a bit pricey--my meal ended up being close to $30 for lunch.

tldr; really yummy chicken stock ramen with rye noodles which is pretty unique. a little on the salty side toward the end. salmon rice bowl is super on point. def try an appetizer or two with your ramen

We ordered the Kewpie Ebi (fried whole prawns) and the Silken Tofu Cesar Salad, along with the Spicy Red Chili Ramen and the Vegetarian Ramen. 

Neither one of us liked our appetizers. There was a lot more watercress salad than prawn in the Kewpie Ebi and it, along with the Cesar salad was too heavily dressed to eat. Both ramens were very good. We eat a lot of ramen and really liked the rye noodles. They were nice and chewy. We would of both liked more meat and/or vegetables in our ramen. These are available as add ons (we both had ordered one each) but these are rather limited (more vegetable options please!) and would quickly ratchet up the cost - we'd be looking at a $25+ bowl of ramen. 

Overall it was a great choice for a cold night but not nearly as good as I had hoped it would be given all the fantastic reviews.

The spicy red chili ramen was probably the best ramen I have ever had. Super spicy upon first bite, but completely delicious once you get used to it. The special treat are the small pieces of pork that seem to gather at the bottom. Rye noodles have this amazing smoky flavor that really complemented the spice in this ramen. 

My friend ordered the vegetarian ramen option and wasn't as blown away. To counteract her less than fab main dish though, her appetizer was the Coney Island tofu dish. It was super inventive and delicious, even for a carnivore like me! 

Kinda confused at the lack of great reviews, as our service was excellent and our wait time (with reservations) non-existent.

Going to Ivan? I say, the more quirky item you order, the more you will enjoy this place.

We were really looking forward to trying this restaurant, but came away disappointed.
The pork meatballs were quite good as was the kewpie ebi.  We then ordered the
dan dan noodles.  They were way too oily for me, so my husband finished those and I ordered the chicken cutlet katsu. When it arrived, my husband and I took one look at it and thought 'shake and bake'.  It had a heavy layer of breadcrumbs and was dry inside.
The sauce was non-existant and the cabbage on top, although a welcome bit of vegetable, was plain. Very disappointing dish.  The people at the table next to us tried
it as well (it was a big portion) and they also thought it quite ordinary.  They had several dishes and were also disappointed in their selections. That sealed it for us, no more trips to this restaurant.
Gets my vote for one of the top ramen spots in the city!  Obsessed with the spicy ramen.  Get the pickles if they have them.  Also get the sake in the can.  The middle one.

My first visit was a 4 star - but on my second visit I nailed the menu. 


Love the spicy ramen, greens and dirty rice. 
The dry ramen is to die for. 

Skip the deviled eggs. 

Yum.

My first visit was a four star review but after going today for lunch I had to revise my review. The service is impeccable! Same as last visit. The food is what improved this time. Maybe it was because I was drink the first time. The coney island is spectacular! I love the play of it looking like loaded chili cheese fries but really it is tofu "fries" with a mushroom "chili" and mustard "cheese"! I really have to go through the entire menu!

I really wanted to love Ivan Ramen. I heard all about Ivan from David Chang's (he owns the Momofuku chain fyi) TV series, "Mind of a Chef." Apparently Ivan, a Jew from Long Island fell in love with a Japanese woman and moved to Japan. He created his own technique of ramen making and it was a massive hit in Japan. 

Knowing this I was excited to go here with my friends. Did I have exceedingly high expectations? Yes. Was I thoroughly disappointed? Yes. 

I came here as a party of 4 at 10:45pm on a Friday night. It was still packed but we were seated immediately. Our server was so knowledgable and kind. He was really good at suggesting what to order and quick to answer all our concerns. Here's a fun fact: all the cartoons that you see by the kitchen are cartoons of Chef Ivan. Apparently he was so famous and popular in Japan that he got a hit anime series! 

Although the service and ambiance of Ivan Ramen is really very nice the food was mediocre. I ordered the spicy chicken ramen and was heavily disappointed with the lack of chicken flavor. All I got was spice with no depth. My significant other ordered the pork garlic maizamen which was deelish.

I think I would come back again but with all costs AVOID all the other ramens and just get the maizamen.

The good: Amazing and courteous service. Clean and well designed surroundings. Food comes quickly.
The bad: Pricey for the quantity. Ramen was saltier than expected and quality was so-so.
Bottom line:  It was ok to try once to see what the hype was all about, but probably not going back anytime soon.
Yikes. Got bad food poisoning after a lackluster dinner here (as did my bf). Hope it was a fluke, or that the original location outshines the GW market spot.

Managed to squeeze a weekend lunch reservation -- menu was slightly limited, however I got the Shoyu ramen and "Japanese michelada." Rye noodles were great, broth was slightly salty but flavorful. Michelada was refreshing I'll definitely be back to try the rest of the menu.

So many people, Japanese style.
I came here last Friday.
Noisy enough, but the food looks pretty.
Nice service, but there is no hot water.
The soup of ramen was a little bit oily, but still delicious.

What a great spot. Ramen is by far one of my favorite things to eat during the Winter and Ivan Ramen's spicy ramen is like none other I've ever had. It's thick yet brothy consistency gives you just enough heat, but still allows for a ton of flavor. This menu is much more extensive than the slurp shop, which I frequent for weekday work lunches, so we had a chance to sample so many more of the appetizers- the pork meatballs, the  roast pork musubi, warm japanese sweet potatoes- all of these were out of this world. The decor is fun and the crowd is diverse- a combination of older couples, families, hipsters and solo's all sharing their love of ramen. It's a fantastic spot, definitely recommend.

I recently moved to the Lower East Side and as soon as the moving van left I ducked into Ivan Ramen and got ready to have an early dinner.  Though most people want to sit at a table, I thought that the seating was too tight so I opted for the spacious bar area and was thankful for that once it started to get packed in.  The name "Ramen" is a little misleading as I think their best dishes are: 1000 Year Old Deviled Egg, Silken Tofu Caesar Salad, and Tofu Coney Island.  If you are going for Ramen, my favorite is the Spicy Red Chili Ramen.  Do yourself a favor though, split the ramen with someone or you will be sorry in the morning. #FireInTheHole

The spicy ramen (fully loaded) was indeed spicy and the veggie ramen had veggies but they were both underwhelming, no depth of flavor, and at this price just nowhere near worth the cost or the wait. Couldn't see the point in finishing either. 

The 1000 year old deviled egg was also a major disappointment. Overwhelmingly fishy taste which the waitress said was the bonito but it couldn't have been just that. Was like sucking on a boiled carp head.

UPDATE: Michael Hojlo of Ivan Ramen was very kind to reply that it's just bonito on the deviled egg. This misses the point or I guess I wasn't clear enough: the deviled egg does not taste good. I know what bonito is. I've had 1000 year old eggs before. This one was disgusting and the waitress was kind enough to take it off the bill. (She was an excellent waitress.) Good luck to you, too, Michael Hojlo of Ivan Ramen.

My good friend Giovanni C suggested that I come to this place. He worked with the owner of Ivan Ramen back in the day and told us about his creativity with food. We showed up here after a night of drinking at roughly 11PM. The place was completely packed and I was worried that we would've had to wait. Lucky for us they were very good about their reservations and seated us immediately at the bar(we like sitting at the bar). 

We started off with two Supashina Biru's. Had no idea what type of drink it was going to be but it was only 6 bucks and hey... My name is Biru too lol. It turned out to be a Sapporo beer poured on top of a very spicy mixture.... Almost hot sauce like. It wasn't bad but it's worth the experience....especially since they don't have a full bar here. 

We ordered the pork meatballs and the deviled eggs. Pork meatballs were excellent. Deviled eggs were decent(they were served refrigerator cold). For the mains my wife got the spicy ramen and I went with the chicken katsu. The ramen noodles were exquisite. They're a bit thinner than what I'm used to but whoa.... Absolutely amazing. The spicy broth was spicy enough to please our south East Asian heritage but not spicy to the point where I needed to down a gallon of milk after every sip. The broth was also relatively "thick" for ramen broth, which we liked. The minced pork and chopped up egg gave it some great texture. My chicken cutlet katsu was exactly what it sounds like. A large breaded deep fried chicken cutlet cut up in to smaller pieces so they're chop stick friendly.  The mustard that they smear on the plate will clear your sinuses instantly. Be careful with that stuff! The shredded cabbage mixture that they put on top was pretty but didn't really do much for me. 

All said and done, the ramen here is the superstar of the meal as it should be. The meal was also pretty cheap. Two people, two cocktails, two appetizers, two mains for 55 bucks. 

I did miss that they didn't have the more traditional pork belly sliders as do most ramen joints but the pork meatballs were a nice change of pace.
Cozy noodle place with a strong energy.

Good ramen, but felt awfully small for the price. This is an unfortunate case of backlash to high expectations. Ah well. Tried the 1000 year old deviled egg and  I also wanted to try their okonomiyaki but since I came at lunch they said I couldn't order it. That was kind of annoying. We tried the omu rice (like a Japanese rice omelet with ketchup) that was ok. 

Hubby had the fully loaded ramen, which was good, but nothing that wowed me. I had the smoked salmon donburi which I felt the same about. 

Decent place, but I don't understand the hype. No wait for lunch on a Sunday.

So, so wanted to love Ivan's but that didn't happen. 

Came with two friends, huge ramen aficionados. We know about his history and understood this will be a modernized experience. Got all that...

The ramen flavors were interesting, and I appreciate the modern twists on dirty rice and the okonomiyaki... but everything was just so salty. Nevermind the quality ingredients used when everything felt so blanketed with salt. 

Each of us had a smaller than average bowl of ramen (even by Tokyo standards), plus shared a okonomiyaki and a dirty rice. Oh and a $4 cup of barley tea (really?!!) Came to almost $50 p/p for what's supposed to be Japanese fast food. 

Don't mind paying for good food but this ain't. While service was excellent, the food hype disappointed *sigh*

I'm surprised that ivan doesn't have a five star rating.  The Coney Island tofu and gem salad are  creative and delicious.  As a vegetarian, I enjoy the veggie ramen but wish that they would make another option w the normal noodle (ie not rye).  Service is great, professional and fast.  And food is very consistent.  Would recommend that everyone try this spot at least once.

I made sure to eat here twice before making up my mind about how much not worth it this place is. I tried the chilli ramen on the weekend and came back to try the most raved about triple pork triple garlic mazemen on a regular week night. The modern twist of this place seems to be salt. Everything was just too salty. But you can't help but eat all of it because the tiny portions also come with the modernized dining experience. 

Overall. Ivan's is absolutely not worth it. For the same price, please do yourself a favor and go to Ippudo; there, you can enjoy a delicious bowl of ramen and those yummy pork buns. And if you somehow want to give this place a try because, for reasons I do not know, it is on one of those Top Ten Ramen lists, please make a reservation and don't do the ridiculous wait time.

We came here for lunch on a Saturday.  There was no wait, we were seated immediately.

Had to have the signature shoyu ramen here.  Was not terribly impressed. Was very salty, and that is all I can say about it. Not sure what all of the word of mouth is about this place.  I guess I should have ordered something else, but the appetizer, at least was good.  

The tab is more than what I would have thought.

Ok. The spicy red chili ramen was pretty good, but not amazing. 

The Roast Pork Musubi was nothing short of astonishing. I'd go back just to taste it again.

Excellent service.

Oh dear, another so-so ramen place. In my quest for the best vegetarian ramen, I certainly had to try this place. The veggie option has buckwheat noodles, a large mound of arugula, a roasted tomato, and enoki mushrooms. Even though I try to go as close to vegan as possible, I had it topped with an egg which was the only thing to save it. 

When a veggie ramen is soy based, you better hope that it doesn't just taste like watered down soy sauce broth. Unfortunately, this one didn't have enough depth of flavor to surpass that sodium surge. And since uncooked enoki mushrooms taste like nothing, that leaves the noodles (which I liked), tomato (a great flavor but so small) and arugula (a heap of it that wilts into nothing).

It's just not worth the $15 + $2 egg.

I feel like a lot of restaurants feel like they can charge NY prices for a shitty meal. This is NOT the case. If you charge outrageous prices and your quality sucks, no one will come visit! Can we please make this loud and clear because Ivan Ramen has been sorely misinformed. 

At all other high-end ramen restaurants a hefty $15 a bowl will get you a lot of food. At Ivan Ramen, $15 got you a tiny bowl of ramen, not enough soup, a whole soft boiled egg (which is about a half egg more than other places), and two skinny, measly portions of pork. Are you serious? I want to say the pork was good, but I can't remember because it was gone in two seconds! My mom couldn't even find her meat in the spicy chili bowl. THE MEAT IS NEARLY NONEXISTENT! 

Max intrinsic value: $8. Price charged: $15.

Usually, after leaving a ramen shop, I'm stuffed. But Ivan Ramen leaves a lot to be desired. Never coming back again.

My boyfriend and I have been looking forward to trying this place for a long time and we finally made it here for Valentines Day (shout out to their willingness to allow reservations via open table). 

The menu is straightforward and organized by course, like usual. The appetizers on offer are all very delicious sounding, but of course we got the pork musubi, which comes on a triangle of salted seaweed and has a ball of sushi rice topped with pork and hot sauce. 

For our entrees, we got ramen (of course). My boyfriend ordered the mazemen, triple pork and garlic, and steeped in a shallow tonkotsu broth. Very good, from what I tried. My own choice was the spicy red chili ramen, which I thought was very good. Mine came with smashed eggs (interesting switch from the usual soft boiled eggs), and I got it topped with enoki mushroom. The enoki was raw, which I wasn't expecting, but still good. The broth was very spicy, perhaps a bit too spicy for my tastes, especially since it was the kind that sticks to your throat. The noodles were amazing though--rye noodles seem to be a specialty at Ivan, and I was not disappointed. I think next time I'll have the shoyu or the shio. 

We also ordered some good beer, and I was happy to have had the chance to eat here.

The tables, FYI, are very small and close together--when packed, I can imagine that it can be a bit of an ordeal to try to leave, considering even the smallest people are wider than 2 inches.

I've been to the slurp shop in Hell's Kitchen and was not too impressed, but decided to give the restaurant a try knowing that they had different things. I really enjoyed the food here more than the slurp shop and the service was great.

I deviled eggs were delicious, but I don't know what about it made it 1000 years old. It tasted like bonito. I loved the mazemen. That was the best dish of the night and I would come back here just for this dish. We also ordered Chinese broccoli which tasted like it might have been pickled with soy sauce, vinegar and garlic and came out cold, which I did not expect. 

The main reason I can't give it better rating is because of the spicy ramen we ordered. It was the saltiest ramen I've ever had in my life. I had to ask for hot water, which they said they didn't have but just warm tap water. I added a whole cup, and it still was salty like no other!

Eat the mazemen!

Went with my brother on a cold snowy day and it was great! Tasty ramen, really refreshing Yuzu lemonade and a very friendly service. Make sure you make a reservation because on Tuesday evening when we were there, 'walk-in's ' had to wait for 1 hour. We will be back :)

Food (4/5)
I don't know why there is so much negativity for Ivan Ramen, but I had a pleasant experience. For my order, I got the shio ramen, which is comprised of rye ramen noodles, chicken-based broth, chashu, and egg. The rye noodles were chewier than I'm used to for ramen, but it wasn't an unpleasant texture. The broth was delicious - just the right amount of heaviness and body without being too salty. I don't think people can come into Ivan Ramen with preconceptions of how the broth should taste. It's not the same base as shoyu, miso, or tonkotsu broths, so don't expect it to taste like that.The chashu was melt-in-your-mouth good with a good level of fat content in the meat. However, the egg was a bit cold, which threw me off a bit but all is forgiven because the yolk was cooked perfectly to still have an ooey-gooey texture. 

Service (4/5)
Our waitress was extremely sweet and patient in describing the menu to us. She seemed pretty knowledgeable in answering all of our questions. I shared a shio ramen with extra noodles (kaedama) with my boyfriend since we weren't super hungry. Normally for kaedama, the server will bring it out once you have finished your initial serving of noodles so as to maintain the freshness / heat. However, given that my boyfriend and I were sharing, she asked if we would like the kaedama and the shio to be brought out together, which I thought was very considerate of her.

Atmosphere (4/5)
Very trendy restaurant. Seating is varied with hybrid booth / seat arrangements in the front of the restaurant space and high-top tables near the back. We were seated at a 4-person high-top near the back. Next to our table are cute Japanese-style cartoons of customers eating ramen, so it gives the restaurant a fun, light-hearted, and trendy feeling. I definitely recommend this place for a night out with friends or family. 

Bottom Line
I came into Ivan Ramen hesitant based upon all the negative reviews. However, after tasting the shio ramen, all my reluctance disappeared. Don't expect anything similar to shoyu, miso, or tonkotsu-based ramen. Shio ramen is chicken-based, and if you're open-minded, you may find it to be just as delicious.

I love ramen. It's something of a personal goal of mine to try every bowl the city has to offer. Ivan Ramen has been a spot that I've been reluctant to hit up - mainly because when I'm craving ramen I want a really good bowl and the reviews for Ivan ramen just aren't that great. So I've been putting it off for a while now. On a whim last week I decided to just go! I was in the mood to try a new ramen place and a foodie friend of mine said that Ivan Ramen is his personal favorite. I trusted his foodpinion.

I understand that the ramen at Ivan Ramen is not your traditional Japanese ramen but rather a Japanese inspired American ramen. Still it doesn't make sense why the ramen was SO salty! The first few bites were good but as I went through the bowl it continued to get saltier and saltier!

My boyfriend got the spicy pork ramen and found hardly any bits of pork. All the meat was chopped into bits and thrown into the broth. To be fair, when he did have some pork he said it was really good. But that doesn't change that there was just not enough pork in the ramen.

Ivan Ramen didn't satisfy my ramen craving and I probably won't be going back again. :(

Yes, the ramen is a little different in it's approach to broth but the end result is still close to normal ramen. The restaurant itself is rather cramped and the waiters have issues handling it's high customer demand.

I write this review based on this Ivan Ramen being my sole experience at a Ramen restaurant (my only prior experience with Ramen is from a foam cup in college).  What I can say is the ambience is artsy, hipster and trendy.  The staff was excellent from hostess to waiter.  Our appetizer (pickles and sweet potatoes) were delicious, fresh and at appropriate timing and temperature.  Our Ramen was served piping hot and all requests for additions and subtractions were made flawlessly.  I had the vegetarian ramen with no enoki and loved it.  I am now a Ramen fan and look forward to trying another venue specializing in Ramen.  

My favorite part of the experience was hearing the story about the owner and the restaurant origins.

Slurp!  Finally make a trip to Ivan Ramen today.   It's been on my list for nearly a year now.   Made the intrepid trip way crosstown on this frigid NY day in order to soothe my craving for a piping bowl of ramen.  And I found it in the $15 bowl of Spicy Ramen.  The spice level of the soup was manageable - hot but not Szechuan-hotpot-mind-numbing-hot.   The ramen did taste more and more salty as I got to the bottom of the bowl but it was curtailed with the copious refills the waitstaff was sending my way - thanks!   Partner ordered the Shoyu Ramen which had more defined and clear flavors.  I would totally go back to try the apps and the fried selections.   Note there are more options on the menu for dinner.

So delicious and fragrant. Such good strong flavors. 

But always so jam packed loud and busy! It's hard to spontaneously go there.

Let's get this out of the way first. This is not Ramen. 
It is hard to categorize the cuisine at IR due to the fact that it serves to imitate Japanese ramen but lacks the nuanced flavors to even approach the most banal level ramen bowl.
The noodles are not true ramen but more like thin imitation soba. The broth is way too oily and they over use dashi so even a salt based chicken broth is dark brown. The chashu consistency varies as well. Instead of two thin slices in my bowl I had one inch thick hunk of meat while the person that I was dining with had barely a shavings worth.
I've heard complaints about portion size at this place but honestly I do not think that should be an issue. If it's about quality over quantity for $15 a bowl I am cool with that. However that just isn't the case here. The palette for this restaurant is very far from its inspiration. And I would understand if Ivan wanted this to be some sloppy nyer version of the traditional Japanese comfort food, but it just lacks even that which makes good  New York slop worth ingesting. It has become like so much else in this generation of brands and identities, a poser.

Came here with friends and we ordered "Ivan dan dan noodles", "tokyo shoyu ramen" and "red chilli ramen". Noodle wise, the dan dan ramen was best because it's thicker and has a better bite. The broth from shoyu ramen was lacking that hearty broth flavor, probably won't be ordering that. The red chili ramen was good with flavor but super spicy. The spiciness over powered the overall ramen experience. I also think it's too pricey for their portion size. However, the overall ambiance of the place was nice and comfortable.

Decent but not outstanding.  Came on the lunch hour and enjoyed a mix of the small plates.  My favorite item was the pork meatballs.  I also had the chicken cutlet katsu which wasn't great.  The pictures of the dish look better than what you experience on the palate.  I wouldn't go out of my way to come back here.

A girfriend and I  went last saturday night without a reservation (yes, apparently THIS ramen place takes ressies!) and managed to snag spots at the bar with a 10 minute wait.  It's fairly roomy for a ramen joint, and modern and airy as well.  

We ordered 2 apps - the daikon appetizer  (good, but a bit heavy on the oil/dressing) and the fried pork meatballs  (tasty, but too heavy as an accompaniment to bowls of rich ramen).  The monkfish liver fried rice piqued my interest.  It looked ginormous, and i'll probably order when I have more people in the party. Next time.

The ramen:
My friend had the spicy chilli ramen.  The broth was rich, decadent and spicy.  The rye noodles were a very thin noodle - kind of like a somen or vermicelli noodle.  It was nice and chewy and very tasty.  The bowl came out warm and not steaming  (according to the bar server, the owner prefers a certain temperature for the ramen - which we found questionable, but whatever, he reordered a second replacement bowl for my friend, when he realized he could not argue with a Japanese person who has eaten plenty of bowls in Japan)

I had the triple pork, triple garlic  mazemen. Very little broth, but super rich and super porky.  And Shioppai!  A bit much, actually.  It hit the spot, with the frigid temps outside, although I felt a bit nauseous afterwards.  I guess eating an equivalent of a half cup of grease will do that to you. 

We had two cans of the seasonal sake - 19 percent alcohol!!!  Yes, dinner was so much better for it.  

Overall, it was good, but a little too rich/greasy/salty and pricier than warranted - (90 bucks for two).   The ramen crawl continues...

Ivan's got good ramen and good dishes.

Ramen in general though, unless it's great tasting and great value, is hard to earn a 5.
It gets kind of busy since it's small, but really good stuff. The ramen was obviously good, but I would also recommend getting the pickles and the yuzu lemonade.
Love the pork masubi, shrimp ebi and the chicken paitan ramen.  Things you should know before eating ramen; Ramen is salty, mazemen is brothless.
You wanna get real bloated, come here and you'll have yourself a real nice time. Everything Is Salty. Drink was nice. Drink was pretty. But don't let the white man try to feed you ramen

Grabbed dinner here last night for a friend's birthday, and was excited to try the slurp shop. I first tasted Ivan's creations over at Gotham West Market over a year ago, and figured I'd use this opportunity to try the expanded menu at his LES location.

We arrived for our 8:30pm reservation, and immediately ordered drinks to celebrate - the ume ginger fizz for me and a red wine for my friend. The ginger fizz was presented in a pint glass with a sugar-crusted peach slice on top. I couldn't really taste the sake, but the drink was fruity and refreshing. Near the end of the drink, the drink had a tinge of saltiness to it - a very interesting touch.

My friend ordered the spicy ramen and I ordered the vegetarian ramen with an added egg. Both were pretty good - mine was very light and had an interesting combination of flavors and textures. The soft boiled egg was creamy and perfect, per usual. I thought the vegetarian ramen had a little too much soy sauce for my liking, and as a result didn't have any unique flavor profile, but the soup was a good fit for my interest in eating healthy-ish for Spring Break next week :)

Overall a very trendy spot, but not one of the ramen heavy hitters for me.
Yall telling a lie! This shit is so good! I had other ramen and this one is best that pulled pork b like a dude pulling my hair!! Plus the egg!! Mmmmmmm yummy

Ramen on a cold night? There is seriously nothing better.  Unfortunately - there seems to be something lacking in this ramen.  The appetizers were delicious but the ramen itself needs work.  I brought a couple friends here because I had read reviews - the appetizers were inventive, fresh and delicious but the ramen itself was nothing to write home about.

Pretty good ramen in a very comfy atmosphere. Tried the one in the food court in midtown west and really didn't like it. They food and ambiance was WAY superior here. Went at lunch and not crowded t all. Good service and prices.

I think it is worth trying this place out, but Minca is much better and not far from here. Also several dollars cheaper. I got the spicy ramen and my boyfriend got the tokyo something ramen. Both were very salty and the portions were not as large as other ramen places. Prices are $15-16 per bowl. Maybe I'll give it another shot, but not anytime soon.

Had dinner here with a friend on a Friday night at 6pm. The place wasn't packed but we had reservations and after being seated the people started pouring in. The place is a bit small and we got seated by the front door, so I couldn't see how big the rest of the restaurant is. 

The service was good and our water was refilled plenty of times. The food also came out within 15 minutes. Anyways let's get to the ramen.

For the appetizer we got the roast pork musubi ($7) which was okay but it only came in 2 and it was really small. I wished it was a little bigger or came with more. The flavor was pretty good(I don't like being teased haha) 

I ordered the triple pork ($16) which was good. It came with 1 piece of char siu, some bacon, veggies, ramen, and some broth. This bowl was very flavorful but not filling at all. The broth was more of a sauce than soup, so if you're looking for something soupy either ask them for more broth or get something else.

My friend got the red chili ramen ($15) with added inoki mushrooms ($2 extra). This dish was pretty spicy for her and she likes spicy foods. I didn't enjoy the dish because I'm not a spicy type of guy lol. I think she sorta enjoyed it but I can't really give a review on it since I had a little bite and I don't like spicy food that I can't handle. 

The reason why I give this place 3 stars is that for the amount of money we paid for the dishes we should've gotten a little more. We ended up going to grab more food from another restaurant. For those that like ramen this place is still a good place to try out, if not you can go grab some pancakes a few steps away haha 

Enjoy!

It's ok, not really worth the price. thought it will have been at least authentic ramen place. I thought Ivan will have bring a bit of Japan in his restaurant but I only find a poor Japanese cooking adapted for American palates. Sad

Delivery Review.

Ordered lunch through trycaviar.com since I was not in the normal delivery zone and Caviar had a coupon code.  Normally Ivan Ramen would not deliver to Midtown but Trycaviar handles the delivery for further distances.

The menu items are limited though and the items most yelpers are talking about was not on the menu for options.

I decided to go with the Tokyo Shio Ramen.  I wasn't sure what Fully Loaded meant, but it means, double the stuffing.

The Ramen noodle itself did taste great and the pork was pretty decent.  The eggs were cooked to perfection but I wish they were seasoned a bit more.  The broth however was a bit bland and incredibly salty.  Like I'm 2 glasses of water after my meal and my mouth is still puckering.  It is not to the level of where a Totto Ramen or Ippudo is.

For $16 + $5 (fully Loaded), this was way overpriced.  I would try it again but only in their location to try this Triple Pork everyone is talking about on Yelp, but otherwise...save your fancy ramen for another spot.

This ramen house was DOPE.  Nicest restaurant staff from host to bar to waiter to kitchen.  Went on a Monday around 7:30pm, no wait.  Smiles, greetings, and departing thank yous from team.  Thank you for a great experience.  Went with the Tokyo Shoyu, and sho should you!  Won't be disappointed.

I've heard so many rave reviews of Ivan Ramen that I knew it would be the one ramen place I'd check out in New York. 

Don't come here expecting a tonkotsu based ramen broth.  Here, I tried the Spicy Red Chili Ramen.  I was definitely not used to this flavor profile of a chicken-based broth.  It tasted a little bitter and I wasn't a fan of the smashed egg. The rye noodles was also something I'm not used too.  So wasn't a huge fan of Ivan's ramen.  Maybe my palate wasn't sophisticated enough to enjoy all of the nuances and subtle touches?

I prefer the ramen at Ippudo's better, since it's more of what I'm used to.  I also think Momofuko's ramen tastes better too.  But in general, I think West Coast ramen tastes better.  

Also tried the Tofu Coney Island  which was interesting but a little strange.  A vegetarian version of a chili dog, but with the mushroom chili served on top of squares of fried tofu.  Pretty good the first few bites, but then the novelty quickly wore off.

Overall, Ivan Ramen was a delightful dining experience and I can definitely say that we will absolutely be back for more.

I made a last minute reservation on a Thursday night for 6:45, my husband and I were running late and didn't arrive until almost 7:15. They held our table and sat us immediately upon arrival, big points there! People seemed to be trickling in as we dined and were willing to wait for a table, which I think says a lot about the establishment.

We started will the pork meatballs, which were some kind of panko, saucy magic. Delish! I had the  Tokyo Shoyu Rmane and my husband had the Spicy Red Chili Ramen. Both dishes were outstanding. Be warned: the spicy red chili is VERY spicy.

Our waitress was very nice (not overly nice) and attentive, despite the fact that she was clearly slammed.

If it's good enough for the @foodbabyny, it's good enough for me!

A+ Ivan Ramen!

The reviews I read were a huge mix of great! and nottttt great! but we went last night and I actually really enjoyed the experience. We shared the following:

- Roast Pork Musubi: this was ok, nothing special in my mind 
- 1000 Year Old Deviled Egg: didn't taste like what i know thousand year old egg to be, just tasted like a delicious deviled egg!
- Spicy Red Chili Ramen: my boyfriend LOVED this. i thought it was good, a little too spicy, but good. BUT HE LOVED IT.
- Ankimo Dirty Rice: I really enjoyed this, it wasn't THE BEST DISH EVER but I loved the crispy rice texture and thought the flavor was really good. I dont' love monkfish liver but it didn't really overpower the flavor and didn't bother me (but I'm not that picky to begin with)

MY FAVORITE hot toddy, and i've tried a lotttt. :)  really interesting and super tasty. i wish the barley tea flavor came out more but it doesn't, but still really good!

"Hottotodi" Sake Hot Toddy
warm Yamahai Junmai and barley tea, anise, cinnamon and cloves

I came here with an open mind after reading some of the reviews. My fiancé and I walked past this place a couple of times and always wanted to try it. I ordered the spicy ramen and my fiancé ordered the shio ramen. It was $15 each. The texture of the noodles was actually good but the soup was really salty. After a few bites, I couldn't even sip on the broth with the noodles. It was that salty! The portion was so small, I didn't even bother complaining or sending it back. After 2 bites, 2/3 of the bowl was gone. It was more like an appetizer than an entree. Maybe if I added the "fully loaded" for $5 and $3 for extra noodles, it would be more fully. I know rent is high in NYC but I can't justify myself paying $25 for a bowl of ramen. The $15 bowl of ramen came with a small portion of noodles, salty broth, a cold smashed egg and some scallions. The chasu that was described on the menu was just some shredded pork. I never felt so strongly about not coming back to a restaurant. This is just way too overpriced. They can at least throw some bamboo shoots or fish cakes in the ramen! I'm actually sitting here at the restaurant as I am writing this while my fiancé is yelping for another spot to eat because we are both still hungry!

I live near Ivan Ramen and after walking by it several times, I finally decided to try it out. It would have been perfect to have a good ramen shop near home, but this won't be my spot. Unfortunately, there isn't much good to say about it.

The atmosphere is pleasant enough and it looked like there was an outdoor area in the back that would be cool to sit in when the weather's nice. It's a basic restaurant with a lot of small tables and a bar. That's where we sat, which was cool because we could watch the cooks make some poor ramen. The service was friendly enough, attentive and careful, but there seemed to be a ton of staff standing around and doing nothing. This only bothers me in retrospect, because I didn't like my experience.

Anyway, I had the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen. The food comes fast, probably because they don't put much in it. Right away I was surprised to see how small the portion was and how little came in it. I know ramen is always salty, but the broth was far more salty than any ramen I've ever had. It was hard for me drink the broth, once I was done with the other ingredients. To add to the misery of it all, it cost $16. Not cool. The worst part of the whole experience was actually an hour later when the ramen started begging me to get out of my stomach. Sorry about that.

There are other great ramen places (Minca, especially) nearby, that are worth the money and wait. I won't be coming back to Ivan Ramen and you should heed my warnings.

My husband and I were beyond excited to try Ivan Ramen and were quoted a 60 minute wait on a Sunday night. After 75 minutes of waiting at the bar down the street we checked in and were told the maitre'd was misquoting wait times and it would be another 30 minutes. While we were less than pleased we had already invested so much time we decided to continue to wait it out. While hanging out by the host stand we realized that a lot of other people were in the same situation. We were also privy the one maitre'd belittling the other maitre'd every time someone asked about their remaining wait time since he was the one misquoting times in the first place. Though we were hungry and frustrated we felt terrible for the maitre'd that made the mistake as no one should have to endure that kind of treatment at their place of employment or anywhere else. 5 minutes before we sat down the wait staff  was handing out what were positioned as free beers until we noticed that we were charged for them when we received our check at the end of the meal! The worst part of whole story is that the food was completely mediocre at best which is less than ideal after waiting over two plus hours. My advice is to go to one of the other ramen shops in the city because even though you will likely wait a long time at least you can be confident your meal will be delicious!
No need for a lengthy review. It's good but with all the hype, expected it to be special.

My boyfriend wanted to try Ivan several times in the last 6 months & I have been reluctant...but we finally made it there this past weekend.  And I have to say I will not be a returning customer unfortunately.  

Overall, atmosphere was okay, a cold place (not very cozy) tables are really close to each other & tight, even for me -- a rather petite person.  Food came relatively fast, but it was quite disappointing how extremely SMALL the portions are & there is not much in the bowl, for the price point!   Not to mention, I usually love to drink the soup when I am having noodles, but it was extremely salty -- too salty for my taste.   A good bowl of ramen is in the soup!   So I was utterly disappointed.  

The pork musubi was also nah, not good.  Overall, for two people, we spent about $70 for lunch & came out quite disappointed.   

Finally, I have to say it didn't sit well for me at all, had a stomach ache within the hour.   Probably its bc the way they handle the bowl -- not hygienic! (the servers wipe the bowl w little pieces of paper-- basically they have their fingers all in your bowl of noodles, before it is served to you!).  

Definitely won't be coming back.   There are so many great ramen places in NYC.  Rai Rai Ken ramen has been around for more than 15 yrs and they are still so good, for less $$.  Chuko in Brooklyn is also fantastic!
A great deal of hype about innovative, but mediocre Ramen.  Friendly service and an interesting long dining room.

Surprised to find so many meh reviews on here. First off sure it's not Ippudo. Ippudo is the gold standard in NYC. If you want Ippudo tho....go to Ippudo. And wait forever for a table (sure I agree it can be worth the wait if you can manage to wrangle all your friends into actually showing up on time together). If you want to be able to make a ressie, like we did for a group of 6, for some pretty good ramen...come here. It's a small cozy spot. We sat out in the back, but there were heaters and we were plenty warm. We sampled a decent variety of the ramen since we were a group and all of us were quite satisfied with the food including the deviled eggs. I was actually a fan of the fact that the bowls were smaller than at Ippudo because I can never make it through but half of it there and then I am normally going out from the restaurant so half just goes to waste. Waiter was really helpful, nice, not overly attentive, and didn't rush us out. If I lived in the hood I would frequent this spot.

One of the best ramen places in the city (better than Ippudo in my opinion).  The spicy version is excellent.  I would recommend getting extra meat on the side.  Their warm sake hot toddy was actually delicious--worth trying.  

FYI, the restaurant has more of a no-frills ambiance, not exactly cozy or romantic.  There's a cool wall with colorful newspapering but the lights are extremely bright.  There's bar seating also.

Awesome, awesome, awesome!  My boyfriend and I stopped in here before a concert nearby and were so surprised by and happy with the experience.  The waitress was great.  She honestly veered us away from the sweeter cocktails and set us up with some delicious sake - something we were a little hesitant to try, but were so happy that we did.  For the meal, we went with the picked daikon, the 1000 year old deviled egg, the pork meatballs (recently named the best meatballs in NYC by NY Magazine), the ankimo dirty rice, and the triple pork triple garlic maze man.  The meatballs were, by far, the major highlight of the meal.  But everything was incredibly yummy.  The egg and dirty rice are VERY fishy - I loved that, but some people might not be into that, so stay away if that's you.  We can't wait to get back to this place to try different noodles.  My full review with all the details and pictures is up at my website, if you check my profile!  Definitely take some time to check this spot out!
Solid ramen spot with some very unique touches. I won't call this place trendy but it's an known entity.

Just because Ivan lived in Japan and has eaten a lot of ramen and has cooked for a long time doesn't qualify him to open a ramen shop. He openly admits that he didn't want to commit to a 2-year apprenticeship. If that isn't good ole American Hubris, I don't know what is. And it shows. If you want a delicious, authentic bowl of Ramen like Ippudo or Totto, keep walking. The soup to noodle portion is deplorable and it's just too salty. Not flavorful, just salty. I could go on, but suffice it to say, I won't return here to eat ramen.

TL;DR (Too Long; Didn't Read):
Chicken Patain Ramen: A- (A winner if it was less salty. Could've been by chance.)
Vegetarian Shoyu Ramen: A- (As a true omnivore and lover of meat, this dish was pretty good. Maybe a real vegetarian would give a more appropriate review, but this dish satisfied me.)
Service: A+
Price: B+ to A-

Positive(s):
+ Noodles that can take care of themselves in flavorful broth.
+ Perfectly cooked eggs!
+ Service is great!
+ Big, bold flavors.

Negative(s):
- A little expensive. Not too out of bounds compared to other ramen places, but things can add up.
- Slight saltiness, but I could've gotten the broth at the bottom of the pot. Not a deal-breaker though.

If I could sum up my experience at Ivan Ramen into one word, it would be "surprised." The first time, I chose a dish that would have normally been my last choice (due to reasons that I won't delve into for your own sanity), and the following time, I chose a dish that I was incredibly interested in trying due to its uniqueness. Surprisingly enough, I was satisfied during these visits despite my untraditional choices.

I want to start off by saying that the service is great. Maybe I've just been lucky, but every waiter/waitress and bartender I've been matched with was kind, attentive, and friendly. Sometimes, a simple conversation goes a long way. I'm not looking to talk for hours, and sometimes I'm not even looking to talk for seconds (small talk can be so draining). But for some reason, I really got the sense that they wanted me to enjoy my dining experience. Shocker, I know... an employee wanting you to have a good experience. But at this place, I feel like it was genuine. Prompt, friendly, service.

The first time I went to Ivan Ramen, I picked the Vegetarian Shoyu Ramen. Like I said, this would have normally been my last choice. I am a meat eater! Meat completely provides us with the amino acids we alone cannot synthesize and need to survive! I mean, you shouldn't go too crazy with it (due to health, financial, and environmental concerns), but it tastes so darn good. So you can only imagine that I was setting myself up for disappointment. Call me crazy, but I really did enjoy it. Not having meat didn't bother me too much. The enoki mushrooms and the rye noodles added a great texture. The tomato added a fresh tartness to the dish. This ramen had that umami, satisfying flavor I did not expect. Delightfully surprised is the best kind of surprise.

The next ramen I tried was the Chicken Paitan Ramen. This one is definitely unique in that it is unlike any ramen I have ever tasted before. Perhaps it's in the chicken paitan broth, or maybe it's the schmaltz, but this ramen is rich, hearty, and dare I say, comforting. The broth coats the inside of your mouth with schmaltzy, umami goodness. The confit chicken is tender, and the schmaltz fried onions add a savoriness that really makes this dish unique. The sturdy, rye noodles hold up well to the powerful flavors in this dish. Take this comment with a grain of salt, but it's like the chicken noodle soup of ramen. Unless you have some secret recipe handed down to you from generations past, this chicken noodle soup is superior and good for soul. I definitely recommend having something to cleanse your pallet as you eat this so you don't get overwhelmed with the flavors. My only critique would be that it was a tad bit salty, but I could have gotten the broth at the bottom. Oh well! Unique surprise!

Surprises everywhere, and I'll probably come back to be even more surprised (hopefully for the better).

Tip: GET THAT EGG! They truly do eggs right here; soft, smooth, creamy, runny yolk. It doesn't get much sexier than that. Also, make reservations or come early to make sure you get a spot. The place is mediocre in size for a ramen joint, but it fills up quickly.
Great food and service here, my favorite dish was the dirty rice (monkfish liver fried rice). The hostess on Sunday was really friendly and helpful.

A bit pricey but worth it, in my opinion. And I love that it takes reservations (if I'm only spending 40 hours in NYC, I want to use my time efficiently... meaning eating and drinking at as many places as possible)! The three of us all chose the triple garlic triple pork ramen ($16), which was SO good. It comes with just a little bit of rather thick broth, but the pile of green garlic, crumbled bacon and gloriously fatty, melty pork is what gives the noodles so much flavor. I didn't find it too salty at all, which can be a problem with some ramen, and I devoured the whole thing super quickly. My only regret is not adding an egg, because I love a soft egg, but it was plenty delicious without it. We also got the thousand-year deviled egg, which is just a regular egg white with an egg yolk mixture that tastes just like the thousand-year egg + cold tofu + soy sauce + bonito flakes dish that my mom often makes. It's amazing how you can get all that in one bite! I'd love to go back and try some of the other (perhaps soupier) noodle dishes.

TLDR:
Food: 10/10 if you get the TRIPLE PORK TRIPLE GARLIC. Seriously, this is the bomb. I wish I ordered it. 7/10 overall. Seriously, get the TRIPLE POKR TRIPLE GARLIC RAMEN!!!
Service: 11/10 (Our waitress kept taking my friend's napkin. Three times. It was hilarious.)
Ambiance: 10/10

With such high scores, why 3 out of 5 stars? The price.


I entered Ivan Ramen slightly annoyed: my goldfish friend was wearing the same coat as me. The coat which I saw and bought first in Hong Kong. But no. He had to be like this penguin and get it too. (http://i.imgur.com/25K5321.gifv watch it, seriously. It's hilarious. Not safe for the office. You'll end up giggle at your cubicle like an idiot.)

We were seated, ordered beer and sake. I like their coasters, they look nice. Then the drinks came, and my 12 year-old looking friend dropped his napkin. Our waitress picked it up and threw it away (1). She never came back with another one. We proceeded to order. For appetizers, we got the Lancaster okonomiyaki and ebi salad. For ramen, he got the Triple Pork, Triple Garlic, something something, while I got the RED HOT SPICY ramen, and our other companion got the Dan-Dan noodles. 

The appetizers came, and my child-like friend asked for another napkin. Lancaster okonomiyaki came on a thin waffle with okonomiyaki sauce and my eternal enemy, BEAN SPROTS!!! Why do I hate bean sprouts? Because they once attempted to murder me, but their sinister plan failed. I thought the flavors were rather peculiar, not quite to my taste. The ebi salad came with lots of greens, pieces of the shrimp heads as well. I usually don't eat shrimp heads. I didn't know why. I remembered why after I threw one into my mouth. I liked the dish overall--it's solid, if unspectacular. Then the waitress took his napkin again (2).

Now onto the main stuff: the napkin. The main dishes came, and he got another napkin. First, my ramen: the RED HOT SPICY RAMEN. Yep, he wasn't kidding about the red hot part. It literally looked like a bowl of red chili oil with noodles and stuff in it. It was spicy enough to make me sweat--and I usually get my dishes medium spicy at Chao Thai and Sriprapphai. I was expecting a spicy miso level of spicy, not this level. Next, the dan-dan noodles. They were flavorful and compared to my RED HOT SPICY BOWL OF INFERNAL SAUCE, had a little bit of a kick to it. Pretty damn good, 8/10. Then, there was the shio ramen. I thought the broth was light, then I remembered that it was a shio ramen. Again, solid if unspectacular. BUT YOU NEVER MENTIONED SHIO IN YOUR INTRO!!! you say! I'll get to that, I promise!

Finally. The bowl of ramen that is so good, it deserves it's own paragraph. The TRIPLE PORK TRIPLE GARLIC RAMEN. It was magical. I took a bite of it, and it felt as though I was Mario getting a mushroom in the Super Mario games. It made me feel alive. The noodles had a strong mushroom flavor to them, and I liked it a lot. My stingy friend only gave me one bite though, so that's all I can write about this amazing dish. 

So the dan-dan noodles turned out to be a bit too spicy for my companion, and the chef was more than happy to swap it out for another ramen dish. And that's where the shio ramen came in! As my penguin friend went to use the restroom, the waitress came by and cleared the table. And took his napkin (3). He came back wanted to dry his hands, but there was no napkin to be found. That's what you get for wearing the same coat as me buddy.

Would I come back to Ivan Ramen? Sure, I'd like to have that TRIPLE PORK TRIPLE GARLIC RAMEN again. Would I go out of my way to come here? Nah, probably not. This is a nice date spot, but it's not what I'm looking for in a ramen place. This palce is comparable to other high-end ramen places such as Ippudo, Momofuku, and Mu Ramen. 

I'm still looking for a ramen place that can match my best ramen experience: drunkenly asking a cabbie in Okinawa to take me to the best ramen place on the island at 10 pm. A 15 minute drive later, I arrived at someone's house, and the cabbie told me to go inside. My feelings of confusion were replaced with amazement when I found out that an old couple were running a ramen shop out of their kitchen. The  counter along the kitchen seated 10 at most, and everything was written in Kanji. Good thing a pachinko parlor attendent came in and I just pointed at what he had and ordered extra char shiu. Took me 30 minutes to get to a main street which had cabs to get back to base as well.

NOT enjoying my Salt Bloat today thanks to my bowl of Tokyo Shoyu Ramen I had last night.  

SOOOOOOOOOOO SALTY!!!!!!
LAY OFF THE SALT!!!! 

This is the 3 and last time I'm coming here. Gave it 3 chances and the broth is just as salty as it was when the place opened.  

Too bad. :(
Wow, such an interesting food ! Waffles made from chicken liver and pork ?? Sooo cool! And beef tongue ! Gourmet food in a casual setting. A bit loud but obviously its crowded cause foo

I went here last week with a friend who was visiting the city. I can't believe it's taken me so long to actually come here as I live nearby. 
The triple pork triple garlic mazeman was AMAZING! I actually dreamt about it later that night and have been dying to go back and have it again!!
The visitor had the vegetarian ramen and absolutely loved it too. She especially loved the enochi mushrooms in it.
The staff were super friendly and the decor was really nice. I hope I get a seat outside next time now that the weather is FINALLY better. 
Will definitely be back very soon!
Ivan ramen was my first ever experience with ramen. Nine months later, It is the only place I will go. I'm simply not interested in trying anyone else's bowl o'ramen!

I'm incredibly tired and at work right now, and what better way to reflect my mood than write a review about something equally depressing?

I can't tell if I'm more angry or sad. Or equally both. Hell, let's throw in some other emotions while we're at it. Disdain, melancholy, hopelessness, erectile dysfuntion. Every. Single. Bite. I didn't expect much and I'm still disappointed. The first thing you'll notice are the portions. It's tiny. The mushrooms are a nice decoration piece, but you don't fool me Ivan. The Shoyu broth might as well be soy sauce and the Shio is less broth and more Sea Salt. I mean, if that's your thing... ;D. It didn't provide the sense of comfort I sought in a bowl of ramen.

The noodles were light and bouncy but it seems pointless without the whole package. Even less pointless at $13 a bowl. Actually, I think it was more but I try not to think about this place.

I've never been a fan of ramen. Wait, let me rephrase... I've never been a fan of the IDEA of ramen. So when my friend told me we had a reservation at Ivan Ramen, I was skeptical. The place is small, but neat and cute. We were quickly seated out back (which is pretty cool, and has heatlamps if you need them) and decided on some sake with the help of our server, who by the way was awesome. She ran us through the menu quickly but thoroughly, answering all of our *many* questions. We chose the pork meatballs (6 per order) and the roast pork musubi (2 per order). Get both of these things! Next time I go back, I will be ordering these as my entree. So good! We had three different kinds of ramen (veggie, which apparently has the best broth on the menu and most people get the veggie ramen and just add meat, the triple pork/triple garlic mazeman aaaannnnddd I can't remember the third ramen, one of the tokyo ones I think) and I got the garlic steak. I tried two of the ramens, and they were ok, but again... I just can't figure out what all the fuss is about. My steak was delicious, though it comes on crispy toast, which I could have done without. I mean, I did do without it, I didn't eat it. The steak was wonderful though, so I am glad that I ordered that. I wish I had thought to see what sake we ordered, because it was pretty amazing. All in all... thumbs up for this place!
Amazing depth in flavor. Got the spicy ramen and it was good to the last drop. Great drink menu as well.

This place was solid, but I wasn't blown away. I guess I was expecting more since it is so heavily acclaimed by culinary experts. I will say that the atmosphere is cool. I loved the comic book-esque decor  and the servers and host were all warm and welcoming.

Ate at Ivan Ramen last night for my birthday. I have been wanting to dine here for a long time and it was everything I had hoped for. It was a wonderful dining experience. Ivan Raman isn't like your typical ramen and it isn't supposed to be. Ivan is a CIA trained chef and these dishes are his take on Raman, they are fun, interesting and unlike anything you will find at a "typical" ramen joint. 

We had the pork meatballs (amazeballs!) Triple garlic/triple pork - truly an indulgent dish with warm buttery flavors and textures! For the finale...the spicy Red Chile ramen. Seriously this stuff is spicy but in a good way. The tang of the broth comes through and the rye in the noodles but it made me schvitz a bit!
The staff was so incredibly friendly and being the foodie I am (and Ivan fan) took the time to talk shop with me. Special thank you to Nicole, who was a doll!

I am a self-professed ramen fiend who will do my damn hardest to finish each bowl of ramen to the last drop, but the salt and general film of oil all over my shoyu ramen stumped me. I ate a few bites and had to give up. Don't get me wrong: the slice of pork and the slightly runny egg were heavenly. The noodles had good mouth chew and I liked the heavy-handed sprinkle of green scallion on top. 

Everything else was not great, especially for the teeny portion and the steep price. 

Also, not a fan of sticking us right next to the door on an unseasonably chilly night. Yeah shame on us for giving up and not waiting the extra 30 minutes for a table on the inside but I was hungry. 

And dammit they didn't have the four cheese mazemen when I went. First mission cantina with no burritos, now Ivan with no cheesy ramen. I actually really loved the noodles they used for the triple pork/triple garlic mazemen, but it got too heavy. 

Tables are packed tightly together such that it was impossible to exit gracefully in a puffy winter coat. I knocked over someone's spoon. Yikes.

How is this place in business? I lived in Tokyo for a year, west coast for 3 years and have had amazing ramen in so many places and this is just something else. I get it "American style ramen", which to me would mean ramen with a cheeseburger and fries in it, which would've probably been better than what i ate there. There are so so so many ramen places in NYC that do great simple ramen for a much cheaper price. Please dont be fooled by the hype. Went down the block afterwards and had Korean fried chicken wings at Seoul Chicken, that was the best part of my night.

I heard so much about the scrapple waffle okonomiyaki but it turned out to be just okay... The dish is slightly too sour for my taste. I think it is sour because of the okonomiyaki sauce and the bean spouts (slightly fermented?) That tops the scrapple waffle.

Ramen is good...in theory. I honestly would have rather made packaged noodles at home that we all know takes 3 minutes to boil with chicken flavor we add at the end. This diner looking place is cool, for $14 drinks, and nothing else. The gentleman at the bar romances the items in the menu eloquently, which hooked me. In the end, I was disappointed. I had more pork fat in my bland broth than I did preferred pork. I can't call the noodles ramen noodles. The deviled eggs I could have made so much better, they were merely powdered with condiments in hopes to overlook the fact that they literally just taste like a hard boiled egg. Their version of a pork bun, is basically pulled pork over rice smothered in some sort of poorly prepared sauce. I asked for something spicy to add to my ramen, and the eloquent man spooges what looks like chipotle sauce from at quarter gallon squeeze bottle, like I'm at SUBWAY(eat fresh). I can tell you I would never bring someone that has never experienced this place, here.

I read some of the amazing reviews and I was so looking forward to trying this restaurant on this trip to NY. Sadly, I was so disappointed that it drove me to write a review, which is not common for me.

The restaurant is small, but super cute. The staff are amazingly nice and knowledgeable. They're very trendy but not intimidating. The one star is definitely for service. 

I had the triple pork garlic mazemen. It was so salty that it masked everything else in the bowl, including the bacon! The roasted garlic smelled amazing, but its flavor was also over powered by the salt. 

We had the daikon and xo sauce appetizer. The acid of the dish literally made my eyes water. It was a lot better when I used it to counter the saltiness of the ramen bowl.

My sister had the shio ramen. It was such a sad looking bowl of ramen. The noodles were too soft and the broth was too salty. Did I mention that I typically like salty foods?

If you want great service and trendy spots, this is your place. If you want a good bowl of ramen, do not come here. I really wanted to like this place. I'm so sad that I didn't.

What a cute little spot!  Nice patio out back, friendly staff, and a great menu.  Ordered the pickles and the meatballs to start, then moved onto ramen.  I had the chicken paitan ramen.  Amazing food.  Not super expensive and interesting ramen options. Weather was perfect for outdoor seating.   Definitely will return.
Decent ramen, fish liver fried rice was far more impressive. Only giving it three stars since other ramen places such as Miso-ya, Ippudo and Ramen-ya have much better ramen.

I heard this place was amazing.... It wasn't for me. 2 stars for good service and for 4 out of the 9 dishes we ordered. Starting with the Akiko's Pickles- completely over salted... Like a mouth full of salt. Being a big pickle fan.. Was highly disappointed, followed by the Pickled Daikon X0, this one is better, but still not satisfying. The Roast Pork Musubi - this was good. 1000 Year Old Deviled Egg - I didn't like it, texturally just not for me
. The beef tongue in dashi- good. The skirt steak over fried shrimp on toast - play on surf and turf was ok. The Lancaster okonomiyaki was not edible, waffle was burnt, dry  and bitter.. (They didn't charge us for it, which is why service got 2 stars for understanding). The Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen was the best thing I had tonight. Saving this dinner from being completely disappointing. I won't be back, sticking to ippudo/minca.

I was grateful that, after a series of drinks at Subject down the street on an empty stomach, I was able to walk in to sit down at the counter for a quick bowl of ramen before returning to my friends at the bar. To their credit, they are well trained and fast. I sat down at the counter, ordered, and was in and out within 10~ minutes. In this respect, it is a truly great ramen place. Consider the Ippudos of the world where you have to go through a bunch of hoops to get in, then once you're in it's like a fancy sitdown. This is extremely against my ramen worldview.

The problem was the ramen, overall. I ordered the chicken paitan ramen which features schmaltz in its soup, which did make it flavorful. The noodles were fresh, and quite different from your typical ramen noodles that you get in NYC -- a bit toothier and each noodle was more distinct. The inexcusable part was the dry ass chicken breast meat served with the ramen. Come on, you are serving schmaltz in your broth, why not thigh meat with chicken skin?

Overall, I left having enjoyed the service, but regretting that I did not order a different bowl of ramen. And at the price ($18-19 after tip), I was expecting any bowl to be a slam dunk for an easy to please, eats-anything ramen devourer like myself. But except for certain shining points of light, it was overall a disappointing experience. And it is hard to come back to try more things, knowing the price.

Bottom line is it's solid but in a city filled with ridiculously good ramen it doesn't stand out.

Came here for lunch on a Sunday, were able to sit down for a party of 4 immediately around noon, when we left around 1:20PM there was a small wait of 5-10 minutes.
