We also got the L.E.S. bun (lower east side) - composed of pastrami, karashi-mayo and daikon slaw. Once again a creative take on an asian dish that also yields a home run. This place had excellent service. The ramen will run you 12$.

If you are more visual check out the tour of the top 5 bowls of ramen in new york city here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rol4vkCIGnU

Have a great time and enjoy!

YUM!

Ivan Ramen.  So. Good.

Their ramen was so fresh and so delicious.  A small shop, experts in ramen, and a nice hideaway in the LES.  I've heard of Ivan Ramen for quite some time and was happy to have tried it. 

I will start off to say our server was SO nice.  Friendly, with a smile, and gave great recommendations.  The pastrami buns were so different.  Presumably thinking they would be heavy, they were actually quite light.  I ordered the Tokyo Shio Ramen, as described by our waitress, one of the more delicate tasting.  It was light, the ramen tasted homemade and it was easy to digest.  The pork was good, but the dish was really about the noodles.  

I enjoyed it!  It's not a super fancy ramen place but it has a nice, chill vibe.  It was delicious, especially on a cold, winter night.

Definitely worth a visit. Great ramen and fun drinks. Came here with a few friends after work one day and it was pretty easy to get a reservation on open table. You can't go wrong with any of the ramens. The four of us all got different dishes - Tokyo Shio Ramen, Tokyo Shoyu Ramen, Spicy Red Chili Ramen, and Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen. The last one if I remember correctly wasn't a traditional ramen with broth but it was still good. The cocktails are super good and they really put a lot of effort in the presentation of the drinks. Good spot for a cute date in the LES.

WARNING: GOT FOOD POISONING FROM IVAN RAMEN

I came to Ivan Ramen a few days ago, as i've passed by here several months ago and saw how packed it was. Per a few recommendations, we thought we would check it out. I ordered the spicy red chili ramen while my cousin got the triple pork ramen. 

The spicy red chili ramen was very oily, and the broth was overwhelming. It was not necessarily enjoyable. The pork cha siu (which was extra, usually is included in ramen like Totto) was a very fatty and disgusting piece of pork. Had the consistency of rubber. 

Overall, we were both very dissatisfied with our meals. My stomach felt very uneasy after having the ramen. 

The day after having Ivan Ramen, I could not eat breakfast - given how bloated and disgusting I get from the previous nights meal. Felt abdominal pain and symptoms of a fever. Thought it was strange.....lo and behold...have food poisoning as I write this. I know it was from the ramen because the only thing I ate that same day was some cereal. 

I will most definitely be filing a complaint with the city, and make sure none of my friends or colleagues ever come to Ivan Ramen. Absolutely horrific experience. The only positive thing I have to say about this place is the relatively fast service. Beware...

As an addition, the ramen here is not good not enjoyable. Definitely not worth the price. This ramen spot is basically catered toward a specific crowd. If you are looking for good ramen, stick to Ippudo or Totto. You will regret coming here.
I had the Triple pork triple garlic Mazeman. Simply delicious.. had the LES buns as a starter and it was so good. A cool hipster atmosphere. I would come here again.

I had such a great experience and Ivan that I needed to write about it!  The food was great, but what was more impressive than the food was the service.  Everyone who worked there was polite and friendly, the food was out quickly and our waitress gave us a great drink recommendation to go with our Ramen.

After a brisk & lengthy stroll due to a confusing subway situation, we arrived at Ivan Ramen on a slightly chilly & somewhat drizzly afternoon. The space is tiny and artsy-hipster but nevertheless welcoming (the universally friendly staff helps). Paige and I split the Kewpie Ebi, whole fried shrimp with a spicy Japanese mayo sauce over watercress, which was delicious-perhaps the most flavorful bite of food of this trip to NYC. The crunchy, shrimpy heads combined with the clean and peppery greens perfectly.
   My lovely wife ordered the Tokyo Shoyu ramen and dissolved into paroxysms of pleasure from both the richly meaty broth, the silken rye noodles and the buttery pieces of pork. My vegetarian ramen may sound like a consolation prize, but I was blown away by the depth of flavor and the toothsome noodles. I am spacing on which cocktail Paige ordered, but I know she enjoyed it, as I did my roasted barley iced-tea. 
    I think Ivan Ramen will be a regular stop on future visits to NYC-we loved it!

We ordered the shoyu ramen and spicy chili ramen. The portion was small like most ramen shops. Their broth is more salty, oily, dense and thick rather than subtle and savory. The spicy ramen was too overpowering. You could only taste the chili rather than the actual broth. The noodle consistency was Chewy and pork was tender. The prices all range $15-$20 and was overpriced. They should also have the option of having side sauces and condiments such as garlic, sesame, chili powder etc.

Came here for the cool back story (Ivan started his ramen shop in Tokyo), yet the whole experience was somewhat disappointing. It was busy on a Saturday night, service could get slow and a reservation is preferable especially with a bigger group. We got coney island tofu for appetizer. When I was going to order triple pork mazemen, the waitress asked if I'd had it and told me in a warning way that it's "not the traditional ramen and no soup there", I got intimidated and had vegetable ramen instead. I'd prefer other broth than shoyu (like miso or tonkotsu), but that seemed to be the only kind they served.

Coney island tofu was a letdown given its price... for $13, I guess I was expecting more than a few fried tofu cubes with chili and mustard that were just too salty for me. Later the vegetable ramen wasn't that impressive, I tried the triple pork mazemen and it was definitely more special and tasty. Despite the overpriced appetizer and shoyu only base, it was still fun trying out their non traditional / western ramen!

I came to Ivan with a girlfriend to have some cozy, hot ramen on a cold winter night. I made a reservation and we were seated instantly...at the bar. At first I was very confused since I saw tables available, but I didn't want to start moving around and being annoying, so bar seating it was. It actually ended up being a nice experience to sit there. You are overlooking the kitchen and the bartender is also your waiter so you get a little more intimate experience when it comes to being served. We shared an order of the roast pork musubi as our appetizer and it was good. It tasted like barbecue pork sushi.  My suggestion is to order a few appetizers, since this one was one bite and poof, it's gone! We didn't do that, sadly. Anyway, both of us ordered the same ramen dish, the spicy red chili ramen, and it was very good as well.

The prices are good and the ambience is certainly nice and trendy, but they don't have dessert! Sadness! Would've been nice to have a sweet treat after a spicy meal.

Price is high for the portion and taste of food. I got the shio (salt base) ramen which has the rye noodles. The broth was ok but the chasyu (pork belly) was 80% fat. My husband had the shoyu (soy sauce base) ramen and his tasted a little sweeter to me and it's brown clear liquid (cuz of he soy sauce.) shio was lighter color clear liquid. His pork belly was also too fatty. We came here as a back up to a back up cuz mr. Taka was closed and then Mimi and coco was closed too. Now Maybe I'll checkout the prosperity dumpling down the street. I think they moved since the city shut them down in the other rat infested location.

The L.E.S. bun was awesome! I had the spicy red chili ramen, which I really enjoyed. I would say on a spice level 6 out of 10. The people I was dining with all opted for chicken dan dan and no one left anything in the bowls. Also, the server was excellent. He knew the menu, answered all our questions, and never rushed us.

They forgot to bring out my Kadame(extra noodles) and weren't very attentive. Had a hard time getting the waitress's attention.

 A larger party was sat before us even though we were waiting for 30 minutes already and they didn't have a reservation. 

The ramen was alright but nothing out of the ordinary.

Would not recommend!

We started a foodie group in our office to try out different cuisines at least once a month. We came across this place and gave it a try. The staff was friendly, attentive and our server took her time to explain the menu to us thoroughly. We started with some appetizers such as Tofu, Oysters and Daikon. I have to say out of the three the Oysters to me were the yummiest followed by the Daikon. I had the Chicken Dan Dan which to be honest I was expecting it to be a lot more spicier but it was good I finish the entire bowl. My coworkers had the Spicy Red Ramen now that had some serious HEAT to it. So if you're looking for something with  more broth and heat in it i would stick to the Spicy Red Ramen.

What I had: Pastrami Pork Bun, Spicy Red Chili Ramen 

Would I go back?: Yes very good Ramen joint 

Story: Had just gotten back to the city from the Holidays and me and my friend were looking for somewhere on our lists to head to dinner. My friend suggested this place. Came here on a friday night after work - place was crowded as expected but they were realistic enough to us about the wait. When we were seated the staff was pleasant and concise about their recommendations - we ordered and the food came out pretty promptly. Pastrami in our pork buns came over from Katz's - DELICIOUS on all fronts- bun was nice and pillowy in texture and pastrami was perfectly cooked. As for the ramen - my thing about ramen is that the broth is just always too salty/heavy to actually ever stomach and finish the entire bowl - so this experience was not any different really in that regard. I had wanted something spicy and usually I go for the standard go to when I head to a Ramen place but I decided to switch it up. The spicy red chili was definitely spicy but just spicy enough for my palette. I loved the rye noodles it gave the noodle some sort of different heir about it. I ended up taking a good portion of the broth home and enjoying it in 2 more meals diluted down a bit and making my own makeshift ramen with it.

Great place to go on a date or with a couple friends. If you're going on a weekend or for dinner expect a wait without a reservation. 

Good ramen but I've honestly I'd better. I got the Tokyo Shio Ramen & found it a bit too salty for my liking. The portion of ramen they give you isn't as huge as other ramen places where you're so full you can't move (hello ramen coma!). You leave satisfied & not bloated which is nice.

I'll be back to try the other menu items - apps to be specific :)

came here yesterday for a date, didn't see the whole store but i loved it anyways. The food from the appetizer to the ramen,and drinks were all amazing. seriously man it was good. To me the best part was the server and the greeter. I think his name was John, had curly hair i believe but he knew the menu better than most places , he was funny nice and very informative. I would say it was pretty pricey but i'll come back without my date for that triple pork!!!

Tasty food and creative fusion, set in a very nice space. Service could be better. Price is a bit steep.

For app, id rec the latke. 
The mushroom casino royal was a creative way to prepare mushrooms like pasta, but mediocre on taste.
Also a pass on the fried oysters- not bad but totally not worth the $$.  The Chinese veggies were tasty, on the sweet side, but unusually ice cold.

The Dan Dan noodles were very tasty, as was the tsukemen. Others at our table enjoyed the spicy chili and the triple pork ramen.  

Everything took forever to come out. Apps were served one at a time and 5-10 min apart. Then a 30+ delay on the ramen.
We made reservation a week ahead for late lunch with friends on Saturday. Place was packed, service was great, broth salty ... In other words we weren't impressed. I doubt we'll go there again.

I'm not the biggest ramen fan, and ironically I have been finding fantastic NY ramen restaurants for wonderful food. My friends and I were seated outside, even though it's the winter the heaters made it warm enough. I started my meal with a tofu Coney Island based on other yelpers recommendations. Then I had the latke nomiyaki, a latke with Japanese toppings. It was an absolutely delicious fusion of New York, Jewish and Japanese food. Having some Japanese craft beer was a great treat. So come here whether or not you like ramen for a treat of a meal.

This place has a really nice outdoor space. You can slurp noodles in the heated enclosed backyard. The pork buns were good, but the chili ramen was a disappointment. The broth was too thick and pasty. The dish was okay at best, really nothing to scream about. The worse part was the weird tingly sensation in my mouth after I left the place. I never found out why, but suspected msg could have been the culprit.
The vegetarian ramen is too salty and the broth is too rich in soy sauce. Then, $4 for a roasted barley tea is definitely too much!

Got a seat at the bar on a weekday. The server was friendly and helpful. On the plus side, they're trying some new and innovative stuff with ramen. On the downside, it's simply not as good as the classic spots like Minca, Totto, and Ippudo. I got the pastrami steamed buns which were a unique twist on traditional Japanese pork buns, only with pastrami and aa mustard-based sauce, and the Spicy Red Chili Ramen with Enoki mushrooms on top. I was a little disappointed by some of the fillings of my ramen being cold. I want my ramen piping hot! All in all, we had a pleasant experience, but with so many other better options nearby, it's hard to justify coming here often.

This place is so ridiculously overpriced plus it was absolutely freezing sitting there for dinner. I would not recommend this restaurant to anybody unless you want to get ripped off. You can go to the store and buy $0.50 Ramen noodles and it will be the same.

He might have learned how to make authentic tasting ramen but he definitely did not learn how to run a restaurant from Tokyo. 

I ordered the Tokotsu Tsukemen but was served the Spicy Chilli Ramen - it looked good so I decided to keep it. It was tasty with the right amount of spicy but just a bit too salty. It comes with egg and pork unfortunately the egg is not a soft boiled egg. But I enjoyed it. 

My friend ordered the Vegetarian Ramen which seemed similar to the vegetarian ramen she's had in Tokyo. The broth was so salty it was as if they had simmered it too many times, for too long. 

When we both got home, we felt so sleepy that there's no doubt the reason why it tasted alright but was so salty is because of MSG. Trust me, I know my MSG. 

Btw, service sucks. The host was rude - looked at us like two asian women in a ramen restaurant is foreign. The staff is too casual for a place that needs a reservation. The kitchen staff was going back and forth with the servers about a ticket order. 

"Can I have what little enjoyment there is and eat my ramen in peace??"

Not to mention, the type of people who dine here. It felt like another world. One guy was karaoking to the music, 3 others ordered ramen without chasu and egg like, "whyyyy are you even here!!"

Overall: would I recommend this place to a friend? Yes, only to serve as a contrast to a good ramen spot.

Ivan Ramen has been on my list for must-try ramen spots for a long time, and I was roaming around the area and stumbled upon it and figured, well, today is the day I finally try this place. When you walk in, the front of the house took our coats and sat us down at the table. It is a spacious restaurant, and has a cool wall of collages spread across the front section of the restaurant. 

I went with the express lunch which included a beer, ramen and a side dish for $21, not bad. I ordered the spicy chili ramen, and my bf ordered the tsukemen. Food took around 10 minutes to arrive, and the servers were attentive when our water was going low and asking if we needed anything else. 

Only downside for when I was ordering is that I ordered the spicy ramen and told them I didn't want the pork which they said was fine, but when I asked if I can get the chicken from the other ramen as a topping instead, they said they cant do that because chicken isn't a side topping. I was bummed at that because the chicken was just essentially replacing the pork, but it was fine.

The food was very good, my ramen was spicy, full of flavor, and the noodle were perfect. My bf ordered the tsukemen and had to bring the broth back to the kitchen because to him the broth was not hot enough. He has ordered an extra side of noodles and said the broth will 100% be cold by the time he gets done with the first batch of noodles. But he said the dish overall was good. I got the pickled radish side dish and that was the perfect palette cleanser as I was eating my spicy ramen.

Overall it was a great experience, service was great and the food was delightful.

Pretentious, over rated, and poor service. I don't get why it's so highly reviewed. All of our ramen was ice cold and when I inquired about more broth or something to make it hot the servers only response was that it was a "dipping soup". Wtf. Don't waste your time on this place

My friend Meghan's review is way too nice so I'm here to write a separate one.

The whole experience has left me forever scarred. I don't even know when will be the next time for me to eat ramen again...and I'm 200% asian.

Okay, first let's just all agree that Ivan Orkin has learned a lot from his own experience in Asia in the 80s and 90s (via the use of msg). I don't doubt his ramen spot in Tokyo was "popular" because what isn't in Tokyo? Plus, a white dude coming to Tokyo to pursue his dream in ramen could easily get at least a half of the curious Tokyo population to try it once, with the right kind of PR. Japanese being the most respectful human beings on earth, probably never told him what he was doing wrong. 

The vegetarian ramen I ordered came tepid. With all the raw enoki mushrooms (for real? raw enoki mushrooms go in hot pot, not ramen)  hovering on top and I could barely see the broth. The broth itself was way too greasy and salty. I could taste a little bit of the hard work of trying to imitate authentic ramen broth behind it. But reheating it numerous times and forgetting to add more water into it to keep the taste of the broth consistent is just not the right attitude. What makes ramen ramen are those delicious freshly made chewy noodles. The rye noodles in my ramen were sloppy, soft and weak. I doubt they were made in house. But if they were, please ivan ramen just stop attempting to make your own noodles and buy them elsewhere. The only tasty thing in my bowl was the roasted tomato. Perfectly roasted. 

To make my ramen experience even worse was the horrible service. The host was staring at me and my friend from head to toe upon entering. Is it really that weird to see 2 asian girls in a ramen restaurant? Or if that's your way of warning us how bad the ramen is, I thank you very much.
Tried the latke, shio ramen, and shuyo ramen. Read about Ivan Ramen in a 2015 list put out by Thrillist. They cited Shio Ramen as one of the top foods to try in NYC.

Ivan Ramen epitomizes the phrase overpromise and underdeliver. When New Yorkers list the top must-visit ramen holes in Manhattan, Ivan Ramen tends to fall somewhere on that list albeit behind the undebatable top 2 or 3.  

On a busy but not overwhelming weekday dinner, we started off with Kyuri pickles and roast pork musubis - the former which had a deliciously sharp sour flavor while the latter seemed almost too simple to be served here. Our biggest mistake was ordering the shio and shoyu ramens. The flavors were both mediocre and predictable, not close to meeting lofted expectations. It felt as if these soups were too traditional for the restaurant to be bothered with mastering. Compounding the issue was that value is not high on the list of considerations here.

While it is Japanese cuisine, there's not much Japanese feel. Ivan Ramen has a nice seating area in the back while the front setting, save for the glowing ramen anime above the bar, looks much like a small diner in the American midwest sans booths. 

The service was inexplicable. Our waitress asked if this was our first time here to which I said yes and awaited some sort of rehearsed prologue to our meal that never came. When we asked what toppings came in each of the ramen dishes, she repeated herself several times and yet, the shio ramen was missing its egg (which had to be brought over in a separate dish - cold). They must not serve this classic very often. This would make sense since the more I try to solve this mystery, the more it seems like most people praise the unorthodox noodle bowls (mazemen, red chili ramen). Maybe it does shine with the experimental dishes but certainly fell flat with the classics. This understanding alone will drag me back to give it one more shot.

Very meh on this place. Nice atmosphere and friendly enough but the ramen just did not taste up to par. I've had pretty amazing ramen in LA and was surprised this joint stood out so little in comparison. 

Not sure if it was the broth but something was awry.
Went there last night with a date and it was awesome...the service went above and beyond to make sure I was informed and got exactly what I was looking for.  Try the Meatballs!!!

Great Ramen!!! With a slight slavic twist. Appetizers are seasonal. Which I Love! Atmosphere is very young and hip. Especially in garden patio area which is perfectly sealed and heated in winter. Great art. Passionate service. I LOVE finding a place i. The LES where servers are truly passionate and excited about the food and drink. 
And honestly, food is fantastic and Not expensive. A great spot for an old classic with a modern twist and you g energy!

It was just eh. 

Came on a Saturday afternoon, and it was pretty busy so we had to wait around 10 minutes for a table. I got the Tokyo Shio Ramen, which is sea salt infused, so it was pretty salty, and left me pretty thirsty after. 

The restaurant is really narrow but long, all the tables are kinda squished together. The waiter was attentive and service was pretty quick.
My boyfriend said, "I'm still hungry", and I replied, "I'm pleasantly not too full!" Clean and uniquely flavored, but not for those craving traditional Japanese fare.

My first Yelp review. Why? DIARRHEA. I went there for a bottomless brunch with some friends and we all ordered the Spicy Red Chili Ramen. It tastes good, its very spicy but I love spicy foods. While I was eating and slurping it all tasted delicious, but I could feel that it wasn't seating well in my stomach, something was off, but I couldn't get enough and I drank all the broth. If only I knew what I was getting myself into. As the hours passed I could feel my stomach acting up but I thought it was from the drinking I did throughout the day. Not really the case here. I woke up at 4 am to find myself best buds with the toilet. I hope my friends are okay since we all ordered the same

Delicious! Definitely among the top ramen I've had in NYC, in line with Ippudo. We sat at the bar and my husband had the spicy dish while I had the chilled noodle Tonkotsu Tsukemen. Wouldn't change a thing - enough saying that we will most definitely be back!

This is SOLELY based on the fact that: I asked the waiter if they had the cold noodles (which was advertised all over social media all day today and yesterday, which is specifically WHY I came here tonight) and he said, "oh noooo that's only in the summer." I looked at him confused but he seemed a bit out of it and kinda of slow maybe high or just ... Slow. I was super bummed and ordered the tskuemen instead but I was craving cold noodles all day and so looking forward to it. So after my friend and I decide to order the tsukemen he responds, "uuuuhhhh you know uuuummmm the broth doesn't come with that. I mean it's not, it's in like a different bowl." By then i really thought he was stoned. Which, I have no issue with and didn't even mind UNTIL I walked out of the restaurant after my meal and just then noticed the chalkboard that said "special cold noodle this week" so I went back inside and asked the hostess and she said they DID have it!!!!!!! I was sooooooooooooooooooo disappointed. When a girl is pmsing and craving something.... I mean you've all seen the memes on social media it AINT pretty. COME ON!! How did this waiter NOT know!!!??!!!!!!!!!!!!!!?????? 

Ok besides that... The latke nomiyake was burnt and cold, so cold the bonito flakes didn't dance. the tsukemen was actually really good. The ramen noodles were the perfect texture chewy yummy. The broth was also super flavorful and surprisingly not overly salted...but still NOT worth $17 (cocoron is just a couple blocks away, nothing on the menu is over $15 AND their waiters know their own menu. Oh yea the foods amazing too) I definitely would have enjoyed it MORE if I had not specifically come for the cold noodles. I just spent $30 on food I didn't even want. So sad.

My friends and I have been plotting to go to Ivan ramen for quite some time, and finally came here Tuesday night for some evening noodz. I was a little nervous given the recent slew of negative reviews, but we were able to navigate our way around the menu and had a pleasant time regardless.

I recommend sitting in the back garden area if you can; it's a bit more tucked away and calm. Our server was incredibly nice and helpful, and was spot on with her recommendations. To start, we got the Tofu Coney Island and the Pork Musubi. Both were different to your traditional Japanese starters, but were definitely very innovative and delicious in their flavor combinations. For noodles, we all got the spicy chili ramen and the tonkatsu tsukemen. The spicy chili ramen uses thai chili for the spice - it's not messing around. Our waitress described the spiciness level to be around a 7 or 8 out of 10. If you're moderate to well versed in spice, you should be fine. The tonkatsu came with broth on the side that you are meant to dip the noodles in - essentially soba style. Everything about the tonkatsu dish will fulfill all of your porky dreams. From the fried pork chunks to the extremely flavorful broth, you won't be disappointed by this one!

We decided to check out Ivan Ramen for late night snack after some all night drinking in a cold running day right before they closed. I was pretty happy with their service and ramen.
I ordered the spicy ramen and also had a little taste of the Shio ramen from my friend. Spicy ramen was alright, but I have to say the Shio ramen broth was pretty impressive. Even though it looked so much darker than a typical Shio ramen, I absolutely loved their rich smoky fishy taste of the broth, probably some katsuobushi overload there. The dashi also tasted pretty complex, much more than simple saltiness. The noodle was actually very interesting as well, not your typical ramen wheat noodle, but got its own unique texture and some weird but good chew on it. I felt like I was having some kind of soba and ramen hybrid noodle that ended up working quite well together. Anyway, it was a great experience overall.

Came here on a rainy day and was warmly welcomed by hostess. Sat at the bar and had Tokyo Ramen with extra bok choy.  Bar waitress was efficient but not as warm (direct and cool... She did her job but that's that) as the Spanish girl at the entrance. The only hot drink choices were hot sake or roasted buckwheat tea. Please add green tea to your list! My ramen had a nice beef broth base and two slabs of deelish roast pork at the bottom.  So with the extras, the soup was excellent. The buckwheat tea was new to me and seriously ... $4?!!! Give me a pot of tea. Happy to pay $15+$4 for my extras for soup. But tea should be $1-2 per cup, even downtown. It is only about $0.10 a cup for them to make. Even my Japanese friends thought that was ridiculous. So... I end up paying $23+tip for soup and tea. Hmm.

Craving ramen on a Friday night is probably one of the worst cravings one can have, especially in a city that has so many choices on great ramen. Finding most of our initial choices booked solid for the night, we thought we'd give this spot a shot and felt lucky when they had one reservation table open for 4.

I'll be completely honest, I had my doubts about this ramen shop. Run by a white chef who cut his teeth in ramen in Japan had me thinking this was more or less a ramen restaurant for those somewhat unfamiliar with authentic Japanese style ramen.

Everyone at the table ordered a different dish (so that we could all get a taste) and we also tried out two of their most popular appetizer dishes.

Though not completely disappointed, the ramen did feel more like a fusion take on ramen with their various Chinese infused tastes and dishes.

If you're looking for authentic Japanese style ramen, I'd suggest checking out some of the other ramen shops in the area (there're a lot) but if you're looking to taste something different with ramen, you might like this place.

I for one thought the dishes here were solid, but not what I'd ultimately call Japanese ramen.

Price: $12+ per person
Wait: 15 mins after ordering (I'd recommend making reservations)

Cool little place with a lot of personality. The flavors were good, but for the cost and portion size, I'd be reluctant to come back.

- Food: Flavorful, but small portions and not enough toppings on the noodles.
- Atmosphere: Trendy and lively; good for friends 
- Service: Really friendly waiters; appreciate that the hostesses held our reservation even though our party was late; couldn't be seated until the whole party had arrived, which was annoying, but pretty commonplace in NYC

Food:
- Tokyo Shio Ramen: Good broth; wheat noodles were unique and had a noticeable wheat flavor; toppings were sparse: only came with one thick slice of pork, one egg and scallions. The pork was good, but the thick slicing made it seem a little rough. Portion was small in general; had to order the Kaedama, which I've never had to do before.

- Chicken Dan Dan: Actually had it on its last night before being removed from the menu. Liked it because the process of eating it was a little unique: you had to mix an egg yolk into the chicken topping, and could flavor it with chili powder at will, before pouring it over noodles.
It was okay. The shoyu was not bad. The shio was pretty bland. Expensive for ramen. And with all these ramen shops opening up all over the city. Not a real stand out. The rye noodle is quite tasty.

I'm not a typical ramen consumer in that I usually strike out with it.  I pushed away Ippudo's fatty pools of ramen, and am not thrilled by the tonkotsu broth I've had, even didn't eat any in college.  But, like a Middle American rube, I was hoping to try Ivan Orkin's place for the best reason: I liked his attitude on Mind of a Chef.  

The secret Hare Krishna's (or "bhakti yoga devotees") of Stanton Street Yoga locked me out when I was late, so I was in a sour, defeated mood and planned to capitalize on it with some impulse eating.  
I wasn't surprised to see that Ivan Ramen is decorated haphazardly, aggressively hitting some Asian fusion "cool" points.  The kind that became popular after David Chang started putting cursewords in his cookbook: Japanese manga/street art-style murals above the kitchen, tattooed chefs.  But, other than the cute private patio, the place is white, starkly lit, and not totally inviting.  

The guy behind the counter was thankfully friendly and helpful.  He recommended the shio ramen and I ordered the cucumber pickles and pork musubi.  

Ivan Orkin's pickles do have an LES Jewish flavor.  They are sweet on the inside, but briny and taste of dill.  Perhaps more Polish than Russian, because our pickles are straight up sour.  They are a bit acidic and cloying after a few bites, making me annoyed by my unsubtle culture.    But I ate them because hey, "they are terrible... and such small portions!"

The pork musubi came, a small bite of soft pork with stewed tomato wrapped in seaweed.  The pork was a bit sweet and flavorful, but had a distinctly Russian Jewish flavor when combined with the stewed tomato, like something your grandma would leave cooking in a big pot when you got sick.  

I liked the Tokyo shio ramen best.  The broth was subtle and salty.  The wheat noodles were well made, thin and toothsome unlike the sloppy thick noodles I've had in the past.  I liked how the salt of the dish combined with the carefully runny eggs and scallions.  Yes, the pork was fatty but I don't mind.  It really remained in my mind, I think I would come back for it.

I commend chef Ivan for thinking outside the box and putting his own twist on ramen. But for me, the staples of ramen are the texture of the noodles (hagotae, or "tooth response" in Japanese) and the depth of the flavor of the broth. Both were just okay here. I'm all for creativity and straying from tradition, but the fundamentals need to be there. 

I got the mazemen noodles, which is dipped in broth instead of in soup. The mazemen noodles, which tend to be sturdier, were in my opinion better than the actual ramen noodles my friend got. But I found myself putting more scallions and spice mix into the dipping broth for more flavor. Overall, I thought it was overpriced for the quality and quantity  (almost everything was an add on, from veggies to the soft boiled eggs and seaweed).

I'll admit to being skeptical of the wheat noodles but they didn't take anything way from the ramen in my opinion. Our sever was fantastic, super knowledgeable about the menu, made our table a great sake recommendation, and was very friendly. 

I ordered the spicy red chili ramen and it was delicious, the shredded pork works well with the chicken broth. The dish comes out bright red but isn't overpoweringly spicy. As others have said, they go light on the toppings but the portions didn't strike me as any smaller than usual. 

They have outdoor seating, always a plus. And Sorachi Ace, a really interesting, complex tasting beer from Brooklyn Brewery that I fell in love with.

Tried the spicy red chili ramen and the dan dan noodles.

Portion sizes were a bit small in my opinion, but they do offer to refill your ramen for a small price. the Dan Dan noodles were a seasonal item so not sure if it is still offered. This version was a dry one and had a bit too much meat to my liking. I wish it was a bit spicier as well but overall it was good. I did enjoy the spicy red chili ramen but there weren't many pieces of meat and the egg was already completely shattered when I received it. Overall, I enjoyed the noodle dishes, but the presentation of the dishes were a bit disappointing. Definitely would rather go to ippudo/minca/ramen-ya for my ramen fix.

AMBIANCE: New, modern, clean, bright, with a bar in the back. Very great place to bring a casual date.

LOCATION: Down one of those streets of NYC. Street parking, but I'd recommend walking.

SERVICE: Friendly, quick, accommodating, knowledgable.

FOOD: I went for happy hour and their deal was too awesome to pass up. I got the Red Spicy Chili Ramen and Pickled Daikon. You can't beat that. The spicy ramen was actually spicy, I have tried too many a times broths that claim to be spicy, but you barely taste any heat. This was definitely there in the route amount. Also the pickled daikon was a great way to either start the meal or wash out the ramen at the end, which ever way you choose to eat it. Honestly, if I was craving spicy ramen, this is where I am going.

PRICING: $11-13/bowl, same price during happy hour, but comes with additional appetizer.

I'm afraid this ramen shop is overhyped as it gets all the attention because of it's white chef. Don't get me wrong, the ramen is ok, but there are much better options in NYC. The ambiance/interior of the place is rather cold too.

Such an awesome dinner here tonight! Got the wings and pork meatballs as an app and chicken shoyu ramen for dinner. Was the perfect amount of food for 2 ppl. The service here is so awesome and the host was so cool and very accommodating. Def will be back!

The Tokyo shoyu ramen here was meh... After a few bites, it started getting really satly and felt like it was drenched with oil and sodium. I would probably visit other ramen places before coming back here...

I'm a huge Ramen fan and have been hearing about this place so maybe my expectations were a little too high but I found it to be overrated and overpriced. The flavored were there but It wasn't to die for. Now that's I have tried it I don't feel the need to go again

This place is great. Great service, great food. Manager and staff were all super friendly. I sat at the bar and had a light dinner, which really hit the spot. I absolutely loved the retro diner-like ambiance with the open service window so you can see the action in the kitchen. I'm a huge fan of anything pickled so I had the pickled daikon starter and the kyuri pickles, both of which were perfectly seasoned and delicious. For my entree I had the Coney Island Tofu, which I thought was very creative and the consistency and  flavor of the mushrooms complimented the fried tofu and yellow  mustard perfectly, and to top it off I had a great glass of dry Sake to pair with the meal. This restaurant is truly a gem in the LES

Nice lower east side ramen place with some awesome appetizers. On the pricey side - probably due the outdoor seating. It's almost $20 for a bowl of ramen with all the fixings. 

The tofu Coney Island however is one of the most amazing things you will ever taste in your life. It's a crazy vegetarian Asian take on a hot dog with a mushroom ragu, dry fried tofu and mustard on top. It's seriously unreal. 

The vegetarian ramen was alright - the broth flavor was a little bland. The spicy ramen broth however was some of the best I've tasted. The problem was add in's were expensive. 

I think I would come back just for the appetizers next time and have some drinks on the back patio.  It's always hard to drink and eat a bunch of ramen :)

overrated. no punch in their ramen dishes. on the heavy side with no noticeably pleasant flavor profile. also it was really expensive: two appetizers, two ramen, two glasses of house wine (pretty lame and apparently $11 each, they don't put it on the menu, the waiter tells about it without telling about the price, smart!) and a yuzu lemonade, paid about $100 plus tip. 

that was my second time. I did not get it at the first time either, but given the rave about this place, I blamed my palate and wanted to try it again -- such lack of self-confidence :)

update: folks, I have just had a fantastic dinner at perla (the next evening, to be precise), not a comparison cuisine-wise, or course, and perla is definitely more upscale (well, you've heard about that place, right?) here is what we got for $120 plus tip at perla, the ones in quotes are the ones we got at perla but not at ivan ramen: two "fantastic" appetizers, two "incredible" pasta dishes, two glasses of "absolutely delicious" wine, "picked from the menu, oh they put the price of the wine on the menu, too :) " and a "to-die-for dessert" -- repeat got no dessert at ivan ramen. 

really, ivan ramen is a joke at that price range, waste your money at your own risk.

One of my many summer to-do's!  Lunch date at Ivan Ramen was good, not raise my roof good but good. 

We got there when it opened at 12, quiet, no Ippudo-like line, so our meal was quick - finished in 45 mins (includes a bathroom break!).

We went for the $22 express lunch (so prix-fix), comes with a draft beer (or choose another non alcoholic beverage), a ramen of your choice or a chicken sandwich, and a side.   

Food: we opted for an ice barley tea and a lemonade (85 degrees high in NYC!), Tokyo Shoyu (soy sauce chicken broth) & the dry triple pork mazemen (great the first 5 bites, then it becomes a task to finish because of its richness from the pork, bacon mix). We chose the Kyuri pickles (on the more sour side, I liked it but lunch partner was not too keen on it) and also the King Trumpet Noodle (aka Mushroom!), now this was freaking ah-mazing! Blown away by the simplicity, refreshing clean broth, and the semi-crunchy texture of the noodle (don't know how they shaped it like noodles!) was "yes sir, may I have another!" Good! 

Lunch partner didn't really like his ramen, he prefers the thicker, more robust type broth vs. what he called... a tribute to Chinese chicken soy base soup, ones he had at home before.  I enjoyed my mazemen, but would probably opt for a lighter version, if we're returning.  

Service was excellent! Quick, efficient and left us to enjoy our food without being overbearing.  20+% tip is well deserved. 

Happy dining my ramen crazed Yelpers!

05.07.16

I wanted to like this place much more than I actually did. We were able to get same day reservations and got seated with no issue. The roast pork musubi was served open faced, and absolutely delicious. The ramen was quite disappointing. I think the spice overtook the entire dish. All the texture of the noodles, the pork, and the egg all ended up being all mushed together.

I will say as a saving grace that the service was excellent.

Total damage for two: $49

I wasn't blown away by Ivan Ramen...their noodles were overcooked and the broth was too salty. I tried the shoyu ramen option. I was appreciative of their vegan ramen option (comes with lots of veggies.) The nitamago (boiled egg) was yummy. Service was REALLY attentive which was a plus. However, there are too many good ramen places around to go back.
Great Ramen find suggested by a business associate.  Great first time ramen experience.  I got the spicy option and it was extremely hot and I eat a lot of spicy food.  Will definitely be back!

Solid 3 star review + 0.5 stars for service however I've decided to rate it 3/5 because I don't think this is a place that you necessarily need to stop at if you're just visiting NY. 

My friend and I were around the area so we decided to stop at Ivan ramen for a quick bite before heading to boba guys next door for tea. The service was great, they kept out water glasses full and were very friendly. 

The ramen itself was decent, I enjoyed the broth (tried both the shoyu + shio) and the chasu was tender. The egg was the star of the show for me, marinated to perfection with a runny center. However the reason for the mediocre review is the noodle texture. The noodles reminded me of wonton noodles more than anything and I prefer my noodles more chewy with good body (if that makes sense). 

Overall if you're in the area it's a good place to stop by and get a bite, however I wouldn't go out of my way to come here. Price is kinda steep for what it is... ($15 for one bowl of ramen) but it's tasty if anything.

I came here to meet up with a college friend. The happy hour deals are awesome, and the food is well worth the visit. There are other ramen places around, but this has a great feel to it with hip seating and friendly staff. It's not pretentious like some of the places in LA and Chicago I've tried. It's small, but the seating is generous and you won't feel squished like typical NYC restaurants. 

There are options for all your friends from purist meat hound to vegan spice master. The soup is solid and the noodles have great texture. Plan to shell out 15-30 bucks here. This would be good for meeting with good friends or a long term significant other, but by virtue of noodles, avoid it for dates unless you are prepared to get splashed.

This place is not your typical ramen when you think Japanese ramen. The broth was super salty and fatty. The portions are small especially for 15$ a bowl - a small bowl. 
Typically in ramen bowls there are different toppings which is all included in price- egg, bamboo shoots, scallions, meat, seaweed, etc. However Ivan ramen, you have to pay extra for different toppings. The noodles used were different than typical - not sure how to explain it but it was not your typical noodles. 
I will not return back. I have it a once try and will not be returning

Not worth $15 for noodles and one piece of boiled pork. Place needs to upgrade themselves. Didn't like the ramen flavor too. Seems more Like a top ramen to me just with added fish powder. Don't waste your money.

My boyfriend and I went to this place because it was highly recommended. It was a HUGE letdown from the beginning. The noise level is so outrageous you can't even hear yourself think let alone what the server is saying to you. We ended up getting moved to a "more quiet area" we were brought food that was not ours..then our server ( whom had forgot what our order was) brought us the wrong food as our appetizer--we finally got our food that was the entree (correct) and it was flavorless (had to over compensate with table hot sauce) and mine was on the cool side when it supposed to be served piping hot. THIS PLACE IS NOT TRUE RAMEN - maybe ramen inspired but certainly not TRUE RAMEN... Pooooooorly inspired!
Had a great experience here. Would recommend the meatballs and wings for appetizer; the spicy ramen was good as well, but be warned--it is VERY spicy.

Went for dinner on a weekend shortly before they closed. Tried the Vegetarian Ramen- it came with a big cluster of enoki mushrooms, one roasted tomato, and the some of the best veggie broth I've had. Added alot of chili sauce to make it spicy enough for me.

Triple Pork Ramen and Spicy Red Chili Ramen were also big hits at my table. The service was great - very helpful in describing menu options and making recommendations.

If you ignore the hyper around Ivan Ramen (backstory of a New Yorker who moved to Japan and came back with a new perspective on ramen and David Chang and other's rave about the ramen) and ignore the lines ... this isn't too bad.

They use chicken broth for their broth and it wasn't especially too powerful. I had the Shio ramen and my gf had the Shoyu ramen... she didn't like the Shoyu... I thought the Shio was good. The noodles were buckwheat (I think) noodles... and the pork didn't add anything to the dish... overall the ramen is average to ok to below average.

The saving grace is really the musubi. It's pretty incredible!!!

Hearing all the rave about this ramen shop, I decided to give it a try. 

The ramen didn't meet my expectations though, but one of their specials did. I believe it was mushrooms, yet it tasted like oysters but it was really good. The dish is shown in the picture posted.

Came in minutes before closing on my drinking buddy's suggestion (him being a knowledgeable ramen fellow). We were seated and an intense ramen discussion followed. I was impressed how much the staff knew. They were really friendly despite the shop being nearly closed. 

We both got the triple pork ramen. Delicious. Loved it. Looking forward to returning soon.

Great outdoor seating patio. We came here for brunch and it was not busy. I love that you can make opentable reservations. Just a note: if you have a party bigger than 6 they want to serve you off a pre fixe menu instead of being able to order a la carte. We came for boozy brunch with unlimited drinks so we wanted to order a la carte. The drinks were absolutely delicious! All of them were good so you can't go wrong. I got their brunch ramen and it was delicious. The brunch congee is also good as well.

Heard the hype about this place, I even made a reservation (as most great places have a line out of the door) only to find only a handful of white people there, I was seated immediately.

My background has been west coast ramen, some places in which you must speak Japanese, I have been spoiled and have fairly high expectations and was not at all impressed. I gauge my opinion on a basic Tonkotsu broth.

The place is pretty hippie/pretentious .... already a turn off as most ramen places are a bar against a hole in the wall. The atmosphere is nice, clean, welcoming. There were no Asians eating there, also a red flag. 

 The menu has a little bit of a twist, but it doesn't really say that in the description. I ordered the Tonkotsu chasu pork ramen, only to find a slash of broth with yakisoba noodles and bacon in it!!! I figured I'd try it, the flavored egg and splash of broth were okay but the bacon was glazed like a dessert item and didn't click with the soup it was in. The portions are small, 5mins in and the bowl was gone, I spent $50 and overpaid for something I could make drunk at home that left me hungry. 

The staff was mediocre, after adding in a couple items to the ramen I was "recommended" to select different ones .... c'mon man .... shave your beard. 

*if you know your ramen then head elsewhere, if you're new to ramen head elsewhere.

I am just curious how the owner invented this taste while trained in japan. this is an invention. it's different from normal "ramen" tastes found anywhere in japan. customer response to this place is very interesting though.

I came here on a Thursday night around 7:30pm. Didn't have reservations but we were quickly seated. However the hostess grabbed my arm when I tried to sit which was kind of weird. She told me the table was not finished but its whatever. Me and my friend each ordered a ramen. He ordered the spicy chili one which was okay. BUT THE DOUBLE DASHI TSUKEMEN IS TOO DIE FOR. the tuna was made so good and the sour sauce was amazing. Been thinking about the tuna for three days already haha. Meal came out a little to about maybe $45 for the two of us. The tuna ramen is $21, pricey but so good!

Yaaaaas I love this place! My boyfriend and I came here a couple of weeks ago for a late Friday night meal before going out. Sat at the bar. Great staff! Such a pleasant experience -- weird and interesting beer selection, and -- as usual -- our meal was spectacular. You MUST get the triple-pork/triple-garlic mazemen... it is one of the most delicious dishes I've ever tasted! Can't recommend Ivan Ramen enough. Low-key, calm, perfect.
Service was good , very helpful with menu etc and the ramen was also tasty but could use some more broth
Way too salty, almost cold broth, and the size of an appetizer. It's never a good sign if there aren't any japanese customers in a Ramen restaurant...

Went here to get in some ramen and noms... Heard about this place from multiple people but I can't say I was a tiny disappointed.  The Tsukeman was ok, the apps were so so.  I had the Chinese vegetables which were a tiny too cold for my taste.  The furukake ribs were so dry :( I wish they moisten up the ribs just a bit... They definitely overcooked those...

The wings weren't bad but the sauce is what really saved the wings.... Not so much the meat itself.  Not sure if I would come back here to be honest.... Not my first choice for ramen in the city.

I had made my reservation through Yelp, which apparently does not work for this restaurant. I arrived at Ivan Ramen, and they had zero record of my reservation despite my confirmation email and text. Fortunately they were able to provide a table for us anyway.  The ramen was good but nothing to write home about especially for the price.  Given the micromachine portions it was way overpriced. Definitely could go for a slice or two afterwards. The two stars is mostly in relation to the price and portion size. Flavors were decent and service was fine. With all the ramen places in the city, I do not think this was a standout.

I heard so many amazing things about Ivan, and I went in feeling so excited to try their ramen, but left feeling so disappointed. 

When the bowl was first presented to me, I found the presentation to be fairly bland; nothing popped out for me. I was glad to see that the bowl came with a whole egg, since most places only serve half an egg. It was cooked well, but it could've spent a little more time in the marinade. Also the soup was sooooooooo salty. Granted I ordered the shio ramen, but I didn't want to only taste salt in the broth. I couldn't taste any of the flavors in the broth, it just tasted like super salty water. The thickness of the broth was right, but the salt level overpowered anything that could've been good about it. 

The best part of the bowl was the noodles, which made me happy. They were cooked well and had an excellent chew. I do wish they were a tad bit thicker, but other than that, they were well made. As for the pork, it was disappointing. It definitely could have been more tender and I wish it had some marinade or seasoning other than salt. The whole bowl just seemed to be on the bland side or simply too salty and most definitely was not worth $16

I also tried my friends vegetarian broth, which was soy sauce based, and it just tasted like soy sauce + water. It was also super salty and lacking in flavor. 

The shop definitely did not live up to the hype.

I always knew Ivan was worth his salt/shio in Japan. However, I didn't think he would be able to produce a product similar to Japan given the differences in wheat and water. 

I rarely say this but I was very impressed with his ramen. I'm personally biased towards Tokyo thick noodles over thin ones. But damn, these thin noodles were amazing -- had that great al dente chew and could stand up to hot dipping sauce very well. 

Definitely the best bowl I've had in NYC or anywhere else outside of Japan for that matter. 

Get the mazemen or the tsukemen and you won't be disappointed.

Working my way through New York ramen and glad to see it has picked up in the years since I last visited. Now New Yorkers actually have ramen on a par with Japan and Ivan Orkin's is a truly sophisticated blend. I didn't get to his joint in Tokyo (even though I was eating 3 ramen a day) but ate at his pop up @Supernormal in Melbourne. This was a class above that with the pork blend, springy noodle and complex flavour combination. Very curious to try the tsukemen and the full soupy options, but I have a rule of always trying the #1 and that seemed to be the triple pork.
It was worth those few extra dollars and as for the small serving - I thought it would allow me to get a tsukemen to follow but those wheat noodles really expanded so I'm thankful I didn't. Those folks complaining about the small servings...this is not a joint where you are looking for quantity over quality, this is about taking your palate for a ride. It wasn't perfect, but the originality ensures it that fifth star. New Yorkers should take great pride in Ivan's Tokyo success, and congratulations on being able to export it back to his home town without turning it into one of those places that exports a famous ramen and turns it into a rancid chain that retains no authenticity.
Ecstatic.

Met up with some friends who are visiting the city and decided to check this place out. Ive read that this is one of the ramen places in the city to try. 

We were a group of 5 and they were super accommodating and the service was great.

I ordered the miso tonkotsu tsukemen which is basically chilled ramen with pork belly and a dipping sauce on the side. the noodles came with a GIANT bed of green onions which i promptly gave my friend all of my green onions. the noodles and the dipping sauce tasted really good. the sauce wasn't too salty which is critical. the pork belly was cooked well and was tender and kind of melts in the mouth. although the dish was good all around i don't think it meets the 18$ price point. i wasn't mind blown and wasn't completely full after. 

my friends tried the veggie ramen and the spicy ramen dish and both enjoyed it but not something they will come back for since there are so many ramen options in the city.

overall this place is okay if you're in the area and want some ramen but nothing amazing that makes it worth the trip to the lower east side for.

Really solid ramen place in LES. I've been here twice, once on a weekend for lunch and another for takeout dinner on a weekday. The soft boiled egg is delicious. The broth is flavorful, and the portion size/amount of noodles is great. 

My only critique is that when I came in for a takeout order, I was told it would be ready in about 5 minutes, when it really took more Iike 20, so my hopes were raised and then let down. Also, it's a bit overpriced in my opinion for ramen (about $20 including tax and tip). More if you want to add any extra vegetables or meat to your bowl. Still a great place to check out though.

I arrived happy; I left happy. I called ahead to see if Monday lunch would be crowded. The affable voice on the phone told me the coast was clear, etc. - no reservation. I liked the decor. I liked the server at the counter. I liked the manager on duty. I liked my fluke appetizer and ramen main dish. The house saki was fine and so was one of the beers offered. Since I've never been in Tokyo, I can only compare it to U.S. joints - but I do think the menu and presentation would hold up anywhere. Got a chuckle to see Woody Allen's Manhattan poster inside the restroom - in Japanese.  Granted, there are a lot of places for Ramen, including your own kitchen, but I can't see how anyone would be terribly disappointed. If anything, I would have liked a bit more pork in my ramen. Ramen critics/experts remind me of coffee snobs, pastrami experts, and grilled cheese sandwich aficionados. "The coffee shop near me has the best BLT in the city! The best!!"

The Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen is possibly the best food I've ever eaten. We went there with another couple and my partner kept trying to get us to order a variety of things but no one wanted to miss out on the Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen, including her. So, four TPTGMs please. 20 minutes of no talking, serious slurping and we were four very happy people. They usually have some kind of cooked greens that go well with the TPTGM.  I wish they had a real bar though -- not a fan of sake.

Nice casual place. I walked in right as it opened so there wasn't anyone there but people did start to flow in. I got the tsukemen. The noodles were perfectly cooked with a nice amount of chewiness to them. It also came with a nice piece of pig. The broth was delicious, and coated the noodles perfectly. Friendly staff, good experience.
there are many different kinds of ramens and its rly good. Pork bun for appetizer is rly good too c:

I've tried many ramen spots in NYC and Ivan's been on my list for awhile. My boyfriend and I finally stopped by on a Sunday night for dinner and I'm really glad that we did!  We were able to walk right in with no wait.  We both ordered the Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen and it was delicious! Although the noodles weren't in a traditional broth - they were in more of a sauce - the dish was still fantastic.  Our waiter told us to stir the dish before eating it so the sauce was evenly distributed. Each bite was packed with flavor and you could taste the richness from the pork. The service and atmosphere was nice too. The wall art and decor had a Tokyo feel to it. My only complaint is that it was a bit expensive for ramen.  With the addition of an egg, the ramen came out to $18 which is pricer than other ramen spots in the area, including Ippudo. Overall though, solid spot.

Arrived to an empty space for lunch.  Still took 20 mins to get a glass of saki.  Ramen arrived similarly slow, was ok, just ok, 15 bucks for some noodles, few much rooms and ok broth.  

Didn't appreciate server having a conversation across the dining room about 'tampons' with a second table of friends that arrived.  Totally unprofessional.  

The bill was $35 for 1 glass and some ok noodles.  Really bad value for what I got, while story meh.  

I don't normally yelp and have never given a bad review before, this one was called for.

I had high expectations for this spot, because Ivan's Ramen is famous in Japan.  

I paid $24 for a bowl of spicy miso ramen with rye noodles, with pork belly and enoki mushrooms.  It was supposed to be an epic bowl of ramen.  

My ramen looked aesthetically pleasing, had great color, and the portion was generous, too.  But the broth was like saltwater, sooo salty.  I cringed slurping it.  My friend told me I needed to add-on the enoki mushrooms, which was a good add, only because it diluted the saltiness a bit.  And, I discovered I don't like rye noodles- the texture was drier and less chewy for my taste.

If you're only going to try one ramen place in NYC, don't let it be Ivan's Ramen.

I love the ramen in this place. I ordered the chili pork ramen and it was definitely on the spicy side which I loved. I loved this ramen it was more on the smaller portion side compared to other ramen places but I love ramen so I appreciated there smaller portion. The broth, noodles, and everything was filled with flavor. Love this place definitely will be coming back. However I ordered the pork buns and believed it could have more depth of flavors. Overall amazing place for ramen.
Hands down the best Ramen i've ever had. It was extra spicy just how i like it.

Hi, it's me, the longest holdout in the world as far as trying Ivan Ramen.

Obviously, the story of some white dude from Long Island conquering a beloved piece of Japanese culture (purely on his own merits, right? cough) and bringing it back to his home city at $16+ per bowl inspired in me at least as much disdain as curiosity. 

The latter won out over the former one fateful day.

I avoided the raved-about garlic mazemen because it's what seems to have pissed people off in terms of tiny portion sizes, and I'll be damned if I walk away from a ramen shop hungry. An overview of the Tokyo Shio Ramen ----

NOODLES: Ivan's signature rye noodles looked fascinating with little specks, and had a texture between regular ramen and slippery cellophane noodles. They were an interesting change, but just too soft. I still far prefer the eerie fragrance and unique bite of traditional yellow ramen made with kansui.

BROTH: I loved how the broth had a strong dashi flavor in addition to the chicken overtones. Loooved. And who can fault a shio broth for being exactly as salty as the name describes?

TOPPINGS: Thoroughly forgettable.

We also ordered chicken wings, whose menu description ("toasted garlic caramel, togarashi and shiso ranch") was 500x more interesting than the dish that came. The wings were soggy, the flavor was muddled and too sweet, and it was $13 for maybe 6 pieces. Get thyself to a Korean fried chicken spot instead. Or drench some wings in BBQ sauce and throw into your oven - either way, just don't bother here.

Cutting to the chase: I half-expected a bowl of ramen that was smarter than it was satisfying. My expectations were exceeded: The ramen was certainly interesting, and good, and the portion size was totally non-offensive! But overall it didn't captivate.

Yes, still worth at least one visit.
Sat at the bar on Saturday night and we had great service from the bartender- friendly, knowledgeable and the food was good.

Don't think i'll be coming back here. One of my guy friends recommended this place, so I decided to come here on a whim with a girlfriend of mine to catch up and try something new in terms of ramen. It was my first time here and her second.  There wasn't a wait at the time (it was around 9PM on a weeknight) and the hostess seated us at a table by the front area near the entrance. There was a mini bar area in the back that had more customers, while my girlfriend and I were the only two customers sitting at the front. I had the impression the place would be packed, but I didn't mind the place being empty either.  

Once we ordered and our food was served on our table, our ramen bowl presentations looked alright. I ordered the Triple Pork ramen. We both like Enoki Mushrooms so we added that as an extra topping. The ramen itself was very salty and that was all I could taste.  I did enjoy the pork chasiu, however, the saltiness of the ramen empowered everything and anything else I ate.  I wanted out. My glass of water was emptied in an instant.  I still had some ramen left, but I felt really cringy about the saltiness that I wasn't about to stuff myself any further.  The server was barely attentive after reciting their specials for the day. I remember waiting for "auto"-water refills from our server, but nope. none.  I think that and the saltiness were the two things that bothered me the most during my visit. Eventually I gave up on finishing my food.  

One star for the cool blue light under the mini bar counter.  Eh..
I didn't see anything worth the hype of coming back for a second try.

Ivan Ramen has a ton of stuff working in their favor, hence the 5 star review. 

Starting with the food...it's pretty damn good. I tend to sit at the bar which gives you a bird's eye view of the whole kitchen and pass. Every time I've been there, it's been abundantly clear that everyone in the kitchen from the dish washer to the head chef care deeply about the food they're putting out. I can't speak for the entire menu but you certainly won't be disappointed by the shoyu, shio, vegetarian or tsukemen ramen. Spring for the shoyu glazed pork belly in whatever you get, you won't be disappointed. As far as appetizers, the buns are pretty good, if not mindblowing. The little gem lettuces however are unreal. Far and above the most delicious salad I've ever eaten. 

They've got you covered on beer, wine, sake and a couple of sake cocktails. If you're drinking, grab one of the cocktails. They're all delicious, they pair well with the menu and they're definitely a bit different. 

The staff is what kicks this place up to a 5. Everyone's great. They're accommodating, knowledgeable and friendly. I was definitely a little taken back the first time I grabbed dinner here as um, how can I put this delicately...the staff isn't particularly Japanese. That said, the entire staff (especially the kitchen staff) approaches the food and the culture they've borrowed it from with reverence, respect and serious attention to detail. 

So, let's call the food a 4.25. The service and the staff are well worth the extra .75 to make this a perfect review.

Came here for lunch on a weekday with a friend who's always up for ramen. The restaurant was rather empty at the time. The decor was nice. We decided to take one of the tables in the back, which was pretty cool. Unlike some people mentioned, the server was quite nice. Though he left us a jug of water on the table, he still checked on us several times and poured water for us.

We both ordered the chili red with additional enoki topping. The ramen itself was pretty good. I slurped off the ramen quickly while talking to my friend, and the enoki, though looked as though raw, was fresh and yummy and didn't taste raw at all. My friend and I both agree that the broth had a nice, mild spicy kick but too salty to drink down. Also the price is a bit high ($16 for the ramen + $3 for the extra topping) when the original topping was only some mash eggs.

One of the worst ramen I've ever had. I literally could not consume it. The broth was absolutely awful. I can't really explain it, but it was bitter. I came here because Time Out often raves about this place, but I cannot agree. 

Service was great, up until the point where the waiter overheard us talking about how disgusting the ramen was, then he gave us the coldest shoulder.

Not sure if I came on a bad day but I came with a large group of friends and we each ordered a different ramen. One thing we all can agree on was that it was very salty, I left very thirsty! It was recently nominated #2 best ramen spot in NYC. I beg to differ, the service was great but it was just way too salty. You can't possibly accidently make 8 ramen dishes all salty.

Pretty disappointed with this place after watching a mini-doc about and hearing about the hype through various media outlets. My boyfriend thought his shio ramen was decent, but disliked my shoyu ramen when he tried some broth. I thought my ramen was fine at first, but gradually became more mediocre the more I ate. The best parts were the egg and chashu, but the broth was kinda weird - didn't really have any depth - and I didn't even finish the noodles, which are supposedly their selling point. And ummm, $16 for what is one of the visually ugliest ramen bowls I've seen in the city? No. 

As my boyfriend put it, "the best thing about this place is the serving size" (which is considerably smaller than the usual conical ramen bowl you see).

Soooo the place was cool the staff was very helpful and decor was nice looking 
Heat lamps in the back kinda cooked my forehead but whatever
Flavor wise my ramen was OK , however temperature wise it wasn't hot in the least... like room temperature 
Saki sangria was off tasting and didn't make me want to have more than one 
Maybe it was an off day idk

Food is meh.  I had the shio ramen, which was lacking in flavor. Worst yet, it took them 45 min between serving the appetizer and the main course - they were making take out orders instead. Not sure you should prioritize takeouts over sit downs.  Food was bland.

Ivan Ramen is tucked away in the Lower East Side and is SO GOOD. The ramen is reasonably priced, and everyone who works there was incredibly nice. I arrived early for my reservation and started at the bar but they were happy to move us to a table once we had finished our beers. The cream ale is a great beer, by the way. The shoyu ramen is classic for a reason, and they do it very well. The noodles are perfectly cooked and the ramen was great and not overly salty like many ramen places can be. This bowl comes heavy on the green onions, so ask them to lighten up on those if you aren't a fan. The spicy ramen is also great, but be warned that if you can't tolerate a lot of heat this might be a mistake. Next time I'm definitely getting the deviled eggs, pork meatballs, and spam musubi.

Been to this location a few times but this was the worst experience ever. I thought Ivan's was not one of those totally pretentious Ramen places...until this time. The hostess wouldn't seat me (party of 2) until my friend was here which is understandable as they were very busy but suggested I could buy a drink. I said sure and asked to go to the bar, but the hostess said a party was coming so I couldn't go to the bar...(?!?). When we were finally seated (about 10min later) we were offered the bar, yes the bar, and told that a table was another 15-20min wait. So we just resigned to taking the bar seats. The icing on the cake was when the waiter poured our water and I was about to drink when I noticed the lipstick stain on the cup. My waiter's response when I asked for a new cup was "oh yea I saw that...". Luckily our experience the rest of the night was much better, our bartender/new waiter gave us recommendations on sake and let us try them before ordering a carafe and the Ramen, as usual, was pretty good. However, given the start of the night, I am wary to go back.

Do yourself a favor and request at least two orders of the Pork Meatballs as an appetizer for your table - they are utterly incredible and flavorful. The Tokyo Shio Ramen is outstanding (add the Minced Garlic Chicken). Order a Wabi-Sabi beer, too! Cheers! Also, ask for Buddy - he is the most wonderful and considerate server!

Triple pork, triple garlic mazeman.  The best non-pork broth ramen I've ever had.  The noodles have an excellent bite and the mix of flavors was fantastic.  

Need to try the LES bun the next time I come based on these other reviews....

I came here for lunch today with a group of coworkers. It was pretty empty, and not the best place for lunch because it's way overpriced for what it was.

We got the vegetarian ramen, shio ramen, and triple pork ramen with the pork belly buns to share. The food was OK - my coworkers thought it was a bit too salty, but it was overall decent food. Make sure to ask for less salty for your ramen! 

The pork buns were pretty good. I loved the bun itself - nothing mind-blowing, but the dish had the right mix of salty, sweet, and spicy. We split the two buns among the four of us, and it was the perfect amount of food. Just a one bite sample. 

I had the triple pork ramen and it had pretty good flavor. What I didn't realize in advance was that it had no broth.... plus it had way too much pork, but the noodles were decent.

The ramen and pork buns here are definitely unique, different from the traditional NYC ramen shops and it's worth a visit once maybe for dinner.... however, we ended up paying $24 each which was pricey for lunch, and the portions aren't that big.

Overall, decent meal with good ambience & service, but overpriced. 3.5 stars.

To be fair, their egg and chashu way above avg.
Noodle and soup, meh~

And their hospitality cold as f.
(Saturday, 11/10/2016, around 5PM. Hostess roll her eyes when I asked for bar seat.)

After shopping nearby, the boyfriend and I decided to stop here for an early dinner. At around 4 on a Saturday, the restaurant was still fairly crowded and the hostess suggested that we sit at the bar for more space. She, along with the other waiters and waitresses were pretty friendly and attentive. 

The two of us ordered the shoyu ramen ($16). My favorite parts of it was the pork belly and the soft boiled egg. The noodles were a good texture as well. My biggest gripe, though, was the soup. It was super salty and I couldn't taste much else. The taste kind of grew on me as I continued eating but I couldn't help but feel like I need to drink a gallon of water when I was done. 

All in all, this is a decent place to get a bowl of ramen. I'd say come here if you're in the area but this isn't a place you should go out of your way for.

Another ramen place that disappointed me. I have been wanting to try this place for a long time and finally went. I went with 2 of my friends and started off with their fried chicken. That was pretty good in taste with the sauce. Entrée, I got the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen. I didn't like it that much. Broth was very salty and it was just a soy sauce flavor. Noodles were perfect texture. I don't think I will go back to this place though - nothing special about it.

After reading a slew of negative reviews on Yelp, I didn't have the highest of expectations coming here...but I very much enjoyed the ramen here and so I'll go out on a limb and be the dissenting opinion.

I had the shio ramen, and absolutely loved it. I think the reason I had such a favorable experience here, was that the ramen just tasted so different. There's so much ramen out there these days that tastes so similar, that it was just refreshing to taste something that I wasn't used to. There was a smokiness to the broth that I really, really liked - it almost reminded me of the smoked BBQ of central Texas. I thought the noodles were cooked well, good bite, and each slurp had a good amount of broth stuck to them. I pretty much lapped up every last drop of that broth.

Two thumbs up from me, but if you haven't been here, definitely recommend you try at least once and form your own opinion!

Super salty broth every time I come here. Pork is decent. Service is great, people are great. 

IVAN ORKIN WHY ARE YOU HYPE GOD. TURN DOWN THE SALT IN YOUR SHIO AND TSUKEMEN.

I've had ramen from NY to Tokyo, and nothing dries my insides harder than this ramen.

Vegetarian ramen was really mediocre, and the tofu in it too salty, though I appreciate the fact that there's an option for substituting the noodles for vegan, gluten-free shirataki noodles. The kyuri pickles were decent, and the Tofu Coney Island was awesome -- if anyone I know wants to go there again, I'm definitely skipping the ramen and getting the tofu dish.
Definitely not the traditional ramen you would typically look for, but if you're feeling adventurous, go ahead!

All in all, this wasn't a great experience. While the service was great and my boyfriend and I were seated immediately even with being a half hour early to our reservation, the food was subpar at best. We ordered an appetizer of steamed pork buns to start, which were fairly tasty but the buns were pretty dense; the pork was seasoned very well, though. For our main courses I got the chicken paitan ramen while my boyfriend got the pork two ways ramen (whatever it was called): mine was VERY peppery and somewhat oily, while his had very little broth, which was chilled without our knowing, and the pork had little to no flavor. The noodles were very good and had a nice chew, but in all we wouldn't go back again. Definitely NOT worth the 50$ we spent for dinner.
Much better options for ramen in the city. Hell even in the neighborhood! Stay clear. Expensive, filled with enthusiastic hipsters that don't know better and meh ramen.

I ordered a spicy ramen, shio ramen and shoyu ramen. They all taste alright... nothing spectacular but edible. I would not recommend this place though. I have had much better ramen somewhere else. The cashier girl was not friendly and helpful at all too... overall, 3 stars.

You want to talk about an ideal way to get into the holiday spirit? Spiced wine, sexy Santa's elves (babe elves of course) and sour cream and onion latkes. December really is the season to be merry, the time to put the Christ back in Christmas, the eight craziest nights. It's a four week party fest culminating in New Years, the number one day of the year where every babe wants a little make out sesh to kick off the near year right. For me, December is not a sprint. It's a goddamn marathon. A marathon of warm drinks, no responsibilities, a few awkward mornings, and a party or date every night of the month. I call it "The Phil W. December to Remember Me Sales Event" because you're buying what I'm selling.

First week of December, and I was on a tear. Seven days. Seven nights out. Yhoagie's office party. Tinder date. Tinder date. Bumble date. Ex-coworker's holiday party. Some holiday party I crashed in my building. And Rolf's. Oh Rolf's. Love Rolf's. If you haven't been you need to go, and if you don't like it, then you don't like life. And of course go during the holidays. That's the only time to go. Lights for days. Any other time of year, and it's just weird. Mad dudes passed out at the bar.

Anyway, I had to go super hard this month since my office wasn't having a holiday party. How do you not have a holiday party? What did the holidays ever do to you to deserve this? My office thinks putting out a box of candy canes is "getting into the holiday spirit." Well it's not. No one likes candy canes because we're not five.

I love office parties because naturally there's always that one dude who decides doing lines of coke in the bathroom (because he can't wait an hour until the party ends) is a good idea. And there's always that one babe who thinks it's cool to profess her love to the coworker who she thinks "has a nice tush." But nope. Not this year. My office is a fun vacuum.

So my week of "The Phil W. December to Remember Me Sales Event" went from 60-0 real fast.
