One week you are the party machine, and the next week it's sitting at home on the couch eating saltines and peanut butter. The old bank account was in a little bit of a pickle. It's the holiday season, what do you want from me? So maybe I like buying rounds of Hot Todds for people at the bars. Maybe I have an obsession with cider. And plus, dates get pricey. I mean it's 2016 and gender is neutral and all, but I'm traditional. A guy pays on the first date. Anything less and my father's head would spin. I can hear him now. "What kind of son did I raise? If you can't pay for dinner then you shouldn't be on a date." Smart man.

I swiped right on the babe of the century. I mean, my type, all the way. The kind of babe who gets a discount at "The Phil W. December to Remember Me Sales Event." Her profile read, "I'm the Elaine Benes to your Jerry Seinfeld." Didn't need any further convincing. We instantly matched. It was a Tuesday night, but neither of us cared. Besides I was at home farting on the couch. We decided to grab dinner, only problem she said was that she was gluten free. Side note: While I do believe in global warming, I don't believe in gluten intolerance. However, this did work in my favor. I was like, "We should totally get ramen. I know just the place." 

In no time we were at Ivan Ramen. She could only eat broth because of the whole gluten thing so I got to eat all the noods and pork. Perfect. One bowl. Two people. Real cheap. Then, she wanted sake. I guess that's gluten free. I love sake, but not the most cost effective way to get buzzed. Told her, "Not a fan. Tastes like dirty water."

"Fine. We'll just do sake bombs then." Whoa. So aggressive. I loved it. 

Dinner was a blur.

The night wasn't over after Ivan. Pretty sure we went back in time with a little prohibition action at Back Room and finished things off in the basement of Late Late. There was def middle school grinding action going on. We were feeling the holiday spirit. The DJ was playing Mariah Carey "All I Want For Christmas Is You" on repeat. It felt like the '90s again, and by 2AM I closed the deal at "The Phil W. December to Remember Me Sales Event." 

THE REST OF THE DETAILS ARE NOT FOR YOU, GET YOUR OWN LIFE!

So the weirdest part was waking up on my couch in an ugly sweater. It wasn't mine. I don't think it was hers. It was a shitty cartoon of Snoop Dogg and the caption said "Happy Ho-lidays." Just awful. My shirt was nowhere to be found. I check my phone and have a message from my babe. "Crzy time last night. Can't believe you traded your shirt for that homeless guy's ugly sweater."

Yikes. Whatever, I was in the giving spirit. 

Oh, and by the way. Ivan Ramen was the bomb. I've prob been there like five times. "Dank noodles, meat and broth sucks," said NO ONE. EVER. My recs, all of them, but if you had to pick then go the spicy ramen or the shoyu. And it's obv the best date spot. Def has the "I read Time Out and Eater so I know cool places to eat" vibe.
Came here because the sign in the window said it was Michelin Recommended (whatever that means).  What I got was a small serving of overpriced mediocre ramen.  Probably won't be coming back.

Soups are amazing. 
Staff friendly and efficient. Love this place will come back to rates other items on menu.

This was fine, but it didn't impress me as much as I had hoped or wanted. We got the Japanese fried chicken, the steamed pork buns, the trumpet mushroom noodles, and the Tokyo shiu ramen. All four were fine, but I wouldn't be overly motivated to come back here to get any of them specifically. I liked the flavors/spices on the chicken, but the meat was a little tough. (It might be intended to be that way, I'm just not a huge fan of that style.) The pork buns were good, but not close to Noodle Bar's. Both the noodles and ramen were perfectly fine, just not overly exciting, and, again, not as good as what you'd typically get at one of the other major ramen places.

The price was in line with what you'd expect (it came to a little over $60 total for the two of us, after tax and tip), but I just wished I had liked it more.

I have no idea how the ramen is because it never got delivered. We ordered 2 bowls, they sent one. We called to tell them, and they told us that we had to re-order to get our original order filled, and they refused to do anything about it at all. The people we extremely patronizing and unhelpful, not to mention dishonest. The woman I spoke with hung up on me the first time I called. When I spoke to her a second time she told me she would call seamless to expedite our order. 40 minutes later, still no food. When I called back, she said that she had not called seamless to expedite anything, and told me that no other deliveries had gone out in the last 40 minutes. Which is impossible to believe at 8 pm on a snowy Saturday night. It's now been over an hour and no food.
It's not the best ramen in New York but still worth a visit. I really enjoyed the cold ramen in the summer time. It was something I never tasted like this before. Great with the fresh lemon.

I haven't found the perfect bowl of ramen here (or anywhere in New York) so I struggle to give this 5 stars. However, Ivan ramen is the most inventive ramen I have ever eaten. 

Despite the friendly service and interior, this is not a beginner's ramen.

Technical quality 5/5 - these are the best noodles you will find in New York. Perfect amount of bite and springiness when served. Deserving of fast slurping.

Creativity 5/5 - my tsukemen was beautiful, but it was my girlfriend's crab yuzu cold ramen that blew my mind. It was like mixing noodles with cold lemonade- except it tasted way better than that sounds. It was not as satisfying as regular ramen, but it grew my understanding of what ramen is. Thank you chef Ivan.

Perfection 4/5 - I own Ivan's book, where he details his recipe over dozens of pages. I expected perfection. I was left impressed, but have not found the golden bowl of ramen I am looking for.

Heard a lot of great things about this place, so I came with a friend who really like ramen a couple of years back, when we still lived really close by. 

I'm a bit of a ramen purist, but I came in with an open mind. Didn't really do it for me, and the dishes and the combinations are a bit forced. 

It's not quite traditional, it's not a modernization, and it's not a regionalistic thing either. Felt a little bit like somebody served you a spaghetti carbonara dish but instead of pancetta they used swedish meatballs, and instead of an egg and pecorino sauce it was butter. Instead of garlic it was ginger and the cracked pepper was replaced with spicy chilis. But they got the spaghetti part, though. 

Aside from that though, the operation is run well, service is great.

Yuzu lemonade - 5 stars!
Ramen - 3 stars...

Overall, not very impressed with the food here. I didn't find much flavor in the pork bun or the shio ramen. The fried chicken appetizer was pretty good but it was also drenched in sauce.

But seriously, that yuzu lemonade was really doing it for me. Even with Boba Guys right next door.

I love this place. My favorite item in their menu is not ramen but the amazing toasted garlic chicken wings that now they have converted into chicken strips (even better). They sauce they come in has been slowly cooked to a caramelized perfection with the right balance of flavors and seasonings and it comes with a unique ranch to dip. As far as ramen goes, it's a bit to salty for my liking but I still order it and just pair it with the Yuzu lemonade that it's refreshing and tastes like mandarin orange. Overall a great spot to catch up with friends and enjoy some salty ramen and out of this world chicken strips!

I feel like preference on ramen is so subjective and personal. Just like a pizza, people have strong preferences on their own style. So having said that, I want to say that Ivan ramen was not my favorite. I like deeper meaty flavor and Ivan ramen was on the lighter side. My boyfriend and I tried this place on a Friday night around 10:30 pm, 30 min before they were closing. No wait and the service was great! Very hipster / relaxed atmosphere which I liked. We started with pork buns, which were delicious. My boyfriend and I had ramen that were recommended by the server, which were Chicken Paitan and Tokyo  Shio Ramen. Again both ramen were good but not phenomenal.

Let me start by saying that it takes A LOTTTTT for me to send food back when at a restaurant and it has probably only happened 3 times in my entire life.... the 3rd being my vegetarian ramen at Ivan last week. The broth was extremely bland but yet salty. Pretty much watered down soy sauce with no complexity. I took one sip and I knew I couldn't get through this bowl. Thankfully our server took it back and I went with the chicken bowl which he highly recommended so I was pretty excited when it came out within a couple minutes. This was much better but still pretty bland to me. Their serving size seems to be smaller than other shops I've been to and I'm not one who can eat much but I left hungry. The winning points to this restaurant are the interior, they take reservations, and their staff is pleasant. Otherwise, I don't think I'll be returning here.

I love this place.
Friendly and knowledgeable service, fantastic food.
The Kyuri pickles are to die for. The Triple Pork Mazemen is a winner every single time.
If I lived downtown, I'd be here all the time.
okay ramen.. i really dont think it worth the trip though.. but if u happen to be in the area it's good try.. i wouldn't come back, i mean nothing really go wrong.. it's just mediocre..

I thought their veggie ramen was really great-- rich and flavorful broth, interesting rye noodles, and a roasted tomato. Portion might have been a bit small. Servers were very friendly. I would definitely come back! I wish it had a bit less of a glossy/fancy/super modern feel though...

We loved our server and our water glasses were full the entire time we were seated. The ramen itself was delicious and so full of flavor! Both of our dishes were licked clean by the end. Fun atmosphere, friendly people, great experience.

***The staff was SUPER friendly!!*** But everything else i ordered was super salty. We got the Shoyu ramen, triple pork triple garlic, and the fried chicken. All were very salty. I mean I ate it because I was hungry (but I didn't finish it nor did I enjoy it) I'm only giving three stars because the porks buns and service was amazing. If it wasn't for those reasons, it would be two stars. It was disappointing.
Get the shio ramen! So flavorful and delicious. Atmostphere is nothing special, but the place is clean and staff is so nice.

I really enjoyed this place but I didn't get your regular bowl of ramen so I can't speak to just that.  We ordered the steamed pork buns (great flavor and loved the pickles), the triple pork triple garlic mazemen, and the chicken paitan. 

The triple pork triple garlic mazemen was awesome - it's a noodle dish that only comes with about half the broth as a normal bowl of ramen and it's a bit thicker so you really get a creamy base with the noodles.  The flavors were on point.  My friend loved the chicken paitan so much he ordered another bowl on the spot.  Both were more specialty dishes so I look forward to coming back to try the regular ramen, but overall was impressed with what we had.

Simple ambiance, great service that was super attentive!  Got in on a Thursday evening around 8'ish with no problems but it was definitely packed.  There were only two of us though.

Excited to try the slurp shop.
I just paid $80 to have mediocre Ramen and a mediocre drink with a friend. Very sad day for a New Yorker.
Lived up to the hype. Excellent. I am full. Also, check out the Chef's Table episode about Ivan.

Ok so we saw Ivan Orkin's featured show on season 3 of Netflix Chef's Table, and 2 days later we literally visited his Lower East Side Ivan Ramen restaurant.  Were we excited the moment we walked in, heck yeah we were.  Did it live up to our expectations, well read on.... its was lunch time but we skipped breakfast and we were really hungry. So we started with with the best part of our meals, the amazing mouth popping crunchy fried boneless chicken with its buttermilk dill dipping sauce that the combo brought tears to our eyes.  Then we also loved the Coney Island tofu appetizer that made us want to find out how we can make it!  Chili over succulent soft creamy tofu squares hello.  Then we had 3 signature ramen bowls that exceeded our expectations, deep vibrant broths, a well spiced dan dan lamb noodles that made me sweat.  We killed every single dish down to last drop.  Netflix got this one right, we just wish Ivan was there so we could of thanked him!

I wish I can give 0 star here. So I came here and line was not long and they said hour wait, OK.So I left and came back hour later,still had to wait 15 min to set . So I set down and made my order 15 minutes later. Waitress are so slow and not paying attention who is first who is second. The food came quick. But OMG my chicken Ramen was so oily, to me. And my boyfriend asked waiter to make Togo and second waiter came and took our food and put on tub other dishes, it's means we couldn't even take to go. So whatever this place, it's not worse it to wait so long and drive from Brooklyn.

We went around 1pm on a Saturday because we had a reservation and it was very nice. We were seated within 2 minutes of being there and got service 5 mins later. We ordered the pork buns, Japanese fried chicken, tokyo shoyu ramen, spicy chili ramen, the triple pork ramen (which didn't have enough pork in it as far as I'm concerned) and a iced roasted barley tea which tastes exactly how it sounds. The bill came to about 80 bucks. The staff were very friendly and we didn't have to wait very long for the food. Personally I think everything is priced well proportionally to the portion size.

I came here the first time and loved it, so I brought friends with me the second time and realized something. 

Ivan is really good at many things, pork buns, tonkotsu, ect, but frankly other people are better at those in NYC.

What you must absolutely try is what he known for in Japan. What he has crafted to be exceptional and truly loves. That is his noodles paired with smaltz and I can't recommend them enough.

The two best manifestations of this are his Shio ramen- easily one of the cleanest and most refreshing broths paired with his fantastic noodles and The Morty Special, aka his Chicken Paitan with 1-3 of his expertly marinated soft eggs, the most decadent, incredibly satisfying soup in the city.

Morty, from Rick and Morty, was named after an old jewish comedian who happened to eat almost exclusively chicken products, so the Morty special is a flavor tsunami that he would appreciate the most. 

So you can get other things and may or may not be impressed, but if you get the shio ramen or especially the Morty special you will have one of the best soup dishes ever that you won't forget.

So enjoy and remember to praise the one true Morty before you eat!

Although I enjoyed my meal, I wouldn't come back to or recommend Ivan Ramen to others. There are just too many good restaurants around here to spend $40/person on a mediocre meal in what is essentially a fast casual environment.

We came in at 5 PM on a Saturday, after making the best available reservation on OpenTable over a week prior. After learning about the restaurant through Netflix's Chefs Table, we came excited, hungry and eager to try as much as we could. Unfortunately, this place just didn't live up to our expectations. I'll start with the food and then move to the service.

We ordered three appetizers, in part based on our waiter's recommendations: the pickled daikon, the Japanese fried chicken and the pork meatballs. I really enjoyed the daikon. It is thinly shredded with a nice sesame sauce on top. It may seem a bit pricey - $10 for a small plate of cold vegetables - but if you're here, it is worth trying. I also enjoyed the Japanese fried chicken. It is very crispy and has a subtle complexity. Some bits taste more of breading while others taste of the tangy chili sauce. There is also a nice ranch dipping sauce you can dip bits into. The meatballs, though, are just odd. They tasted more of fish than anything else, which isn't expected given the way the dish is described on the menu and by staff.

We also ordered two entrees, the Tokyo shiyo ramen and the triple pork triple garlic mazemen, which were merely good. I don't have a developed palate for ramen but based on other cuisines, I just expected more from each element of my dish. None of it - not the noodles, the broth nor the pork belly - stood out as particularly delicious. And it didn't come together to become any better. I enjoyed the triple pork mazemen more, but again felt like the neither the pork nor the noodles stood out. And together, it really had a flavor akin to greasy pork dishes I've had before for at a much lower price.

Then there's the service, which while quick, left things to be desired. First, despite having a reservation, we were seated at an unforgivably bad table. It was right by the front door, and so we both ended up in our winter coats for the entire meal. Second, after being seated, we had to wait an unreasonably long time for our waiter. I appreciate that our water glasses were filled immediately but it took too long for our waiter to come by to properly welcome us and take our drink and appetizer order. Third, there were some mix-ups. We saw our daikon dish improperly delivered to the table next to ours and we received someone else's meatballs after eating our own. Fourth, although we arrived on time for our reservation and ate quickly, we were rushed out the door. As soon as our bowls were cleared, they handed us our check, without any prompting. 

Anyway, if you're still interested in Ivan Ramen, I would highly recommend making a reservation. We were seated by the hostess and saw many dejected folks leave after being told of an hour plus wait at 5:30 PM on a Saturday.

I didn't think this place had the traditional flavorful Japanese ramen. It's more of a fusion place. The noodles also don't taste as handmade as Japanese places I've had in Japan, LA and Toronto. My boyfriend ordered the vegetarian ramen which was extremely salty and not much flavor to the soup. My friend was disappointed at her chicken tonkotsu ramen. My shio ramen was very average. Prices are also high compared to authenticate Japanese places whereas portions are small.
This ramen is good. The roasted tomato topping is different and delightful! I would give it 4 stars but the ramen is a little salty for my taste.

Okay, let's preface this review by saying I would normally never go to a ramen place for brunch because nothing about Ramen screams, "eat me when u roll out of bed" however, my friends were hella bent on going after seeing the documentary of the owner on Chef's Table. So, I obliged, bc I am open to new experiences.  On the positive, we got sat right away because we had a reservation, and the server was pleasant. He seemed a little frazzled but overall fine. What was totally unexpected was seeing Ivan, the owner there, seeming as how it was a Sunday. But, he was incredibly nice and informative about the menu, offered suggestions to the group and explained his cooking process.  So after a quick glance of the menu we settled on the following: the Coney Island tofu and mushroom tempura appetizers, and a combo of the vegetarian ramen, chicken paitan, Tokyo shio noodles, and the triple pork mazemen.  Okay, so either everyone was lying to the one person who wanted to go or I was the only one not overly impressed with this place. The owner really sold me on the vegetarian ramen, but it was salty and not overly flavorful, and could have used more cooked vegetables besides the steamed tofu and raw mushroom.  Although I finished most of it, I left pretty hungry, and unsatisfied, and this place is by no means cheap. The ramen was decent but not great. I think the pork dish was good according to my friend, as was the shio dish, but I don't think my friend loved the chicken Paitan. As far as the appetizers go, the tofu was good but I don't particularly care for mustard. The mushroom tempura tasted pretty good although it was the greasiest tempura I have ever sampled. One bite gave off a burst of oil into your mouth. It was a little bland, had it not been for the dipping sauce. Overall, half then dishes were decent, but I don't forsee myself going back.

Uhmazing!!!!! Best Raman noodles ever!!! Wasn't sure about the rye noodles but, YES!, so good! Service was excellent & the drinks were great, too. Small place & I would recommend making a reservation.
Came here after watching Chefs Table and it was up to expectations. Tried the Shio as well as the appetizer and both were amazing. Also got a chance to chat with Ivan and he was pleasant to speak to.

Normally I don't like to write reviews about restaurants I've never eaten in, but in this instance I feel entitled. On a Sunday afternoon at 12:15 we walked in to this restaurant and put our names on the waiting list. They told us it would be an hour. An hour and 30 minutes later we walked up to the restaurant to inquire when our table will be ready. We were told "no table for you."

We spent 90 minutes waiting for a table at a restaurant that had no intention of seating us. They took our cell phone number so they could text us when our table was ready, but they never texted us to tell us they were not going to seat us. They had our phone number but they never called to tell us they weren't going to seat us. They just left us to cool our heels walking around waiting for a table they had no intention of providing.

If you want a restaurant that will make you wait for an hour and a half for nothing, this is your place. If you want a restaurant that serves food I suggest you go somewhere else. The manager did give us a call after we had been turned away but because we were sitting in a restaurant that was actually serving food we chose not to take up his offer.

Amazed at all the negative reviews. Guys, you're not rating a 3-star Michelin restaurant expecting a mind-blowing, out of body experience. It's a ramen place, a legit ramen place. Compared to other ramen places in the city, the broth and the noodles here have a much better quality. The price is a LITTLE higher than Totto, Ippudo NYC or Sapporo (about 1-3 dollars depending on the type of ramen) so it isn't that bad. So if you're expecting something much cheaper, open a packet of instant ramen and cook one at home. 

For appetizers, the Japanese fried chicken and pork meatballs were excellent. The tofu Coney Island is more of a New York twist. You can't go wrong with the Tokyo Shio ramen with a roasted tomato add-on. I'll probably try the chicken paitan next time.

Again, it's just a ramen place - a good ramen place. So we'd better be realistic on the ratings we provide.

After watching Chef's Table, I immediately made a reservation! It was packed, so be prepared to wait if you don't have a reso. I loved the style of the place, and the ramen was truly excellent. Go with the Chicken Ramen! The broth is outstanding.
OMG,  came with my wife coz of Netflix show,  honestly it is explosively good,  heavy and hardcore flavor with friendly staff, it is perfect for me!!

After Ivan's special on Chef's Table, we immediately booked a table at Ivan Ramen.

The space itself is weird. Narrow and pretty tight/uncomfortable.

However, service was extremely friendly. Don't miss the unfiltered sake cause that milky substance was GOOD! The appetizers were excellent - the meatball was like a flare gun getting shot off in your mouth. Also delicious were the pork buns and fried chicken. But meatball was #1!

The ramen, to be honest, wasn't as memorable as the appetizers. My companions thought the triple garlic mazeman and the shio ramen were lacking a punch. However, the chicken paitan was fantastic. I was caught off guard, however, that his famous roasted tomato was served cold! Mixed reviews from this crowd.

Not for everyone. It was a good bowl of ramen no doubt, but probably not coming back anytime soon. Ordered the tonkatsu and the spicy ramen. Both were full of flavor and the noodles impeccable. Only downside would be the salt level but that's personal taste. The tofu Coney island was unique and worth a try. If I come back, will probably stick to the shoyu or maybe try out the vegetarian ramen.

Will probably have to give this place another try but first impressions are hard to break. Me and couple friends lined up before opening and were greeted by visibly unhappy staff. Maybe it was the cold, maybe they had a rough night prior, but the whole vibe was "why are you here?"   Maybe it was because we didn't have reservations... for a RAMEN place, but we were seated outside in the patio under a broken heat lamp because the working ones were for the guest who had reservations. Maybe serving the customers who are present and willing to wait out in the cold should be your priority, but I guess not. We were forgotten about about for about 10 minutes while the staff figured out "who had our table." Orders went in fine and aside and food came out at a decent pace. Staff didn't have much input on which ramen they preferred and when asked wether to choose from the spicy and tonkotsu the only advice was if you don't like spicy don't get spicy, thanks. 

Enough of the downside. The noodles were great, I finished my bowl almost immediately was satisfied. The portion wasn't large, but the quality and richness of the both will make you satisfied. I was tempted to order more noodles, but I didn't want to bother the staff, as my group were merely peons who waited and had no reservation. 

TLDR: Ramen - OK, Staff- Meh, Use open table for a reservation probably get better service

P.S. Why does a ramen shop take reservations? Huh?
Most regretful bowl of ramen ever. Tonkotsu = hypertension. Wish the kitchen staff had actual passion for ramen, could only taste salt. Hype is real.
Not quite as good as I expected after hearing the hype.  The chicken Dan Dan was pretty one dimensional.  Service was good, but food didn't justify the price.

Unique taste for ramen. Broth doesn't taste like a chicken broth or pho soup. We watched about Ivan ramen on chefs table and decided to check it out when we are in New York. And it turned out a great experience. Service was great as well. Although make a reservation few days in advance

Phenomenal Ramen in a crowded diner-like setting. 

I ordered Ivan's Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen paired with the marinated chicken. It's not ramen. The noodles are thick. They are fresh and chewy. Chewing them down is a playful exercise in umami goodness and robust noodle mouthfeel. 

The pork slice is perfectly executed, tender meat succumbs to the pressure of your lips as the fat melts on your tongue. The crisped pork belly adds a mouthfeel element, just enough salt to help flavor the dish. 

The broth is pure gold. Savory pork essence soaks deep into the fresh noodles and permeates the dish in a non-overpowering way. The dish is shockingly savory. It's deep and intense flavors envelop your whole mouth and nose. 

The sprouts on top are just light enough to not hinder the mouthfeel while adding and element of freshness to the palate. 

This is oh so good. Definitely compares to the quality and experience of eating at Tsuta's Michelin-star Ramen in Tokyo.  The flavors in this dish are slightly less subtle, complex, and respectful of the Japanese way of light ingredients.

I enjoyed my meal here...I had the Chicken Paitan Ramen and it was really good.  Rich and full of flavor (probably from the addition of the egg yolk), this was a bit more than I expected from typical chicken ramen so this was a nice surprise.  I also tried the Steamed Pork Buns, which were good.

This place is not very big, but they try to make the most out of what they have so expect a lively, loud and cozy experience.

The service was friendly and attentive.
Great food -- pork bun super tasty and chicken paitan ramen was awesome! Service could have been much better.

Japanese fried chicken was best fried chicken I've ever had and the soup was very flavorful!

Very friendly service.

After watching the episode of Chef's Table where they show Ivan's journey, we instantly made a reservation (first time I see a ramen place that takes rezzies). Unfortunately we were seated in the outdoor patio (enclosed during winter) where there was no music and vibe was not that great for a couple (maybe for groups it works better). The hostess should be more mindful about people with reservations.
Food was great, we had:
- Tofu Coney Island: as seen in the show. The miso mushroom chili and yellow mustard sauce make this dish one of my favorites (along with the Paitan)
- Steamed Pork Buns: not a fan, but bf liked it. Regular pork buns, but have to say very well executed
- Tokyo Shoyu Ramen: soy sauce, dashi with chicken broth, pork belly, soft egg, braised bamboo and rye noodles. Good but kind of on the heavier side. Bf was sleepy after this.
- Chicken Paitan Noodle: chicken broth, minced chicken, egg yolk, shio kombu and rye noodles. Comes with lime. I added roasted tomato. Umami! Umami! Deliciousness in every spoon.
Service was also remarkably good, food came pretty quick and server was super nice.
Would recommend to bring out of towners. I also find it special that they make their own noodles. I'm not a noodle expert, but thought these were perfect and lived up to expectations from the show.

The waiter was very nice and friendly so they gained another star. The appetizers were good but the ramen was salty and had a very artificial smokey taste that is still lingering about two hours later. I did find a piece of sharp plastic in my ramen and they comped my ramen but a restaurant is usually more generous with the meal or at least another round of drinks too when something like that happens. They did confirm it came from the kitchen and replaced it right away.

I really wanted to love it... I had high hopes after seeing the Chef's Table episode and decided it was a must during my visit to New York. I ordered the Tokyo Shio Ramen and added a roasted tomato. My husband ordered the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen. My ramen had so much garnish! It was too much. The ratio between noodles and garnish was 1:1. There was very little broth in my ramen and everything was luke warm at best. I bit into a tomato and it was cold. I popped an egg in my mouth and the runny yolk was cold. My husband's ramen was cold so he left most of it uneaten. 

Overall, the flavor was there but it was cold. On the plus side, the service was great and we really loved our servers. Very friendly and attentive service. I wouldn't recommend this place though after being served cold food and $60 bill.

Like many of its recent customers, I came here because of Chef's table. For starter, I ordered the Coney Island. The tofu was fried perfectly, crunchy outside and soft inside. Unfortunately, it was topped by a very ugly looking and nasty tasting topping overkilled by soy sauce :( 

Moving onto to the tonkatsu ramen, it's different from traditional soupy ramen, the one has very thick sauce. I enjoyed the ramen. The thick sauce prevents the noodles from being too soggy and it maintained its chewiness. Overall, it wasn't a bad experience, albeit too salty for my palate.

Had to check this place out after watching Chef's table. Started off with the Coney Island appetizer which I was pleasantly surprised by. The mushrooms mixed with yellow mustard on top of some fried tofu worked very well. Definitely a unique dish worth trying!

For the ramen, I ordered a shio ramen with a roasted tomato after seeing the tomato so hyped up on Chef's table. I will say the roasted tomato does completely change the flavor profile of the ramen and what you would expect. Biting into the tomato and eating the ramen reminded me of eating spaghetti bolognese, something you would never expect while eating ramen. Thankfully, the tomato doesn't spill over too much into the broth so you can still enjoy the dashi broth separately. I also enjoyed their rye noodles but I wish mine were a little less cooked. The noodles were not so much chewy as they were mushy.

Overall, I would say this place is worth checking out to get a different twist on ramen. I do appreciate the creativity of everything, which makes it hard to compare this to traditional ramen shops.

Not a big fan of chicken broth. Would prefer iPuddo any day .

Their fried chicken is good though

Ivan's Ramen did not disappoint no not at all. It's unique interpretation of ramen. I tried the Dan Dan noodles the spicy ramen and the chicken paitan. Let me tell you the stand out star was the chicken paitan. You get sucked into the flavor. The noodle stay perfect throughout, start to finish nj sogginess. The service is quick and they take reservations. The ambiance was hipster and cool. Be ready for a wait though if u don't make reservations but they have a bar and some cool spots close by. Go and enjoy!

To start off, if I could rate in between stars I would rate this a 4.3. My girlfriend and I decided to take a trip to NYC for the day from The Atlantic City area to visit Ivan Ramen and a few other spots in NYC. After seeing the Chefs Table episode on Netflix it was a must!

Disclaimer: I have never eaten ramen before besides the cheap packaged stuff but I have a great palette and a cook in my own rights so take my review as you may!

Ok so the restaurant itself was fairly cramped and the seats from what I could tell were all two tops and very close together. So it was a bit cramped but from many reviews I've seen from NYC restaurants that is the semi normal. It didn't bother us much and the couple next too us were very friendly. 

Service was very fast. We were seated right away with our reservation and our waiter had our water poured right away. The menu is rather small so it was pretty easy to make our selections. The waiter was very quick and attentive and we had our order placed within five minutes of being sat. I ordered the classic Ramen and my gf ordered the lamb Dan dan. We also got the fried chicken appetizer. The waiters kept our glasses full with water before they ever went empty.

The appetizer was good. Fresh a juicy chicken with a light crunch. The abundant sauce on it kept it from being extra crispy but it was still good. The sauce also was very sweet so I could only eat a little bit but was tasty

My Ramen was very delishes. The noodles were the star of the dish. They were perfectly cooked and had an amazing al dente type texture. The broth was an it boring at first but as the flavors seeped in and I hit the bottom of the bowl the flavor got more intense. The eggs were very tasty and a great addition. And the enoki were refreshing. I also opted for the roasted tomato a d enjoyed that also. The only down side was the pork that was in it. It was very chewy with a rubbery texture and I could have done without it. Overall it was very enjoyable and it was just the right size serving (I'm not a small guy lol) I left full and satisified.

The girlfriends Dan Dan lamb was very flavorful but it was super spicy. I love spice and so does she but it kept you going back for water over and over.

Overall we were very satisfied and would definitely recommend trying Ivan Ramen out. 4.3 out of 5

I was seriously blown away by the sophistication and depth of flavor. The noodles were perfectly cooked, which added to the enjoyment of the broth. My suggestion is order the chicken paitan if you want a pop of amazing flavor in every slurp!

I would have given it a 1 star, but it gets 2 stars because one appetizer (Daikon XO) was decent and the wait staff were all really friendly and funny. 

Being a huge ramen fan, I make it a point to try every "famous" NYC ramen spot. Like many others, after seeing the Chef's Table episode I knew I had to try. I ordered two bowls (the Tokyo Shoyu and the Triple Pork Tonkotsu) and both were abominable. The Tonkotsu was slightly better but both were sorry excuses and should not be allowed to call itself ramen. The broth was completely over-salted, there was ONE piece of pork belly and the noodles itself were pathetic.

Perhaps I ordered wrong. But my theory is, at a good restaurant there's not such thing as "ordering wrong." Ramen lovers, run away from this place like it's the plague.

Stopped in here for lunch and wasn't expecting to be blown away by chicken broth but it was absolutely delicious ramen and the broth was rich and tasty.  The atmosphere is fun and the staff is friendly. Can't really ask for more.

You definitely should have reservations if you dont like waiting. We didnt care though because we liked walking around the area. Thankfully we didnt go far because half way we received a text that they were ready to seat us. We only waited 10 mins even though she said itll be 30to40 mins. I thought it was awesome that they sat us in a quiet empty room with dim orange lights, away from everyone else in the restaurant. Why were we sat there ? I dont know because we didnt ask for it and we saw 2 empty tables with the crowd but i guess we just got lucky for our date night :). We ate at peace. Overall the ramen was pretty good i enjoyed it. I cannot remember what i ordered i just chose randomly. But i enjoyed it! Its not like the usual ramen i would eat but it was decent. I think i was more pleased then him. His ramen wasnt what he expected lol. We both did very much enjoy their pork buns a must try. The staff was super friendly so that was awesome! They made you smile and feel comfortable. Its a nice place to go to for a date.

*Ahem* I came here inspired by Chef's Table as well; call it an impulse reservation.

I ordered a bowl of the Spicy Red Chili Ramen. Now usually I'm pretty apprehensive about spicy dishes in NYC restaurants, purely because the spice level has to be noticeable enough to actually affirm its name, but also mild enough so that most people can enjoy it without consuming gallons of water. This ramen had a pretty nice kick to it, but not so much that I would actually deem it "spicy." More like "Oh this is spicier than Tabasco but only marginally so" Red Chili Ramen. It was really quite good. Noodles had a nice firmness to them, and I loved the smashed egg. I also got a roasted tomato in my ramen, just to get that "umami" flavor. Not sure if my palate can actually distinguish that quite yet, but it was a nice add-on.

There were some disappointing elements among my friend's dishes. Some were upset that they only got 1 slice of pork. They were relatively large slices though to be fair. Others also believed that their bowls were quite salty. Even so, many of us still finished the delicious broth, something that I rarely do at other restaurants; one friend claimed he had never done so before at any other ramen restaurant. 

Service was extremely friendly. The servers were willing to chat and help us out with recommendations. They also know quite well about the Chef's Table influence, but they are more than happy to help describe ramen. One woman beside us had never had ramen before, and the server took plenty of time trying to give her a full experience of the ramen world/culture. 

It's priced at the same as every other ramen place in New York, so if you like all the other spots, you should give Ivan a try just based off the man's legacy. If he can make it big in Japan, then that's all the resume one should need.

Oh, at last - a ramen joint I can make online reservations for and just a few days ahead of the intended date too! 

Pleasantly surprised to find that planning a dinner date here would be stress-free, I came here on a Friday night with my boyfriend to sample some ramen unlike the more traditional bowls touted around the city. Ivan Ramen is a small, narrow restaurant with little flair aside from the pop art that lines some of the walls. Being as small and popular as it is, service is quick but super friendly and helpful. 

We made some quick decisions and opted to start with the Fried Japanese Chicken before diving into the ramen. The garlic caramel with the chicken was rich and flavorful. Though a touch too salty for me, the shiso ranch helps off-set that. For the ramen, I went with the Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen, which the server warned the broth is more of a sauce and the dish is more like pasta. I wasn't here for another fantastic but traditional bowl of ramen, so I was fine with ordering it, and I was glad I did. The sauce was very flavorful, the cut up bits of pork mixed in added a delicious, smoky flavor to the dish, and the large amount of shredded scallion cut the saltiness of the sauce nicely. The ramen itself was also whole wheat but I honestly couldn't taste the difference.

I really enjoyed my meal here, and after overhearing the server recommend the Chicken Paintan to the table next to us, I'll probably be back to try it for myself. Ignore the hype because it seems to be a double edged sword -- the ramen here's different, and that's the whole point.

Watched an episode of Chef's Table and had to try it out with my friends. I ordered the classic shoyu which had a soy sauce base (it was a bit salty for my taste) but I loved the wholewheat noodles. I've tried many ramen shops in New York including ippudo and totto ramen but the texture of the noodles was quite distinct - it is a lot chewier and thicker. One of my friends ordered the spicy ramen (the heat didn't seem too strong) while the other got a vegetarian ramen. We also got pork buns which is definitely a good appetizer to share! (Comes with two). The wait is very long, definitely make reservations on open table beforehand otherwise you may be waiting for up to 2 hours (we went on Sunday at 12:30). The service was quite fast, as with many ramen shops, and the servers will tell give you great recommendations such as pairings or add-ons to specific ramen bowls. My interest was peaked from chefs table and overall, it was a great experience but I have to say ippudo still remains my all-time favourite.

One thing I like about Ivan Ramen is the Rye noodle. It's great that the chef brought his food culture to Japanese one and it was good. Everything else is substandard. I would not recommend it. The place is always packed tightly and it was not exactly a pleasant dining experience.

Good but not worth the price.
We took the classic shoyu ramen, noodles are great and firm, soup is good, but it's really not enough for the price. There is literally only one piece of meat, which is very frustrating as it is actually very tasty. Ramen is not supposed to be an expensive meal. Also as soon as we finished they brought us to bill as to push us out even if nobody was waiting.

Of course, came here intrigued after watching Ivan on Chef's Table. I was expecting something unexpected after watching the documentary, and wasn't disappointed.

I ordered the pork belly buns and Tokyo Shoyu Ramen. There's a generous heaping of pickled radish in the bun that brings big flavor different from the typical sweet BBQ sauce. It was unexpected. Pork itself wasn't as tasty, was a bit on the lean side. Quality is questionable.

The ramen was also very unique. The noodles were excellent. Had a nice chewiness and stood out in the bowl. I had to add roasted tomato of course after Netflix made it look so good. And it was. The broth was a very different sweet flavor but just didn't quite appeal to me. While I enjoyed having a different take on the ramen I don't think it is my favorite especially after having so much good ramen in Japan.

Service was attentive overall.

Definitely doesn't hurt to try it at least once!

Bad ramen that is not worth your time.

I went to Ivan Ramen in the mid-afternoon after the lunch rush, so no excuse for the quality of the ramen.  I was seated immediately and ordered the Shoyu ramen, which had a broth that tasted like hot, diluted soy sauce.  It was too sour and had absolutely no depth to the flavor.  The noodles were overcooked, with no chewiness to them.  They kind of just dissolved in my mouth and felt insubstantial.

Pretty disappointed as I had medium-high expectations after Chef's Table.  I think they should focus less on the decor and more on making good ramen.  Try Sapporo in midtown instead (almost no effort on decor, but solid ramen - spicy miso was great).  Or just buy a quality instant ramen and make it at home.  It will definitely taste better.

Interesting variations on ramen, and toned-down broth. 

Understandable for Ivan Orkin to do so given that NYC standards for ramen are for more dumbed-down, less-salty, less-oily ramen broths. So what we have here are thinner and seemingly-healthier versions of true Japanese ramen, presented with several variations (e.g. truffle) and a relatively steep price point (portions are pretty small given what you are paying for). Nonetheless the interesting variations and fun side dishes do warrant a repeat visit every now and then.

Be careful!!  The stair out front doesn't extend as far to the right as to where the door is.   I fell off and hurt my ankle, and I saw other people having problems with it.  It's a bad design that should be fixed!!

I watched a Netflix doc on Ivan and wanted to love this place. It was a great noodle and savory broth but it left more to be desired. It was good ramen don't get me wrong but I just wanted more from this bowl.
A little too salty for my palate. They were out of the pork meatballs. Fried chicken is really good. Place is small but intimate. I recommend making a reservation otherwise you end up at the bar

I came to lunch here today with two friends, one of which has celiac disease. She ordered tofu noodles, but they gave her regular noodles. She had to take medication to prevent a hospital visit, and has been sick most of the night. When it came time to pay the bill, not only did they make her pay for the ramen, but was even charging extra for the tofu noodles! Never again!

Had the loveliest experience here. The fried chicken starter was amazing, and as good as the ramen (which is saying a lot). I got the spicy ramen and added tomato, a must, and thought it was the perfect level of spice with a broth that was addictive. My friend got the triple garlic mazemen and said it was "superb" (although I was partial to the ramen). Moreover, the bartender was incredibly friendly and made us feel immediately welcomed (and the Tokyo tea is delicious/deadly). It's obviously on the pricy side for ramen, but worth every penny. Will be back very soon.

I discovered Ivan's Ramen on the Netflix show, Chef's Table, and I was heading to NYC a week after I watched the show, so I decided to try it out, so I did. The staff were really friendly and welcoming. I ordered the Shoyu Ramen - it was a bit too salty, but it was still delicious! Good portion for the price.

I am no ramen expert, but of the many ramens I've had in NYC, Ivan Ramen is the most memorable, though most likely not my favorite. The broth was faintly smoky, and the noodles were (as others have said) chewy - the combination of both creating a bowl that, though initially unusual, added up to a satisfying late night meal well worth the price (~$16). We started with the Coney Island Tofu that tasted exactly how it sounded, chili and mustard on tofu, paired with a sake the waiter recommended.

The atmosphere inside is buzzing with discussions about Chef's Table and conversations between eaters and the very knowledgeable staff. We made a reasonable reservation for a Friday night the night before, but it seems that walk-ins don't encounter an absurd wait, and there are plenty of things to do nearby in the meantime. 

I can't speak to authenticity, but there is a dynamic and unique combination of flavors and ingredients used in the dishes (and bowls) here that make it a hipper-than-casual, very New York spot, that deserves the growing attention.

This was a very average ramen restaurant. I got the pork buns and the Tokyo Shio ramen. It was all good, but nothing special in comparison to any other ramen I'd find in the city and definitely a bit pricer than most. One thing that stands out is the rye noodles used in most dishes.

The hostess told us to sit and order before our fifth party arrived because they were "pretty booked for the evening." Not your warmest welcome...

Nonetheless, I was with great company and we were excited to try out the Chef's Table Ivan Ramen (actually Ivan Orkin sat at the table behind us). I had the vegetarian ramen which was loaded with enoki, roasted tomato, and tofu. I'm Japanese, and you definitely don't add tomatoes into ramen (a native would have been appalled) but I get it, you're trying to change things up a bit. 

The broth was a bit salty, though lacked strong flavor. To be honest though, it's hard to get that delicious ramen flavor out of a vegetarian broth. The noodles were delicious, thin and not too chewy. Honestly, I downed my dinner. It wasn't the best, but it certainly was not bad! 
The three is for the service and the food (average).  I would dine here again, but there are several other ramen shops to try!

The pork buns were delicious and had a topping that was like an Asian take on sauerkraut. Instead of cabbage, it was shredded daikon. I also got the chicken paitan which was fantastic. It came with a raw egg on top and half a fresh lime that you squeeze in. The chicken wasn't shredded but instead ground which worked for me. Very rich and delicious with the egg thickening the broth. I preferred the chicken paitan over the one spoonful of triple pork triple garlic that my friend ordered but both were very good.

The chicken ramen w raw egg was awesome!  The other two we got (shoyu and some other kind) were ok. 

The karaage with shiso ranch was very tasty too!  Great staff, ... we had reservations for a Tue night at 9pm. 

My friend saw the place on Chef's Table. So it's pretty popular for people now. I'd imagine there's a lot of tourists like myself along w natives.

Ivan Ramen.

Loved the decor. Disliked the cultural appropriation. White person (Ivan!) tryna make ramen. It's not bad no it's not, but whatever.

One of the interesting things I was told before heading there was the roasted tomatoes. My australian friend got it so instead of roasted tomatoes we had roasted to'ma'toes. Idk why this was the special thing (maybe cuz no one has tried it) but end of the day it didn't compliment the ramen THAT well....

Also we waited for like 1.5 hours for this spot on a Friday night, but you can go next door to the boba guys to get some boba while waiting.

I've been to this place once before and it didn't make a deep impression on me. However, I saw the documentary on Netflix and decided to give this place another try. And I have to say, I'm a little disappointed...

I went on a Friday night, around 8pm, and had to wait around 1.5 hrs for a table, which is normal for NYC restaurant so I didn't mind it. (There are also many good bars nearby) 

For appetizer, we ordered the Coney Island tofu and the fried chicken. The tofu was really creative and I really feel like I'm eating a hotdog. The fried chicken batter was slightly soggy probably due to the dressing. Both dishes have good flavor, but both are over-SALTED. (I enjoy salty food, and rarely do I find something too salty)

For ramen, we had the classic shio and the triple pork triple garlic. The flavors are good, the Umami is there, but the noodle is way too SOFT and the soup is just WARM... it makes me feel like the bowls were probably sitting out for a long time before it get delivered. 

Overall, if you want to succeed in NYC. You need consistency on your food, especially when you are busy. Even with good flavor, the combination of warm soup and soggy noodle make me not want to recommend this restaurant for ramen fans out there.

Tips:
- roasted tomato is a side order, it doesn't come with the ramen
- small place, just one restroom

I am unsophisticated when it comes to ramen and to be honest, I can barely tell the difference between one bowl or another. But Ivan Ramen is pushing the envelope on flavors and ingredients. I'd say this place is a must-try if you're a ramen lover.

The trumpet mushroom noodles were amazing! If you have a friend that's on a gluten free diet, they will fall in love with these. The texture of the mushrooms is indeed noodley. Why are we eating spaghetti squash and cauliflower rice when we can have mushroom noodles?! The chili oil paired with the cold noodles is spectacular. I'd come back just for this.

The Tokyo Shoyu Ramen is incredibly flavorful. The broth is divinely heavy with oil and chicken flavors. I also liked that the noodles for this dish were on the thinner side.

I was underwhelmed by the mazemen and the pork buns.

Service was fast and the staff was patient and friendly. They've got a tiny outdoor space, so don't let summer deter you from slurping down these delicious noodz.

It's funny: the two big noodle shops that have gained notoriety in the City get mediocre reviews. As I slurped up my delicious bowl of Chili Noodles, I realized that it really comes down to where you like to eat. Ramen is Ramen: it's all somewhat the same, sort of different, and unless you really mess it up, it's still a good bowl of noodles and broth. 

Although a longtime fan of ramen, I'm in the "Netflix Camp" and Ivan does a great noodle bowl. They switch it up enough to try out new ideas, they're no longer "hole-in-the-wall" status which I think the foodie/hipsters don't really like but yikes, it's still a solid bowl of goodness. 

Stoked: Great space, swap-able ingredients (for us VegHeads) and the rye noodles are on point! Staff was friendly and super accommodating. 

Bummed: A little pricey, but at least the bowls are huge! 

Tip: Unless you're ravenously hungry or love taking a box home, you could easily split a starter and a bowl...

Wow! I'm forever ruined and will not be able to have ramen anywhere else. The shoyu broth was incredibly flavorful. The noodles are perfection: just the right amount of chew and great flavor. The other toppings were just perfection. I'm anxiously waiting to come back and slurp some more.

I tried not to have high expectations for the infamous Ivan ramen but it still failed me. 

Got spicy ramen. 

The good: flavors, presentation, cooking time.

The bad: the broth was almost non-existent, making the dish mostly consist of noodles. 

The ugly: let's talk spicy. I'm not a stranger to heat, having enjoyed hot dishes in Mala project or xian famous foods. This ramen was borderline inedible due to all the burn. I'm not sure if they accidentally overdid it with chili paste but it spoiled the entire experience.

On the plus side, fried chicken appetizer was delicious and perfectly executed.

Like some I learned about Ivan ramen via the new season of chefs table. I was disappointed to say that my bowl of ramen was below average. I added the roasted tomato which was a house special and found it enjoyable but nothing crazy. The broth was bland and smelled a little too fishy for my liking, the noodles were good and had a nice chewy texture and our server was extremely friendly. Cool spot and decor but the food wasn't great sadly and have had much better ramen elsewhere in city.
Awesome Ramen! My roommate and I both had the vegetarian option and added the egg to it. Very flavorful broth--great choice!

I watched an episode of Chef's table and this restaurant was on it, so I thought it would be fun to go.  I made a reservation and went by myself because I was traveling for work.  

I had a 12:30pm reservation on Saturday.  I thought it would have been more crowded but surprisingly it wasn't as bad as I thought.  The place filled up quickly after they opened.  

The staff was really nice, friendly, and helpful.  I asked for their recommendation and they said their favorite was a chicken dish, which I got with a side of pork belly.  This was hands down the best ramen and pork belly I have ever had! I was extremely impressed, the flavors of the ramen broth were so good.  

I will definitely be going back.  

If you go, I highly suggest making a reservation.

This was a really lackluster experience that left me disappointed. I had the Chicken Paitan ramen which was very salty despite the fact that they provided lime to go with it. It is definitely unique for sure but not delicious. Our group also had pork buns each and it was nothing to rave about. It wasn't horrible. Lastly I had taken some lamb Dandan noodle to go and ate it around midnight when I got home - it was spicy enough for my taste but bland. There was no waiting area and a lot of people were just crowded by the door - where our table was.

Been wanting to try Ivan Ramen ever since I watched it on Chefs Table. Went here after making reservations, nice cozy place with friendly staff and artistic interior. 

I ordered the Spicy red chili Ramen while my Husband got the Chicken Paitan. He is not a big fan of Ramen but he enjoyed it too. As for me, I've always been crazy about Ramen and I just fell in love. It was the most delicious and flavorful bowl of Ramen I've ever had - also the most expensive.

I had really high expectations for this place given all the fanfare and the episode of Chef's Table on Netflix about the legendary Long Island turned Tokyo Ramen legend, Ivan Orkin. I felt, however, that when it came down to it the ramen was sorely lacking.

Ambiance: very loud, very bustling, fairly cramped. The space is narrow with mostly white decor inside. I was seated in the enclosed patio which was too cold, too dark, and  the chairs were too wide for the table such that you could not scoot in at all.

Service: The service was okay but nothing too special. The server seemed a bit distracted or aloof, but he was friendly and our orders were correct and were served reasonably quickly.

Food: I started off with the pickles which were quite good with the perfect amount of kick. I also had the pork bun with pickled radish in which the pork seemed uninspired and underseasoned. The radish was nice and provided a twist on the classic, but, at the end of the day it could not compensate for lackluster pork.

The ramen was playful and had a vision but fell short in flavor, texture, and just in general. I went with the classic shio ramen which is a more delicate dashi-based broth seasoned with sea salt. To start, the bowl was MAYBE lukewarm if not "cool" in temperature. As the shio broth is more delicate in its nature it can take on the characteristics of what goes into the broth, which was generally insipid or couldn't have its flavors extracted because the broth itself was cold. The famous rye-based noodles had the consistency of overcooked instant ramen noodles without any texture whatsoever. The pork belly was almost entirely congealed gristle, again without any notable seasoning. The enoki mushrooms, as opposed to the typical kirkurage mushrooms are more subtle in flavor, they also were not separated from each other which made them very difficult to eat with the other ingredients. The seaweed was abundant to the point of being overpowering as well. The only saving grace, if it could be called that, was the soft boiled egg, which was perfectly cooked. I did not care to finish the broth after I had finished my noodles.

Overall: Not worth the hype given to it from the Netflix special. The ramen is pricey at $16 a bowl and frankly I'd rather have a hot bowl of instant ramen and save $15.50. Somewhat embarrassing culinary display. I will not return and actively discourage others from attending.
Okay ramen.  Too Salty unfortunately for me.  But good was tasty..  enjoyed the pickles.

Ok food, WORST SERVICE...I'll never go back because of the bad service. So rude, uninformative, attitudes which is a bummer because we had heard such good things, only to be very disappointed. Food isn't good enough for the bad service, plenty of other ramen places in NY I'd rather spend my money. Very fishy and when I asked the server to describe the flavors he just replied "ramen flavors" with an attitude.

Service: 5 stars.
The servers are always very friendly and kind, but never intrusive.  They tell you if they think you're ordering too much food, which I really appreciate, and they always make you feel good about your order, no matter how strange the request (we ordered 3 pork buns though an order comes with 2, and we ordered 4 ramen: 3 for stay and 1 to go with lots of extra add-ons).  

Food: 5 stars.
I've had the shoyu ramen, the shio ramen, the spicy red chili ramen, and the chicken paitan.  All are phenomenal.  We loved the food so much we went twice in one weekend.  In fact, we went to a ramen competition in Midtown and tried some of the best ramen from New Jersey to Boston to Japan to Cambodia, and Ivan's beats them all.  Huge fan.

Wow!!!!! This place is freakin awesome!!The hole-in-the-walk ramen joint knows how to make some good food!! The Japanese fried chicken pork meatballs were the bomb and don't get me started on the ramen!!!! We saw this guy on chefs table and said we had to go. No wonder this guy had the best ramen IN ALL OF JAPAN! That's crazy!!! The handmade noodles go so well with the rich broths made every day all day and dashi (a Japanese fish broth) and the expertly crafted toppings. I recommend the Tokyo shio ramen, triple pork triple garlic mazemen, and basically everything else. Got a shirt and a book! Can't get enough of this place!! Want to live here!!!!!!!!!!!

Overrated! There was a long line when we came here, we had a reservation so we didn't have to wait, but felt rushed because of the line. They handed our check before we finished. Anyway, aside from that, the food was nothing special -
pork buns tasted raw - and the ramen was overly salty!! Not sure what the hype is about. Definitely not going back.

The ramen is good. I ordered the Tokyo Shio Ramen, and the noodles were soft, and the mushrooms and pork belly tasted good.

The service is great. We made a reservation a week and a half before, then asked if we could add another person the morning of, and the staff were very kind and accommodating. We were able to add another person given we had to get a table an hour and 15 minutes later, but we were fine with that. The service was great, except when one of the waiters threw the napkins on our table in a rush, which came off rude.

I'm not sure if the wait and making an early reservation are worth the hype though. I would maybe go again, but it's not on the top of my list.

We had a great, fun, tasty dinner here back in December! We made reservations and got in right away on a busy Saturday night. The hostess was very nice. We chose to sit at the bar so we could see all the action. The bar was a little tight... intimate, maybe? And with with winter coats, it took a few minutes to feel settled. But once there and talking to the girl behind the counter, we felt great! My husband and I order d the pork steam buns and loved them. We each ordered different bowls, mine was the heartier one described more as a chicken noodle soup base. Both were delicious!! We left satisfied and will definitely be back!

I give it 3 stars because its a cute place.

I asked the waitress if they had any cold noodle dish, I just recall seeing a picture of a cold noodle dish before but didn't see it on the menu so I thought I ask. She gave me a nasty face as if I was asking for pork at a vegan place. I asked her what she recommend and she said the chicken paitan is a staff favorite, therefore, that's what I ordered because I told her I like a tasty broth. 
Chicken Paitan- Super rich broth= fat isn't skimmed. There was a lot of oil. A good 1/3 cm sat at the top. Also the broth was super salty. too salty for my liking, and i'm the type to like flavorful dish. I really really wanted to like this place but for $17, it is a bit pricey for the portion we get.....
Tried the chicken paitan. It was so-so and a bit too salty. The queue was amazing (approximately 30-45mins). Friendly staffs!!!

Our Order
1) Pork Buns- 7/10
2) Japanese Fried Chicken- 8/10 (only because it tasted like cashew nut chicken)

The ramen we had was really heavy and didn't match up to our expectations.

Dont know what the fuss is  all about. We didn't like our experience last week. Been trying to convinced my husband to go and finally he said yes as he was hesitant  in the beginning. We been to so many ramen ya and this one was a disappointment.   Here is what we ordered. 

Meatballs : fillers.  It has taste but texture was so soft like it have so much fillers. Not worth the $10

Pork buns: was tasty and big but so much fat that my husband had to pick them out in result bun got smaller.  Unebible pork meat. 

Tonkotsu ramen  (husbsnd ) broth was so salty. He was totally turned off. Definitely not worth $18

Shoyu ramen: so so salty.  I had asked if I they can make it less salty but our waiter shoyu ramen is usually on the  salty side. But i ordered it anyways I gave it a try. What a mistake. This broth sent my blood pressures to another notch. Not worth $16. 

On the positive part. Service was understanding.  Our waiter Marvin was so helpful, knowledgeable and professional in what he does. He came back to ask me if my ramen was salty and he tried his best to correct it.  I really appreciate him for his professionalism. I would go back to say hi to him. As food, will not go back.  For the price I would go to Momofuko, Mu Ramen.

Before Nakamaru showed up, there wasn't really a better ramen choice in the area. I probably would have given a bare 4 otherwise.

One time I had the Shoyu Ramen + enoki/Kaedama. I had the triple pork triple garlic mazeman the other time. Both meals were a little pricy, especially for ramen. I find the noodles to be a bit different in a good way though the Shoyu broth was nothing  special.

They have a very interesting drink selection. 3.3
Meets up to expectations, nice staff, good food, perfect proportions -  get a reservation

Far and away the most amazing Ramen experience of my life. I've never been to Japan, so I won't speak to authenticity, but this was an umami experience like no other. 

Went around 6pm on a Friday, and it wasn't too busy yet. Wait staff were pleasant and friendly, and guided us through the menu. Started with pork buns, which were fantastic. Only got better from there when the Japanese fried chicken came out. Perfect blend of heat, spice, salt and umami. We got the Shio and Shoyu bowls. Added the roasted tomato "umami bombs" as per our waiters suggestion. BEST LIFE CHOICE EVER. 

Those tomatoes were worth the trip alone. Biting into them and getting that bomb-blast of flavor is something akin to a religious experience. 

The broth in both the Shio and Shoyu were unique and satisfying on the deepest levels. 

Five star reviews are so easy to write. It's so easy to "love it"; it's so easy to say "everything was amazing" and "I'll be going back for sure."  But please. Please! Do yourself a favor and experience this place at least once. 11 Madison Park may be "The Best Restaurant in the World"  but Ivan Ramen may be the most satisfying. Enjoy every bite, and tell all your friends!

EXCELLENT! Got the chicken paitan and spicy red chili ramen.  Both are delicious!  Couldn't decide on favorite.  One is rich and ohhh sooo flavorful while the over delivers the spice kick if you're craving it.  We also got the meatball starter - which was amazing. A perfect marriage of flavors.  I could eat those morning noon night.

In NYC to visit my sis for the first time in 10 years and just HAD to experience Ivan Ramen. My BF and I have watched his amazing story on Chef's Table twice now and the meal was unbelievable. We had probably the best saki I've ever tasted, beer and started with the fried chicken. It was incredibly well balanced and delicious. Then we had the ramen. Wow!! SO good! On top of it all our waiter was fantastic. Such a great dinner. Thank you, Ivan!!

This review is only for the triple pork triple garlic mazemen - full of umami with every bite. I was particularly impressed with the unique noodles. 

Definitely not your typical ramen with bits of crunchy bacon, a small amount of super-concentrated sauce-like pork broth, and slightly chewy whole wheat noodles. 

We added the roasted tomato (curiosity piqued by the Chef's Table episode), which added a juicy and fresh savory taste to the meal. 

Service was quick and attentive. 

My one suggestion is to add one more piece of pork belly to the dish - the meat portion was small compared to other high end ramen joints like Mu and Ippudo. 

Definitely make reservations a week out as this place has exploded after being featured on Chef's Table! Even on weeknights.

We tried the vegetarian ramen and Tokyo Shoyu ramen but weren't fans of either. Perhaps it's just personal preference, but the combination of the strongly flavored rye noodles with the broth just didn't work for us.

The staff was very friendly and the service was good. Unfortunately the ramen was too westernized and salty for me. The chicken patian is much better and more authentic at TOTO ramen and the seasame ramen looked like noodles on curry sauce (even though it wasn't curry). It was just a bit off for me. I'm sure the food is great for many people but I guess I will stick with traditional ramen for now. Also ramen for two with side and a beer was ~$70.

Glad I tried it though!

Ivan Ramen had been on my list of Ramen places to hit for quite some time. After watching Ivan's Chef's Table episode, I knew I had to pop in as soon as I could. A friend of mine and I came in on a Thursday evening. We were seated at the bar and ordered some drinks and pork buns. The drink was an average cocktail, nothing special. The pork buns; however, were some of the best I've had. Now to the noodles...I ordered the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen. It was a pretty standard soy-sauce based broth, but I just didn't love the taste. It was salty and felt almost heavy going down. 

Ambiance is cool. It's a small spot, but they take reservations. The bar was a nice place to sit, because you can see the kitchen at work. It's noisy, but you can still have a conversation with your table. Service is really nice. They like to move things along, but they're all great. Our waitress even made some good recommendations for us.

Overall, I just didn't love the food. Wasn't the worst Ramen I've had, but Ippudo and Totto still take the bill for me.
This is the best Ramen I've had in NYC. I can't wait to go back again! So worth the wait and the noodles are really good. The atmosphere is great and the service was fast and friendly.

After watching the special on Netflix I knew I had to make a reservation here to try out Ivan's specialty Rye Noodles. This is probably one of the few ramen shops which allow for reservations to be made online which made the experience a lot better. My reservation was for 6pm on a Friday, the restaurant wasn't full by the time I got there but when I left around 7 there were probably only two tables left so I would recommend making a reservation in advance if you can.

For Food:
- Steamed Pork Buns - 4/5 - Not the best pork buns I've ever had but definitely up there. Their use of pickled daikon is different than the traditional lettuce/ mayo combination.
- Spicy Red Chili Ramen - 4/5 - The use of rye noodles is definitely different from your traditional ramen noodle. My only complaint was that the broth was a little too salty for my taste. This bowl definitely has some heat so don't get it if you don't like spicy.

Service was great- they would refill my water glass every time it got to half full. All in all I had a positive experience here and would return if I'm in the area
Food. Good. Makes you want to have sex after. Just kidding but just in case you're reading this, you should still go. Even if you don't want sex afterwards. Enjoy every drop of it. Thank you.

Sweet.  Tragic.   Inspiring.  Redeeming.

In all, the story is endearing...and covered beautifully during season 3 of Chefs Table.  Ivan, a white Jewish guy from NY, with a fascination from afar with Japan.  When taking his first post-college vacation there, he felt at home.  On a follow-up trip, he fell in love, got married quickly, had a little boy, and lost his young wife to a fatal medical problem.   Struggling to find his way, he met another Japanese woman years later, established his own little Ramen shop in Japan (where 80,000 exist), and quickly because a sensation, gaining Ramen "Chef of the Year" honors, and later, "top 10" ramen restaurants in Japan. 

Pretty cool, indeed.

A few years ago, he with his family moved back to NY.  He wanted to establish another ramen shop, with some of his renown recipes along with some new ones -- wanting to reinvent himself, slightly anyway.

With a trip to NY for business, I was thrilled at the chance to eat at Ivan Ramen.  Unfortunately, Ivan was off the night I was there.  Still, I imagine, it was fun, creative, colorful, Japanese-fusion.  My dining partner, George, and I, ordered away and a little too much...if that's at all possible.

1.  Summer Snow Sake [$57, 3.5 stars] -- unfiltered and cold (my fav), but a little more than average for the price, which is totally unnecessary.  After all, one just needs a cold beer with ramen, and they carry a few beers, I got Orion [$6, 4.5 stars].

2.  Japanese Fried Chicken [$13, 5.0 stars] with Kyurri Pickles [$5, 5.0 stars] -- recommended by our counter server, Zachary, it was a perfect pairing.  Wonderful flavor, and crunch.

3.  Meatballs [$10, 5.0 stars] -- deep fried meatballs (already good right there) with a creamy sauce and bonito flakes.  They had the right amount of crunch, softness, and flavor.

4.  Triple Pork Mazemen [$16, 4.0 stars] -- with tonkotsu broth, pork belly two different ways, and whole wheat noodles.  Perhaps a little more marketing than anything, I love Pork Belly...and it was a little light.

5.  Chicken Paitan [$17, 4.5 stars] -- the chicken fat broth is a winner, and highlight of this delicious bowl.  Quite plain, otherwise, with a loose egg, fried onions, and green onions...but phenomenal bites.  I loved the housemade rye noodles.

Zachary made it fun with his casual, confident, and knowledgable style.  All in all, it was an absolute blast of a time.  Loved it, and will have to go back sometime on another visit to meet up with Ivan in-person.

Ivan Ramen unfortunately did not live up to the hype for me. I've heard about this place since before I moved to NYC 8 months ago and decided i had to try it after watching an episode about it on Chef's Table Season 3.

I came here on a weekday night with a friend and sat at the bar area right in front of the kitchen and the cartoon illustrations above it. Loved the cool vibes here, it's hip but casual. We ordered the Japanese Fried Chicken to start. This dish was definitely not what I expected. I could definitely taste the garlic and togarashi, which is a seven-spice ingredient commonly used in cooking. The fried chicken definitely had a lot of flavor to it - it was salty, sour and sweet at the same time, which was interesting but I'm not sure if I was a big fan of it. The shiso ranch was nice too but I felt like there was too much going on when I ate it with the chicken.

For our ramens, I got the Chicken Paitan and my friend got the Spicy Red Chili Ramen. We both added pork belly to our ramen. In terms of the broth, I felt that it was flavorful but on the oilier side. The pork belly didn't melt in my mouth but it was delicious and perfectly seared. My favorite part of the ramen was the rye noodles. Loved the flavor, texture and its originality. It definitely added another dimension to the flavor of the broth. I only wished the ramen was a little thicker as I usually prefer to have thicker and firmer noodles go with thicker or heavier broths. I also tried a little bit of my friend's Spicy Red Chili Ramen. It was good but it didn't blow me away. The chicken flavor in the broth wasn't as strong as the Chicken Paitan but the rye noodles worked well with the broth. 

Through the food and restaurant vibes, I can feel the creative and adventurous side of Ivan's personality. The ramens were definitely unique and flavorful. I can even taste what he means by Umami. I struggled with whether to give this place 3 or 4 stars but sadly I don't think my experience here changed how I like my ramen.
Really small portions. Noodles and broth is way overhyped. I guess when you get a feature on Netflix people will praise anything. $16 for a bowl of ramen here is really insulting.

Probably one of my least favorite ramen joints. I didn't like that all the noodles were either wheat or rye, neither of which I enjoyed. 

The ramen overall was eh. I'll definitely stick to my favorites. We were all pretty disappointed walking out of there.

While I appreciate unique ramen, this place fell short of the flavor and quality broth that is a must for ramen. Both dishes were overly fishy and leaves much to be desired. The service is friendly but it's not worth the wait or the price.
Food was way below average, lacked flavor (forget about any umami sensation) and worst of all, the ingredients were definitely not fresh.

Like everybody else, came here after watching the episode on Ivan Ramen on Chef's Table. 

We got the Tokyo Shio and Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen. The former was disappointing; the broth was somewhat bland, the enoki not cooked enough, and the ramen eggs, while a nice consistency, didn't have much flavor. You could get comparable or better ramen at just about any ramen-ya in Japan for half the price. The latter, on the other hand, was worthwhile. The broth, garlic topping, and pork were all very flavorful. I personally really enjoyed the springiness of the noodles in both, including the rather quirky rye noodles in the shio, but wish they gave more than one slice of chashu.

The fact that they were able to temper down the sweetness of the yuzu lemonade (it had a very pleasant tang), combined with the friendliness of the service, pushes Ivan over to 4 stars for me. If I come back, I'll pass on the classic ramen and try the more unique items, since that seems to be where their strengths lie.

For all the hype built around the chefs table episode, I expected this place to provide top quality ramen. I left a bit disappointed. 

Walked in and quickly realized I didn't need to have made a reservation. Pleeenty of tables available. We sat in the semi outdoor space in the back.

To start we had the pork buns and the Japanese fried chicken appetizers. Buns were juicy inside but the bun itself was a bit dry. 

The chicken was one of the best things we ate. Well seasoned, crispy, delicious! Recommend this dish for sure. 

I had the chicken paitan ramen. This dish was tasty, but it wasn't the flavor bomb I was expecting. Beyond this, the presentation also didn't wow me. Something you expect when you pay a little extra for Ramen. Friends had the triple pork/triple garlic. Again, tasty, but nothing out of the ordinary and no special presentation at all. 

If I had come here with no expectations, I would probably have given this place 4 stars. But because of the hype and the price, it falls short. In essence, you can get better Ramen at Ippudo's or Mr Taka Ramen for a better price. Sad truth!
