Like most people, I came here after watching the episode on Chefs Table. I initially ordered the Tsukemen which had this very flavorful Anchovy dipping broth, very similar to Nagi in Golden Gai Tokyo, but less strong which I assume it's to please the American palette. After finishing the ramen, I felt I had enough room for another bowl so I ordered the Chicken Paitan. The broth was very rich and flavorful, just like how ramen broth should be. It came with a lime, which I don't recommend squeezing into the broth unless it is too rich for you. I would definitely come back here again. For me this place served some really delicious ramen, but nothing mind blowing.

Came here with my boyfriend after seeing the Chef's Table episode on Netflix. 

By far the best ramen I've ever had, but I haven't tried that many places. We got the Japanese fried chicken which came with buttermilk ranch dipping sauce, kyuri pickles, and my boyfriend and I both tried the Tokyo Shio ramen with roasted tomato. The fried chicken was amazing - slightly spicy, perfectly juicy and crispy. I've never had Japanese fried chicken before, but I'm never going back to Kentucky fried (not that I had it much before but still). The pickles were light, flavorful with the fresh dill, and zesty. Our waiter recommended we save them for the fried chicken and it did not disappoint. The Ramen was delicious - but the most exciting part was the roasted tomato! It is what they're known for, and I normally don't enjoy tomatoes but was pleasantly surprised by how smoothly and fluidly it added to the broth in flavor and texture. I can't wait to go back and try something new!

I came with two others on a Thursday night. It was fairly empty when we came at 6, but pretty packed by the time we left. I had the chicken paitan, as well as my friend who is a regular, and my boyfriend got the tsukemen and chicken paitan. Because my friend comes a lot, the chef gave us a daikon appetizer on the house, which was very good. The ramen was fine - normal portions, soup taste, abd noodle texture. But the quality, portion, and fillings were definitely not worth $16. Also, $3 for a topping of tomatoes or bok choy is very steep. Probably won't be back.

3.5 Stars

Good but not great. I really wanted to be blown away by this place after seeing it on Chef's Table and I don't mind paying 16 dollars for an amazing bowl of ramen but portions were a bit small. Ramen is comfort food and I want a huge bowl with a Flinstones size hunk of meat. I ordered the Tokyo Shio Ramen with roasted tomato and my bowl was petite. I had a hard time finding the pork belly piece it was so small. The egg was stellar and super flavorful from the broth and the mushrooms were a lovely texture too. The rye noodles were flavorful and cooked to perfection. Broth was a bit too salty for my taste and made it hard to make out any other flavors. 

My husband and his friend both ordered the Shoyu Tonkotsu Tsukemen and they both liked the wheat noodles but complained they were still hungry afterwards. We had the pork buns as an appetizer and they were good but forgettable. In retrospect we should have gotten a few more appetizers but I really thought the Ramen would be enough.

Service was very good and friendly especially considering the amount of hype they have gotten recently. I got a sake cocktail and it tasted a bit watered down. My fault, I probably should have just gotten some straight sake.

It's evident that they use great quality ingredient but c'mon just give me a little more broth and noodles. I might give this place another shot but I won't go out of my way.

The ramen was great, especially after a few drinks! But the real star was the pork buns. These were the best I've ever tasted. The meat was unbelievably soft! I got the triple pork triple garlic mazeman and it was very tasty. Yes, it's not a traditional soupy Ramen and was salty but not overly so. The waiter let me know that it didn't have much soup when I ordered too. We will be back!
Delicious. Worth a hike to the LES. Great noodles, inventive dishes. There's a lot of so-so ramen in this city. This place rises way above.

The Japanese fried chicken with kyuri pickles was the highlight of the evening. We also really enjoyed the triple pork triple garlic mazemen. The sauce was rich and luscious. Very flavorful! The spicy red chile ramen was good, but it was heavy and intensely spicy... probably would have enjoyed it more if we hadn't indulged in the starters.

Ivan's story is quite amazing and like many others, I was drawn here by it.  

I've always loved tonkotsu ramen, but as I got older, the super fatty broths are falling out of favor. When I saw his shio ramen, I was intrigued.  Since shio ramen is usually bland or just salty.  I was interested to try something different with a broth I never cared for.

My wife and I came down about 2:00pm.  Lower East Side has a lot of eating areas and Ivan's Ramen was crowded at a relatively late hour.  It was going to be a 45 minute wait, but we were able to be seated in 10 minutes since we were able to eat at the bar.  

I ordered the shio ramen with roasted tomatoes.  My wife ordered the chicken paitan ramen.  The shio ramen has a chicken and fish broth taste.  The chicken paitan was very rich and a little on the salty side, but not overly salty, just saltier than the shio.  The noodles were very good.  I did love the custom noodles, which were nice and chewy.

Ivan's Ramen is pretty special and it's a place I'd love to visit again.

Amazing ramen. Different choices available. Chilli red ramen great for those that need their spice fix.
Great service that keeps you wanting to stay and order more.
Make sure to make a reservation to avoid disappointment.

Well,I don't really write reviews on Yelp.But I wanted to tell you this is the place you GOTTA try at least once and see how you'll like here or not.Im from SF bay and there's so many good Japanese ramen places out there.I would give them 4.5 stars.We tried chicken paitan and spice chili.They both were good.But chicken paitan would be my favorite.We would comeback if we visit NYC again.
And one more thing!!Don't let yelp review fool you guys.I tried a few places had super good reviews.Some of them were disappointing

This was not a place we planned to go, it was a "we're hungry, let's try this place" kind of situation. 

Sometimes this results in a pleasant surprise. Unfortunately this was not one of them. 

This is my first ramen place in the US and I have to say I'm disappointed. The pork was more like a slab of fat, the enoki mushroom looked like it was raw and I had to submerge it into the soup to cook it. The soup was also less than inspiring. 

This place is a skip.
The food was good.  The service was impeccable. A bit loud and hard to hold a conversation. Wine and beer, but didn't see a hard liquor menu. Prices seems reasonable.

Ivan Ramen was a 3.5 for me. There's always a crowd (even when I went there at 4pm) because it's a popular place, and so I had high expectations going in. The ramen turned out to be pretty good - in fact, above average - but not deserving of the hype around it (or the wait, either). I'd drop by again if there's no line, but I wouldn't wait an hour to try it out. I'd recommend Ippudu or Nakamura instead.

Pros: Cool decor. Geared towards a younger crowd. Service was great, making sure we had water and food, but not overbearing. Mazeman was good, pork belly was tender, just the right amount of sauce (too thick to be broth at this point). The chicken wings were fantastic (although I prefer bone in, not boneless like they served). Food comes out pretty quick and in a reasonable order.

Cons: It was pretty dark in the middle of the place. We were seated at the running along the wall, high traffic area. The Tokyo Shio ramen had an "instant" texture to the noodles, I prefer not that but if that's what Ivan was going for then he hit it on the nail.

Other: This place definitely gets packed, reservations are not a bad idea.

Final thought: I'll be back to try the other ramens.

I came to this place after watching their featured episode on Netflix (Chef's Table). the chef has a really interesting back story and made me want to come and try. while the chef's story was great, the ramen left a bit more to be desired for. Compared to some of the other ramens I've had like Totto, this does not really stack up as well. my group got both the ramen and another dry noodle dish. the noodles tasted more like chinese noodles than ramen. while it was still good, it just wasn't the ramen I was expecting. Also, the pork in my pork ramen was nowhere near as good and as fatty as the pork I got at Totto. It is definitely worth a try if you are in the area, but if you are looking for the best ramen in NYC, I would look elsewhere.

Don't listen to the negative reviews unless they have been to Japan. Hyped up? Yes. Great ramen? Yes. Either way it doesn't matter, he won best amateur ramen shop in JAPAN his first year there and you can taste it. Some people expect a "flavor bomb" no, that's the msg you've been used to in American ramen. Shhhh, just try it yourself.

TRIPLE PORK TRIPLE GARLIC. You need to try it.....definitely one of my favorite ramen I've ever had. The atmosphere is cool and the staff is nice. It's definitely worth the trip there. You can even stop at boba guys next door for dessert after you finish

I visited Ivan Ramen with a large party of eight during the winter months. The decor of the restaurant was amazing and made me feel like I was being transported to Tokyo. I appreciated the heated enclosed outdoor seating (wooden cabin - hard to describe), which was surprisingly warm as we were surrounded in the bright red lights of the heating lamps. We all felt very comfortable. 

The vegetarian ramen was filling, wholesome, and contained many complex flavors. I had a hard time communicating with my friends, because I was so focused on finishing my bowl of noodles. I think I entered a possibly hypnotic trance, went to a different planet, and came back to Earth only when I finished slurping the last bits of soup and eating a few of the remaining enoki mushrooms at the bottom of the bowl. Overall, I was very happy with my first ramen experience and look forward to going back in the future.
Good ramen, but quite expensive for what you get. For ramen + beer, total came out to around $30--a bit on the pricey side for a ramen spot. Service was good.

The ramen as good but really a little too rich for my taste. My friend and I ordered the Classic Shoyu and Spicy. But still very tasty. The sleeper hit at our table was the Endive with hazelnuts. Would go again.

i had really high hopes for ivan ramen! have been following the man on instagram for years and have seen his chef's table episodes a few times, lol.  was super excited to have a day off in nyc and roam around, and to try his noodles!  this place opens on the later side - i got there at noon thinking it would be prime time for noods, but it doesnt open til 12:30. good thing the laboratorio de gelato is right down the street - so i sampled a couple flavors there - dessert before lunch? SURE!

by the time i came back to ivan, there were already 6-8 people lined up waiting for it to open. such hype!  i sat at the counter and excitedly perused the menu of delicious options. started with a refreshing beverage (forget which one, but definitely nyc priced).  for appetizer i got the tokyo fried chicken - because, duh - the serving size for this was HUGE - and my waiter was SUPER surprised that i finished every last bite.  apparently they had not seen this before. hmmmmm. this dish was pretty good - 4 stars - a little on the salty side but great value.

i got the spicy chili ramen and added a marinated soft egg in addition to the smashed egg that came with the bowl.  the smashed egg was actually pretty tasty and i probably didnt need the extra protein/cholestrol, but im not complaining cuz...how ramen chefs make marinated eggs is also pretty key. i thought it was a good bowl, but probably doesnt warrant coming back to the restaurant by itself.  the rye noodles are very interesting - thin, but chewy enough! im happy to revisit with more people so we can try all of the cold/hot appetizers, and the tokyo shio which is the chef's signature.  

service is energetic and attentive and very friendly. restaurant decor is pretty awesome, spunky and cute.  overall not a bad experience.

One of the best eating experiences you can get in lower manhattan. Pricey but worth it if you're feeling a little bougie-- hey come on: you deserve it, you're doing great! My favorite thing there is the cold sesame noodles but try the traditional ramen too if that's what you're craving. It's all delish. All the starters are off the charts as well -- the Kyuri pickles and the Chinese fried chicken are a particularly great combo to share with some friends. The service here is unsurprisingly friendly and supportive. They make you feel like every choice you make here is going to lead to a unique but always incredible evening. And they're right!

As a ramen fan, I have tried several ramen restaurants in New York City. Ivan Ramen is definitely the standout. The noodles have a great flavor, and texture. The broth is so savory and flavorful, and they have a good variety of ramen to choose from!

The decor at Ivan Ramen definitely adds to the experience. I felt as if I was transported into busy Ramen shop in Asia! Cool, graphic comic strip art lines the window to the kitchen, which catches everyone's eye. 

I am convinced that this is one of the absolute best ramen spots in the city. You won't be disappointed!
The Triple Garlic/Triple Pork is one of the finest dishes I've ever had in my life. Ivan knocks it out of the park! This is a must experience for any New Yorker or anyone visiting.
One of the best meals I've had. Highly recommend the spicy red chili ramen, it has the perfect amount of kick to it. Great food great staff!

This place won a ramen award in Japan? I saw the episode about this place on chefs table, it looked so amazing, made a reservation. In my opinion, I'm no ramen expert like Ivan, but I've had better in the city. Final thoughts, Meh...
Not worth the buzz. Saltier than the saltiest ramen and served luke warm - about as appealing as old bathwater.

Great food great staff! THE place to go for noodles in the city. I ordered the Tokyo Tea cocktail, it was very refreshing and just what I needed after a long walk getting there. For food I had the Spicy Red Chili Ramen. Our waiter rated it 8/10 on spice scale and he was pretty accurate. The broth itself had amazing flavor, but nothing compared to Ivan's rye flour noodles.

Was very excited to try this. The fried chicken lived up to the hype. Had the recommended chicken ramen and it was delicious. Also the friendly and attentive wait staff -even with several large parties being sat- made this a great meal.

Came here after seeing it on Netflix chefs table and had a great experience. Had a reservation for 5:45 didn't get crowded until we were finishing tho. The waiter was super nice and actually cared about engaging us with the menu. Octopus appetizer was meatiest perfectly charred octopus I had ever had and the ramen was good, especially the chicken paitan that is the way to go here it's indescribably flavorful and unique with shredded chicken, delicious broth, an egg yolk and yummy noodles. So full I couldn't even finish. Place is mostly minimalist with a colorful collage wall. Reasonable price. Highly recommend! Stop waiting at the 2 hour wait place (I won't say the name but you know.)

First heard of Ivan Ramen when watching Chef's Table. Lucky enough, it's 4 blocks from my apartment! The service was amazing, quick and friendly.  Started with the Japanese Fried Chicken, which was dope. Then moved on to the Chicken Paitan, which was flavorful and delicious. Definitely recommend. Totally lives up to the hype.

Honestly came here because of the Chef's Table episode and everything lived up to expectations from the waiters to the food and drinks. We ordered the tofu Coney Island starter which had such great flavors. I had the shio ramen and the sake sangria. The ramen was the perfect size that I was completely satisfied without that extremely full feeling a lot of ramen places leave you with. Or table ordered a variety of other dishes including the triple pork triple garlic and the vegetarian ramen, and everyone left the lunch extremely happy.

I got the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen. 

Pros:
- the porkbelly was sooooo tender and the cut was generous. 
- noodles were perfect; they were chewy and there was a nice amount in there. 
- I was really happy that I got two pieces of eggs in there. And they were cooked to perfection. 
- place looks cool and sitting at the bar was comfortable. 
- wait/bar staff is attentive without being overbearing. 

Cons:
- ramen was too salty. Ramen is essentially salty, but this one was overboard. The broth makes or breaks it for me, and unfortunately, it broke. So sad.

Since Ivan has yet to open a shop in Minnesota, it is going to take me a few more trips to NY to get through the menu.  With all due respect to other ramen shops in the US and Japan, if there is better ramen out there, I haven't found it!  

The depth of flavor in Ivan's Shio Ramen was phenomenal.  It is hard when you find something fantastic to venture to another menu item, but the Shio Ramen gave the Shoyu a run for it's money.  Couldn't pass on a repeat on the pickled daikon in chili oil and XO sauce.  

Collection of local and specialty beverages was impressive and fit my current interest in sour beers.  Why didn't I realize you could make Yuzu lemonade like Ivan's when we had a Yuzu tree in our garden in Japan?

Each time at Ivan Ramen, the interaction with the serving staff has been awesome, quick to sample something new.

One of the worst ramen place i have ever been to. I went there today with moderate expectations and while the decors were mildly interesting, that was the only positive review I can give to this restaurant. For starters, we ordered the summer watermelon appetizer and found the odd combination flavors of tofu, seaweed and cubes of watermelon to be off putting. When our ramen came, my vegetarian ramen was so salty that it was almost inedible. We had the pleasure of sitting at the table where Ivan and his family happened to be dinning at the same time and didn't have the heart to commented about how salty the food was to the staff. Would not return to this restaurant anytime soon.

Got there for lunch with some friends. I had the Tonkotsu Tsukemen and my friends had the classic shoyu, which was their most popular ramen. The Tonkotsu Tsukemen was very delicious as its a noodle dip. My friends thought the classic shoyu was very salty. Service was good.
Opened the door to let my boyfriend in. Manager yelled/screamed across the restaurant to shut the door. Twice. Turned right back around.

I've heard many things about tasty ramen, and this place was definitely on my list to try just that. I gotta say, I wasn't disappointed! My friend and I started off with the Tofu Coney Island appetizer, which was a delicacy. It was tofu, onions and mushrooms galore. We then proceeded with the Vegetarian Ramen, which overall exceeded my expectations! The only thing I would say I didn't like was how salty the broth was. But overall it was delicious! If you're looking for a solid ramen experience in the city, look no further than Ivan Ramen.

I've had better.

Came here with a group of 3 on Monday for dinner. We didn't make a reservation but had no trouble getting a table probably because it was on a week day. There's more seating in the back and outside for larger groups. But I wouldn't bring more than 4 people here. 

So my friends and I were led to the seatings outside where a large fan was blowing in the corner. The weather was in the low 80s with a bit of humidity and as I was following the server, I wasn't sure if eating a hot bowl of ramen outside would be a good idea on a day like this. Nonetheless, we ordered the following:

- Veggie Shoyu ($15): Vegetarian option with rye noodles. The best part about this bowl of noodle was the single roasted tomato. It was juicy and burst as soon as I took that first bite. However, I wasn't too crazy about the broth, which was soy sauce and vegetable based. It wasn't too bland or salty but something was missing.. But besides that, I think they could've added more broth. My noodles were drying out either because they put too much noodles or too little broth in the bowl. As for the veggie toppings, it was simple with the salad leaves, enoki mushrooms, tofu and a single roasted tomato. 

- Cold Sesame ($17): Creamy! It has whole wheat noodles with minced chicken, roasted peppers and preserved chili. They also sprinkle tons of scallions, which I love. It's a great dish to eat when it's hot out since the noodles are meant to be eaten cold. Also, I don't know what the sauce is made of but it was creamy and full of flavor. Not only did I taste sesame but there was a bit of spice and tanginess to it. I personally loved this one the most out of the three.

- Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen ($17): Also made with whole wheat noodles. It has a tonkotsu broth and pork belly. which I think they can add more of.. and perhaps cut them a bit thicker? It kinda leaves you unsatisfied with the meat. 

My favorite was definitely the cold sesame. The the thing is, despite the great service the food wasn't all that for me. My friend ended up eating half of her cold sesame and took the other half to go. I ate a little bit over half of my bowl. My other friend was famished and devoured her's since she didn't eat anything all day. This place is pricer than most ramen places and I just can't justify the price. I'd expect every single dish on their menu to be phenomenal with the price range that they have but.. it's not. 

Pretty sure I won't be back here cause aforementioned, I've had better.

Man, after watching Ivan's story on Chef's Table, I really was expecting a lot more. 

The vibe of the restaurant was fun, very upbeat and lively. I will say if you are craving ramen, want to come here AND it's a hot day, you might want to rethink things. The restaurant was on the warmer side (lacking AC) and after eating hot ramen, we were sweating...only to be welcomed by more heat and humidity outside. 

Our server was wonderful as was the service we received! Our waters were constantly being filled up and our server was very helpful and accessible despite the business of the restaurant. 

I ordered the Spicy Red Chili Ramen. I wasn't too impressed by its overall look- but they do say never judge a book by its cover so I was willing to move past this. The ramen itself was what killed it. It was thin wheat ramen- hard and grainy. Definitely not the best ramen I have tried at all. The broth was pretty good though. I did try my husband's Veggie Ramen and I did like that a lot more but again the ramen itself killed both dishes. 

Breaks my heart, but I won't be back to visit. We are going to Japan in a couple of months so I am interested to compare traditional ramen to Ivan's creation.

We managed to secure a table last minute. After reading all the good reviews, this place didn't disappoint. We had the watermelon w tofu and pork buns for entree, the flavour of these dishes was devine - a perfect introduction of what was to come. For main we had chicken paitan and the triple pork triple garlic mazeman. Both of which were delicious. Waitstaff were friendly and service was great. Can't fault this place and hope to return soon.

After many years (and many other bowls of ramen) I returned to Ivan Ramen. The Chicken Paitan is unlike any other ramen I've had - much more of a homey-chicken noodle soup of sorts, but absolutely delicious. Love the inventiveness of the ramen at this place and now that the hype and crowds have died down it's more of chill joint where you can just get good food.

Bumping up my rating after all this time. I have a newfound love of this place.

Good experience and watched the Chef's table
Episode prior to going to this restaurant. The food was good and interesting options.

Ivan Ramen was a lot of fun with an adorable backyard garden. However, the food was a 4 and not the 5+ I was expecting after watching chef's table and learning about Ivan's  history and fame. The chicken ramen was a 5, but the Tokyo ramen and the Japanese fried chicken were 3.5s in my opinion. They were both good and tasty but would want to order differently next time. The ramen tasted a bit bland after tasting the flavorful chicken one, and the fried chicken was a bit soggy with the sauces on top. Overall - cute place but didn't live up to my high expectations. 

The waiters were also really nice and helpful!

Finally stopped by and it is very good. 

I had a watermelon appetizer with tofu and a kudzu dressing that was sweet, cooking and spicy. Sharp flavor contrasts seem to be the thing here. 

I also had the pork dipping noodles. The ingredient quality was great. The whole wheat noodles were great. Broth was very nice but not thick enough for my personal tastes. The green veg on the dish were tasty but chopped so thick they didn't feel as integrated as most ramen toppings if that makes sense. The pork belly was well cooked but too salty on it own but in the broth was very tasty. 

I will definitely add it to my rotation.

Ps. The service is top notch. The staff is energetic and informed.

after all the hype and chef's table this and that, I was excited to try this place. Overall, I was a little let down based on how everyone was talking, BUT it was good and really innovative. I had the triple pork garlic mazemen, which was only the second time I had mazemen. I am down with the concept, and everything was delicious- the chashu, the bacon, the pork belly- but I was hoping for something a *little* more. I would recommend this place if you want to try a different type of ramen in NY.

Had the appetizer of Chinese mixed greens which were tangy and absolutely delicious! Would definitely get those again if I came back.

However, I always ask for the richest & most flavorful ramen wherever I go and here they recommended the Chicken Paitan. It was underwhelming - too outright peppery and not enough depth to the soup. While their noodles were yummy and different, the ramen just did not wow me the way many other ramens in the city have. Would try a different ramen if I ever came back here.

UPDATE: Ithey still suck.



It was nearly empty when i was there at 7:15pm on a Saturday, one of the hosts huddled around an ipad eventually lifted her head to say, "OK it'll be about a 90 min wait."  Really?!  

Even if reservations take priority, I could have dined, tipped, and left in time.  At least 2 servers approached the host station wishing to help me, but had to just twiddle their thumbs waiting for RSVP's instead.  Like I said: the place looked Empty. On a reasonable dining hour on a Saturday night.  What message does that send?  That you're an exclusive club, not a restaurant?

From what I saw, the layout of the place is tight, even for Manhattan standards.  The bar is reserved, the stools are built into the ground- if you sit there, you'll be well within one's personal bubble.  Basically if you eat here, assume you'll be bumped into numerous times, be willing to share your food with strangers, or at least with their breath: The tables are THISCLOSE to each other, so much that hosts move them out to let you sit.  Which I'm sure is a burden on everyone involved when the place actually hits capacity.  

The wait staff seemed to encourage me to stay, but like your new normal "LESclusive" scene, those who worked the door turn down the wrong people sometimes. But there's always somewhere else to go.  If you want good food, keep walking North, cross Houston, make a left, and have Punjabi.

The best ramen I have ever had maybe some of the best food I have ever had. The waiter and host were great super helpful with all of my question. Amazing vibe in the restaurant. Any time I am in New York I will be making Ivan ramen my number one stop can't wait to come back for more.
Food, service and atmosphere were great!! Ivan was in the house that day chatting with everyone!! Quite the experience!!

This ramen is so good, I don't know where to start. Overall, I feel like it's not as salty or fatty as other ramen places.  We were in NY for a week and ate there 3 times because my kids love it so much. For kids, they will serve a half portion with noodles and shio broth only.  They charge $10 instead of $16. We tried the spicy red chili ramen. Be aware that it's spicy,  so if you like it hot, it's great. Also had the chicken paitan ramen with the straight rye noodles and another time substituted for wavy wheat noodles.  This taste like a classic chicken noodle soup on steroids. Great, safe one to try. The straight noodles as served is best.  Ask for the chili hot paste in a bottle if like a kick.  My husband loves the triple pork triple garlic mazemen. It's not as brothy but same deliciousness, super tasty. We had the pork buns... meat is tasty with a classic, fluffy Asian white bun. We love it here and the staff could not be nicer!  They are very busy but we never felt rushed. They recognized that we had been there several times and were so friendly to our kids. Best to have reservations or you can come when they first open at 12:30p. We did that on a Sat and got in.  Another time,  we ate dinner a little early at 530pm on a weekday and got in.   The best part is they make their own noodles. Nothing taste better than fresh carbs!! Go try it!

I've been wanting ramen for a few weeks now. I'm vegetarian and sometimes it's hard to find a place that serves ramen w vegetable broth- and Ivan Ramen does! I got the vegetarian bowl and it was delicious! Hit the spot perfectly! I thought it was going to take a long time to get a table bc there is always a lot of people waiting and in the restaurant but when we came only 20 min wait! Will def return!

I only give this four stars because the ramen was not spicy enough! However, the appetizers for vegetarians were so good. I ordered tofu with mushrooms, mustard, and spring onions and the sweet corn. The shiitake mushroom flavor was pretty subtle.

Saw Ivan Ramen on Chef's Table and living in NYC, had to come try it! It was delicious; I suppose it was the best ramen I've ever had?? But I am vegan so it's a bit hard for a ramen place to mess up a vegetarian ramen too badly. For an appetizer we had the tofu coney island which was flavorful and rich. Then we both ordered the vegetarian ramen. The broth was also super rich and wonderful, and the tofu was the most flavorful tofu I've ever had. I appreciated the unconventionality of the rye noodles (I could really taste a difference from regular wheat noodles) and the roasted tomato was such a great flavor addition! We ate everything. The waiter was also very nice, welcoming, and accommodating. I do agree however that the ramen is a tad overpriced... I think for vegetarian ramen to be $15 -- when it doesn't contain any expensive, more demanding ingredients such as meat or an egg -- is a bit steep. Veggie broth, tofu, and some veggies doesn't equal $15 to me.. but hey, it's a bit of a touristy spot so what can you expect. I doubt we will return due to having already tried the only two vegan options, and the price. But all in all I'm glad we went.

We were 'one of those people' who watched Ivan on Chefs Table, so of course had to go check out the ramen for ourselves.

The vegetarian ramen was very good; heavy on the soy sauce and umami. The roasted tomato added a sweetness, and the mushrooms gave the dish a fun texture. I was surprised by how much the noodle reminded me of angle hair pasta. 

Tip:
Eat at the counter! The restaurant is quite loud, so eating next to your date allows for a more pleasant conversation and gets your mouth closer to your food so it's easier to slurp.

Been here twice and I must say, they serve the best ramen i've tasted in New York city. 

Me and my girlfriend went here on a Sunday afternoon, around 2 PM. We made reservations through Open Table. When we got there, place was not that packed and we're able to secure a table right away.

Interior's good -- well lit, clean, and i think space is pretty optimized. I love how there is a collage of Japanese and Western themed pictures in the wall; like a representation of eastern and western culture fusion. There is also a space in the back where big groups can sit.

Now onto the service. It was awesome. The servers really know everything there is to know about the menu. They are really attentive and very friendly. This is how servers should be!

Let's move on to the most important aspect -- the food. Their menu is pretty good -- not so limited, and not so vast. Price is pretty reasonable (except maybe for the corn which I feel is a little expensive, a cob cut in half for $6). They have salads, appetizers, hot and cold ramen, and a selection of drinks.

I've tried a couple of items:
a. Tuna Squared - this one is good, serving-wise and taste-wise. Lettuce was really crisp. You can taste the freshness in each bite. Tuna chunks are citrusy good!
b. Japanese Fried Chicken - serving also good but the taste is just okay for me. I want it to be crunchier. I also want to taste the garlic more. 
c. Spicy Green Beans - this one is the bomb. We can't stop eating this. It's a bit pricey but I think it's worth it. The green bean is firm. The cheese sauce , spiciness, sesame seeds, and nori combination is awesome. There were also some toasted hazelnut which adds flavor and texture to the dish.
d. Steamed Pork Buns - this is also good. At first, i thought that the daikon will not go well with the pork. Boy, was i wrong. Pork belly used is tender and tasty. The only comment i have is the color of the bun which is less white than your normal pork buns.
e. Tokyo Shoyu Ramen - not a fan. Tastes normal for me. The pork belly was good though -- tender and tasty. 
f. Spicy Red Chili Ramen - if you're not a fan of spicy food, then this is not for you. This is spicy! I perspired a lot while eating this. I think taste is good but for the price, the toppings included are a bit lacking. Maybe throw in some pork chashu?
g. Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen - remember mix, mix, and mix your noodles! This is different from your normal ramen as it doesn't have that soupy base. I made the mistake of not mixing it properly so i ended up with sad noodles. It was just later when i saw the "sauce" at the bottom where I truly appreciated this bowl's deliciousness. Whole wheat noodles are thick. Pork belly is good. The only comment i have is also the amount of topping for the price.
h. Chicken Paitan - if you're visiting Ivan Ramen only once, then this is what you should order. It has this home-y chicken noodle soup taste but leveled up. The yolk which you have to mix on your own really added richness to the broth. They serve it with lime which you can drizzle to balance the taste to your liking. For me, soup alone is good. I love the ground chicken. Only comment I can give is maybe more toppings? 

Overall, this is place is good. They have amazing items in their menu. If not for the price-topping ratio, I would've given this 5 stars.

You should try it!

I'm not quite sure this place gets so many 3 star reviews. Aside from managing expectations that this is not your typical ramen shop, I thought Ivan Ramen was fantastic. We came for lunch on a Sunday. We had made a reservation and were promptly seated. The place filled up at about 1:00. Our server was great, explaining his favorite dishes and how their ramen is different vs traditional ramen. But after his descriptions, we were ready to jump right in. I ordered the triple garlic triple pork mazemen that others have mentioned in reviews. It wasn't a typical ramen as it didn't really come in a broth but more like a pork stew. It was still super tasty. The ramen noodles were what made it for me. The noodles had a strength to them when you bit into them but still absorbed the flavor of the meat and the broth. I would go again just for the noodles. My friends ordered the cold noodles that were served with hot broth. That was also really good and when we had broth left over, we ordered another set of noodles to finish it off with. We came away stuffed and very satisfied. Definitely a different spin on ramen

I am here a few times a week.

Noodles 'Classics' - 2.5 out of 5
I am not a fan of these ramen at all. The rye noodles are very awkward for a ramen and have a squishy texture. Broth is too little and extra salty/fatty. Moreover, the portions are extremely small for the value.

Ivan's Specials 4.0 - 4.5 out of 5

I would ONLY recommend this establishment if you are here to see his Ivan's take on Japanese dishes and ingredients. I have tried all of this menu and find them much more enjoyable. The Shoyu Tonkotsu Tsukeme and Cold Sesame Noodles are excellent. 

Their fried chicken is particularly good, if you are into that. However, it does not remind me of Japanese style-fried chicken at all. It comes with a ranch sauce too.

The restaurant is definitely overpriced by 15% but the service is always perfect.
So good! I got the triple pork ramen which is drier (on purpose, they use less broth) and it was delicious. The service was fantastic- I'll definitely be back!

I have a very strong stomach, when I went to Ivan ramen last week Thursday with my girlfriend we thought we were going to have the ultimate ramen experience. It was the total opposite ! I had the tuna with cold ramen. The waiter was boasting about it and I thought I was in for a treat. Later on that evening I was feeling really awful my stomach felt like it was a washing machine. I slept it off and the next morning was even worse I was on the train with cold sweat and I had to get off to vomit. This whole ordeal lasted till Saturday evening I had to drink tons of electrolytes and water. Diarrhea for the entire weekend and stomach pains as if I was getting stabbed. There must have been some cross contamination in the kitchen. I will never visit Ivan ramen again It was the worst experience of any restaurant I have even been to.

I was there because I saw ' The chef's table'. Extremely appreciated how Ivan take Ramen seriously. Ramen taste surprisly authentic and very causal atmosphere. But just feel the price is a bit high for causal food

Oh My God!!! Obsessed with Ivan Ramen!!! I can eat there food Morning, noon and night!!!
The service is great! 
My husband surprised me with date night and it was absolutely perfect!!! 
The chicken wings were amazing too! And who would have know that fried tofu could be ohhhh so yummy! Run don't walk if you have not tried them yet

HOLY DAMN THIS RAMEN IS AMAZING. 

Seriously though, this ramen totally lives up to the hype. We saw this on chef's table and decided to give it a go. The wait was an hour on a rainy Saturday night, but they sent us to a great local bar and gave us a discount. 
The pork buns were great, and the Tokyo Shoyu ramen showed me the face of god. Word to the wise, though: the spicy stuff on the menu is pretty wu-tang.

I really did not like the ramen here. We had the shio, mazemen, tsukemen and some apps. All disappointed. The chicken broth in the shio tasted dirty and watery all at the same time. The mazemen didn't have enough broth. The tsukemen was just ok. The noodles themselves were just poorly executed and had a weird aftertaste.

I love ramen and noodles in general. But These were hard to like. With all the hype, I wish my experience had been better.
Delicious Ramen and Japanese Fried Chicken. Out waiter was very helpful and friendly, and made our experience so pleasant! Highly recommend!

Truly excellent place to eat.  I learned about Ivan Ramen from Chef's Table, and had been looking forward to visiting for quite some time.  We arrived a little before opening to find a crowd waiting.  Despite the early rush, we were served promptly and courteously.

I ordered the spicy red chili ramen, and my wife ordered the Tokyo shoyu.  Both were fantastic!  The spice level was just above my comfort level, which was great - too often am I let down by spice levels that aren't that spicy, but this lived up to the billing.

I am something of a Ramen shop noobie, and when the waitress noticed that I was struggling with the chopsticks she kindly provided me with a chopstick helper, which let me get through the meal without issue.  I truly appreciate that level of service.

We will definitely visit Ivan Ramen again on a future visit to NYC!
This place was so delicious I'm dying to go back. Definitely try the tofu Coney Island and triple pork triple garlic ramen.

Ramen is good.  Personally I've had better but it's still pretty good.  What I don't like are the prices.  I find this place too expensive for the taste.  Year it's really great,  but it's nyc and there are a billion other ramen places for almost the same quality and cheaper.  BUT  what I will say the ambiance is also great!  The aesthetic is wonderful and the appetizers are good and big portions so definetly come at least once.

Sorry to say that Ivan Ramen struck all of my party of five as overrated and overpriced.    They are great at PR but the ramen does not live up to the hype.    I have been to dozens of Ramen places, so have some frame of reference.   We ordered the house favorite ramen.    Broth was disappointing, not rich and flavorful which is what I like best about ramen.   The noodles did not stand up.    One of our party (admittedly exaggerating) compared it to cup a soup.   There are so many better ramen places in NYC.   The location is off the beaten track, which I liked.    Had not been to that neighborhood before.

My boyfriend and I watched Chef's Table and really wanted to try out Ivan. Unfortunately, it didn't live up to the hype. The decor was really cool. I loved the mosaic ramen bowl mural out back. 

The Japanese Fried Chicken was super savory and saucy. It had a lot of extra flavors...garlicky, togarashi, spicy, sweet. We had mixed feelings about it. Definitely interesting. We got the Chicken Paitan and Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen so we can try one dryish whole wheat noodle and one soup rye noodle. The pork slice was pretty good, fatty and flavorful. But you only get one slice per bowl. The noodles, his main focus, were pretty special. The Chicken Paitan broth was good, but nothing special. The noodles had good texture. It seems dumb to say the triple garlic was too garlicky but it was just overwhleming in the broth. It tasted like one thing: Garlic. I did love the whole wheat noodles though, super chewy and a good texture.

Finally visited this place and found out it was featured on Chef's Table, despite not having reservations we waited 20 mins and were seated relatively quickly. Ramen was great, flavorful. Always feel ramen is a bit too salty, but it was good but not best ramen I've ever had. Do applaud the ambiance, felt like I was in Tokyo. Recommend sitting at bar though, too loud in the main area

3.5 Stars, more so for that delicious hot sauce they make and not the Chicken ramen which was just A-OK.

TIPS: 
- Add the house made chili sauce to your ramen, gives it way more flavor. 
- Heard stories about long wait times, luckily we came right when they opened during lunch and there was no line. 

FOOD:
- Chicken Paitan: Extremely oily, don't get me wrong, I'm all down for oily food. However, with this I couldn't get past the giant layer of oil floating on top of my ramen (see pics). Evan after you've mixed the broth a little bit, the oil is still overpowering. As for taste, the broth was definitely rich in chicken and black pepper. The chicken paitan reminded me of a similar Southeast Asian dish with glass noodles and pepper chicken. The dish is also served with a slice of lime to undercut the heaviness of the oil; however, I asked for 2 more limes since it was so heavy. 


OVERALL:
- Chicken Paitan was A-OK, new for ramen maybe? But not new for other Asian noodle dishes. 
- Another thing that should be noted is the history of food critics (and yelpers), to shame Asian owned restaurants for making "oily and greasy food," but when a white guy does it, it becomes trendy and cool.

My wife and I made sure to eat here after watching Chef's table and had a wonderful meal. The appetizers were creative and surprisingly good, the summer watermelon and chinese greens were the standouts for us. I went with the chicken paitan ramen and was very happy with it. Nice texture to the noodles and soup was flavorful. My wife's vegetarian ramen was just okay though.

This wasn't my first time here, but when I went today for a quick lunch before my shift (I bartend in the neighborhood) i felt the need to pipe up about these guys because they're doing a great job of putting out wonderfully flavorful food. 

    I've read a handful of reviews about them on Yelp from people who have extensive knowledge and experience with this cuisine, and they seem to be underwhelmed. I do not share that knowledge or experience, although I consider myself a foodie 100%. 

    The spicy chili ramen was my choice, and I asked for it to be extra spicy if possible, to which their response was not really, but that they would bring me a side of their chili sauce to add as I went. Well, the ramen itself was already a 6/10 spicy, with wonderful flavor. The chili sauce bumped it up to about a 7.5/10 (I love absurdly spicy food, so I dumped the entire side of chili sauce into the ramen). I will say that it DID get me sweating a bit, which is a good sign. Jonathan was my guy behind the bar and he did everything he could to accommodate me with my spicy cravings and the manager (I assumed that was his position)was also super chill and made a joke with me that cracked me up. 

    Overall: no, I don't share these folks' ramen expertise, but I love flavorful, well put together food, and Ivan accomplishes that. If you're one of the weird humans like me that want their entire gastrointestinal tract to be melted by spice and heat, then you may be underwhelmed, but the flavor will still kick ass. 5/5. Staff also: 5/5.

I'm so torn about this place. I enjoyed the ramen but my husband really didn't. We rarely differ on our tastes, so this was interesting. I thought the broth was really rich and flavorful, not too salty like a lot of reviews have said. The noodles were good, but not enough texture. The yuzu lemonade was really good! 

My husband, on the other hand, thought the broth tasted muddy and he didn't care for the noodles. 

It certainly wasn't the best ramen I've ever had (that would be the burnt miso ramen I had in Kyoto, holy cow), but it wasn't terrible. I'd go back again if I didn't live 3000 miles away!

3 and 1/2 stars?! Do you people not have taste buds?

If you aren't a ramen junkie, how can you compare this to anywhere? If you aren't a "huge fan" of ramen then don't waste your time checking this place out just because you saw it on Netflix! That would be like me saying "oh I'm not really a "huge fan" of pig" and then going to a pig roast and reviewing it. Uh... stay home!

Yes, I saw the Netflix special and blah blah blah but I very much related as I have a similar personality to Ivan (straight forward / ADD / entrepreneurial) and also have a deep fascination with Asia (food / the men / you name it).

I wanted to check this place out as I have frequented many ramen spots in NYC and was not too thrilled with any (even the famous Ippudo). 

I came here the very next day after watching this on Netflix Chefs Table. I came by myself for lunch. I didn't need to make a reservation and although it was busy, it wasn't packed. I REALLY liked that you could make a reservation on OpenTable. It drives me crazy when I can't make reservations anywhere and well, most ramen spots (99.9%), you can't. It will be hard to snag a last minute prime dinner time reservation though.

I digress...

So I sat at the counter and ordered the spicy sesame cold noodles. Can I just tell you that I came back the very next day, the next weekend, and the following weekend (and pretty much have been there once a week for the past few months). Do you think I liked the dish? With my friends we have tried pretty much every single thing on the menu and the two best dishes are:

+++++++ Spicy cold sesame ramen ++++++  if I could have dreamed what my perfect dish would taste like, this is 100% hands down IT. 

+ shoyu tonkotsu tsukemen (shoyu glazed pork belly, pickled collards, soft egg, chives, whole wheat noodle

For appetizers, I've tried the pickled daikon xo and loved it (the daikon is cut very thin), and my friend LOVED the fried chicken.

If these guys offered delivery, I would most likely go bankrupt.

MUST GO!

These people are nuts. I actually ended up here because Nakamura was closed /: anyway, I loved this place - the art on the walls, music playing, friendly staff.... and it all comes down to the ramen itself. I got the spicy - so flavorful, loved the noodles, plus the chopsticks with ridges to better capture each bite. Topped it off with a lemonade - more tart than sweet, perfect accompaniment. I was hungover as hell and tired from a week of working in the city, and this hit the spot.

Not your average ramen place! Don't come here with your Japanese flavor expectations. Flavors are taste quite other-Asian fusion with hints of Chinese. The cauliflower starter is nice. This place would have been 3-stars for me but our waitress was too kind. It's definitely a unique place. The rundown: Classic Tokyo Shio Ramen wasn't memorable, Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen is like an Asian stirfry and the Chicken Paitan is hella peppery

Had a nice quick lunch here this week. We were a group of four (with reservations), and sat outside on a beautiful day. The decor is something between cosy and funky diner... and I think it would be a cool spot to come back to in the winter. 
We enjoyed all our appetizers: the autumn salad, broccoli, BBQ chicken, and cauliflower. The chicken was particularly delicious, spicy and flavorful, whereas the cauliflower seemed to lack that wow factor (perhaps it needs to be a little crispier). 
We each ordered a different ramen, and were all quite happy, though next time I will opt for a shoyu instead of the shio that I chose. While it is more of a classic and a favorite of many, I thought it was a bit overpowered by the dashi. I would come back again to try more.

Let's be honest. I came here because I saw Ivan's feature on Chef's table. I was hoping to meet him on an off chance but of course he wasn't there. 

I'm not a huge ramen connoisseur but my girlfriend is. She is from LA where ramen is cheap and more abundant. I dragged her to come with me because I wanted to eat at Ivan's restaurant. Off the bat, my girlfriend was turned off by the price of the ramen. $16 for a barebone ramen (noodles, an egg and a piece of pork belly). all other sides were extra. I know I live in NYC and food is expensive, but thats just a lot for ramen. According to my girlfriend, its better and cheaper in California and not unnecessarily expensive. She also thought the soy sauce broth was a little too salty. 

Overall I actually thought the food/price was 3/5, but the staff there is incredibly friendly. Our waiter talked to us for awhile and the service was excellent when I went. Really friendly people working there.

I'm one of the millions of unique people who calls himself a foodie and is easily influenced to eat anything a talking head recommends on Netflix. Heck, you feature a chain fast food restaurant on food Network one day, and I'll likely be camping out to get a bland dry chicken sandwich the next day.

So naturally after watching Chef's Table...



The place is clean and the bartender was very friendly. I had the triple pork ramen. A little on the salty side, the ramen nevertheless was still flavorful and very satisfying. Definitively worth a try. It is a little on the pricier side, but nothing too crazy. 

A bit disappointed by the small pours of beer for such a high price, but when it comes down to it I'm really there for the ramen

This ramen is good. I went with my girlfriend I got the Tokyo Shio Ramen, and she got the Tokyo Shoyu, we both got it with the roasted tomato. WOW, the tomato adds so much to it, I've since made ramen at home and added the roasted tomato, such a unique and good addition. 
I thought the Shoyu was a better broth and liked the bamboo in the shoyu over the mushrooms of the shio.
You can definitely taste the uniqueness in the rye noodles, some people on here said they tasted grainy, I did not think that one bit and really liked them.
Staff was very friendly and inviting, answering any questions and attentive, but not too annoyingly attentive. Food also came out EXTREMELY fast. Would highly recommend.

I came here at lunchtime on a Monday and there was (thankfully) no wait.

Miso sweet roasted corn - Corn was well-cooked and the sauce was really good.

Chicken paitan - I'd give it a 4/5 for taste, but felt that it was too pricy at $17. The noodles were surprisingly good and chewy considering that I don't usually love thin noodles. The broth was flavorful but there was too much grease at the top. 

Triple pork triple garlic mazeman - The flavor was good initially, but it got way too salty after a couple of bites. I shared this with my friend and I couldn't even finish my half because of how salty it was, and I HATE wasting food. 

I don't regret coming here but I wouldn't return.

I am glad they took reservations since it's a very small restaurant. If I had to wait it wouldn't be worth it. We got there 5 mins late but they seat us immediately when we notified the server our whole party was here. The menu was very simple. I ordered the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen. It was only mediocre. I felt the broth didn't have enough taste and the noodles were soggy. I like my noodles with more of a chewy texture. Usually, I finish my whole bowl of ramen but I ended up leaving some behind. It tasted like ramen I could make at home. I don't think I'll be back for the ramen.

We saw Ivan Ramen episode on Chef's Table and was expecting a lot. We ordered the fried chicken, the shio ramen, and the shoyu ramen. The fried chicken was a bit too salty. It was also not very crispy. Disappointing. The ramen was both better and worse. Mine (shio) was again a bit too salty but tasty. The noodles were excellent for both ramens. The shoyu broth, however, was WAY over salted. It was actually inedible. My husband got the noodles down but couldn't eat the broth at all and had to give up on the pork belly as well. Whoever prepared that broth did not taste it before sending it out. I also wished the park was sliced more thinly. Way too thick to enjoy in a couple of bites. We will probably not visit again given how many other great ramen places there are in NYC. Competition is tough and the over over-salted palette of our dishes was a turn off.

Coming from a HUGE foodie and Food Science/Entrepreneurship graduate:

After seeing Ivan Orkin's story on Chef's Table, I HAD to plan a trip to Ivan Ramen. They opened at noon and I sat outside for about a half hour (with several others) in excitement for the experience. Ivan Ramen lived up to all of my expectations!  Staff was funny, knowledgeable, and accommodating. 

I enjoyed the triple pork ramen which was the ULTIMATE hangover cure, as well as a local craft beer that was recommended by the friendly bartender. I can't wait to be back with my boyfriend to show him what all the hype is about! I will also be wearing my Ivan Ramen T-shirt around to recommend to others :)

I've been back multiple times since my original review.  I just get what I like there, now -the shaved Daikon w/ XO sauce & the veggie broth with char siu... and it's awesome... mostly because the noodles are just top notch.  Vibe is nice.  Even the stuff I didn't like when it first opened must've just been teething troubles, because I've since tasted other folks' orders of those same things, and they're good.  Also it's open pretty late, which is nice.  

Apologies to the folks at Ivan Ramen for not updating this review sooner.

Ok, It was my birthday dinner and the first place chosen did NOT work out. My sister's BF suggested this place on a very nice Summer night. We went as a group, they were busy but we were seated almost immediately in the outdoor garden space. The appetizers were amazing and the drinks were a little weird but interesting and good. It's always good and adventurous to try new things. Everyone got their ramen and I the birthday girl got my vegetarian ramen. It was SOOOOO salty, too salty to eat. We notified the waiter who notified the manager on duty. The manager came over her us out and offered another vegetarian ramen or something else from the menu. I choose the Chicken paitan ramen and it was A-M-A-Z-I-N-G! 

This place was a win from the minute I walked through the door, saw the decor and the chill vibe. The salty dish was a fluke! They made everything else marvelously.
Went to NY for 4 days and tried 3 different ramen places, but Ivan ramen was definitely the winner!!! Ended up going there twice during my trip.

This place exudes a fresh outlook on ramen that gives a young vibrant front yet respects ramen for what it is - ramen. I came with a group of 3 people and waited for several minutes after our reserved time. We were met with a very courteous and respectful staff who even supplied complimentary apps because of our wait. Overall, a very pleasant experience. I will be coming back.
Went to the one at Gotham west market. Noodles are fresh and very favorable. There's no wait at the market.

My lady brought me here for her second visit in three days on a four day trip to NY, because it had already changed her life.

The five stars are for the food, the friendly service, the fun energetic ambience, the drink selection plus knowledge, and the entire experience as a whole.

We had Kyuri Pickles, Steamed Pork Buns, Chicken Meatballs, Curry Cauliflower and of course, the Chicken Paitan (me with the iconic roasted tomato, her with mushrooms). We also had a Brett Saison that was a collab between Transmitter and somebody else I can't remember. I would eat this exact meal again right now if I could.

I was so inspired that I went home and watched the Chef's Table episode featuring Ivan which moved me almost to tears, and made instant pot ramen from whatever was left in my fridge after this NY trip.

Go to this place. The wait (30-60 min on Thursday or Saturday night) was absolutely worth it.

We saw the piece about  Ivan the founder chef on the Netflix show Chef's Table and made a reservation to visit when we were in NYC.  We were not disappointed!  The atmosphere is not much (small ,crowded, and noisy), but the food is more than worth it.  The best Brussels sprouts I have ever had, and the ramen itself is in a different universe from what one usually experiences.  Our waiter too was outstandingly friendly and helpful.  This is a pilgrimage destination for great food to be sure, and Ivan is one of the great chefs of the world!

Innovative, busy tight place. They do ramen differently. It's dry and more pasta like if you will. Both our dishes were stellar but we left hungry. It needed to be double the size but we weren't going to spring double admission for what is already an overpriced boutique item to start with! Better make it IR plus mcDs night if you are coming here.

Very salty and 45 min wait for us

Came here today with high expectations but left with disappointment 

Ordered the vegetarian ramen - extremely salty the soup and the tofu was so salty like they marinated with salt only.  The best things were the roasted tomato and the noodle.

The service was fast and good 

The yuzu lemonade was good too if you like very sour stuff

Don't get the vegetarian noodle - maybe other items are good but I am not planning to go back

Pretty good ramen! I know it was a Netflix episode that started the craze but I see where it's coming from. Came around opening time and there was already a line (but was seated pretty quickly. I'm guessing if you come a little later there might be a wait :o

Got recommendations from our server who was super helpful.
The chicken paitian was apparently the servers and chefs favorite - admittedly pretty good. They give ou a line to squeeze if you want something a little more citrus like but it was already spot on for us with the peppery and rich chicken broth! 

We also go the cold buckwheat ramen that you have to dunk into a separate side soup. It was good too and the noodles were chewy and just right and the side of charsiew on the side that you eat it was so soft and melted right in our mouths!!!

Both are def recommended - a little pricey though being around 17-19 dollars for a bowl of ramen but I think it's worth checking out

The interior is also very well done and makes you feel like you have stepped into a corner shop in Japab

My initial motivation to go here was the Chefs Table that I had seen. I can safely say that the place and food lived up to my expectations. I went here with a friend on a cold and rainy Saturday night. This place gets pretty busy, so make sure you have a reservation. We ordered sake cocktails for drinks. Mine was cherry infused and it was good (not great). For appetizers, we got the fried chicken, which was simply amazing. I would highly recommend the chicken - it was super crisp, very flavorful and tossed in this amazing dressing. 

For the main course, I got the tripple pork ramen. It was super super pork-y in the best possible way. The waiter was correct to tell me that its not a very broth-y ramen. I was totally okay with that, but If you like a ramen that has a lot of broth, this may not be the one for you. My friend got the shoyu ramen, and I had some. it was also super super good and a more traditional ramen dish. 

Will definitely be back. This place is a standout culinary experience, and not very expensive.

GD that's delicious. Chicken paitan with an added egg has the most umami chicken broth paired with chewy al dente noodles that'll change your life. The pork tsukemen was very good too. The brussel sprouts with spicy sauce was definitely a must order. The shio ramen with the roasted tomato was just ok.
Excellent service, amazing food, and a wonderful atmosphere. The chicken paitan is the stuff that dreams are made of!

Went for dinner on a weekday night -- our party of 3 to wait about 15-20 minutes, and we ended up sitting at the bar. 

We ended up getting the Japanese fried chicken to share -- highly recommend. It's bursting with flavor and just the right amount of crispy. 

I got the triple pork triple garlic mazemen, and my friends got the chicken paitan and the shoyu tonkotsu tsukemen. My favorite was the chicken paitan -- great flavor, loved the rye noodles. The shoyu tonkotsu tsukemen came in second -- love the fact that you dip the noodles in the broth so it's less salty and more dry. Mine was way too salty, and I wish I'd had gotten something with rye noodles instead.

The quest for the best and most interesting ramen continues!
As a ramen geek, I was intrigued by Ivan's story.  There are many restaurants started by NYC locals who lived abroad and wanted to bring their favorite dish back to the US.  That is not rare, but what is rare is to have someone bring the dishes back with their own personal take while at the same time preserve the spirit of that foreign country.  

In the last 2 decades, ramen has prolificated throughout NYC and most other major metros of the US. However, after being in Japan, I found most of these Ramen places, sold decent ramen, it felt like a commodity. Many, if not most of these Ramen joints, including some of the Japanese chains, just couldn't preserve the spirit or essence of Japan that makes dining out in Japan so amazing.  There is something about Ivan Ramen that captures that spirit of Japan. Maybe it's the cleanliness? Maybe it's the fact that the staff was knowledgeable and can actually pronounce the names of the ingredients in Japanese, while still being American?  Maybe its the attention to details in how the food is presented. Maybe its how the dishes were crafted? Maybe it's the thoughtful decor?  Regardless if you are one of those yelpers who only eat at "authentic" places, one must give some props to Ivan in bringing back some of that Japanese spirit that many of us Japanese food lovers so long for.  I believe the spirit of the restaurant is just as important as the food itself in fully enjoying my meal, this is especially true for anyone who dined in Japan.

Anyways on to the food:

Excellent Brussels sprouts. The togarashi in brussels sprouts made the app savory and spicy at the same time.  Brussel was both tender while maintained its slightly crunchy texture. The dish included some crushed almonds that gave it some more crunch.

For the ramen, I got the Chicken Pai Tan. The chicken broth was rich and peppery There's that happy umami taste that lingers after you slurp. No, it's not as amazeballs as some of the Japan's Ramen God's tonkotsu broth, but it's not trying to be. Rye Noodles had a slight snap. The noodles didn't absorb the broth even at the end. What i really liked was the sesame seeds in the ramen. This gave it a pebbly my crunch as I slurped the Ramen.

My gf had the shio ramen.  While the shio was great, I think traditionalist will dismiss it for not being amazing enough.  She commented the shio ramen was heavy on the dashi.

My friend had the spicy red chili ramen. He actually wanted a veg version of it, but the staff explained to us the way the broth was made included simmering it in spicy paste and its not something they can just "whip" up since it takes time (like any good ramen broth). Anyways, the broth was fairly spicy, and reminded us of mapo-tofu.

Overall, excellent service. We enjoyed the heated cozy rear patio dining area. I just had a sense that someone took time and consideration in crafting the meal and ambiance for the customer. This is thoughtfulness is what I miss most about eating in Japan.  Ivan delivers on all front. Great food while retaining some of that Japanese essence.

i heard that Ivan was in town, so me and my friend decided to try this place out. We got the Shio ramen and triple pork ramen, they were both great quality ramen. However, we tried this place again a few months later that quality i was expecting from the first visit was nowhere to be found. It seems that this place is only good when Ivan is around to do the quality control ;P

This is a dope ramen spot. They have a small menu that gets right to the point. Service is quick even when busy and they have some great appetizers. Our friend had been there before and had the fried chicken which he said was amazing. But we had a vegetarian amongst our group so we got the spicy brussels sprouts which were delicious. Then we all got ramen and had a gay old time. The ramen was super flavorful: the broth was delicious and the noodles had a great texture to them. Good beer too. Go here. Now.

Long overdue lunch visit.
Starters
Kyuri pickles - thin chilled slices of cucumber in a sweet and tart vinegar sauce topped with dill. Love it!
Miso roasted cauliflower - very good. bonito flakes top the crunchy miso glazed cauliflower. Don't worry, the red pepper slices are not spicy so dig in!

Triple Pork, Triple Garlic Mazemen with an added egg.
Noodles - mix well in the broth. The whole wheat noodles are thick, firm and do a good job of absorbing the concentrated broth.
Broth - Mix well! The broth at the bottom of the bowl is porky and creamy. Not as salty as some mazemen I have enjoyed.
Toppings - Garlic (sliced and grated) comes on subtly at first but by the end f the bowl, you know it's there. What was third third way?
Pork - in addition to the broth, the minced pork comes through in every bite. The chunk of pork belly is salacious and fatty, First rate and I wish there was more than one.
The scallions add the needed texture and, if you mix thoroughly, they will be there to accompany you to the end of the bowl.
The egg was nicely soft boiled, but subtle. I couldn't tell if the flavor of the egg came from the marinade or sitting in the broth.
A well balanced bowl of noodles. I thought at first that I would miss the salty impact of other mazemen that I've had. Make no mistake it is salty but the salt is countered by a confident hand that allows the pork and garlic to nicely balance out the profile. The noodles are great, but I would have enjoyed a less subtle hand in the marinade of the egg. 
Bottom line? When I was done I wished I had another bowl to keep the flavor party going!

This is one of those places I've heard about for many many years, but finally getting to trying.  Years ago, I would walk along Clinton St to go to WD-50 and I'd always see a line in front of Ivan Ramen.  I've seen Ivan Orkin featured on Mind of a Chef and multiple other food shows.  As I continue my quest to try every good ramen shop in NYC, I figured it was time to finally try Ivan Ramen.

Unfortunately, it was a rather disappointing experience.  From the very beginning, I had a cold intro to the place.  We arrived 20 minutes prior to opening and was third in line.  When they opened, I walked into an empty restaurant and the first thing the host did was ask if we had a reservation.  It's 12:30pm and there's a total of 11 people in line.  No, I did not have a reservation.  We were brought to the bar top.

I got the triple pork triple garlic mazeman, which the waiter suggested was his favorite.  He did mention to me that it was more a "sauce" instead of a ramen broth, but the flavor was excellent so I went ahead and ordered it.  It was not memorable at all.  The noodles were nicely cooked and perfectly al dente, with a chew that only comes with freshly made ramen noodles (I don't know if Ivan Ramen makes their noodles in-house or if Sun Ramen Co makes noodles for them).  The "broth" was pretty salty and just tasted like bacon.  To me, it was pretty one-note and lacked the complexity I was expecting.  The slice of pork belly was okay, but again nothing all that special.  The worst part of the pork was that it was luke warm, which made the fatty part pretty unpleasant from a texture perspective.  I paid $2 for the ajitama egg, which was a bit past soft boiled.  The egg itself was cold, which meant it lost that sort of "sexy" richness you get from an ajitama egg.

The only standout from the meal was the "Ivan Palmer".  It is an "Arnold Palmer" made from the roasted barley tea and the yuzu lemonade.  It was perfect and I wish they bottled it as I'd drink it daily.  It was super refreshing and cut through the muddled salty richness of the ramen.  The taste of the yuzu really stood out and the tea rounded out the flavor and balanced out the sweetness from the lemonade.  The drink was more tart than sweet.  

I would return just to order the Ivan Palmer.  I'd probably also try the chicken paitan, as it seems a more classic bowl and the splash of lime seems interesting.

My favorite ramen shops in NY are still Totto Ramen, Ramen Zundo-ya, Ichiran, Ramen Shack, and Ramen Lab (although that one depends on which pop-up is happening).

I think they spilled all the salt laying around in the kitchen into the ramen. Superrrrr salty broth. Not a fan. 

Eggs were cooked perfectly though.

So far this is the second worst ramen I ever had in new york. I have heard about this place for years, and read so many positive reviews in the past but never actually have a chance to try. lst week I went to Delancy with my wife to meet up with friends so we stop at Ivan Ramen to get a quick meal before meeting our friends. We ordered 2 items, the tokyo shio ramen and the triple pork ramen. Both are very disappointed and not worth the $16 price tag (each). 

Allow me to describe each one.
The shio ramen is consisted of bland stock that look like tap water mix with some kind fat and has no flavor. Moreover, they add kind of soft overcooked noodle with excessive amount of scallion. 

The triple pork is a little better. it is almost taste like real Asian food, as there are a bit salty and have some flavor. once again the excessive amount of scallion tend to ruined the taste of the sauce. 

Overall, I think it doesn't worth $16 a bowl for as I know is higher than most Japanese ramen in the city. from what I experience, the food lack authenticity and the flavor isn't what I usually expected from ramen. Maybe it's another style of ramen, but we really don't like it. So it is yet another proof that the review isn't always right.

Why is the ramen here so salty??

A quick Yelp search of the word "salty" within the reviews generated 150+ results. You'd think with that many people bothering to comment on the same issue, someone at Ivan Ramen would consider toning it down a bit in the salt department by now. 

My friend and I shared the Japanese fried chicken appetizer and found it unremarkable. The pieces of chicken were tiny chunks, making them not as tender and juicy as the chicken karaage typically found at other restaurants. The paired shio ranch dip tasted like your typical ranch salad dressing. For noodles, we both picked the triple pork triple garlic mazemen with additional marinated eggs on top. Our server informed us that this ramen would have less broth compared to other more traditional options. What she failed to mention was how salty it would be. I have to say the flavor was unique and the whole wheat noodles had the perfect al dente consistency. I could appreciate Ivan's vision to create an innovative bowl of ramen. Unfortunately, the execution fell flat. 

It pains me to say this, but Ivan Ramen easily tops my list of overrated restaurants in NYC. Valuable stomach real estate could be saved for more delicious ramen elsewhere.

I think the food here is only mediocre, but the service is remarkable. We were told our wait was going to be approximately 45 minutes, but we were actually seated within 10 minutes. I like how they overestimated the wait time since they aren't able to gauge how long customers would be staying around for. Our server was extremely nice and let us sample a few beers before we decided which ones to order.

We ordered the chicken paitan, shoyu tonkotsu tsukemen, and japanese fried chicken. The chicken paitan's broth was amazing and filled with flavor. I felt like the giant piece of porkbelly topped on top of my noodles in the tsukemen was actually a bit too much and the meat was rather dry. The soft egg was perfect, but the pickled collards didn't go too well with it. The fried chicken was way too salty.

Breaking this review down in 4 parts, wait time, service, food and drink 

Time: Took us a hour and a half to be seated while the host told us 45 mins, the food was fast.

Service: lucky we got a good server, he got us our foods and drinks quick 

Food: salty! Wtf! Like why so salty, imma need few bottles of water to rehydrate myself. Over priced too 

Drink: not worth it! We order a sake cocktail for two.  All it was sake with apple juice frozen in to ice cube. Not worth the 25 dollars.

2 stars goes to the waiter.

Omg! Definitely all it's cracked up to be. Thought about going on a Saturday after bingeing Chef's Table on Friday night and seeing this episode, but there were no reservations available and NYC's dining experience over the weekend essentially requires a reservation or good company while the time passes to get a table... so ended up making the reservation for Sunday night dinner and I was beyond pleased.

We got there about 10 minutes late (due to typical subway delays), but called the restaurant and they ended up holding our reservation so we were seated right away upon arrival. Our server was very friendly and gave us the rundown on the entire menu, sharing what his favorites are, what the most ordered options are, and even what add ons we should get for our ramen dishes. I ended up going with the vegetarian ramen and my friend chose the spicy red chili ramen... WOW. The dishes were both extremely flavorful (the spicy ramen is like really spicy lol) and quite filling. My bowl was completely gone, and my friend's would've been too if her nose wasn't running so much from the spice haha (that's a good reaction though, guys). The dishes also came out super quick, which worked because we were practically starving.

The ambiance is really cool too - we decided to sit on the back patio because although it's November, it was in the 60s last night! There were heaters too which is really convenient due to the small restaurant space so they're still able to accommodate people on the patio despite the chilly temps. 

We will DEFINITELY be back, hoping to try the chicken paitan and some of the other ramen dishes as well. Wine selection (aka 2 choices) was good too! The carafe of white wine paired really nicely with both our dishes.

Thanks for a great experience!

I've always loved ramen, and I've eaten at plenty of ramen joints, but I've never had an experience quite like this. The staff is outstanding - friendly, fun, personable, and above all, human. They're service dog friendly and I've never felt judged when I've stopped in for lunch. And their food is just as stellar as their service - seriously, it's outrageously good. Don't take my word for it! Check it out for yourself!

Came here because of Chef's Table. I have had Ramen in Japan, Tokyo, Osaka, Okinawa, Kyoto. 

Went on a weekday with a reservation. Dropped by early to see if they could slip me in. Not many people were there so I was accommodated. Sat at the bar and the decor is interesting, bright and colorful.

I was surprised to see Orion beer here since Orion is not as popular, being from Okinawa, it isn't well known. So that was cool.

The Ramen. I asked for whatever was on Chef's Table and the most popular. Honestly? The Ramen I got was Average at best. Nothing Truly stood out to me. This review is difficult to write. Won't lie, expected a bit more.

Overall, definitely a bit on the pricey side, but it's NY. And it's gotten a lot of press, being featured on an awesome show. Definitely care more for the story than the food.

Came here on a Monday lunch just past 12:30. No wait. Ordered the shio pork belly rye ramen. Soup and pork belly were perfect. But the rye noodle was overlooked. And didn't really taste any different than wonton noodle. Service was very friendly. Overall it was good but not really worth a return trip considering the price. Portion size is on the small side, quite common for New York standard though.

Everything I thought it would be. Originally got the Tokyo Shio Ramen but then my friend got the Ivan Special Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen and HOLY FUCK. Best ramen experience of my life. I definitely prefer thicker noodles than the thin, so the switch out literally made my Ivan Ramen experience everything I hoped for! I'm from LA so this was my first dining stop when we got to NY and I'm so beyond stoked. Oh the Sake Sangria was delicious as well. Thanks guys!
Excellent Gluten Free Ramen.  So nice to have food this flavorful and interesting and GF.

My friends were visiting on the weekend and they reserved this place for Sunday brunch.
