I was pleased to see that they had a clearly marked vegetarian ramen option as well as some sides, and thus I would be able to eat something with my mind at ease. I was about 10 minutes late on account of weekend MTA tomfoolery and they wouldn't let my friends take their table until I arrived. Just something to note if you have a group booking and perpetually late companions.

The server we had was prompt and friendly. He came up right after we sat down and asked if we had been there before. As we hadn't he gave us a run down of the menu and his recommendations. The triple pork ramen was his number one.

We ordered fried chicken and pickles for starters. My friends ordered the triple pork and chili ramen and I had the vegetarian. My friend and I got the yuzu lemonade sake cocktail while the other got a draft IPA.

My friends really enjoyed the fried chicken, so I will give it the stamp of approval on their behalf. The pickles were also delicious and so was the yuzu cocktail. My friends both really enjoyed their ramens. Mine was just alright. I prefer creamy broths rather than clear or soy sauce based. The broth was tasty but salty, although it had a more rounded flavour than just soy sauce. I found the rest of the ingredients were not that substantial. The main item (aside from the ramen itself) was green lettuce, which wasn't mentioned on the menu. With lettuce I can take it or leave it, but definitely prefer it fresh than in a hot soup. But yes, I know that hot lettuce is a part of asian cuisine. Aside from that there was a half tomato, one enoki mushroom and a few bits of tofu. I'd have liked to see some more substantial vegetables packed in there.

Another note is that the draft IPAs are fairly small in size, 12oz for $9. I think it was because they were craft and high in alcohol content. The selection was decent and I was not familiar with a lot of them. They had a reasonable bottled/canned beer offering also. Some were pricey at $14 but were from craft breweries and high %.

The service here was really good. I felt our server was very present and always checking in without being pushy. Other staff also asked us if we needed anything when they walked by. My friend ended up with the wrong beer - they dealt with it well and were happy to offer him a new one. It is nice, clean and bright inside. Long high tables and a bar with seats, and a nice looking covered patio at the back. It managed to be full without being noisy and staff were calm rather than stressed. They have only one washroom so there was often a few people waiting for it.

Honestly by far the best vegetarian ramen I have ever had!! Delicious broth, which can sometimes be difficult with vegetarian ramen. Plus the staff was very nice and everything came out really quick! An excellent stop on a chilly day on the lower east side.

My boyfriend and I went here with a group of his friends, and was suggested to us because of Chef's Table.  The ramen was subpar for how expensive and the portion size.

The reason I'm giving one star is because despite the waiter splitting the bill exactly three ways, two cards and cash, he mixed up mine and another dining companion's card.  This dining companion and I happen to have the same TD credit card, and the waiter placed the cards in front of us.

After the meal we went our separate ways and I went home.  While checking my email later that night, I got an email about spending $50 dollars at a theatre refreshment stand.

In a panic, I looked through my wallet and found my dining companion's card and not mine.  I went through the hassle of calling the bank, putting in a dispute to get the charges reversed, and getting a new credit card at the bank the next day because I needed it immediately, and I didn't know my dining companion.  Unfortunately, my bank could not print me a new card, so I had to wait until Tuesday and it created a lot of unneeded stress.

I emailed Ivan Ramen to make them aware of their mistake, and to see if they could refund my money.  Although they were sympathetic, my companion and I happen to tip the same amount.

Because of this experience, I give the restaurant one star.

It is a good to try.

I have to say that their ramen is not cheap. Of course, everything is expensive in Manhattans.

If you wish to have a different kind of ramen, this is the place to try. If you want to have more traditional Japanese ramen, you might want to go a different place. I do like this place but I can see that some people may not like it.

Their chashu is great.

First time I tried the food was last year- like many others I was fascinated by the chefs story on Netflix series-, loved the food and the drink. Second time two weeks ago,  I order the same ramen, so disappointing, horrible. Appetizer chicken soaked in salt and burnt, noodles in ramen rough and not cooked well enough. Extremely Unhealthy- and horrible taste! 
"Consistency" is the key for me to be a permanent customer...I'll have unhealthy food once in a while but only when it is exquisite, not just cheap! I'm not going back to this place ever again!

1.5/5 not sure what the hype is around this ramen spot...

Fried chicken appetizer was larger than we had expected, which is good, but then with the taste, I would have been fine eating less of it. The sauce taste like something i would get out of those frozen chicken you buy and make at home.

I order the supposedly spicy ramen with extra pork since I was starving at the beginning of the meal. The ramen was way way too salty to me. No hint of any spiciness (and i know i wasn't expecting insane spice coz you know that doesnt rly exist in japanese food) this was just pure salty. The pork wasnt bad but also wasn't amazing.

My friend's soups were not that great either i forgot what they ordered but we all got different food. I was probably the most upset one but they were also not v happy with theirs. One tasted like the chicken broth msg thing i buy from Chinese market.

It would have been a 2 or 2.5 hadn't been of how overpriced this place is. I probably won't be coming back. If my other friend saw the hype somewhere I'm just gonna drag him/her to some other places I want to try around the area.

The flavor of the broth was really basic as well as lacking flavor and the noodles were like the ones you get out of the packet. Had great dark beer there but that's about all I would recommend. I wouldn't go back again.. just gotta step up their flavors

Definitely not your traditional ramen but tasty it is! The chicken paitan ramen is so flavorful and unique- I highly recommend this bowl out if all the others. The noodles here also have more of a bite which I personally prefer. It is pricey just like any other ramen shop in the city but if you're looking for something different, this is the place to check out. I'll definitely be back!

The fried chicken was amazingly good! We ordered spicy ramen but it was definitly not as good as the appitezer. It was actually rather disappointing. It was only a bowl filled with wheat noodles, eggs and bok choy. I love spicy food but the broth was not to my taste.

Definitly not the place you want to go if you want to have more traditional Japanese ramen.

However, the service was good.

I got the shio, which was serviceable, but nothing to write home about.  Ratio of soup to noodles was off - I wanted more soup.  Also, the noodles were a bit too soft.  The broth itself was tasty and the ingredients included were good - hard boiled egg with soft yolk, enoki mushrooms, scallions, pork belly.  I also got the roasted tomatoes in the ramen per the waiter's recommendation.  It was tasty, but the oddness of it did not provide a commensurate wow factor.  The place was packed and there was a line out the door.  This is the type of place I wouldn't mind wandering into if there were no line.  Thankfully I had a reservation so didn't have to wait.  Friendly, knowledgeable staff.  Maybe if I'm in the neighborhood, I'll come back and try something under Ivan's Specials.  The regular ol' shio ramen was definitely not worth the hype.

I love good ramen, and this place knows what they're doing. I don't think I can make recommendation, because it's all about what kind of ramen you like, but I haven't had a bad bowl of Ramen here. yeah the wait can be long, but get here early.

This place is BOMB! Sat on the patio which was nice but the heat lamps are a little too hot. Felt like I was getting cooked myself. Ordered the Pork Bun for an app followed by the Spicy Tonkatsu. Both were very good. Will definitely be going back next time I'm in NYC!
My favorite is the spicy Ramen. What I like about this place is that they always put a twist on the traditional dishes. The decor is pretty cool too

Checked this place out after picking up my kid from school.  I was excited to find this one but I was overwhelmed by the quality of the ramen noodles - for a specialty ramen place I expected more quality noodles - the ones I ate tasted like they were of the pre-packaged variety which was a let down.  There are better ramen restaurants in the neighborhood.

This review is based on what I ordered and experienced. Your experience may differ.

The service. If you are going to try this place, I recommend you to call ahead and make a reservation. Or else you would be waiting for 45mins, luckily for me, they put me wit other people in a table. So I didn't wait that long. My waiter was kind and friendly, it felt as he welcomed me in. 

I ordered chicken Paitan as recommended by the waiter. I had say the flavor is great but way too thick in your throat. I had to drink every time I slurp. The noodle itself is delicious, had a bite to it. I would just come back for the noodle. I wish there was more sides on the dish to enhance the taste of the ramen. I know you can order more side but I believe it should already come with it. Half boiled egg, bean sprout, bamboo shoot, pork belly. It's a good effort to recreate ramen from Japan to New York. Can't really say much more but it was good in its own way, but I wouldn't say authentic ramen flavor.

Next thing I ordered is the Pork Bun. I love pork bun so I was expecting that I would love this one too. But for me, the slice of pork is too thick for the bread. Maybe make the bread a little bigger but the same thickness or a thinner slice pork. Just get the right between the pork and the bun. I seen it done before, maybe more of the glaze sauce. But the flavor though on the pork, is delicious. But the pickle radish (I think that's what in it) wasn't necessary. Replacing it with green onion maybe better. I just think the pork bun is great by itself without another layer of flavor on top of it.
Apparently you need reservations for the place, but the Vegetarian Ramen was awesome!!

We went to Ivan Ramen on a Saturday night and had to wait the standard 45 minute wait. It was totally worth it though. First off, the area is great to walk around in. While we waited we walked down the street to Yoppari and had some Sake to get in the mood. Great and small place with a wonderful staff. When we got a text that our table was about to be ready we paid and walked right over to Ivan's.

The decore and atmosphere is great. The tables were a bit tight but honestly you don't even feel it. The people that come to Ivan seem to know a bit about the chef before they walk in. If you don't know, Ivan was featured on the Netflix series Chef's table. After making a name for himself as a Ramen chef in Japan, he came to New York with his skills to open up the acclaimed noodle shop. 

When our server came up he asked me what I wanted and I replied, "I'd like to have the best bowl of Ramen in the World." Although I was a bit sarcastic, he immediately pointed me in the direction of the Chicken Paitan. We also ordered a bowl of the Spicy Red chili Ramen and the Japanese Fried Chicken Appetizer. 

The fried Chicken is a must. It was crunchy and tasty bite sizes. I would usually not order an app at a ramen place, but I noticed that the Ramen bowls at Ivan are smaller than your traditional bowl of ramen. Which was great since it allowed us to try this superb twist on fried chicken. Sweet and flavorful. Totally recommended!

Chicken Paitan: This is not your traditional Ramen. I believe that a bowl of Ramen can truly tell a story and Ivan's rendition of the ageless soup truly tells his own. I have never seen a bowl of Ramen served with a lime before (although I hear its becoming a thing), but it was a great bit of fusion. My lime was a bit unripe, but I'll forgive the kitchen for that one. I was squeezing the life out of this lemon until I hurt my wrist. I didn't come to work out my fingers! The bowl was great and different, but again this isn't Ramen... This is Ivan's Ramen. Totally recommended dish.

Spicy Red chili Ramen: This dish was Far too spicy!!!! If you're into that sorta thing, then you should get it. The flavors seemed great, but I couldn't handle a whole bowl of this on my own. Also, I'm usually a fan of the Hardboiled Egg, but here they mix the egg inside which wasn't my favorite. My partner, who loves spicy food and orders things that are titled Spicy Red Chili Ramen, also agrees that it was a bit too spicy for their taste...

I would totally go back to Ivan, and its definitely worth at least one visit. We ended up spending $100 total for all our courses plus a bottle of Sake (along with tip and taxes).

Enjoy!

I have to say that, I chose the wrong ramen (haha) Shio ramen. I wish I actually got a different ramen and that is best, I tried the triple pork and was it porky oink oink oink. I wish I tried the special ramen because those had more of a depth of flavor.

Legit great ramen! We kept hearing about this place from coworkers and friends. They quoted us a 1.5 hour wait for a party of 3 at 9:30 PM but we were able to get swayed by 10 PM :) We got the spicy shout ramen- a solid 7/10 on the heat scale, the double pork mazamen, and the chicken paitan. Everything we ordered was excellent and worth the wait.

Great service, fun atmosphere, and that's about where the positives stop. We wandered over at 8:30 on a Saturday night without a reservation and were seated around 9:45pm. I ordered the Shoyu ramen and my boyfriend ordered the chicken peitan ramen and the kyori pickles. My Shoyu soup was like drinking soy sauce--it was inedible. I very nicely asked if I could exchange it for a Shio ramen (the classic). Thankfully, the waiter was super nice and agreed right away, but the next ramen just tasted like nothing. My boyfriend's chicken paitan soup broth was delicious, but the noodles weren't on par with what we'd expect from a high grade ramen bar--tasted more like instant. He really liked the kyori pickles though. 

Overall, probably going to be disappointing if you have to wait but maybe worth a trip if you make a reservation? Didn't live up to the hype about the Chef.
Watched the Chef's Table on this, so of course had to add the roast tomato-so good! Had high expectations for the Ramen, and they were exceeded! Pork bun appetizer was also incredible.

We were visitting from out of town and a friend of mine swore by Ivan.We made reservations for the day after we arrived. The japanese fried chicken was pretty good. I got the Tokyo Shio Ramen, which was alright. I tried someone's chicken ramen (Ivan's favourite), and I think that is the way to go, because it blew my ramen out of the water... I totally regretted not ordering it. Ah well, next time I'm in town!

Short, but sweet review: this ramen is amazing, and you need to get it. Prices were reasonable, we didn't have to wait in line during lunchtime, the casual yet informative server helped us pick the best dishes for us, and the food was outstanding. Best ramen I have ever had, and I'm usually one of those people who automatically is suspicious of things everybody else likes ;) I'm surprised this place doesn't have 5 stars straight across- I would be here weekly if I lived closeby.

I got the shoyu ramen, but it was a bit salty for me. My friend got the shio and it was pretty good. I like the vibes and the workers are very friendly and helpful. I would go back for the shio, not shoyu.

Filling delicious comfort food. Sinple menu - choose from 5 specialties, 5 ramens, 5 cold apps, and 5 hot apps.
Came the day after David from Chef's Table did. Lovely view from the bar.

Got lucky and waited about 30 minutes to get a seat at the bar. What a lively restaurant. Fun experience and great ramen! Had the pork belly bowl and the original/standard bowl. Both were unique and well executed. Highly recommended!

I'm not at all embarrassed to admit that we made plans to go here after watching a FoodNetwork documentary about Ivan Orkin and his ramen.  C'mon - a Jewish guy from Brooklyn who moved to Japan and set up an empire doing Ramen IN JAPAN?!  The comes back to NYC and does the same thing here ... we had to see this (and taste this for ourselves!)

It was a snowy Saturday in December, and we had been walking around the Winter Village at Bryant Park, posed for a photo in front of the tree at Rockerfeller, and were ready to warm up with something yummy!  Around 2:35 we asked for a table of 4, and were told an hour wait - no big, headed over to a coffee stop around the corner.  Within 35 minutes, our table was ready - hoorah!  

We lucked out at had a seat at the cool indoor/outdoor space in the back; somewhat like picnic tables and long benches - much more comfortable and less crowded than the actual restaurant (and ANY other Ramen shop I've been to).

To start (hey - we were hungry!) we decided to share the Steamed Pork Buns, and SO glad we did! Two come to an order, so we ordered 2 orders since there were 4 of us.  These were pork dumplings on a whole other level - soy-mushroom glaze, pickled daikon, steamed pork, fluffy delicious buns... YES.  I probably could have happily eaten all 4 of these myself.  But onto the Ramen. 

After debating for about 10 minutes, we ordered.  My husband ordered the Chicken Paitan, which was a less traditional Ramen, and more Ivan-style Ramen.   I almost ordered this but didn't in favor of trying some more of the menu.  It was described as a "sort of jewish chicken soup-style ramen"  - a rich chicken broth, minced chicken, egg yolk, shio kombu, and rye noodles.  It was served with a lime for extra acidity if the consumer wanted.  I tried it and it was delicious.  The broth was a bit thicker, sort of ... silky? Had a smokiness and cozy flavor - not too salty - I would order this next time!  

Like I said, I ordered something different than him; I HATE ordering the same dish as my husband - there's nothing to share!  I ultimately went with the Vegetarian Ramen (I added minced garlic chicken) - This was a more "traditional" ramen - soy sauce & vegetable broth, enoki mushrooms, roasted tomato, koji tofu, and rye noodles.  I couldn't get enough of the noodles or the mushrooms - both of which were fantastic.  Mostly salty and ramen-like; non-traditionally, it is served with a roasted tomato which really added depth to the dish!!  Very good!

The good thing about this place is that it takes reservations, has more seating than most Ramen shops, and doesn't rush you through the door.  Lots of options for non-fish eats or vegetarian peeps (not all ramen shops have multiple dishes for vegetarians!)  Very good, I would come back for the Chicken Paitan - it was so good!

I'm not a NYer but Ive finally been around enough to know my way around the eateries this city has to offer. Ivan Ramen is easily one of my top 5 ramen choices! You had better believe the hype. 

More importantly. Do. Not. Pass. Up. On. Those. Buns!

Was so excited to visit after seeing it on Chef's Table. I ended up coming in solo, and sat at the counter. I made a reservation which I would definitely recommend because it gets busy, but they did not rush me out of there by any means.

I immediately got some amazing recommendations from the server, and promptly inhaled the food. I had the steak special appetizer (it was some sort of magical fried steak that I wish I could remember what it was called) and also had the pickles which were SO yummy. I opted for the Chicken Paitan ramen and it did not disappoint! 

Can't wait to come back, it was a great meal on a chilly night.

Best RAMEN!!! 

I'm not much of a ramen kind of gal but this place has definitely got me hooked on their ramen!! It's amazing, the chicken ramen is very good the broth is full of flavor and it's got a rich kind of fatty taste to it that's so very delicious. The pork buns were ok, the fried chicken is much much better definitely recommend it! 

Make sure to get there early, we got there five minutes before they opened and there was already a group of people waiting outside. Within an hour the entire place was full

Stopped by here a few months back.  The place was mostly empty, just wanted a quick bowl of simple ramen.  I order a bowl, and the waiter asks if I want pork with it. What kind of ramen has no pork or meat in it, that should be considered a default, so I said yes of course.  During my meal, the waiter harrassed me every 5 minutes for 'kaidama' (more noodles).  As the original amount of food was so little, I said sure.  When the bill came out, much to my surprise, it was multiple times the original listed price for a bowl of ramen on the menu (they had charged something like $6 -$7 for the piece of pork in the ramen! I guess if I had not ordered it, it would have just been a noodle soup?).  I had never payed so much for ramen in my life.  But regardless of the price, the waiter was the worst part of this experience. For whatever reason, it seems he made it his mission to rack up as many costs on me as possible, and he was very aggressive in his doing so. It's a shame, I would have been a regular customer as the ramen itself was pretty good, but I will never return after this experience. Gave it three stars despite the terrible experience since the ramen itself was pretty good, despite the service and price.
The service was good even though the restaurant was super busy.  The ramen was delicious.

Ivan the Terrible! 

Tricked. Bamboozled. Scammed.
Ya know that feeling when you walk out of a restaurant and you're not sure what to say to your date and then both of you burst out with "that was the worst ramen ever" at the same time?? Oh- I see- you've been here too!! 

These are the words that came to mind as I chewed the flavorless noodles. The sickening feeling that you are not even going to be able to pull the haze of self delusion over your eyes and think "this is interesting." Ivan's ramen is not interesting, it's not ramen and it's not good. 

And yet- throngs are waiting for tables. What is it?? I guess the same thing that brought us here- chefs table-- but we will never be back.

The service here is really great, they're so nice and welcoming. The ramen is solid too! Not sure why this place doesn't have better reviews, I was a little skeptical because of it but I'm glad I gave it a try. They have lots non traditional ramen and appetizers. Unfortunately I didn't have a chance to give the apps a try but I did get the spicy ramen (forgot the exact name) and it was good definitely a ramen with a kick. And I also got to try the triple pork ramen which was really flavorful. The triple pork didn't come with that much broth I think it was supposed to be like that so it brought out the flavor a lot. Anyway I would give it a try and not think too much about the reviews below. I don't think it's overpriced either considering how much GOOD ramen is in nyc anyway.

Saw this on Chef's table on Netflix so was greatly interested in trying. It sure didn't disappoint. I came here with a group of 4 on Saturday around 6:30. I think the wait was perhaps an hour which was fine because they take your number and text you when your table is almost ready so we just went to a bar nearby. When we were texted, it was a simple confirmation and were seated immediately when we arrived.

We started with their pork buns which was amazing! It's two per order. The pork belly was super moist, soft and flavorful with some I believe picked daikon. So good! 

Then I got the Tokyo shio ramen with added topping of roasted tomatoes. Had to do it because that was what made them so unique, adding roasted tomatoes to enhance the umami flavor. It was very delicious. The chicken broth was super flavorful and the noodles were plentiful with a nice chew. I liked the raw enoki mushrooms and scallions as it added more texture to the dish. 

Very good and definitely worth a try!

This is my second time here, the first time when it first opened. I had the shio ramen, which is the basic dish that you would judge a ramen restaurant by. That was okay. But today I went there and tried the tsukemen. It was very disappointing. The flavours are unbalanced, often leaning to too salty. I've had incredible tsukemen in Japan, and my partner is a ramen chef from Tokyo so I think I am at least well versed enough to know from good to not good. I am baffled how he gets so much publicity and media coverage.

We first heard of Ivan Ramen through the Netflix series "Chef's Table" (must watch!!!) and were so excited to have the opportunity to actually experience it. 

The location is small but typical for a New York restaurant. We were a party of 10, which we know may be difficult to seat, and were told it would be a 2 hour wait. The hostess never asked us if we were willing to split up the party in order to sit down faster (there were a few 2 seat tables near each other, a 5 seat table outside, and a bar with 6 seats free). Half of our party ended up leaving so we sat at the bar on our own accord with the help of a different hostess.

Having tried many traditional ramen restaurants I opted for the Chef's recommendation: Chicken Paitan. It was very flavorful and I was able to add a lime for the perfect amount of acidity. I really enjoyed it! My boyfriend had the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen which was more of a traditional dish. It was a very rich broth. The eggs were amazing.

All in all I enjoyed my experience and I would probably visit again when I'm in New York
Best ramen! Flavorful, savory, perfectly cooked noodles. Also, the Pork Buns as an appetizer rocked!  Saw this place on Chefs Table as recommended by a friend. I will be back soon!

Wooohoo! After watching the Ivan Ramen episode on Chef's table, I was determined to try this place in New York. I placed a reservation for two however there were some vacant tables when we arrived for dinner so it might not have been necessary. The service was prompt and we were excited to order. We got the Ivan ramen and it was incredible! The ramen was cooked to perfection and it was one of my top 3 ramen places. I would highly recommend trying this place out and seeing what all the hype is about. It is worth it!

Please, don't go here if you are planning to try this place because you saw this on Netflix show. Have a low expectation. Don't get hyped up. Don't wait 2 hours like I did to try it coz its not worth the wait. I have tried ramen all over the world. I don't ever bother to write reviews but because of the Netflix show, i am sure a lot of people believe this place is actually good. 
FYI: while waiting for 2 hrs to try this mediocre ramen, we tried Rizzos Pizza 2 blocks down from Ivan. Mind blowing amazing.

Came for ramen on a cold winter Wednesday afternoon. Was a tad bit late for my reservation but it wasn't a problem. Ordered the ramen and added the signature roasted tomato. Pork bun was a bit underwhelming but the ramen was good. My colleague and I did not was the egg yolk just the egg white and they were able to accommodate. Overall was a good experience. Unfortunately Ivan wasn't there. Would have loved to shake his hand after seeing him on Chef Table a week before. 

Until next time!
Better than advertised, the Coney Island Tofu was a pleasant surprise! Wait can be long, so definitely make a reservation.

I heard that it's always best to get reservations here but by the time we decided to make them, they were fully booked. (This was on a Friday. There were no openings until Monday). We took a chance and got there at around 4:45pm. There was only a 5 minute wait. We sat and we're quickly greeted by our server. He was very friendly and explained the menu and offered suggestions. The appetizers and drinks came out very quickly. The ramen came out about 15 mins later. Everything tasted great. We had pork buns and Japanese fried chicken for starters and then Chicken Paitan and Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazeman. The chicken came with rye noodles which are thin and considered vegan. The Triple Pork Mazeman came with whole wheat noodles which were thicker to pick up the thicker sauce. Both were great. I will definitely be back and want to try the Spicy Red Chili Ramen. We even met the owner on the way out. He was very personable and wanted to hear our opinions on our experience. We shared a few laughs before we left. I would say if you're going on a Friday evening, try to get there before 5 to avoid the rush, especially if you don't have a reservation.

Much like a lot of other reviews my boyfriend and I made reservations, on Open Table, to visit after watching Chef's Table the Netflix documentary. We were so excited to be able to eat the food after learning so much about the man behind its creation. 

We visited on New Year's Eve but the place wasn't too busy; there were people waiting but we didn't have to wait because we made reservations.

The staff is really friendly and knowable.

Ivan is a Jewish man that lived in Japan. This is accurate to the food, because it is average at best ramen with overpriced Jewish deli prices! It's okay, but literally any other ramen place will give you the same quality at a cheaper price.

Ivan ramen is awesome. Apparently the owner was on some sort of cooking tv show but the ramen is legit. 

We had the Ika fried rice as an appetizer, which has rice, squid, a side of lemon, and probably crack. Because it's really good. The ramen is likewise also pretty good. I'm pretty picky about my shio ramen because light (assari) broth ramen is hard to make flavorful without being too heavy but Ivan ramen does it. Also appreciated that they gave tons of shredded green onion. Portion wise it's the standard ramen bowl size. There's more I wanted to try here because the menu looks good so I'll be back.

P.s. the spicy ramen is spicy.

I saw this place as many have in the Chef's Table episode on Netflix. I have to say, it certainly lives up to the hype. I always get this Triple Pork Triple Garlic bowl that comes with about half the broth of a normal ramen bowl. The service is great as well. Highly recommend checking it out.

I had a terrible experience here last night. We had a reservation at 8:45 and we were sat at 9:30. The hosts were incredibly rude, there were no apologies at how late they were on our reservation. We were yelled at by the staff for being in the way--but there was no chance we were going to stand outside waiting for our reservation which they were already half an hour late on. They then sat us in an OUTSIDE area in the back and said very casually that there were some blankets if we were cold...We were freezing. 
Nothing on the bill was comped--there were no apologies for how long we waited for our reservation. The food was delicious but was absolutely ruined by the terrible customer service.

Sigh. I wanted to like this place because it was recommended, but this was pretty disappointing. 

I got the spicy ramen on the waitress's recommendation. It was spicy like she mentioned, but it felt like two competing tastes. The first sip was tasty, but then it hit the back of my throat and it felt like I just inhaled a spoon of chili powder. The spice level was fine, but the chili powder on the back of my throat during the entire meal was irritating. It came with a smashed egg sitting on top of the ramen. When I took a bite, it was cold and after dunking it in the warm (not hot) broth, it was only a little better. 

GF got the shoyu ramen. It was decent, but not to the quality or toppings quantity you can get at ippudo, ichiran, zendoya, or many of the other great ramen places in NY. 

I might give this place another try to check out the Ivan specials to see if those are what makes this place stand out.
Chef Ivan and Ivan Ramen's reputation is spot on. One of the best bowls of Ramen you'll find not only in NY but the world alike. Umami at its finest!
Real good food, a little pricey. The staff was really nice. They ask for reservations because it is a small place.
Fairly decent entry level ramen but really not as inspired as I'd been led to believe. Noodles were a little disappointing but service was quick and friendly.

Dined here on a Sunday evening. Table for 2. I was seated on a bar beneath a mural of some sort. I was told a 45 minute wait, but was texted about 30minutes later that my seats were ready. 

I'm making my way through as many ramen spots as I can, and Ivan Ramen has been on my list for awhile. I was a little nervous about what I would encounter with Ivan's recent "Netflix" fame, but my evening turned out great. 

The service really set this apart for me. Our server was calm, cool and collected, extremely attentive, and really made our dinner special. He walked us through the menu, somewhat casually but very knowledgeable about everything. Suggested his (and Ivan's) favorites and almost wouldn't let us choose otherwise. In the end we followed his guidance and were extremely pleased. Food was delicious, served fairly quickly, and waitstaff was attentive when it came to refilling water, bussing tables etc. 

Definitely in the upper echelons of NYC ramen spots, this one is a must try.

3.5 stars which I believe is a good solid rating.

Where were you when I needed some soup during the arctic blast last week, Ivan? I'm an all year 'round soup kind of gal and don't eat it just during the cold months.

Seriously, I wasn't familiar with Ivan Ramen before this recommendation.
It's all things related to ramen noodles and then some. 

Apparently Ivan Ramen is a celebrity of sorts having been on Food Network and from the stellar/positive reviews I read.

Upon arrival (btw, reservations are accepted), the cheerful restaurant had various seating options.  There was bar counter style, table/chairs, counter and a smaller enclosed room in the back.

After going through 20 questions with the waitress, we settled on ramen broth (as opposed to non soup). She was super helpful and service was very attentive. Never an empty water glass for long.

Back to our order. Our selections were vegetarian and the chicken Patain (my choice) soups. We chose the seasoned pickles for starter. 

Verdict? 
I enjoyed my first time at Ivan Ramen. My soup had a lot going for it (although I couldn't identify some of the ingredients). My soup seemed to be the highly recommended one and the most ordered. The noodles were plentiful and the explosion of combined flavors also included a soft cooked egg. I asked for the least salty broth and the waitress suggested this one. However, the broth was still quite salty. Very brown and salty.

I also enjoyed the pickles which were dressed with sesame seeds and red chilli flakes so it had a nice, spicy kick to it.
Overall, we were pleased with our selections. I think the price point is a tad high for a medium sized bowl of soup.

I'm not too familiar with Ramen soups and the varieties, but I assume this is a good place to explore if you want to get started.
Good experience.

The Coney Island tofu was some of the best fried tofu I've ever had. It looked lightly fried and it was so soft in the middle.  The triple pork ramen was so flavorful with a thick cut of chasu. The veggie ramen broth was so rich and flavorful too.

I discovered Ivan Ramen after watching Chef's Table last year. Since then, I've been here about 6-7 times which speaks alot about how good their ramen is! 

Ivan Ramen is an essential spot whenever I have friends in town. I love talking about how Ivan Sorkin, a Jewish guy from New York ended up opening a ramen shop in Tokyo. Note, the ramen here can't really be compared to the likes of Ichiran or Ippudo. The ramen here is inspired by Sorkin's Jewish roots, e.g the use of rye noodles. Very interesting flavours come out of it, and I would definitely concur that Ivan has perfected the art of achieving "umami". 

My tried and true recommendations:
Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen
Chicken Pai Tan Ramen

It does get crowded though so make sure you come early or call ahead for reservations. Service here is great and this 5 star review is well deserved. I wish I could give them an extra star for being RIGHT next to my favourite bubble tea spot, Boba Guys. Nom nom.

I feel immense guilt whenever I give a restaurant 3 stars when they're more of a 3.5. Solid, but I don't particularly feel the need to come back, especially with so many other options for ramen in NYC. 

Went on a weekday night at were quickly seated at the bar. We started off with some chilled greens. I was hesitant about ordering this because cold vegetables aren't really quite my go to, but this strangely stood out to me and I really enjoyed it. For the main, I got the tonkatsu ramen with the tomato (the umami tomato that they talk about on Chef's table). Again, solid broth, but nothing particularly stood out to me as excellent. Even with the roasted tomato. 

I'm glad I came here before I watched the episode on Chef's Table, otherwise I'm sure I would have been biased in some way. Maybe the more non-traditional ramen would have impressed me more.

Pretty good ramen, good flavors. Felt a bit rushed while eating. Ordered some hot tea, which came in a can which was fun. My husband ordered a beer which was tiny and expensive. I'd like to try it again.

Great service. Ramen soup was excellent, so were the pork buns. Garlicky ramen noodles were also very good. Even enjoyed the music they play. Beware tables by the door on a cold night, also back room everyone was wearing their parkas. I enjoy soup on a cold night and we got lucky to sit at the counter.

Honestly, there is too much scallion, and the strong smell just couldn't go away. BTW I came because of the Netflix documentary, but I found the third season of the serious just not reliable. Very disappointed

Seeking a quick late lunch, my family of four ducked into Ivan Ramen. While our four soups had a few green leaves and were hot, they were very salty and a bit too spicy for my kids. We had no beverages. What shocked me was the pricetag. 16 dollars for noodle in so so salty broth? This snack on the way to capoeira turned into $85 dollars for two adults and two kids.

Excellent ramen! The broth on our shoyu ramen was incredible. The chicken patein was wonderful. The triple pork ramen terrific! The people are truly friendly, helpful and knowledgeable. We tried the green tea and it was not the norm and flavorful.
Best ramen I've ever had; hands down! Had the vegetable ramen with an egg - delicious! Very good beer selection too. Good layout. Will definitely be coming back

Came here for a dinner on a Saturday evening. We had a wait time of about an hour, which we expected to we went to a bar nearby to kill the time. 
I got the spicy chicken ramen and husband got the chicken paitan and we both thoroughly enjoyed our ramen. I loved how unconventional the ramen was , but yet satisfied our ramen craving quite well.

First restaurant featured on Chef's Table I've actually be able to go to & it did not disappoint!
Sat at the bar to get a feel for the kitchen & everyone seemed to really enjoy working there which gave the place good vibes. 

Listen to the wait staff's recommendations & you can't go wrong! Even gave a shot of some sake on the house! 

Excellent experience all around!

Ivan Ramen was highly recommended and it did not disappoint. The staff were incredibly friendly, the service was very fast and the food was absolutely delicious. In the past I've not been a huge fan of ramen but the flavors present and the high quality of ingredients blew me away. They also have a large selection of non-ramen dishes with many wonderful appetizers and noodles entrees. I would certainly go here again, and would highly recommend it to anyone who's in the mood for noodles.
This place was GREAT - I had the chicken paitan and it was delicious. Rich chicken broth with lots of yummy noodles. Great sized portion, super satisfying and delicious.

Made a reservation for my birthday and little did I know, it'd also be a dinner celebrating my engagement :) The pork buns were insane! Highly recommend. Also got the brussels sprouts to start with. We all got different ramens to try and all were very good. Especially the Triple Pork Triple Garlic's broth! So rich. I got the Tokyo Shio and my fiancé got the Tokyo Shoyu and we requested the roasted tomato to be added to each of them and it was a very good decision. Fantastic beer list & fantastic service. Can't wait to go back next time we're in the city.

Summary: Service was very good. Food was mediocre at best. Price was outrageous.

We sat down and waiter was very friendly and explained every item on the menu. We ordered and food came within 2 minutes which included 2 bowls of ramen and a japanese style fried chicken.

The speed of food delivery was a bad sign already. Let's start with the ramen. I ordered the spicy chicken ramen and my wife the chicken broth ramen. The noodles was plain and simple. I immediately recognized it's a chinese style noodle. Nothing wrong with the chinese style noodle, it's just that I can walk down the street to china town and get the same kind for $6. The broth was mediocre at best, tasted like a lot of chilly oil on a salty soup. I also found some pieces of egg and a little bit of minced pork. All of this for $16 dollars.

For the same price you have many other options:
1. Take a subway to china town for $2.75 then order a real chinese noodle for $6.95. Save the remaining $6.3.
2. Take a subway to midtown for $2.75 then order a real paitan at Totto ramen for $12.
3. Take a subway to Brooklyn for Mu Ramen.
...

The japanese style fried chicken is $12 and it does not taste good. If the hot sauce is not enough to cover the tasteless dry meat then there's ranch sauce for dipping.

2 stars for food quality. 5 stars for service. I can't eat service so 3 stars overall.

I was really excited to try the Chicken Paitan ramen after reading so much about it. Tried to get a table on a Sunday night - they told us an hour wait, an hour and 40 min passed and still no table, so we gave up. We came the next day right at opening for lunch (noon) and got a table right before the big rush (seems like there's always high demand). 

The chicken pai tan ramen was very very rich. I didn't think the yolk was necessary and made it even more rich. The first few bites were good but I honestly felt uncomfortably full and pretty gross for the rest of the afternoon. I think the clear broth based ramen is probably much easier to digest (although not what it's known for). The Coney Island tofu was a cool concept, but I thought the taste was too sweet and I didn't enjoy the flavor. 

Overall, a bit disappointing, probably given how much it has been hyped up. Will probably stick to more low-key ramen spots, but is cool to say you went to a Chef's Table restaurant.

It was a pretty grey rainy day on Sunday and I felt like it was a great opportunity to get a hearty bowl of ramen...I watched Ivan's "chefs table" episode and made it my duty to make it to Ivan Ramen. I had a pork bun and the chicken paitan after talking to the waiter at the bar (who was pretty helpful with sake, beer, and food choices) I was left so full and a happy camper after not just getting very helpful and enjoyable service my meal was hearty and filling where I wanna make more trips to Ivan ramen and get disgustingly satisfied again!

This place is amazing. Incredible, westernized take on traditional Japanese (and other pan-asian) fare. 

Good beer and sake selection. I was impressed to see cans of Nightshift from Boston on the menu. 

We ordered a pretty big spread of appetizers and entrees. I had the Dan Dan noodles which were an incredibly inventive take on the classic dish. It incorporated brown butter miso and squash into the dish's normal Sichuan spiciness. This was complete, of course, with some really tasty noodz.  

I would also recommend the Daikon with XO sauce. While I feel like XO sauce tends to run the gambit of "wow this is way too fishy" to "oh man this is way too fermented", Ivan's XO sauce is definitely a great balance of these flavors without being too far out of the western palate comfort zone.

I was recommended by a friend to come here for the ramen. I was unfortunately very disappointed. The ramen was very small in portion and I'm a very light eater to begin with, then, the one slice roast pork was very tough and the soup base was a little too salty, there was half of an runny egg, and that was it for toppings. I was quite disappointed when I saw the ramen and was even more disappointed when I tasted it. Lastly, it was also expensive. It wasn't too crowded when I went but I have seen this place being packed. Perhaps it was a one-off bad experience?
Oh man, that chicken paitan ramen? SHEER HEAVEN. I think I inhaled it far too quickly because it was so delicious. We also shared rose carafe, the pork buns and the tuna squared. Ramen goodness.....

This is good place for some delicious Ramen! Gets pretty busy so make sure you book ahead! For appetizers the cauliflower is delicious and so is the fried chicken! Very tasty and filling. Highly recommend the spicy chicken ramen (it's def spicy!) 

The ramen we great tasting with allot of flavor. Highly recommend this place!

Whoa.  Where to begin when the name has been so hyped up & then the delivery is so poor. My Ramen partner and I stopped by for a quick warm dinner -- she had warned me multiple times that this place was over rated, but we were hungry and wanted something quick on this cold evening. Hunger couldn't mask this. Got the Shoyu Ramen; my mouth and tummy were damn disappointed. The noodles weren't cooked prooerly-- came out clumpy and undercooked. The eggs were cold (? How??, behooves me). The broth was too salty and improperly seasoned-- basically drinking soy sauce. 
This style Ramen caters to a very american/western concept and taste bud of Japanese food. For two who have a strictly Asian diet, we hope to speak from experience. Save your 16$ (overpriced) and take it elsewhere. Please.

Sad,i really want to like this place so much but the ramen is really salty...me and my friend finally got the chance to try this place,we order japanese fried chicken as an appetizer,nothing special,kinda soggy for my like and doesnt really have a lot of seasoning,i had to eat it with  alot of hot sauce.as for ramen,i order chicken paitan and my friend order triple pork  tonkatsu ,the server said both is their popular item.first bite is good (maybe i just too hungry and expect something amazing about to happen)and then from there is just go down the drain,the more i ate the more i can feel the saltines,the server had to fill up my water everytime he passed by.my friend experience the same,although i like the texture of noodles that my friend got,and for the 1st time we end up cannot finish our ramen.1 extra star just for the nice service,but so far this is the worse ramen i ever had.
Best ramen anywhere, warmed my sole!!!  Lives up to the hype.  Be sure you make a reservation in advance.
Ramen was great in flavor. Nice viscosity of stock egg cooked perfect. Chicken could have been better but was still good. Bao were really good and you get two per order definitely recommend them.

Ivan Ramen lives up to its reputation. The ramens are all excellent--I prefer the shoyu among them--but the mazamen is the thing to get. Full of strong umami flavors and depth, this is a bowl worth celebrating. The tofu coney dog is a fun and tasty snack and the pastrami buns were a great twist on and tribute to some of New York's greatest food traditions. My only complaint is that the sizes of the beer on tap are very small.

I don't understand the hour line.  Service is good. But the ramen flavors are not.  Had the pork broth... which was fatty yet lacked flavor.  Wife had a chicken broth that was just odd (too much cloves?).  The noodles also have such different texture (which does not appeal to me).  I much, much, much prefer Hide Chan, Totto, Ipuddo, etc.

We decided to try this place out after striking out at Clinton Street Bakery.  We were interested because all the food people raved about it.  Perhaps that set expectations too high because we found the food underwhelming and all around salty.  Cramped seating (guess a LES standard?) and the service was...odd.  The Draft IPA wasn't too bad but beer is beer is beer.

Was very excited to come here after watching Chef's Table. Unfortunately, place is very over hyped. I am happy I came to at least try it out but won't be coming back. The service was phenomenal though and great beer selection.

Were it not for the other dishes, I'd probably give this place one star higher but unfortunately some of the dishes were pretty regretful.

FOOD QUALITY:
It's nice to have perfectly cooked cauliflower, topped with peppers for a small kick, .. then sprinkled with day old chopped green onions, ... and sitting under a miso sauce that doesn't taste like miso?  What first sounded like a promising good idea suddenly became a regretful decision despite this dish being recommended when the flavors just fell flat like when a club plays the same song ten times in one night. Somehow their sauce and the old green onions failed to bring out flavors such that we could hear the patrons next to us even complaining about how heavy it is. 

So we decided to get the "Japanese Fried Chicken"  -- call it chicken karaage and your waiter will be confused; this still boggles my mind. 
The chicken itself had this nice yuzu-barbecue flavor to it, but the aoili-ranch really cut the heaviness of the breading. But there was this weird zing. Kind of a small, pungent pull that tasted like raw cilantro. It was forgivable, until minutes later when I realized that the breading completely mopped up all the sauce so all the crunchy texture drowned equally as fast as our initial impressions. 

So at this point we're hoping for the ramen to do us justice, and it kind of did. Tokyo Shio Ramen still resembles almost everything but Tokyo, but of all the ramens I've had I really liked the chewiness of the noodles that could absorb the flavors of the broth while retaining its texture. This is done the best. BUT... after the tenth bite I found myself kind of wanting to get this bowl over and done with; the amount of green onions is quite staggering and its flavors argue against the shio broth instead of working together. TL;DR: medium flavor, good texture, weird ratios.

SERVICE:
They fill your glass of water without asking, but they had a tendency to spill a little over the cup. 

ENVIRONMENT:
Tiny, cramped, small. Watch your limbs if you're clumsy as my friend got bruised when she turned and accidentally hit her hand on something. 

Overall, the price is a little offensive but if I were to disregard the price it's a decent bowl of ramen.

A hip little ramen place that, while not exactly similar to what you might have in Japan, is still worth a visit.

Ivan Ramen is a cute little ramen place in the LES.  It's surprisingly spacious despite the small entrance.  Prices are a hair high, but not unreasonably so for the area and/or Manhattan and general.  The vibe is hip and food-focused, which I liked.

The ramen here is pretty good, though not particularly the best I've had.  I tried one of their specials, the Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen, which I found tasty but a bit simple - it was a single powerful flavor and some pretty great noodles but not much more than that.  Definitely add an egg.

Sitting here paying the bill and couldn't contain myself from writing a review. Staff is very knowledgeable and maintain great energy, as a server myself I know how repetitive it can get. My server Marvin walked us through the menu and I still couldn't keep my eyes off of the triple pork triple garlic, while not a soup it was so delicious. Still perfectly coated in a tonkatsu broth. Pork buns were great. And the miso roasted cauliflower had nice heat but a little too rich for me personally. All in all the experience was great. Thank you Ivan ramen I will be back.

I love Shio Ramen wherever I go and it was a nice hip place that had an accommodating staff when I messed up my reservation on Open Table.

If we examine each component of the ramen:
Greens - unnecessary and added nothing to the ramen (which there was something more edible like spinach or something?) 

Egg - well seasoned and well cooked

Broth - could taste the bonito flakes and the broth had a richness to it; wish there were other components to elevate it (idk I was expecting the roasted tomato or something) It would have made it sweeter / more tart at the same time.

Noodles - well cooked and still had a good chew to it. Warm little cozy place to escape the cold of NY.

Inventive ramen menu with some classical combinations but also some unique choices.  The chicken paitan ramen was rich and delicious.  The pork buns and the Coney Island tofu were standouts as well.  Everything was a little salty.  Service was friendly and attentive.  Fun place for a group.

I had high hopes for this place bc it had so much buzz online. Went here for the first time today and got the chicken ramen with pork belly on the side as recommended by server. I would say it's about 3/5. Texture of the ramen was great, and the pork belly was slightly charred on the outside and melts in your mouth...BUT the broth is extremely salty (and I eat A LOT of ramen on a regular basis). I literally had to pour my drinking water into the soup to dilute it. I would suggest whoever come here to get the vegetarian ramen (4/5) in instead and add whatever you want to it bc that's what my friend got and his was way better than mine. Oh well. I'll stick to Totto Ramen and Nakamura next time.

5/5 for service. The server was extremely nice and attentive. So thank you so much!

My hubby and I had a late lunch/early dinner here last week right before getting on the road to drive 6 hours back to Rochester, NY. We weren't sure what to expect based on the varied reviews, but I was insistent we try it since I am a fan of 'Chef's Table' and loved the episode about Ivan, his broth and his rye noodles. And I am happy to report our experience was a good one!

We arrived around 4 pm and just beat a huge rush of people with reservations. We were super happy to have snagged a table along the 'graffiti' wall, and to have a couple of servers who also seemed to be foodies. They were intimately familiar with the menu, able to answer all our questions and make recommendations for us, and they were just really friendly and fun.

My hubby ordered the triple pork/triple garlic noodles. He was pleased with the whole dish - volume of noodles, seasoning, and also with the amount of broth, even though our server pointed out that this dish was really more of a dry-noodle dish than a ramen/soup dish. 

I got the Tokyo Shio Ramen. I just wanted to try the 'basic' one so I have something to compare against ramen of my past and my future. It was delicious! Those rye noodles have the perfect texture, the broth was rich and delicious, and I added roasted tomatoes to mine since the tomatoes were noted as part of the 'umami' in the Chef's Table episode. 

I forgot to note that we started our meal the crispy mushrooms and squash appetizer - basically tempura vegetables with a delicious dipping sauce. Perfect portion for sharing, excellent crisp batter, and the mushrooms were hen of the woods, instead of what we expected (oyster or shiitake)....and if you know the flavor of hen of the woods....they were amazing. 

We will definitely be back and will bring friends!

I come here for one thing and one thing only: 

Triple Pork Triple Garlic

One of the best bites of food in NYC. Get this one item, be happy, go home. You'll thank me later. 

I don't care about anything else in this restaurant; haven't tried it, not interested. 

Don't care about the service, its very good but even if it wasn't, don't worry. Place is packed like crazy but looks nice, not important though. 

Just get this one item every time and keep coming back, ok?

My sister is also a Yelp Elite and spoke very highly of Ivan Ramen after watching some documentary (or reading an article) about it. He was a ramen chef in Japan who came to America to pursue his dream and his restaurant blew up with popularity and fame! I made a reservation for 4 and was excited to see what they had to offer. I guess I missed the memo that this place specializes in chicken ramen... and I ordered the one tonkotsu broth they had which wasn't even a full bowl of broth, but rather a half-full bowl of broth with regular amount of noodles (why tho). It was way too salty and the ramen texture was nothing special. The bean sprouts and other vegetables were nothing special, not fresh, didn't enhance the taste and overall really disappointing. I even tried my other friends' chicken ramens and they too were overly salty, and nothing special. I was pretty upset that Ivan Ramen didn't live up to its hype! Should I go back and give it another try? Did I just order the wrong thing on the menu? I'm not sure, but it also definitely was pretty standard price for ramen ($14-18/bowl) and I know so many other places of the same price that I prefer. What to do, what to do... What are your thoughts?

Super stoked to go here after watching chefs table. The fried chicken was spicy and delicious. The cauliflower was so interesting and delicious. I had the spicy chili ramen that was soooooooooo spicy and awesome! My wife had the OG chicken shoyu. Honestly, that was not super flavorful. It may be very authentic but I've just had a few that are more enjoyable. Overall... so great! Loved it.

This place is so freaking dope. Eclectic fun interior, friendly welcoming staff, great tunes, incredible beers. We inhaled the Brussel sprouts. I've been there several times and been able to try lots of different ramens and they are all super tasty!

First off I'll just say I love Ivan Ramen's story. Jewish boy from Long Island learns to cook ramen in Japan and becomes a Japanese star. He then has a glorious homecoming and opens a killer restaurant in the New York City. I want the movie rights. 

The restaurant is just super cool. Great eclectic music and a colorful, cozy interior. We sat at the bar which was perfect because we had a line of sight right into the kitchen. 

We started off with the Tofu Coney Island. Really whimsical and delicious concept. The texture of the tofu was perfect, and the addition of mustard was inspired. I thought the sauce overall could've used a bit more body and maybe some spice, but overall very good. 

For my main course I ordered the spicy red chili ramen. Usually spicy ramens aren't quite hot enough for me, but the spice dial on this was tuned a little higher and I loved it. I would've preferred a classic slice of juicy pork rather than the ground pork that all sank to the bottom, but the texture of the rye noodles is exquisite and more than made up for it. I'll be back!

Saw this place on the Netflix serious my boyfriend and I were really excited to try this place out... 

Shop was cute well decorated- enjoyed Ivan's story. Yet the ramen was just OK? Even went ahead and got the tomato yet which was a weird sweet taste to the ramen. This pace was over priced and not the best. Sad and disappointed we had high expectations.

I went to  ivan ramen  after watching the chef table on netflix. So i went there with high expectations and ordered both triple pork and chicken paitan for  myself. I have to say the flavor is too salty and strong for me. Besides that the noodles are super great. But still I m disappointed.
Best ramen I've ever had in my life. I had the chicken paitan. If you like ramen and you have a pulse their Is no doubt you should come here.

Best ramen I've ever had. The serve up classic ramen here and also have put their own touch on it. I go here every time I am in NYC some times multiple times. Very cool aesthetics, kind of a small place so make a reservation or put your name down and wander the neighborhood, bar hop until they can seat you. Well worth the wait. Service is very friendly. Semi noise but hey it's NyC. As for other things to eat you really can't go wrong I had to fried chicken and it was killer. All I can say lastly is that you must check this place out if you are in NYC you will not be disappointed and if you are something is probably wrong with you.

The pork buns and the triple pork triple garlic mazemen were delicious. I tend to be a little turned off by fatty meat and surprisingly the pork belly in the buns wasn't bad however the pork belly in the mazemen I couldn't eat. I would like to go back to try their other versions of ramen.

I was super interested and excited in trying this place after seeing it on chef's table and I'm glad it's as good as I expected! Really a 4.5/5 for me.

We got the chicken paitan and Tokyo shio ramen and there is so many layers of flavor in both dishes. The chicken broth was rich, tasty, fatty, salty but not too salty, and the rye noodles almost had a smoky flavor to them, so so good! I just wish they were more on the chewy side. Adding roasted tomatoes is also a must! It's supposed to enhance the umami, and I must say it sure did.

Def not your "traditional" ramen (I mean lime in your ramen? Wut??), but I don't think it's trying to be. It's Ivan ramen! I think it delivered on all fronts and it's a must try if ever in the LES! Wish I also tried the triple pork triple garlic mazemen. That's going on my list for next time.

After watching the Netflix series, I was excited to try the his food. It was EPIC disappointment! Everything was super salty and the ramen broth was eh... the apps were all very saucy and salty. Nothing was memorable. It was almost like every dish was trying too hard with a ton of stuff all over it.

After seeing the whimsical episode of Ivan Ramen on "Chefs Table", I knew I had to give this place a try.  As a veg, I usually find it difficult to find a good tasting broth for Ramen thats also packed with veggie goodness.  Since coming here initially back in October, I have made many visits and always enjoyed my time.  

The place is ALWAYS busy, put your name on the list, grab a beer around the corner at some bar, and they will call you when the table is ready.  Speaking of beer, thats one aspect of Ivan that keeps me coming back, they have an amazing bar program!  Beers such as Gun Hill Brewery, Hill farmstead, Hudson Valley, etc.   I noticed a lot of sours or gose style beers frequent the menu, which I think actually pair quite well with the Ramen.  The staff is super knowledgable about the beers and food, friendly, quick all around great experience.  

The vegetarian Ramen is interesting as it is a soy sauce base (rather than some that are more of a clear veggie broth).  But this gives it a great depth of flavor, especially with the addition of the mushrooms and roasted tomato.  The noodles are perfect al dente, and made with Rye which is something I have never seen before.  mmmm, just writing this review makes me want to take a trip back there and cozy up with some great beer and Ramen, cheers Ivan!
Omg best service I've ever had. The triple pork and triple garlic is what you need to order. And the beer list is insane. Best ramen in nyc.

Ivan's Specials are certainly unique and have a very different flavor profile from traditional ramen, but maybe I'm more of a purist. The Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen ($16) is bursting with garlic flavor and the noodles have a nice chewy texture to them, while the Chicken Paitan ($17) is very...chicken-y, in a good way. On the recommendation of Chef's Table, we decided to add roasted tomato ($3) and was expecting a burst of incredible umami flavor, but they were just regular tomatoes. While the special ramens we ordered were both yummy, I felt like they didn't give that deep soul-nourishing, heart-warming feeling that traditional ramen usually provides. After watching the episode of Chef's Table, I really wanted the meal to be life-changing, but maybe I went in with my expectations too high. The special ramen is definitely worth trying for the novelty, but I would choose Totto or Ippudo over Ivan any day.

The pork buns were delicious but the ramen didn't live up to the hype.  From the aggressive marketing I was expecting a slap in the face kind of flavor bomb. But the broth was under seasoned at best. Definitely better options in NYC.

Service was good. Much more hyped than expected, especially after being featured in Chefs table. I got the chicken paitan which was good but not great and my other half got the shio ramen which I just thought was not very good. It almost tasted fishy to me and lacked flavors, while the paitan was very salty. Personally I did not enjoy the minced chicken would have much preferred sliced chicken. The noodles themselves were delicious so that is the biggest selling point for this restaurant for sure.

The best ramen I ever had. And I have had many many many. 
We had the chicken paitan and one that had pork, veggies, the egg and mushrooms, I believe it was the tokyo shoyo classic, it was SO good. 
No way to describe it. The price was a bit over... manhattan... right?
The atmosphere super cool/chic/cozy... like a mix of lounge and asian chateau.. i don't know... very nice. Apparently great place for drinks as well. Unfortunately I was pregnant at the time.. BUT the food was tremendously good. Great spot for quick meal or a dinner date.


Order the chicken aperitif its the best! (japanese fried chicken)


The service. Very on point and sharp and fast, and rude. 
Maybe its because its a busy place and theres a line at the door through out the night and people waiting to sit but still... its not polite to rush a guest, a paying costumer... I don't believe is something any business owner would advice even if the place is poping and popular. 
Politness and friendliness is half of the experience...

Anyways, I still will come back again :D

The best noodle ever!!! Perfect what else 
Is the best ramen I never try, the staff is cool 
Just one things they doesn't accept reservation!

I watched the Netflix show about Ivan ramen and I was quite intrigued. So my wife and I took a trip on a Saturday night. Totally forgot how busy it gets. Thinking with my stomach...it's a two hour wait. So we waited!

We didn't really had one server. So there was no real customer service. The hostess ended up talking with us about the menu. She was very cool and friendly. We ordered the pickles, Japanese fried chicken, shio ramen and chicken paitan.

The pickles were great! When we got the chicken, it looked to die for! Extremely disappointed because the batter was great but it was tossed in a very salty sauce(and I love very salty foods) and the dipping sauce was great but it had too many flavors so these two heavy sauces was just a big mash of flavors and it made us both sick. 

The chicken paitan and shio ramen was really nice but the fried chicken ruined it for us. The servers took the chicken off the check and apologized. But if you're reading this, it's not a bad place, but I really think momofuku noodle bar is better.

I went on Saturday morning, and waited in about a 20 minute line to get sat at the bar. I got the triple pork, triple garlic mazeman and it was great. The main reason for the 4 star review is the price is pretty steep for the amount of ramen and food you do get. And yes it is better quality than some ramen places but there are other places that give you significantly more for the same price and the same level of quality.

Went with a friend and ordered the wings to split as an appetizer and the chicken paitan as my main course. Wings were to die for, I could have eaten a whole plate myself and I loved he ranch dipping sauce. Chicken paitan was the best ramen I have ever had. Super tasty broth with perfect noodles- lived up to the Chef's table hype! 

tip: we went at an off-peak time of around 4 and got a table right away with great service

I had been asking my boyfriend to come here being that we both love ramen and I wanted to see what all the hype was about.
 First thing we noticed was the gross pickled cabbage smell but we forgave it to try what we thought would be some of the best we tasted in the city....
The Devil is a Liar.
 Whenever we go to a new ramen place i always order the pork buns because i love steamed pork buns....usually.
These had some pickled (cabbage?) Instead of the standard cucumber/lettuce spicy mayo combo and im not not opposed to trying new things but this was not a good flavor combo for us.
 Now on to the main disappointment 
Triple Pork, Triple garlic ramen....
Barely any broth, one piece of pork, and what reminded me of bacon bits all in the soup with something once again pickled (bean sprouts?) . We ate because we don't waste and I paid because I felt bad for dragging my boyfriend here. 
 I do encourage you to go and experience your own disappointment. But if youve had Ippudo and Ichiran this place comes no where near those broth and flavor filled bowls.

Came here with a friend on Friday at around 3:30 and it was PACKED. I was so surprised there were so many people eating at this time of the day, and luckily we managed to snag the last table available. I've been to Ivan ramen before, and while the flavors were good, the prices were and still are a bit steep. The concept is intriguing - white Jewish chef moves to japan to learn about Japanese cuisine and brings it back to New York, and adds his own flair. No where else can you get fusion ramen like this - and it's delicious!

My friend and I started with the tofu Coney Island and the fried chicken. The tofu Coney Island was pretty bad actually - the tofu was no where near crispy enough and I thought the miso mushroom chili was weird. But the fried chicken was so good! It was nice and saucy which I like (big fan of Korean  fried chicken and anything down that aisle). The sauce was sweet sticky and delicious. The chicken was perfectly crispy, and the shiso ranch was so refreshing. 

I opted for the triple pork mazeman, whole my friend got the Tokyo shoyu. The tokyo shoyu was nothing special in my opinion; you can get a similar tasting ramen at Ippudo. The triple pork mazemen is Ivan's unique creative, and it is a delicious garlicky mess with a super tender pork belly. The sauce was rich and heavy, and it was exactly what I was looking for. When you eat this ramen, you get a sense of fullness that is pretty rare nowadays. A common theme with all of his ramens is the generous heap of green onion and slightly pickled bean sprouts (I think they were pickled they had a nice source crunch to them). 

When I came here previously I tried his version of the spam musubi which is missing in the current iteration of the menu. A bit pricey at $6 for 2 tiny bites, but it was a perfect bite of food. The pulled pork was tender and flavorful, but it was the roasted tomato on top that really make it amazing. The tomato is available as a topping on the ramens, and I HGHLY recommend everyone to give it a try. 

Overall this is a nice and very unique ramen joint in New York, and definitely worth the hype and all the videos he's featured on. It is pricey though, as all of the appetizers are over $10, and the ramens are $16 but quite small for that price.

Ivan Ramen is definitely a great place to take any visiting friends and family to eat. Ivan's status as a celebrity chef makes this a very popular place to eat ramen, so if you intend on eating there, make a reservation, otherwise I guarantee you will be waiting 1-2 hours to eat. In terms of dishes, the pork buns are hands down to die for. Buns are perfectly fluffy and warm, and the pickled toppings really make the buns amazing. In terms of ramen, all of the four options are delicious, but I would note the Shio ramen is the least impressive. Mainly because the broth is a bit watery and absent of flavor. 

My only qualm with this place is the pork. Every time I've eaten here, the pork belly in the ramen fails to execute. It's always been over cooked, making the pork rather dry and tough -- I can find better ramen elsewhere. Otherwise, Ivan is a solid place to take your visiting friend or mom to eat.

Ivan doesn't disappoint! Fun atmosphere with a great friendly staff. The food was served quickly and delicious, as seen on Netflix's Chef's Table. Recommend the fried chicken appetizer, and I enjoyed the Shoyu Ramen. The soft boiled egg was cooked to perfection.
Delightful. Superb. Out of this world. Even my chicken-hating wife loved their chicken. Seriously, go and enjoy it!

I eat a lot of Ramen, I've had it all over Japan and all over the US. Ivan makes a pretty decent bowl of Ramen but it's the smallest bowl of Ramen that I've ever been served and it's $16. The point of Ramen is that it's supposed to fill you up, I left hungry, with a bad taste in my mouth.

This is an absolute MUST every time I come to NY. The space and atmosphere is fun, and the staff are always lively. With so many great meals in NY costing minimally upwards of $75 a person, this place is great for budget-friendly, just amazing food that you will never regret going to have. 

You must try the yuzu lemonade, kyuri pickles, miso-roasted cauliflower, Coney Island tofu, ika fried rice, pork buns, and of course any of their delicious ramen bowls. This place hosts great dishes for carnivores, vegetarians and vegans alike.
The broth in the ramen is amazing and wait until you try these noodles! Out of this world and different from any other you've tried.

We had a 12:30 reservation (reservations are a must even though they do accept walk-ins), their first sitting of the day in the middle of the week. The restaurant was packed with a line out the door for people to get seated. That's something to say for sure.

Watch the Ivan Orkin episode on the Netflix show "Chef's Table" and you'll get a brief introduction as to why you must make a stop here. I'll be back every time.
It's different than traditional ramen and it's a good difference from tradition. But the meat is too thick and a little overpriced

I consider myself someone who knows ramen. With that in mind, I came into Ivan Ramen with HUGE expectations, only to be let down in the most saddest of ways. Tonkotsu ramen had only one slice of pork belly the size of half a credit card. The noodles where way to thin and there was no other ramen topping appart from a buch of greens. The broth was the saving point but that's it. It was so sad. To make matters worse, something was off because I was woken up in the middle of the night with stomach problems. I cannot tell you how much this has bummed me out.
Fried chicken wings were tasty but the ramen egh. It was insanely salty and not much in terms of flavor except salt.

Ramen is pretty salty. The texture of the noodle is a little different from your typical ramen noodles. I don't think I'd ever come here on my own. Just not exactly my style. My perfect bowl is a bit more soupy, and perhaps a little bigger in portion. Excellent service though!

Ambiance: hole in the wall and hip. Service very friendly but they won't seat you unless your party is with you. If you've watched Chef's Table and learned about Ivan, the restaurant exemplifies his personality.

Food: Definitely order: Japanese fried chicken, Tokyo shio Ramen (can sub pork for other meat) and chicken Paitan. Don't come here if carbs scare you...you'd be missing out tho. Rich and fresh flavors everywhere!

Totally coming back!

Bon apetit!

Like many others, I came here because of the Chef's Table episode. It did not disappoint - every ingredient blended into the ramen perfectly. A perfectly cooked egg and the noodles made me want to keep eating. We tried the Coney Island appetizer and it was really good! Much better than I had expected - would recommend even for those that aren't the biggest fans of tofu. The service was amazing - the waiters were really friendly and engaging. They gave awesome tips about the menu as well.

This is a very small, but quaint place to eat. Very intimate setting and the staff are all great and accommodating. I had ramen the pork belly inside. It was DELICIOUS!!!! My friend had the Dan Dan lamb noodles. It was very Spicy. But it was really good. It gets packed inside because it's very popular.  But it's a must go if you live in NYC and especially if you live in Lowe east side. Good eats!

Took the husband here after a weekend in Atlantic City.  He was apprehensive. I was having withdrawal shakes from something I've never eaten. Lol ! We shared the Japanese fried chicken. It was delicious. We have watched the Chef's Table episode about Ivan. To be clear I made him watch it 32 times.  That's how we were able to zero in on what type of Ramen we exactly wanted. I chose the Tokyo Shio Ramen. He chose the Spicy  Ramen. I immediately slurped my broth and I was in hog heaven. Husband loved his broth as well. The noodles were amazing. As was the egg and pork belly. I'm happy to say we will return with our two Vegetarian daughters.  They happily offer a vegetarian broth
Great food. Some people might think it's a little salty but I like the strong flavor. You can tell the texture of the ramen is quite different from the regular ones. The fried rice is not bad either.

Incredible. I LOVE this ramen restaurant. A friend told me about it and I always go on my layovers. The service is EXCELLENT and the food is amazing! 
They consider that everyone is there for their own reasons and want to make it special. They accommodated us despite how incredibly busy they were and it just made for the best experience for my bfs birthday. They genuinely cared. Thank you Ivan ramen and crew!

What can I say about Ivan Ramen except that the food seems... sloppy. 

I ordered the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen. In comparison to other restaurants, the actual content of the bowl was a bit thin. A few slices of pork, an egg and a piece of seaweed. It was as they were thrown into the bowl as an afterthought. My friend's vegetarian ramen was lacking, too. 

The flavor was underwhelming considering all the hype surrounding this place. It was nothing special and for the price, I'd recommend going to any number of ramen places around the city.

Wow!!! We visited here last night around 8:00 PM on our way to JFK for our flight.   Found street parking, so saved some parking money.   We did make a reservation so we got in fairly fast.  The garlic slices in the triple pork triple garlic are out of this world.  They were great.   We also tried the  Lamb Dan Dan (no soup in the bowl, so like a noodle salad).   Plus, we got the tempura mushrooms & Squash.   Great quality ingredients and very good broth in the Ramen.  This special dishes do not have as much broth as the traditional dishes, so you need to be ready for that.   The combination was very good.
