Based on the slightly grungy exterior, I was not expecting this ramen place to be so good! But once you walk inside, you are in a very funky but casual restaurant with great service. The Miso Roasted Cauliflower as a shared starter was to die for, and I had the Triple Pork Mazemen as my main. Would definitely go back again and try one of the actual ramen dishes.
Excellent ramen. Enjoyed the chicken soup version of ramen. The broth was perfect and the noodles were cooked so perfectly.
Solid ramen but everyone felt they had better. Would say 3 stars but the service was so great that we decided this was worth 4 stars. We loved the fried chicken too!!!

Overrated. Fried chicken was good but overly sweet. Spicy chili ramen was horrible. Tasted like Tabasco sauce. Pork buns were standard, one of the buns was stale. Fried rice was more like squid paella but was not bad. 

Wouldn't recommend for the price or the hype. It was fine and edible but not great.

Not that great compared to other ramen in NYC.

Was loud, not as filling, slow and unresponsive service, and more expensive than other places.

We came to Ivan Ramen as part of a "one ramen shop per week" initiative among our group of friends. We had heard about Ivan's story through Chef's Table and we were excited to try it out.

We managed to get seated with a minimal wait for our party of four and the waiter gave us a great spiel off the bat about the menu and the various ramen options (not your ordinary choices).

I settled for the double garlic ramen and we shared several appetizers for the table. The flavors were fantastic but I had two pickles with the food. The first is that I am not a fan of the unorthodox less-soupy style that Ivan uses (no fault to him just personal preference) and the second was that portion sizes were small and there was no option to add extra noodles. The fried chicken was absolutely amazing though!

My final note is that the back seating area is a little strange and it was super cold because one of the heaters weren't working. This place is a borderline five with just a few small negatives!

I heard many great things about Ivan Ramen and was curious to try it out. Keep in mind my experience with ramen is somewhat extensive, but I have found all to be disappointingly salty for my taste. I may just be a ramen hater.

Ivan Ramen has a really cool hip vibe and is nice and clean. We came right when they opened and there was a line forming outside. The staff are all really nice and enthusiastic with customers. They vibe off each other well, which translates to a really upbeat atmosphere. The music also matches the overall ambience of the joint. 

We ordered the Tokyo shio ramen and spicy red chili ramen. Once again, we found the ramen to be a bit salty. You don't notice the saltiness at first, but it gets saltier as you eat it.
The Tokyo ship ramen felt light overall. It didn't feel too heavy or filling compared to the usual ramen places.
The spicy red chili ramen, on the other hand, felt quite heavy and fills you up. The flavour is not too spicy, in my opinion, and has a bit of a peanut taste to it. It's very reminiscent of the Thai peanut sauce flavour mixed with Szechuan style spice.

Ivan Ramen felt very average compared to most ramen places. Their unique difference is probably their use of rye noodles instead of the usual wheat noodles. I would recommend you try this place out if you're into tasting spiciness (instead of torturing your tongue) in ramen and to judge for yourself if this ramen is for you. Perhaps I really am a ramen hater and this place wasn't quite for me, but I will say it's one of the better ramen places I've tried--the least salty of the salty ramen.

My search for non-salty ramen continues.

Awesome place a new Ramen joint that I am going to keep coming. Attention is on the spot and flavor above all does not Taste like a cup of noodles it's delicious Ramen with amazing flavors I want to try them all

I'm a traditionalist when it comes to ramen having lived in Japan but, must say the triple pork, triple garlic mazemen and kara age Japanese fried chicken were prepared with a unique blend of spices that worked. Flavors are strong yet balanced.  Chicken was plentiful, moist with just the right amount of crisp. Great beer selections and cool yet cheerful village vibe. I'll definitely be back to sample more on the menu in the eve.

Life is about balance.

You have a Jewish guy from Long Island opening up a ramen restaurant, but people don't cry "cultural appropriation" because he went to Japan to hone his craft and actually won awards.

You go to one of the Ivan food court outposts (in Gotham West) and aren't impressed, but think you'll eventually give the real deal a fair shake sometime.

And then you're inspired to finally go after watching an episode of Chef's Table about Ivan. It was the first video featuring him that actually made him sympathetic and not 100% an asshole.

So yeah, balance.

I was dining alone for lunch, so I was immediately seated at the bar with full view into the kitchen. Lots of quirky, fun artwork on the walls and generally great decor.

They also have an awesome beer selection, though you pay for it.

I started out with the fluke crudo, which was amazing. It was seasoned with pickled chilis, sesame oil, and slices of satsuma orange. Tangy, spicy, sweet. Balanced.

When I come back, I think I'll do the pickled daikon XO, since I love XO and the guy next to me got it, and I heard it was a favorite of the staff.

For my ramen, I went with the chicken paitan with an added roasted tomato ($17 + $3). It came with their signature rye noodles, with a runny egg, and topped with a TON of minced chicken.

The broth was light but also rich. The roasted tomato is a must for a burst of umami. Everything just blended together and the rye noodles had a nice toothiness to them. All together, it made for a great whole. Again, balanced.

I wish I had more stomach space because I would've otherwise done kae-dama with how much ground chicken and broth was left over.

If you can swing it and there's not too crazy of a wait, definitely stop by Ivan!

3.5 stars. Good noodles, but not worth the wait. Yes, it's been profiled on "Chef's Table." Yes, it's good. But was it worth waiting almost an hour on a Monday night? Probably not. Would I go back? Sure. 

I started off with the mushroom and squash tempura. It's a clever idea to use hen of the woods type mushrooms in tempura. Sadly, neither the squash nor the mushrooms had any flavor! The white sauce also had no flavor. Definitely would not order these again.

The triple pork triple garlic mazemen, on the other hand, was pretty good. Similar to a Chinese dry pork noodle, it featured the best cooked pork I have ever had in ramen. It's a nice fusion-style dish - the bacon and broth add an American comfort food vibe to the rich noodles. I could see this being a go-to comfort takeout dish if I lived in the area.

I love this place, I've been there many times with friends and family and we love it!! If it wasn't because I don't live in NY I probably would be there at least once a week. Service is friendly and the food is amazing, I try something new every time I go. I recommend you to make a reservation 'cause it is not a huge space, that means waiting time is longer than usual. Overall 5 stars for everything!!
The noodles are so fresh and delicious! You can ask for more if you still have broth.

Had a fantastic Friday dinner at this ramen restaurant. I've eaten a lot of ramen over the years and tried many places in nyc and Japan. This one stands out for the quality of the noodles - thicker, chewier and made with part rye flour - and for the flavor packed into every bite. My boyfriend had the triple garlic noodles (a low-broth dish), I had the tsukeman dipping noodles with spicy, flavorful greens, and we both shared the chilled shrimp over fried green tomatoes appetizer. Each dish burst with flavor and different textures, and even though some flavors seemed to hail from Korea or the south, they all blended well together. I definitely want to go back and try the more standard ramen as well as the spicy one (the person next to me had this and slurped up every last drop). Very happy that this experience lived up to the hype, and happier still that I made reservations and avoided a long wait.

It will probably sound cliche by now, but I found out about Ivan Ramen after seeing Orkin's episode on Chef's Table Season 3. I am in a constant mission of finding the best ramen, or at least my favorite. And along the way I'll be lucky to find some unique takes on it. I was really into Orkin's story, and knew I had to try out his spot as soon as I had a chance.

The restaurant has a nice clean & minimal ambiance. With great indoor and outdoor seating. I went ahead and started with the Japanese fried chicken, which I highly recommend getting. And I had to get the triple pork triple garlic mazeman, with a name like that who can't resist? I would name my 1st born son Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazeman. Keep in mind that there is not much broth in this and it is predominantly noodle being a mazeman. It was tasty but I would definitely be getting a regular classic ramen dish later on.

I saw this on "Chef's Table" for the segment regarding ramen and was literally the reason why I came to visit. I have had my fair share of ramen up to this point, and when it comes to Ivan's Ramen unfortunately I feel like it was average compared to all the other places I have been to. My friend and I tried the "Chicken Paitan w/added roasted tomato" and I ordered the "Triple Pork" noodles (this is my dry-based- not really much broth. One would have to pay an additional $6 for extra broth...) The "Triple pork" noodles were a bit more on the too salty end, while the "Chicken Paitan" was too too rich. This location did offer a great selection of beers and drinks but again this was on the pricier end. We also ordered the "Japanese Fried Chicken". It was flavorful but unfortunately did not spark any of my taste buds. 

The actual restaurant itself was really nice, and the staff were super friendly.

I liked it, but not really worth the hour wait. If a friend from out of town really needed to come here for the novelty, I'd go with them. Otherwise, probably pass.

Chicken paiten was good. Triple pork was a bit too salty for me. Staff was extremely helpful and friendly; they seemed to really enjoy their job.

If you are in New York, you must come here!  Our server Jon (aka Jam) was super knowledgeable and helpful about the beer and the menu. The beer list is incredible, and the food is amazing.  I had the vegetarian ramen and the tofu appetizer.
Had the Chicken Paitan Ramen.  It was phenomenal.  Service was also excellent.  Booked table on opentable.  No wait.

Like the majority, me and my boyfriend wanted to try this place after watching the saddest Chef's Table episode we've ever seen. 

I wanted to love this place so badly, but sadly it was only alright. 

The service was 10/10 - rather than waiting an hour for a table our server had us sit outside after they dried down the tables from the rain and we had the whole back area to ourselves for a bit. 

Appetizers: 7/10 - As a group of 3, we had the cauliflower appetizer and pickles as another appetizer. The cauliflower was so damn good, what do they put in there?! Nothing healthy that's for sure. The pickles were too spicy and there was way too much dill on them. Nobody wanted to eat them except me so I took one for the team and pretended to like these.

The actual ramen itself was VERY expensive (~$20 each) and not worth it. 6/10. Me and my boyfriend ordered the shio ramen and another one the waiter had recommended (chicken Paitan), both with the holy roasted tomato. The tomato was nothing special, I'd say do without it. The ramen noodles were a nice texture and quite flavorful, as was the soup itself in both dishes. But the shio was not as good as other places and the meat portions were so sad. Only 2 pieces of pork belly :( my chicken paitan ramen had much more flavor than the shio and I'd recommend getting this one since it's one of Ivan's specials. Save your money for shio elsewhere.

I'm so disappointed in this place. I love ramen but not for this price and wouldn't make the 30 minute walk back here from where I live for it again. Overhyped and overpriced, as most places in the media these days. Oh well.

My friends were really looking forward to this place. Meal started off with 2 flat diet cokes. Pork buns and Fried Chicken were very delicious. My Spicy Ramen was just ok - it was oily and we all had belly aches and indigestion for the rest of the day / night.

My friends know how much I love Chef's Table, so they surprised me tonight by bringing me here for dinner. We started off with Pork Buns, Fried Chicken and Pickled Daikon. The Pork Buns were delicious, definitely recommend getting them. Also, the Fried Chicken was easily one of the best I've had. There was a ranch dipping sauce that really compliments the flavors. As for the ramen, I got the Chicken Paitan. It was sooo delicious. I needed to add a little bit of hot sauce into it for a kick, but that's probably just because I love extra spicy foods. It's worth going to! I look forward to coming back!

First, amazing starters, especially the Japanese fried chicken, and califower. Second, amazing ramen, the chicken paitan and tsukemen are worth to die for. Lastly,amazing service. I give it a triple AAA.

We had a great time here! Ramen was tasty, my brother enjoyed the beer selection, atmosphere was upbeat (although definitely on the louder side). The noodles were some of the best ramen noodles I've had, would recommend!

The chicken paitan alone is worth 6 stars.  It's so, so good. It's a very simple dish done very, very well.  Absolutely divine.

It's rich and comforting but not too heavy in only the way ramen can be.  The broth is heavenly.  And the noodles... lawd. So good.

Other menu favorites: 

Apps- Japanese Fried Chicken. amazing fried chicken with some sort of sweet and tangy sauce and shiso ranch - excellent.

Tofu coney island- I didn't even know this was vegan.  So freaking good.  Like the non-processed, wholesome version of a ballpark chili dog.

Kyuri pickles- perfect light and scrumptious, and good palate cleanser.

Japanese Fried Chicken：best i've ever had in New York
Spicy Ramen：try it if you are spicy lover cos it's reaaally hot and spicy, in a good way
Paitan chicken ramen: greaaaaaaat!!!
Friendly staff and great atmosphere, I will definitely recommend to anyone looking for the best ramen restaurant in New York

Every time I visit NYC, I make a point to check out one of their amazing noodle shops, and this go around I found myself and two others dining at Ivan Ramen when the noodle craving hit.

We arrived at Ivan Ramen around 9 pm, and put our name in for three, but were told it was unlikely we'd get seated before they closed at 11 pm as there was a two-hour wait. Regardless, we left our name and began scouring the neighborhood for another option, when less than 30 minutes later, we received a phone call that a table was available for us.

We were immediately seated at a bar at the back of the restaurant, which goes back much further than you might think. The atmosphere was lively, with bright and funky colors and anime-like caricatures on the walls. We were greeted by a friendly-enough bartender for our drink order; FYI only the first six beers on the draft list are available despite the long list on the menu. Beers and sake were pricey - no beer under $8 or sake under $14, which I suppose is to be expected for New York.

We ordered the Spicy Red Chili Ramen, Triple Garlic Triple Pork Mazeman, and Shoyu Pork Ramen. Options were upwards of $16, but being our last night in NYC, we splurged on add-ons, such as a marinated, soft boiled egg. The Spicy Red Chili Ramen was *spicy* but full of flavor, though the noodles were thinner and broke apart easier than I've seen in other ramen. The Mazeman completely stole the show with the chewy ramen noodles, perfect melt-in-your-mouth pork belly, and deep garlic flavors. Though it doesn't come with broth, the reduced sauce is rich enough to satisfy your umami needs. Shoyu Pork Ramen was a classic option, with traditional ramen broth. Synopsis: If I had to pick, Mazeman all the way!

We had an overall enjoyable experience at Ivan Ramen, and left with warm, full bellies and a craving that was completely satisfied. The service was efficient, but didn't make us feel very welcome - almost snarky and pretentious - and the prices are a special occasion kind of night for us, but I'd be lying if I said I won't be thinking about that Mazeman from time-to-time.

I've been looking forward to visiting Ivan Ramen after watching the Chef's Table episode on Ivan Orkin. Really enjoyed hearing about his background. It was a pretty rainy day in NYC and I was in the neighborhood running errands and decided to stop by for lunch around 2 p.m. No wait, but the restaurant was pretty packed for  Tuesday afternoon. 

I'm obsessed with garlic, so obviously decided to get the TRIPLE PORK TRIPLE GARLIC MAZEMEN. Yum yum and yum. It's not your traditional ramen with lots of broth. There wasn't much broth and it's not your traditional soupy broth. I was a little hesitant of the whole wheat noodles, but I really enjoyed them -- pretty chewy and you can't really tell it's whole wheat, especially with the broth. The pork belly was a little too dry for my taste, but the soft-boiled egg (extra order) went so well with this type of broth. One of my favorite parts of the dish was the pickled garlic and the bean sprouts -- gave the dish lots of texture. 

I also ordered the SQUID FRIED RICE which was alright -- I loved that the rice was a little crunchy. There was a little bit of a kick to this dish as well. Overall, I enjoyed the meal. Don't think the ramen was worth $16 but I did appreciate the different take on ramen. I'll have to come back and try some of the ramen -- interested in the cold one next time!

Yeah, I'm definitely going to come back here!! 

Came in around 2:00 on a Sunday. They had some open spots and I got a seat at the counter right away.  There were enough open tables that I think they could have sat most parties right away around this time. 

I ordered the "TRIPLE PORK TRIPLE GARLIC MAZEMEN" which was absolutely to die for. This one comes light on the "broth" which was almost more like a sauce than a broth. But it was exactly the perfect amount. The flavor was amazing.  The noodles were perfectly cooked. I rarely eat all the meat in ramen bowls, same was true here, I didn't need the pork. I did eat about half of it, which was more than usual for me, but it wasn't anything special. 

When I come back I will want to try so many other things because of how good this was, but I will also be upset I can't have this too!

I will absolutely be coming back, likely multiple times to try all the other items!!!

So the chicken paitan is probably the only thing I really liked here. The other ramens I've tried were underwhelming. I don't really see why this place has such long lines (well, I guess in general most places do in NYC). Their ramens are not like the typical Japanese ramen spots in the city, since they use other ingredients like rye noodles, and also gluten free noodles. I guess it would be worth it to try this place once, but when I came back to try other noodles for the second time I was still underwhelmed. Customer service is pretty good though!

Very meh ramen, the chicken paitan was good but nothing amazing. The chasu was ridiculously big, so made it difficult to eat with ramen and was not as tender. I was very hype about this place but was met with disappointment. 

The staff was excellent though, very friendly and professional. 5 stars to them.
We wanted to try this place out since it was on Chef's Table so our expectations were high and thrilled for the experience. It was disappointing as the broth tasted bland and it was pricey.

As other reviewers- my husband and I found the ramen "meh"

We ordered the sticky buns and crispy eggplant for appetizers. The buns were awesome. The eggplant was okay. 

I got the Shio Ramen and it was good but nothing special. My husband got the Shoyu and it was terrible. The broth just tasted like soy sauce. Service was great and the place was packed. 2 hour plus wait on a Sunday night. 

Overall- it's good Ramen but nothing near how amazing Chef Table pretends it to be.

Came here because of netflix...no surprise. This place is expensive, there's no question about that.

Came here and got the chicken ramen + karage + cauliflower + pork buns.

This place definitely tries to be unique and make a spin on traditional japanese ramen places. 

The karage was very saucy (salty) and almost reminded me of korean bbq, except with much smaller pieces of chicken. Was not really a fan of it. The cauliflower was sauteed and then drenched in a miso sauce. I didn't think it was that special. The pork buns were tasty. Normally it's just some soft pork belly in a bun, they also added some sauteed onions (maybe a little pickled too). When I focused on that flavor a bit more, I didn't prefer it, but the pork belly itself is very nice. The chicken ramen...is quite unlike all other traditional ramen. The noodles are great and the broth is rich (which is unlike normal chicken ramen). They leave an egg yolk on top to be stirred in which gives you that extra moistness in the noodles which I liked.

Like many of us, I came to Ivan Ramen after watching the episode on Chef's Table. The episode followed a Jewish chef from Long Island open up a Ramen restaurant in the lower east side of Manhattan. Despite his struggles and challenges, he discovered his true passion in life and was given a ton of awards for his famous ramen.

Now, I've tried a variety of ramen all over New York City, so I was eager to see if his ramen was worth the hype.  A Jewish guy's interpretation of Japanese ramen does sound pretty whacky, but I was intrigued. 

The restaurant is located in the hustle of the lower east side. It's small, so If you happen to go on a weekend or for dinner, you may have to wait a while. There's quirky Japanese artwork and decor all over. The counter seating has a great view of the kitchen--which in my opinion, is the best place to sit. 

As for the ramen, I decided on the chicken paitan with roasted tomato ($15). It's his signature dish with the added roasted tomato. The broth was tasty, but I wasn't blown away. Overly salty, in my opinion. The overall dish was good, but not as amazing as it was hyped to be. 

I really really wanted to love this place, especially after watching the episode, but sadly it turned out just okay. Trying Ivan's Ramen is definitely worth a stop if you love ramen, but nothing to write home about.

Love this place.  Went the first time because of the show on Netflix, keep going back because it is awesome.   The Appetizers  are my fav!!  No Brussels sprouts today , but the cauliflower was a great substitute, and the Shrimp was nice.  The pickles are a must, yummy spicy.

The ramen is entirely different at Ivan Ramen than many other ramen places I've been to. Being a traditional ramen connoisseur it isn't quite my cup of tea, but I do appreciate the different types of ramen they have. My favorite is the Chicken Paitan ramen which has a silky smooth chicken broth flavor. The noodles at Ivan are great slurping noodles, and you can tell how good the quality of the noodles are. The ramen is quite pricey, so I expected a little more than what I was served, as the one bowl was not filling. 

My favorite dish at Ivan is the Japanese Fried Chicken! The caramelized Chicken is absolutely divine! Overall, the aesthetic at Ivan is very pleasing and is a place I could see myself coming back for an occasional lunch.

This review is overdue and mainly for the gentleman host for an afternoon shift on Thursday, May 10th at around 1:30pm-2:30pm. He was AMAZING. Not only was he hosting, he was also waiting tables and super punctual at multitasking - enough to warrant a few minutes of my time to write a review on Yelp. Just swift service, someone give this man a raise! 

Aside from the service, Ivan's is a favorite when I visit nyc. When I crave contemporary meets traditional ramen, Ivan's is my go-to.

A very enjoyable experience. If you've seen Ivan Orkin featured on that Netflix show, please don't let the hype get to you; understand that meeting and/or exceeding expectations about ANYTHING is difficult in our short-attention-span, instant gratification world.

I've eaten a lot of ramen and love it, and while I don't consider myself an expert (and reading some of these reviews, the internet and simply eating ramen and having an opinion doesn't make you one), this place was very good. I'm talking about the entire experience from start to finish. 

I arrived early for my reservation and my friend hadn't shown up yet, but the lovely staff invited me to sit at the long bar-like tables in the back and offered water or anything else I would like to drink as I waited. It was a hot day, so I was grateful for the hydration and air conditioning. I was able to observe what others were eating and drinking and take in the relaxed vibe. Every member of the staff was great. And they seated me at my table shortly before my reservation time, even though my friend had not yet arrived.

When he did, I was excited to order the drink I'd seen a couple get while I was waiting: Mio sparkling sake, served over what looked like a giant blackberry ice cube in a small glass. Absolutely delicious, and so refreshing! A winner. We were told it's seasonal, so get it NOW.

To eat, we had the Japanese fried chicken appetizer: addictive, crunchy, carmelized, garlicky goodness. I went with the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen, and my friend had the Chicken Paitan. Yummy, and DIFFERENT. Rye, thin noodles make for a bit of an unusual experience. Understand this going in, and you'll have a better time not comparing it to every other ramen you've had. We had a great time, and left oh so satisfied... but maybe wanting more of that sparkling sake. ;)
Ivan ramen is TOO GOOD! I've never experienced noodles that absorb the broth like Ivan's do. The spicy red chili ramen is my go to every time, so delicious. The sake drinks are also unbelievable.

My absolute favorite ramen place of all time. I have been to all of the top ramen shops in NYC, DC and all along the east coast and this place tops the charts by far. Ivan is a creative genius and I enjoy every bite of his delicious masterpieces. The pickled daikon is the most amazing tasty creation along with the spicy ramen. I could eat here everyday, such a treat when I get to go. Thank you Ivan! Keep doing what your doing.

It was a great afternoon to eat in the backyard. 

We tried some ribs... which were good.  Limited time menu item. 

The triple pork triple garlic mazeman was not what was expected by anyone in the dinner party. Felt like more of an Italian dish, but lacked in garlic flavor compared to what 1 may expect from a dish called "triple garlic..".

The noodles in the spicy red chili ramen is the best noodle I have tried in any ramen in NYC. The rye noodle is wonderful. Thin, light, absorbs lots of flavor. This should be a product for sale on it's own. 

We tried the squid fries rice. The squid was perfectly cooked. Really nice. Needs some squid ink. 

The crispy eggplant dish was delightful. Great mix of flavor and texture. 

Cool points for the chop sticks. They are textured at the bottom which helps keep slippery noodles in place! Great design.

I foolishly forgot to make a reservation on a Friday night, so I ended up waiting for an hour and a half to grab a table and even then, they were counter seating. Nonetheless, it was well worth the wait! 

We started with the fluke crudo, which was marinated in a sweet and spicy sauce, topped with orange slices, chili peppers, and scallions. Fluke is a pretty mild and buttery fish, but the marinade and the fruit were cleverly combined to yield a symphony of flavors in my mouth (a symphony of flavors is a reoccurring theme at Ivan Ramen). On our server's recommendation, we also ordered the cauliflower. The sauce was creamier (thanks to the shio-koji butter) and the roasted califlower was topped with chili peppers, scallions, and bonito flakes. Contrasted with the lighter, more delicate flavors of the fluke crudo, the cauliflower was creamier and richer (so good!)

I ordered the chicken paitan as that is one of my favorite ramen bases ever since I had it at the Nagakura Ramen pop-up at Ganko up in Boston. I would recommend it if you're a fan of tonkotsu as a soup base. Both are extremely rich, thick, and creamy. It's not the most diet-friendly/healthiest choice in the world (my bowl was covered in a layer of schmaltz), but I love the body and flavor it yields. Served with a raw egg yolk, minced chicken, scallions, nori, and lime (definitely needed that acidity), I found the soup to be a little too salty for my taste. Maybe I just needed some more lime to counteract all that richness from the soup and yolk, or maybe the minced chicken was too salty combined with the soup. Regardless, it was still very tasty with the rye noodles. 

My friend ordered the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen, which was well-received. I noticed that many people also ordered this (and the chicken paitan). Having sipped a bit of the shoyu broth, I still personally prefer the paitan but if you like chintan (clear) soup bases, don't be afraid to try the shoyu.

Went for late lunch on a Monday no reservations and we got seated right away, being from Boston with such limited Ramen selections this place made me VERY happy not to mention the beer selection was popping! i look forward to going back!! i got the Spicy Red Chili and didn't regret any moment of it ! the heat was great and well balanced ! boyfriend got the Chicken Paitan and i feel like that should be the reason to go there,, for that ramen. its Chef Ivan in a bowl and its delicious ! on the pricey side but its NY what else do you expect?
Delicious and flavorful ramen but a bit overpriced. Very nice staff though! If you are a ramen lover there is better places in NYC. We had the pork buns which were good.

Excellent ramen - especially given I am from Michigan and struggle to find truly good ramen here. 

The kyuri pickles were surpisingly good - very well balanced heat and acidity. 

The triple garlic ramen (with an egg) was very, very good. The texture of the noodles was spot on.

Sat outside on the patio in the back, which was nice and casual. The service was on point - servers always asking if we needed anything and brought out the food quickly. The squid fried rice, Japanese fried chicken, crispy eggplant, pork buns, miso-roasted cauliflower, and triple pork triple garlic mazemen were perfectly done. Ivan Orkin definitely knows what he's doing...10/10 recommend for a casual, inexpensive, and delicious meal!
Great ramen and service. Cute place to meet someone for lunch and catch up or to talk biz, lively but not too loud for conversation. Good menu options and choices.

Great food, but long wait; make a reservation.

Service: Heard good things about this place so friends and I made a trip all the way from Queens just to have some ramen. The wait was ridiculously long, but we gave a number and waited at a nearby bar. When we weren't called for 2 hours, we checked and it seemed like they lost our place/number. In the end, the manager came over to apologize and seated us immediately with a complimentary app. Next time, we'll call ahead. 
Food: Pickled daikon was super delicious thanks to the toasted shrimp topping. It was so hard to savor it till our ramen arrived. We ordered the miso-roasted cauliflower app as well along with vegetarian ramen, triple pork triple garlic mazemen, and some other stuff which were all good. Definitely coming back again.
Decor: Pretty cool/interesting artwork inside.

This place was fantastic. Our party of three ordered and split the Japanese Fried Chicken (good), Pickled Daikon topped with fried shrimp and scallop (mind-blowingly delicious, I could have eaten a bowl of the shrimp and scallop topping by itself but the daikon provided a nice contrast), the Triple Pork Garlic Mazeman, which I also adored (you have to really be a garlic lover for this one though.  With a healthy dose of raw, pickled and roasted garlic will taste and have garlic wafting from your body for about a day afterward - worth it though.  Also had the Chicken Paitan Ramen with egg yolk, the broth was rich and delicious and the rye noodles, which I'd never had before in a ramen, gave that same toothy bite that I love in buckwheat udon, making for a much more texturally interesting and satisfying dish than those made with wheat or rice flour.  .  The acoustics aren't the greatest for tableside conversation though but the food is so tasty that you probably won't have time to chat.  The carafe of unfiltered house sake was sweet, not my favorite but interesting and contrasted well with the salt/umami blast most of the dishes provided.  I'll definitely be back.
The food was amazing, staff was amazing, everything was AMAZING!!!!!!! Honestly the best, silkiest tofu I've had in my entire life. 10/10 will return. get the watermelon/tofu nigiri it is weird good.

Ivan,

When in Japan you lost the meaning of ramen How did you concept friendship warmth and love meant orofit in NYC. I am sorry but sir you have lost it.

Michael Sato Osaka
Try the Tofu Coney Island!  Absolutely delicious.  I had the Ramen w the pork belly eggs and tomato with the sea salt broth and it was out of this world.

I decided to visit this spot after watching the Netflix special on the chef. I've had ramen in Japan multiple times and it's pretty good in comparison. Although my expectations were fairly high; it did the job.

Came here for a birthday dinner and there were 7 of us in the group, with reservation on a Saturday. 

SERVICE - Very friendly staff. Our server gave us good recommendations. We arrived a bit late but thankfully the host was very accommodating and we were seated right away. Appetizers came out fast and drinks were served right away.

AMBIENCE - Our group was seated in a backroom with 3 larger tables. (There was also another open-air section with 2 other tables adjacent to us.) It felt very intimate in there, casual and relaxed. I also loved the rustic decor. 

FOOD - Everything had very strong flavors and a bit more salty than what I'm used to but tasty! Portions are ok. 

[CRISPY EGGPLANT] - $10 - Very delicious blend of spices on top. Perfectly crispy texture on the outside and juicy on the inside. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

[STEAMED PORK BUNS] - $10/2pcs - Nice piece of pork with decent flavor but not worth the hefty price tag.

[CHICKEN PAITAN] - $17 - Distinct and strong flavor. Most of us really liked this. Pretty salty and greasy compared to the usual ramen.

[TRIPLE PORK TRIPLE GARLIC MAZEMEN] - $16 - This is a dry noodle dish. I love anything garlic so I really enjoyed this flavor. It's quite refreshing!

Best ramen in NYC!!! One of the only places I go to in NY for veggie ramen and it tastes the same every single time. Best broth, best noodles, and overall best everything. I also like to add a hard boiled egg. For starters I get the tofu Coney Island, which is definitely on the salty side, but I do come here to splurge so don't mind, but a little less salt would be a plus! The staff is always so so nice!

We came here on a tip of a friend, we did a reservation and didn't need to wait , as you can check on my profile I eat a lot ramen nearly every 3 day when I'm on Tour, this place is not only good it is really good, there broth has the perfect taste , the noudels are tasty and the pork belly hmmmmmm I'm leaving happy. Only Minus it is very loud specialy at the entry area .

Had to pay a visit to see the hype.

That was about it, though.

Space: Make a reservation, but if not the bar seats are good.
Service: Friendly, professional.
Food: The Coney Island was a way too salty and over the top for a tofu and mushroom dish.
The chicken paitan ramen had a unique flavored soup but portion was small for a $16 dish. 
I have other legit ramen places I can recommend.

I was so excited to come here after watching Ivan on Chef's Table, but the ramen somewhat disappointed. The apps somehow stole the show though. Here's what we got:

1. Japanese fried chicken - a cross between Karage and Bonchon. I really liked it.
2. Buttery cauliflower (with bonito flakes) - very creamy, great texture.
3. Shio Ramen - Great broth and the rye noodles definitely lived up to the hype. 

However, the pork belly in the ramen was completely over-cooked and did not taste that great. Thought this was weird - another friend indicated that he had the same feedback, so maybe this is something you guys can fix?

My wife and I came with a couple friends after watching chefs table. The place has a great ambiance for a ramen shop. The ramen overall was very good, although my wife and I weren't blown away by the flavors as I was expecting. Broth was very flavorful, the pork was cooked well, and fresh vegetables. You definitely won't be disappointed if you are looking for a good bowl of ramen.
Heaven in a bowl. Had the Cold Sesame noodles for lunch with diced chicken and some palate pleasing kicked up seasoning. Service was prompt and attentive. Friendly staff.

I came here with some family after seeing the restaurant on Chef's table and was not disappointed! The ramen was excellent, particularly the triple pork ramen (which is more like a pasta), and the spicy red pepper ramen. However, the best thing we had were the steamed pork buns.

The service was excellent, as was the drink menu. Overall, a great meal! There is a ceiling to how good Ramen can be, but I think Ivan Ramen comes close to hitting it.

Five stars for the Japanese Fried Chicken. On point!

Also, really cool how Ivan Ramen puts rye into the noodles, as well as creative assortments of vegetables into the ramen. It's absolutely delicious AND adds health in small measures!

Only negative is the VERY loud music played indoors. Sitting outdoors would be a solution, but NYC summers have humidity..
This place is amazing. The flavors in the bowls are immense, and they also have an incredible beer menu. There is a great atmosphere, the people are super friendly, and the patio feels great!

If you're looking for good ramen and an unbelievable craft beer selection, this is probably going to be your favorite place on Earth.

Lets start with the Chicken Paitan ramen. Absolutely unreal flavored broth and even more amazing is there's no beef or pork used. I could drink just the broth and be pretty happy.

I was completely blown away by the depth and diversity of the beer list and tried some amazing stuff you would have a hard time finding in NYC, much less anywhere.

The spicy pickles are also a standout.

All in all, this place is a must visit if you're a ramen fan. Also highly recommend the Chefs Table episode on Netflix on Ivan Orkin himself.

It's not everyday that you hear a story as inspiring as Ivan Orkin. Ever since that episode of Chefs Table, I knew I had to stop by and try this revolutionary ramen. Least to say that the expectations were very high and mostly all of them were met. I ordered the chicken paitan because I heard that was the most unique of his ramen dishes. I'm glad I ordered it because it was one of the ramen broth that wasn't pork based and absolutely delicious - rich and seasoned to perfection without being too strong. If you don't eat pork, this ramen will fulfill your ramen satiation. 

The noodles were thin but definitely over cooked and not springy. The eggs were perfect and I personally enjoyed the garnish. I couldn't get over the rye noodles which were a bit of disappointment because I had such high expectations from the master! The wait, the price and hype that surrounds Ivan is personally not worth it for me with the short time I usually have in NYC. There are better ramen places like Ippudo whose Tonkotsu broth is legendary. However, if you're nearby do check it out. Ivans story is still really cool and the ramen is one of the better ones out there! The staff is wonderful and the decoration is very playful and fun.

Personally, this is the best Ramen I've ever had. The broth was very tasty but not totally overpowering. It also had quite a bit of depth of flavor. The noodles were chewy and flavorful. The egg was cooked perfectly. I'm glad I was able to taste this ramen to get some perspective on what ramen can be. 

The fried eggplant appetizer was delicious as well. The service was excellent and we got in and out quickly. I would definitely recommend Ivan Ramen to someone looking for great ramen in Manhattan.

A friend had recommended this place a few months ago and I finally got the chance to try it. They have the most delicious and beautiful Ramen dishes I have ever tried. The appetizers are creative, beautiful and delicious! Definitely will come.back as soon as I can.

Came here because a friend saw this place on the Netflix show Chef's Table. Luckily we made a reservation before coming. Our reservation was at 9:15PM on a Saturday night and we were seated immediately but people who came after us looking for a table were told to wait for over an hour. 

Very surprising because this is the worst ramen shop I have ever been too. Main reason being that the broth was completely not to my liking. I noticed that on the menu most of the ramen use chicken stock instead of pork stock. In addition the pork belly pieces we got were all overcooked and too firm. It wasn't soft and melt in your mouth like other ramen places. The japanese fried chicken is cut into small pieces, fried, and tossed in a sauce but it was all overpowered by how much salt was on the chicken. I was only able to eat a few bites before I ran out of water and had to take a break.

In terms of service, the waitress was very attentive and I have no complaints against any of the wait staff but unfortunately I cannot recommend this place for people who are ramen fans.

Like a ton of tourists, we made our way to Ivan Ramen based on the owner's appearance on Chef's Table. And what a wonderful experience. A great staff and incredible food. I'm not even a huge ramen fan (my wife loves it, hence us making the reservation) but I could take down a bowl of the Triple Pork Triple Garlic every day of my life.

I came here during a special event featuring several sour beers which was lovely. I ordered the special chicken sesame noodle, which is more Chinese than Japanese but when the chef is white what do you care. The noodles were crazy delicious and tasted just as good out of the fridge the next day. The whole wheat noodles have the best texture and are way better than the rye noodles in my opinion.

AMAZING FLAVOR! I would definitely say this is one the best spots I visited in New York, the food is really tasty and you can tell is made with high quality products, I had the Triple Pork Ramen and the Steamed Pork Buns! The taste of everything in my ramen was perfect and delicious! The wait time can be a little bit long but it's totally worth it. My waitress was really kind and she helped me in my decision since they actually have a lot of different ramen! I highly recommend this place.

Thoroughly enjoyed everything about this place. The mosaic of spilled ramen on the walls was creative and original. The service was prompt and the servers were kind and patient. They clearly explained each dish that was brought out and kept our glasses filled. A large group of us came and we all did the tasting menu with bottomless sake or Japanese beer. Every item was delicious and carefully made. We tried every appetizer and each got to select one ramen. Pictures of all to come...
Blown away! The food is incredible, definitely worth the hype. Broth is so flavorful, the noodles were so unique and they have great vegan options!
As a vegetarian I can say the ramen was very good, maybe just short of great. My husband had the pork dish and he absolutely loved it. Pickles we're great.
Dangerously in love with the spicy red chili ramen! I highly recommend making reservations.

Loved it. Have had Ramen all over LA, in Japan and Ivan was quite good - definitely one of the best Shoyu broths I've had. Great beer list as well. I read through some of the negative reviews before going and none really seemed credible. I would definitely suggest making a reservation - was lined up 30-40 people right at opening. Will come again.

I came in a group of 4. 3 people tried different ramen, 1 person got the spicy fried chicken. Nobody finished their food for different distasteful reasons. The spicy chicken was too salty and needed to be drenched in the sauce to offset the harsh taste. The spicy ramen was overly hot. The chicken paitan was too salty. All of the ramen noodles were soggy. The broth was watery, basically just tasted like water with a hint of flavor. For appetizer we started off with pork buns each. Those were too salty as well, the only thing good was the actual bun.

Like many others I came here with a friend visiting town who saw an episode on Netflix about Ivan. I was disappointed in general - to me the decor seemed inauthentic (like many other places in the LES area), and the food was generally salty, sweet, fatty, blunt, and not very unique or interesting. Personally I wouldn't say this is something you should go out of your way to try. Since the prices are normal for the area, if you're hungry and short on time this could work (except for the 90 minutes wait for a table), but if you're looking for great ramen you have many better options in NYC. On a positive note the staff were very friendly and helpful.

The order that you should experience Ivan Ramen should be the following:
1) Eat the ramen
2) Watch the "Chef's Table" episode about the ramen
3) Make plans feverishly to go back to eat more ramen

My gal pal was telling me on a cold, rainy Saturday that she was in need to ramen, and insisted we come here for my first real ramen experience.  She wanted me to have a pure, erotic, and sensual moment with that piping hot bowl of God given glory rye noodles.  So, I gave in.  This first time didn't pacify me, so this Friday, we went back with my bestie, and relived the memory.

To start, we opted for the spicy shrimp with the fried green tomatoes.  This is a wonderfully great choice to get your tastebuds going, and the sauce was just spicy enough to be enjoyable and not painful.  Fried to crispy perfection, the tomato was fried completely in tact and was juicy.  Really a lovely way to start!

Chicken paitan is hands down the noodle bowl to end all noodle bowls.  The umami of the fatty beef and the broth is really a palette overload of flavor.  You will risk burning your mouth just to slurp this goodness up as fast as possible.  The bits of beef on top of the mount of rye noodles are like little presents in every bite.  

I want my marriage to be compared to this bowl of chicken paitan - good to the last drop and amazing compliments!  Cooked to perfection, I wouldn't change anything about it, except try the soil boiled egg instead of the raw egg cracked on top.  The rye noodles are bouncy, elastic and are totally coated in the broth from end to end.  

Slurp loud and proud people!  Let Ivan hear you, even if he isn't there.
I'm getting spoiled by my obsession to ramen in nyc. This place is great, but not necessarily more outstanding than the other top tier ramens. Perfect if you're already in the hood.

I like that this place is trying new things like rye noodles and Ivan definitely knows ramen because I read his book and made some recipies. There were a few big problems with the execution at this place though that make it seem like its turned into a profit making enterprise, not really trying to be a serious contender for top NYC ramen (maybe 4 years ago it would have been).

First the portions were way too small for the premium prices, for $16 the Triple Garlic Triple Pork Mazemen was like an appetizer size. This was the first time I've ever ordered two bowls of ramen. The whole wheat noodles were nice and firm and paired well with the tonkotsu and green onions and garlic. For my second bowl I got chicken paitan with rye noodles which to me were disappointingly a little thin and mushy. 

My other issue was that it was too salty, which I'd read elsewhere but was skeptical of, because ramen is supposed to be pretty salty. But no, the salt really overpowered any subtler flavors.

Just came away a little disappointed about somewhere I'd wanted to try for a while. There is much better ramen in NYC now.

I've been meaning to visit this place ever since I saw some kind of documentary about it. The premise is that a New Yorker opens up a ramen place in Japan - and it's pretty good. My honest review is that it's exactly that, pretty good. 

The problem is that the ramen is too expensive. I think I paid $16 for a shoyu ramen, which is as basic as it gets. I'm a really big fan of Japanese food so I usually go with something basic first and if it's good, I get other items. Sadly, I don't think I'll be coming back. It's not that the ramen isn't good, it's just that it isn't good enough for the price.

The staff was super friendly and helpful as well.

Ordered: TOKYO SHOYU RAMEN

Ramen is mystery to me.  "Craft" ramen is really riding this wave recently and I'm not really sure how I feel about it.  That being said I am in no position to predict where the market for ramen is going. I am writing here strictly to deliver my opinion of this establishment.

Is Ivan Ramen good? Yes.

Is there better ramen in Manhattan? Yes.

The shoyu ramen is not going to take most people by storm but it did satisfy my requirements for what I am looking for in good ramen. It covers the basics. Good broth, solid noodles, and the accouterments did not disappoint.

Disclaimer - I am by no means a ramen expert. In fact this was my very first time having it from a restauraunt  
Ivan Ramen was so hyped up that I had high expectations. We started with the fried chicken and Japanese pickles and WOW did they live up to any hype
The ramen, however, was totally underwhelming and I do not understand why people love it. Its expensive for food that seems like it should cost $5. Relatively bland and not worth it
I will definitely be returning for the two apps and might give this another shot, but my first actual ramen experience was lackluster

Aggressively trendy, but satisfying chicken-based ramen nonetheless.

Showed up for lunch having made online reservations the night before (walk-ins were waiting 40 minutes at 1:30pm) Saturday 1pm and was seated promptly at a raucous four-top (imagine a Decemberists accordion-backed cover of David Bowie's Space Oddity).

Ordered the chicken paitan ramen, which emerged steaming hot with a raw egg yolk to be pulverized into the already schmaltz-heavy broth, intensifying the savory richness.  So much so that the chicken-based broth almost approximated the mouthfeel of a properly done (pork) tonkotsu bowl.  This is probably the best chicken-based broth in the city and a step up from Totto Ramen's standard chicken paitan.

Rye-blend noodles were a nice addition with excellent tooth, and just a hint of an underlying rye flavor (other than the fact that the noodles have a green tone).  The noodles also hold their firmness longer than its white ramen counterparts (think Ippudo, Nishida Sho-Ten, etc).  Worth a try.

Also tried the classic Tokyo shio ramen (still chicken), which was good, but seemed underpowered in comparison to the paitan.  And not as good as a bowl at totto's.

Two unexpected relevations included the watermelon and tofu nigiri and yuzu lemonade.  The combination of watermelon (on bottom), tofu, and hot chili oil blend in an unexpected medley of flavors in the mouth approximating spicy ... cotton candy(?!?).  And the yuzu lemonade packs a powerful citrus+Asian citrus punch.  Definitely helps cut the ramen oil going down.

So delicious! We had pork buns, miso cauliflower and each a bowl of ramen.  I had the shoyu ramen and it converted me to a noodle lover.  We left full and happy.  This would be a go to spot if we lived in the city.

Ivan Ramen satisfied in every way.

The ramen is delicious, and my whole group couldn't stop raving about the broth. I would highly recommend the Chicken Paitan. I'm definitely going to be back to try the Spicy Chili Ramen.

The service is superb. The staff was inviting from the moment we stepped in to request a table until we left. Our waiter was full of energy and gave an elaborate rundown of the menu.

I find the atmopshere really cool. I'm into the comic book style art on the walls. The seating layout is open and comfortable. 

My whole group left happy. This should be a top considering for ramen in lower Manhattan.

We only got to Ivan Ramen in NYC because we are fans of Chef`s Table in which Ivan Ramen was featured, only to find out that they deserve the spot indeed. I cannot vote for all the dishes served by them but the spicy ramen we had was awesome. It had the right amount of spiciness in it so for the people who like spicy food this is a perfect point, not too little, and not to overwhelming. The service is prompt and very friendly and the place has a nice modern like look with nice seating outside which we took. Their little mosaic tile art work is very appealing. Definitely a good food experience in NYC !!!

Ivan ramen was a cool little hole in the wall with a hipster vibe to it. Who doesn't love craft beer with ramen. Everyone that I was with enjoyed their ramen and their brews. Prices are a little too high for my liking when considering the price we paid. Their were three of us and we each got a ramen dish and one beer, resulting in an $85 bill. I think I would've been cooler with spending that if the portions and pours were more. Definitely, still enjoying my meal and the experience and wouldn't tell someone to not go there but I'd also say look for a cheaper ramen place.

So I'd seen a Netflix documentary on Ivan Ramen so I really wanted to try when I was moving my daughter there a month ago. We went around 9:30 that night and we were told there would be an hour and a half wait. All fine, we went down the street to another bar. Wen back about 2 hours later to the hostess saying "Oh yeah! I was just about to text you!" Right. Anyway, we got in and the ramen was different that anything I'd ever had. It was very much like a chicken soup. Delicious but not what I expected.

Came here with a friend who raves about the broth and the backstory of Ivan's store in Japan.

Mb my expectations were too high, but I wasn't blown away by the ramen. I ordered the Tokyo shio, a chicken broth with an extra glazed pork. 

Good but not great. I'm not accustomed to chicken broth and still prefer pork based broth. 

Probably will not come back.

The broth is flavorful, the noodles have the perfect tensile strength and elasticity, protein is perfection. The memory of this place is etched into my hippocampus as a truly GREAT Ramen shop. I am dumbfounded to how someone could rate this place under a 5. I guess there are a lot of haters in NYC. Don't hate the Ramen! Embrace it, slurp it, bathe in it. Seriously good eats. Thank you Ivan!!

Love love love the noodles. 
Had the shoyu, the noodles were fine broth was delicious. Had the pork bun too, really really really nice! A must have. Will be visiting again to try their other bowls!

I give Ivan 4.5 stars. A friend of mine brought me here for lunch a while ago. We both ordered the Spicy Red Chili Ramen and we loved it. Very flavorful and pretty legit spicy. After that we finally went again last night because we enjoyed our last visit. We got the Pork Belly Buns, melt in my mouth amazing, and the Crispy Eggplant, which was my favorite dish of the night. We wanted to try a different ramen but last minute we both just got the Spicy Red Chili Ramen, it was just as delicious the second time.

First time here! The Restaurant itself has a cool vibe inside and they also have some outdoor seating. There were some flies buzzing around, especially near the bathroom which we were originally seated near. We asked to move because you could smell it a little bit. I had the shoyu ramen and it was just OK. The flavor was a bit too light for my taste. The pork belly buns were really good however. Also ordered the tofu chili which I do not recommend..I don't think mustard goes well with tofu here.

One word: umami.  Tried the tokyo shio and the chicken paitan, loved them both. 
Tip: we were offered to sit at a table or at the counter, we chose table, we were wrong. Sitting at the counter seems to be a better choice (you'll get more space, and you can watch all the action coming from the kitchen)

Incredible Ramen - same level of attention to noodle as there is to the broth and toppings. Chicken broth is best I've had - went twice within 2 days. Downside is cost but the umami punch to the face is worth it

Even after all the hype from chef's table. ivans didn't disappoint. Coming from Asia and having tried some of the best ramen noodle shops, I can honestly say Ivan's can hold hold their own. My friend and I ordered the tsukemen, pork bao, karage, and spicy ramen. All dishes were well above average. Each bite being an umami explosion. My favorite dish was the pork bao. Very well done. 3.5 stars? Underrated. 4.5 stars I  my book.

Food: I haven't been to many ramen places, but this is definitely one of my favorites. One thing I particularly enjoy about Ivan Ramen is their specials. They have really awesome specials that most ramen places would not have and the Tsukemen dipping ramen was amazing. The appetizers were good as well, and overall a really solid ramen spot you can go to with friends or family.

Environment: this place was really busy and service took a while. It was a long time for the food to get out but the staff were friendly. Pretty tight space and dim lighting.

Price: the price is what you will see at most good ramen spots in NY. Plan to pay around $20+. 

Overall: there isn't much I can complain about here at Ivan Ramen, and if there is, the food makes everything better here. One of the best ramen I've tasted, and I would say definitely worth a try

Autumnal equinox passed and we leave the sweat behind for sweater weather.  This Sunday had all the chill that makes your tummy cry out "Ramen comfort me my old friend."  You can equally replace 'ramen' with bourbon, but it was only half past two pm and we had several games of MegaTouch in our future we had to be spry for.  

So first, we spring for IVAN RAMEN's Clinton Street location.  

We belly up to the bar and our server sized us up quick.  Sake?  Yes.  If you order a beer, a sake glass is only $5... Yes, yes.  

Kos ordered the vegetarian ramen with a soft boiled egg and GF noodles.  Tello hit the Chicken Paitan.  We started with the Kyuri Pickles.  

A quick toast of sake to take comfort in our comfort food and the pickles are placed for us.  A large serving, plentiful with fresh dill week and chili.  The bite comes first and the heat comes later.  And the heat lingers, which pleases Kos because she's a masochist for the spicy spice.  

Ramen arrives and the golden soft boiled yoke widens Kos eye bigger than her stomach.  The temperature was perfect, you could dig right in without testing your patience.  The individual flavors in each bowl were great.  The tofu pierced with soup melts upon first bite.  The egg perfectly cooked.  The GF noodles were a great replacement.  After mouthing the order and then slurping it into the mouth, there was no reason to talk about it again.  

Our server also recommended Tello add Bok Choy with the Chicken.  On point!   By the time we ate all the fresh ingredients out of the bowl, the broth stewed with the noodles long enough the distinct flavors were lost.  Had to hit the pickles again to freshen the palette.

It's a large enough serving to either take pause or take some home.  If you glutton for punishment, prepare to walk off a full full stomach.  Good thing this place is so deep down and east in the LES.  Round trip we did 5 miles.  Weight was gained.  Further gained was a new recommendation for friends.  We'll be back!  The winter is long.

Absolutely unbelievable. We placed our name on the waitlist and was quoted 45min to 1 hour wait. An hour later we check in with them to see what the status was only to find out that they apparently had us cancelled on the system. Since we've already waited so long we decided to continue waiting and was quoted 30min. 25 min later we check in with them again and was quoted another 30min. Seriously they were absolutely unapologetic and made it seem like it was our problem and not that their fault that they cancelled us on the wait list for no reason! 
 
Two hours wait for this place is not worth it and I'm sure you can find a place with better service and better ramen. Absolutely terrible.

Not as good as I imagined. As expected with places like this, they gave us a ridiculously long wait time only to text us after 20 minutes saying our table was ready. 

The ramen itself wasn't bad but I had higher hopes! It reminded me a lot of Ramen Shop in Berkeley...but that's not obviously as popular or raved about! I'd prefer going to Ippudo.

Ivan Ramen was my first meal at NYC. While I can't say that the shoyu ramen was the best ramen I've had, it was definitely worthy of a return trip. The broth was soy based and it was slightly on the saltier end. However, I ordered enoki mushroom as an add-on, which somewhat counterbalanced the saltiness of the broth. We also ordered Tokyo fried chicken as an appetizer. The portion size was very generous and can easily feed 3 people. Despite the thickness of the sauce, the chicken was still quite crispy. 

The service was excellent! Each of us ordered different ramen and the waiter brought us extra bowls so that we can try each other's dishes. 

The restaurant is split into two areas. The area near the entrance is super loud while the inner area is quieter since it seats less people. If you want to eat your meal in peace like me, try to get a seat at the inner area. 

Wait is horrendous due to the popularity of the restaurant. If you come here during prime dinner time, then be prepared to wait for up to an hour.

I loved Ivan's story on Chef's Table and have been wanting to go to Ivan Ramen since. It did not disappoint. We ordered the Kabocha Squash Tempura and the Charred Eggplant appetizers. The squash was a tasty blend of sweet and savory. The eggplant was like a deconstructed babaganoush with slightly crispy pieces of eggplant paired with a tahini sauce. I appreciated how the eggplant wasn't soggy in oil which often happens when fried. I got the Chicken Paitan ramen with the rich chicken broth, fresh, slightly nutty rye noodles and topped with a creamy egg yolk - yum!

Service was great, the staff was helpful and cool. The ramen was ok... have much better ones in NY and the restaurant is pretty far from anywhere in our visit list this time. So it wasn't worth the "trip". Oh... and the tables were all under reservation... but for any reason a lot of them were empty...

We got soo lucky, but thanks to the awesome lady in the front who got us in between reservations. We were about to wait an hour to an hour and half to get seated. The triple pork triple garlic was good and the pork belly in it was suuppeerrrr tender & delicious. Cool spot!!

Atmosphere: 3.5/5 because unisex bathroom and there's a line standing next to customer table. Tight tables space. High school wooden chairs.
Food presentation: 4/5 great presentation, but portion was less.
Food taste: 4/5 noodle was perfect, tender and texture was great.
Service: 5/5 water kept on coming..
Price: 3/5 
Total: 3.5 stars 

Came to "Ivan Ramen" on Sunday 2pm and the the line was 1/2 hour wait.
My tourist instinct kicked in and I have to try it.
 I gave the hostess my cellphone # to text me, when my table is ready. Outside the restaurant has a bench, so waiting time was pleasant.
When my phone rang, the hostess showed my table. Inside the left wall were picture collages, I forgot to take picture of. Then I notice there were bar seats and back yard dining.
I ordered Brussels spout, Tokyo shoyu ramen and chicken paitan. Brussels spout were roasted perfectly, drizzled with soy sauce.
Tokyo shoyu broth was clear soy sauce broth. Chicken paitan broth was thicker- raw egg, I think it's miso broth; but they gave you a lime to squeeze into the soup.

This place is EXCELLENT. Sorry, the haters are big babies. The ramen is perfect to the tooth, the broth is complex and not too salty. The 2 service people I had were super friendly and nice. Everyone here is busting their behinds to get people in, fed, and out the door. Initially I had to wait 15 minutes for a single on a Saturday night at 7. I got seated along what I called the "penalty box", a narrow counter where a half dozen people can sit facing a wall. As soon as the server said hello, I asked if I could move to a single stool at the bar facing the kitchen. Even though it put me in another servers territory, she pleasantly asked the front desk and cheerfully re-seated me. I loved it all. No place is perfect but these people are dishing up great memorable ramen quickly and pleasantly. Give them a break.  ::-)

DO NOT attempt to order take out there because they will forget about you, asked you to wait outside and claimed that they will take out your order to you. I sat on the smelly street and waited 25 minutes. Hungry and sad. Then I back to check my order - here it was, sitting on the counter for who knows how long. Nothing inside feels hot or warm. 
Over priced ramen, not authentic. The vegetarian ramen is basically soy sauce with noodles and it's $15. Stop going to this ramen shop because it is so overrated.

Update: not only that - I am a vegetarian and I order cold sesame noodles and it is usually just plain noodles and now there's pork inside! I can't eat it I will get sick. I am so so disappointed! Wasted $17

After watching about Ivan Ramen on Chef's Table, we decided to make a reservation when traveling to NYC. Our server, Jonathan, was extremely helpful, knowledgeable and friendly. We took his suggestions and loved every thing we got! Service was fast- food was warm and memorable. I literally haven't had ramen in years- but the portion sizes were more than ample. The others were ramen fans and loved this more than the typical ramen.   After appetizers- we couldn't' finish our bowls- so they were boxed up and just as good later!  Make reservations- as the seating is limited. The only thing that would have made it better- would have been if Ivan were there to sign a cookbook...

Noodles from grocery store are better than this place. It's all about the broth, which is bland and salty here. My date got sick, and is still sick in the stomach from the soup. There's so many better places in NYC.

Still struggling to figure out who's bright idea it was to open a noodle shop that doesn't even have spaghetti. Spaghetti is the quintessential noodle. How hard is it to put some tomato sauce on a plate of pasta?

I also can't really figure out why these guys are so into soup. I mean, I get it, some people like soup, but it shouldn't be your main menu item.  Most of us just want some pasta and tomato sauce. Also I wish they had chicken noodle.

Definitely going back.

Not the best place for ramen. Friends got the Tokyo shoyu and spicy red chili. Both had the same ramen noodles and it was not good. It wasn't even real ramen the one where u expect to be chewy and thick. The soup lacked any flavor and depth. I got the triple pork. This wasn't even a real bowl of ramen with soup. It was a thick sauce. It was okay but it was small and it only came with ONE piece of pork belly! There are definitely other ramen spots that are much better right would recommend minca which is pretty close to the area if you're looking for a good spot.

Learned about Ivan and his story from my husband and then chef table @ Netflix.  Love ramen so this weekend in NYC I stoped by to have dinner @ Ivan Ramen.  I suggested to make a reservation to void to wait long time, I am saying this by my own experience, I did not reserve just walked in on Saturday night and not luck to find a table so I have to wait 1 hour and half. The place is not that big, the hostess was not too polite neither nice to us, the service in general was average but it was worthy to wait I tried the soups. I had one of the classic Tokyo Shoyu ramen great flavor if you like pork and eggs and one special- chicken paitan, amazing flavor with a touch of lime was the perfect ramen to finished my night.

This place is awesome, I had the spicy pork, with a add on pork belly. Broth was very rich and tasty! The Price is great for the love that goes into the noodles .  Will definitely come back next time I'm in the city!

The fried chicken was delicious!as one would hope. We were surprised that the chicken ramen soup was flavorless. It was like smoky water. And when I substituted noodles it was $22. So that clearly was upsetting.

I travel for this Umami. Best noodle...the noodle itself I've tasted in life. Some of the seating faces a wall 11 inches away which is not awesome but the bar in front of the pass is one of my favorite seats in town.

The Eggplant Togarashi is more compelling than mid-eighties crack in alphabet city IMO. My memories from those days are hazy but I stand by it.

It has been awhile since I've been here and it's even better than I last remember it! The service here is still superb even years since my first review. The staff is welcoming and full of energy from beginning to end. They really take time to give you suggestions on items from the menu which is also really great. If you're looking for a dish that isn't soupy I would recommend the triple pork triple garlic mazemen. This is extremely flavorful and so filling. It has you craving for more of its deliciousness! Definitely made it to my list of one of the best ramen places in NYC.

Huge hype about it from my colleagues who are in their 20' however what a disappointment for me, if you are looking for traditional Osaka style of ramen, this is not for you.  If you just want see/meet young beautiful sexy noodle slurp 20's, this is an awesome date place for you.

Hands down the best ramen place in town..perhaps even more unique than ippudo..every dish is a surprise - was impressed by all the appetizers (esp the eggplant!) and def try their chicken paitan..their noodle's texture is so different from all other ramen shops and the chicken broth is so rich and flavorful.

Everything was delicious.  Spicy red chili was not hot for me. It was good amount hot because  I eat spice all the time. Fried chicken was crunch and taste.  I don't usually  like ramen. I tried couple  of place and I was disappointed.  I wanted to give last shot ramen and I found my place.

My coworkers and I went to Ivan Ramen after work, expecting a wait. We were told 30-40 minutes which was fine so we put our names down. 40 minutes later, we checked in on our table only to find out they never actually put our names down, then blamed it on us for "cancelling" - which never happened because we never even got any messages with updates. We were told we could wait another 30 minutes, so we did. Then, when checking in on our table 30 minutes later, we were told it would be another hour. The staff was so rude and unapologetic. No clue what the ramen tastes like but I definitely won't waste my time here again.
This place is too expensive for the quality of the ramen its not bad but its not worth $16 for a shio. Go to st. Marks. Get some $9 ramen. Dont bother with this overpriced place.

If you want amazing ramen, look no further. Ivan ramen has one of the best ramen in the city. Dishes are fantastic. The restaurant also has a great vibe. Would definitely recommend! They also have a great outdoor space if the weather is good enough!

We waited one hour to get a seat - definitely exciting. But, over expectation killed my experience - I wish ramen were better than what I was served. Egg wasn't seasoned and broth was too salty. It would have been fine for some other spots but I was hoping something amazing. I am sad to put 3 star but may be my I suck at eating ramen - sorry Iavn.
Fresh ramen, can get salty in the end. Cute space, good for casual meeting with friends!! #nycfoodcouple

If you've watched Chef's Table, then you know why you're here This place is awesome! Slurp'n-licious good. Great service, savory ramen, excellent music and vibe. The hubby and I came here celebrating our 1 year anniversary and we Loved it! Very satisfied. Just in case, I'd make a reservation if you're coming in the evening.

Go for the experience, but don't stay for the food. 

I love ramen and made it a goal to try a lot of different Ramen places both in Japan and in the US.  Ivan Ramen, based on its food alone, would rank near the bottom of the places I've tried. This was especially disappointing given the hype and price hence the 2 stars. However, the story behind the place is interesting (a la Chef's Table) and the ambience is fun making it perhaps worth your time if you drastically lower your foodie expectations and drink enough. 

FOOD
They have an extensive drinks list including a lot of interesting beers and sake. We had two different sakes including one from Brooklyn which tasted quite unique. 

We had the fried chicken appetizer. The chicken was barely crispy and coated in an overly flavored sauce. I've had better fried chicken from fast food restaurants. From other pictures on yelp, the chicken looks more fried so perhaps they just messed it up ? 

I had the Chicken Paitan ramen. The broth was salty to put it lightly. They give you a lime to squeeze into it; thank goodness as it sort of cuts through the saltiness. However, this is ramen, not a tequila shot! Ramen is all about the rich flavorful broth. Adding a ton of extra salt does count as flavor, and ruins complexity which should be built up by cooking the broth for hours. The chicken was your basic ground chicken and the egg yolk was nothing special. The noodles were the best part. 

My boyfriend had the Shoyu tonkotsu. Note these are cold dipping noodles, pork belly, and collard  greens. The pork belly was also extremely salty and a bit dry. So disappointing when it should be juicy and rich. The broth tasted like it had been flavored and thickened with seaweed which is different in a very bad way. The collard greens were pickled and extremely spicy, not meshing well with the other parts of the dish.

SERVICE 
The wait was long (1 hour on a Monday night) but we knew that it would be. They entered our name in an iPad and texted us when the table was ready. The service was great and the best part of the visit. Sat at the counter. The bar tender was helpful and friendly - refilled my water constantly. Thank goodness because I needed a lot of water to eat such salty food.

The charm of Ivan's story exceeds the actual meal. While I appreciate his take on reinterpreting ramen, my overall experience fell short. 

Pretty crowded even on a warm day but we got seats at the bar. Per our server's recommendation, I had the triple pork triple garlic mazemen with the roasted tomato and soft-boiled egg. From a flavor perspective, I thought it was tasty and appreciated the oddly western umami addition of the roasted tomato that Ivan became known for in Tokyo. But there wasn't enough broth and to compound it, the temperature of the broth was awkwardly tepid. Kinda like a tsukemen but not really. Good sake selection though. 

Admirable take on ramen but perhaps just a bit too far off center for me.

I first came here when they opened a few years ago and for some reason, didn't quite enjoy the food however, today was a cold snowy NY day and a bowl of spicy pork ramen just hit the spot. I also added the garlic chicken for an even extra boost.

Service was great.  Menu selection was impressive.  Unfortunately, the broth was too salty and greasy.  The pork slices were too thick and fatty for my taste.  If you like ramen with fatty, salty pork broth and fatty thick pork slices, you will love this place.  For those who crave more delicate broths and thiner and more flavorful pork slices, there are definitely better places for ramen in NY.

If you're a vegetarian... I would NEVER suggest this place. The Vegetarian Ramen literally tastes like soy sauce broth with noodles, oh and 3 random cubes of soft tofu.
I understand making vegetarian ramen is hard Bc of the broth, but literally, this was awful. Nothing but a soy sauce taste. 
I've had much better had smaller joints that are fast food which have more vegetables and more tofu. I ate the three pieces of tofu floating in my bowl when then put it down, only to then realize, that was the only tofu I got.
I can't vouch for the chicken ones obviously... my Bf seemed to enjoy his. But if you're vegetarian, don't go here with your friends, you'll be so(y) disappointed! The pic looks way better than the taste

Very glad my friend recommended this place and brought me along with him. We didn't make a reservation because the only times available were 6pm and 9pm or later options (on a Tuesday night), and decided to try walking in and waiting instead. We arrived around 8pm and less than 5 minutes after putting our name down they seated us at the bar area. (Tip: you can order drinks while you wait!)

We skipped appetizers because we solely came ready for the ramen (and a beer), and it was plenty. I'm not vegetarian but sometimes feel like going for a meatless dish, so I had the vegetarian ramen. I LOVED it. The broth was super flavorful, garlicky, and hearty, just what I needed on a cold night. The rye noodles were DELICIOUS and plentiful and paired with a decent amount of veggies in the ramen. There were only three pieces of tofu which was a little lacking in my opinion for the price, but I still loved it nonetheless. The person I was with had the Spicy Chili Ramen (he specifically wanted to come back for this as it's been his go-to each time he's come here before) and loved it, as he always does, but it's spicy so make sure you're prepared for that.

Service was wonderful. Our waitress was quick and attentive and made sure to give us the rundown on specials going on that night as well as good appetizers to try.

Will definitely be going back!

That was just amazing! (Probably because I was seated in the heated patio in the back otherwise the place was crowded and loud.) I got a classic basic shoyu ramen that didn't taste basic at all -- flavor, noodles, broth -- everything was up to par and delicious. Staff was very attentive and helpful! Wouldn't make it my casual go to spot but the patio is actually perfect for special occasions.

Enjoyed the Japanese fried chicken as the sauce was flavorful but not as crispy as Korean fried chicken. We also had the pork baos; forget their name. They were good too. I got the chicken paitan based on that seeming to have the most consistent yelp reviews. It was a bit salty and not as umami as I'm used to, in typical ramens.
