My family enjoyed their veggie ramen and shoyo ramens but I wasn't a dns of their flavors. Guess I'm a purist!

Had the chicken paitan and grilled corn. Very quintessential NYC fusion food, but like many of these joints, Ivan Ramen was overhyped. The broth was oily, heavy, thick, and lacked depth. The noodles weren't al dente. Combined with the long wait time (despite not having a full house on a Saturday afternoon), this place did not live up to the buzz. It's great that this place has such a strong following, but it just didn't do it for me.

Such a disappointment!! My husband and I had watch his episode of Chef's Table and were looking forward to visiting his restaurant. I LOVE ramen but his Tokyo Shoya lacks serious flavor. The soy sauce broth was very one dimensional. I had asked for extra garlic and was told NO! I couldn't get extra garlic, paste, or oil, stating they didn't have any to give! The only saving grace was my husband's Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen. The noodles and sauce were delicious! Definitely not a soup, but the flavors were much better. Also a little expensive for ramen. Mine was $16. Not worth it!

I was so excited to eat here. I was so hopeful that it was going to be amazing, but it was simply awful. I've had many bowls of ramen in my life in the states, in Korea and in Japan. But this bowl was definitely the worst. Let me go into detail...

The wait:
I understood that it was going to be a long wait, because of it's feature on Netflix. BUT, when it was our turn to get seated we recieived NO text message. When we asked why, they had no answer and gave us free drinks to compensate. Nice!

The food:
I ordered the spicy red chili ramen and the Japanese fried chicken appetizer. Let's talk about the karaage first.

Japanese fried chicken (Karaage):
This was not karaage. It was decently tasty, but it was not karaage. To me, it tasted like jajjangmyun (Korean black bean noodle dish). It was not crispy when it came out, it was almost as if it was sitting out for a while and became soggy.

The ramen:
I have never sent a dish back in my entire life, but this was the first time I had to. The broth was almost like a spicy tomato soup. It had no hint of dashi and its consistency was far too much like water. The noodles, as I understand, are not supposed to be traditional ramen noodles. Cool. But, they were just awful. They were over cooked, horrid chalky texture, no flavor, and did not grab onto the broth at all. Just about the only good thing about the ramen was its chashu (which was still mediocre at best).

I had to send mine back for a Tokyo shoyu ramen, and that was equally disappointing. Better! But still disappointing.

My fiancée had the triple pork triple garlic mazemen. Which, was much better than the ramen but still subpar. 

I sincerely wanted this to be an amazing experience, but it just wasn't. I can not see myself coming back here, but I'll give anything a second chance.

There's two type of people who eat ramen: Spicy & non-spicy.

I'm a South-east Asian, pepper eating, fiery broth slurping type of guy. Of course I went for the famed Spicy Ivan. The broth appeared extremely red as to warn me not to eat it. It did not disappoint as my eyes watered a bit, but the spiciness was on point. As for the rest of the bowl, the meat was a bit scarce. The other toppings, personally, not my thing as I didn't feel it complimented the ramen well. I ended up ordering chashu on the side and it ended up being one of the most smoky tasting chashu's I've ever had. Delicious!

Ivan Ramen is a legit spot for the adventurous spicy eater, but I do recommend customizing the bowl a bit more.

Ivan ramen is for sure the best ramen I've ever had. It's something about the flavors and the noodles- it's just super unique and his flavors are MIND BLOWING. 

So.
We sat outside on the patio under heating lights and an awning (it was warm cozy quiet and refreshing) which was dope. Our waiter was clutch, he came through right away with the warm welcome, run down of the menu and personal faves and answer all our questions. He was patient nice and attentive!! The hostess was so nice as well. I honestly can't say enough good things about the service or location. 

We had the fried chicken app (this was literally the best chicken dish i've ever had, I can't think of a chicken dish that i've ever had that I thought was superior to that. Like damn. The flavors the texture the sauce, the size of the pieces, the amount, the chicken was PERFECT, nice green spices on top- fireeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee delish magnificent. Not like any fried chicken flavor you've ever had and will exceed ur expectations. Perfect to share with 2 or 3. Even 4. (But you'll want another) Sweet, crunchy, soft, chewy, salty, a little kick, omg

We also had the red hot chili ramen which was so delicious and red and spicy 7/10 for sure. Only spice lovers eat and it will rock ur sox so yummy noodles greens yay was even almost too spicy for me yay bc usually dishes at these places arent as spicy! also had the chicken patain (something like that) ramen this was the most unique ramen ive ever tasted and the best flavor ive ever tasted it is like the comfort of chicken soup in a bowl but so much better in ramen form with fresh lime omg 


getting this and chicken every time!!!!!!! WE LOVE IVAN AND IVAN RAMEN!!

Good ramen place. Not for soup people. I prefer more variety in soup based ramen. However, their three pork ramen (forget exact name) was great. It was not soup based. Little soup, almost like sauce. But great tasting and will go back for it.
Went as 2 people, got sat pretty reasonably, around 40 minutes, but went to boba drink place next door.

The rudest people I've ever come across. I came with a group of 9 and they wouldn't seat us even though there were 9 open seats at the bar. There was no reason for the host to turn away our business and then to be as rude as he was. So disappointing. I'm sure that an owner would not have behaved in such a way. RUDE RUDE RUDE staff. Close the store and retrain your people.

I like the tofu Coney Island. It really taste like when east meet west. Curry flower is creative and Beef tongue sando has great balance of tender juicy tongue texture and crispy crumb crust. I sampled Tokyo Shio pork ramen and triple garlic triple pork mazemen. Both of them are extremely salty and I had to drink three cups of water to clean my palette. Approximately, I had more than 100 bowls of ramen before between Asia and America, unfortunately, Ivan Ramen isn't my top three. I do appreciate the new creative flavors and bold usage of tomato. However, the seasoning of ramen and mazemen is too heavy, I wish it could be more balanced.
My first Ramen place and I definitely fell in love! I was watching Chef's table show about Ivan and now so happy that we finally tried it! It's absolutely amazing

Hour and a half wait on a Saturday night ended up being about only 50 min. and we were seated at the bar. Our bartender/server was nice. We tasted a few sake's before deciding on Dragon God and it went well with our ramen. We ordered pork musubi and crispy eggplant to start. The eggplant was the star of the night. The musubi was forgettable. We each had the Tokyo Shoyu ramen and it was good. How good? Just good. The broth was fairly lackluster. The deep soy umami that carries a bowl of Shoyu was not there. There are lots of ramen places popping up everywhere. This one is popular and trendy, but I've had much better.

Service was good but the food was way too salty. Had a few bites and couldn't finish the dish. I understand ramen is a salty dish but it was way too much. This is the first time I had a bad experience eating ramen. Not sure if they were just having a bad night... this is a hard pass, there are plenty of other great ramen places in NYC.

Had the triple pork and triple garlic dry ramen.
I think it is just ok. The source is little to acidic for me.

Decent ramen but the place is so packed you would definitely want to make a reservation if you plan on going around regular meal times. The soup is on the saltier side in my opinion, but still delicious and hot so on a cold day you slurp all the ramen down fast. The portions are large. It's not the best ramen I've had, but if I were in the area and it didn't seem super busy I might pop in again.

I went to this place after seeing it on the Chef Table! I had the spicy lamb dan dan with no egg on top and it was so good that I want to have it again and again! The staff was very friendly and have full knowledge of the menu!

Their popularity definitely ruins the experience a little.
When we walked over, we had bout 30min before they opened, so stupidly we sat next door with a bubble tea until about 5min before open, and holy crap a long line had already formed. People really line up to eat this? We were so surprised and worried we'd have to wait. But the place is really bigger than it looks with an outdoor enclosed patio thing, so we made the first seating somehow...

So even though they're prepared for this kind of opening rush (and if you don't make the first seating, I heard the host say the wait is 1-1.5hrs), they really treat it like one big buyout. Water on the table before open, appetizer orders all go out first, then ramen orders trickle out one by one. So even though we already ate first lunch and passed on apps, we waited about 45min for our ramen while other tables ate their appetizers.
But at least you get to wait inside, sitting down.

And when our ramen finally came, they were not. hot. Lukewarm at best? It was good for eating it super quickly, but I like when the first bite is at a good temperature. The classic Ivan shio... the broth you could taste dashi and chicken if you really tried, the noodles had a nice bite, but it just was not unique or all that memorable - kind of just the bare minimum to pass as a credible ramen shop. The triple pork mazemen reminds me of Chinese noodles and had a more aggressive and salty flavor, which I liked, but felt like I could have gotten that in any good Chinese restaurant. But again, lukewarm and sad.

Overall, I liked it okay, esp since stl has nothing even resembling good ramen. I would not wait 1.5hrs if I don't make the first seating. I would not arrive 20min early + wait 45min to eat this again either, but maybe if you had good company and plenty of time to kill, it would be an enjoyable experience. Service is good and the place is pretty lively since it is pretty packed, after all.

I have been dying to come here.I highly suggest making reservations because the line was very long and even on a Wednesday night. Started off with the pork belly sticky buns and the cauliflower curry. My my my...The sticky buns were delicious; they were filled with a pickled relish and a sweet sauce. The cauliflower curry were the highlight of the night. They were crispy and soft at the same time. The ginger curry gave it a perfect balance. I had the spicy red chili ramen. The rye noodles were cooked perfectly and the broth I would say was a 6.5 out of 10 in spice level. Overall decent ramen. I look forward to trying more!

I'm a noodz enthusiast and Ivan Ramen has been floating around as a place to eat ramen for awhile now (the Chef's Table episode probably increased that by tenfold). Our group of 5 came about 30 minutes or an hour after opening and we had a 45 minute wait for a table outside under some awning. A great tip is that it is right next door to a Boba Guys so you can grab some delicious boba while you wait.

Once we got seated service was pretty quick and our waitress gave us helpful suggestions and guidance. We ordered brussels sprouts after our waitress pushed us to get them and we're so glad she did. They were salty, crunchy, and a great start to the meal. We also ordered from kyuri pickles to cut through our ramens and that was a good choice, although they are pretty spicy.

- Spicy red chili ramen: the smashed egg was like the creamiest egg custard omelette you could order. The noodles was similar to soba and held their own against the strong flavors of the broth. I'm a fan. 
- Chicken paitan: our waitress described it as the best chicken noodle soup and that's pretty accurate. The chicken flavor was throughout the whole dish but still tasted balanced and light. This was a comforting bowl of nostalgia, ramen style
- Shoyu Tonkotsu Tsukemen: Tsukemen isn't as common as ramen, udon, or soba so I get excited when I see it on the menu. It was slightly room temperature with a hot dipping broth. Unfortunately we didn't realize it was spicy so my sister swapped bowls with someone else. I loved the dish especially the pickled collard greens.

Ivan Ramen is a nice change of pace from your traditional ramen places. I didn't try any of the classics but there are so many other places to go if you want a classic bowl of ramen. I enjoy Ivan for the remixed versions.

There is no way this place should have 3.5 stars. This is why talented chefs hate yelp - which is shame because yelp is great. At the end of the day, this is great ramen. Its New York so it isn't cheap. Get over it. It is trendy so it is busy. Get over it. And no bowl of ramen should be able to change your life so reset your expectations. Get over it.

On my recent trip to NYC, my friends and I went to Ivan Ramen for lunch. I wasn't particularly hungry when we arrived, but no matter because there was a 1.5 hour wait in order to get a table for 4. I figured I would be hungry by the time we got our table.

Once we finally got the text to be seated, I felt a faint sense of hunger. Looking through their menu, nothing immediately jumped at me. I wasn't craving anything too heave so any miso-based broth was out of the question. I ended up ordering the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen that comes with 
 soy sauce, dashi + chicken broth, pork belly, soft egg, toasted nori, and rye noodles.

The food itself was underwhelming. I do have to say I could find better ramen. I probably wouldn't make my way back to Ivan Ramen unless someone specifically wanted to. Not the best, but also not the worst.

My girlfriend and I came here after watching Chef's Table one afternoon.  We're ramen fanatics and have been to quite a few joints.  Ivan's atmosphere was hip and nicely themed and the Ramen itself was pretty good.  Not the best we've had, but definitely tasty and quality ramen.  Will give extra credit to the actual ramen noodles themselves because they're made with rye and I found the texture and taste intriguing.

Loved this place! Definitely recommended getting a reservation. This place fills up fast! Not many seats inside and very popular. However food comes out fast so there is quick turnover of tables. I tried the famous spicy red chili ramen and the broth was delicious! My friends tried the veggie ramen and the chicken paitan which were also excellent! We especially loved the pork musumi bites. This is a fun place to come for a date or with friends. A great NYC ramen spot!

Been wanting to go here since I watched the chefs table feature and it lived up to all my expectations. It was super crowded  and small so def make reservations. It was the perfect portions too. We had the curry cauliflower to staff as the waiter suggested and so happy we did! I had the spicy lamb Dan Dan it had no broth but I loved it!

I am a lawyer. I go to New York often to depose corporations. So after a grueling day of deposing a company in Battery Park, I needed lunch. I took a Lyft to Ivan Ramen for a late lunch, because I saw the documentary about Ivan Orkin on Netflix. 

And I am really glad I visited. 

I was instantly seated. Immediately, the staff offered me beer and a menu. For a starter I had the fried chicken tenders with a bowl of ground chicken ramen soup. 

It hit the spot. My mind slipped from the adrenaline strip of litigation to the soothing calm of chicken ramen. And I felt great. Ivan Ramen is a must visit lunch spot in New York. Its affordable, delicious, and well worth your time.

I had a surprise birthday party for my husband at Ivan Ramen because we always love the food. Honestly though, as amazing as the food is, it was nothing compared to the outstanding service we received during the planning and execution of the event. Cat and Jake were so flexible, accommodating and friendly, Chad the GM was so thoughtful and welcoming, and Elmer, our server, dealt flawlessly with our large group. The private patio room was perfect and everyone had a great time eating way too much delicious food. Can't thank the team enough!

Overall:
I really wanted to like this place!  Heard so much about it, saw it on Netflix, and watched a few youtube videos on it.  I'm a huge ramen fan (especially tsukemen) so I was excited to come try such a popular ramen shop.  This location is a bit smaller than I expected but I waited about 30 minutes for a seat at the bar.  The server was friendly and the food came out quickly.

Food:
I was so excited about this place that I ordered two dishes just for myself and one to go... yeah I can eat a lot ramen.  I ordered the triple pork triple garlic mazemen and the shoyu tonkotsu tsukemen.  First off, the dishes aren't very big so I feel that you can easily get away with eating more than one bowl if you're hungry.  My favorite part about all of the dishes is the noodles which have a nice texture and firmness.  Now what I didn't enjoy much was the overall combination of flavors.  The triple pork mazemen was extra salty and the shaved green onion plus minced pork sounded like they would be a perfect fit with the noodles but something just tasted off.  As for the tsukemen, I love dipping noodles but the broth was very thin compared to the usual thicker broth.  They also put small dried fish at the bottom of the broth but it just didn't taste very good with the whole dish, especially since the fish were harder.
I ordered the chicken paitan to go which tasted the best out all three dishes but the broth was also very salty.

We were walking casually around the neighborhood on a Sunday evening and found that there's  no wait  in Ivan. So we just walked in to try some Ramen.

I tried chicken paitan and my wife tried shoyu ramen. We both liked our own order more than each other's. That just means we just liked our ramen a lot. Ramen is a bit on salty side, but it just adds to taste. And if you are someone who don't like salty taste much, definitely stay away from chicken paitan (it tasted good though)

And unlike most ramen places they DO accept cards

Truth be told, I never knew of Ivan Orkin until chef's table but after that, I knew I would one day try the ramen for myself

Noodles were definitely the biggest noticeable standout, really enjoyed the chew factor

As for the broth, well seasoned with good depth that warmed your soul

Overall Thoughts

Chef's table has a gift of finding amazing restaurants!

As a fan of Chef's Table (and ramen), I was really excited to try Ivan Ramen. I'd say it was a cool experience to try, but I wasn't quite as wowed as I hoped I'd be after watching the episode. Stellar service bumped this from a 3 star to a 4 star review.

To start, the set up/seating was just okay - we were seated at a space facing a wall with backless chairs, neither of which I was a fan of. Our server was Gina, and she was awesome! We ordered the curry flower cauliflower appetizer, which was the best thing we ate - so much umami and the sauce was incredible. We also got some sake and Japanese beers to try. The sake was okay but came in fun panda glasses we got to keep :) For ramen, I was torn whether or not to get the red, which is what I usually like, but I was worried it would be too spicy. Our server said I could switch it out if that was the case, which was so kind of her. My first few bites weren't too spicy, but it really builds over time, so after a minute or so, it was definitely too much. She was so nice and switched it out for me for the chicken paitan. My friend got the shio ramen. I was so bummed that all 3 ramens were really just okay. Maybe my expectations were just too high. It was still a fun experience and really wonderful and fast service, but outside of the appetizer, the food didn't wow me. I still think it's worth coming to, and it isn't too expensive, so even if it isn't the best food you've ever had, it'll be a fun time and a cool story.

After seeing Ivan on the Netflix series chef table, I was really excited to go to Ivan Ramen in NYC! Totally worth it. But you should reserve a table in advance. The location is super stylish. The waiters are friendly and funny as well. As a starter we had the fried chicken. It was well flavored and super delicious! On a rainy NYC day Ramen is the best. My spicy Ramen was excellent! Highly recommend this restaurant!

Good but not memorable and certainly not better than many of the other ramen spots in the city. We had a reservation to try it after its feature on Chef's Table but certainly wouldn't consider waiting in line for the food. It's good but there's better!

The place was recommended by an Asian foodie friend. Living in LA, I have had ramen many times before--in Little Osaka, DTLA, and elsewhere. Ivan Ramen, unfortunately, did not compare well. The ramen itself was good, but the tsukemen dipping sauce was salty (as others have pointed out) and it was served rather lukewarm. I ended up asking the waiter to warm it up for me.

I also ordered the cucumber pickle appetizer, which was frankly mediocre. The cucumbers had been pickled past the point of crunchiness. The sprigs of dill on top clashed with the Japanese spices. The combination tasted like a Middle-Eastern chef and a Japanese had fought over making the dish and neither had won.

I went there after I saw chef's table. I didn't know his achivement in Japan, so I became interested in him. Then I orderd Japanese shio ramen and fried chicken. No wonder, it tasted good !! It's sort of good balancing of essences of ingridients, so I felt that is the classic shio ramen. I understand this was also popular in Japan. Fried chicken -Karaage- is also authentic. I want to choose other foods. Finally, all these are expensive for me... all ramen in the USA are too. I think Ramen should be eaten easier by everyone.

I ordered the Spicy Red Chili Ramen-BEST Ramen that I've ever had. I want to book a flight to NY just to go there again but I'm not rich. I wish they could send me some ramen haha. My boyfriend ordered the Tokyo Shio Ramen and he was extremely happy as well. Japanese Fried Chicken and pickled Daikon Xo were so good.

Ivan ramen is exceptional. Whenever I am in New York I make sure to stop by. The ramen is the best I've had, and the appetizers and other dishes are very good as well. I love the chicken Paitan and the triple pork mazemen is also great. The service at Ivan ramen is good. If you make a reservation in advance you'll have no problem being seated. Love this place.

Not only was the food absolutely incredible but the customer service is extraordinary. Our food delivery driver got lost on his way with our food, and we called the restaurant to ask the whereabouts about an hour after we ordered it. They were so helpful and even called back multiple times to ensure we got the food. Once we got it we found they wrote a nice note and gave us some extra appetizers for the wait. Truly such a great experience. We will definitely be returning. Thanks go Zach for the help!

I have never eaten in the restaurant (I'm sure it's better), but I ordered delivery from here last night and it was so disappointing. I got the vegetarian ramen, and they package the broth separately from the noodles/toppings, as most places do. However, they gave me barely a cup of broth, which didn't even come close to covering the noodles, much less the toppings. Nowhere close to being a soup. Attaching a photo of my noodles with the broth on them so you can see how dry it all is. On top of that, it was cold when it arrived. The restaurant argued that it was *supposed* to be like that. That they meant to only fill the broth container halfway and that you are supposed to have to heat it up yourself when you get it! Which is a joke. Especially for an $18 bowl of ramen.

Category: Japanese
Size: Kinda small. 
Service: It was fine. The place was a little busy. 
The Chicken Dan Dan is a ramen dish with spiced chicken, pickled garlic, and a yolk. The broth of the ramen wasn't bad. You can tell that they used a chicken broth for this noodle dish. The texture of the chicken was like normal shredded chicken, and had little flavor. The noodles itself was nice. It was the right amount of chewy and elasticity. The only thing wrong with this dish is that they used way too much salt. I thought it was just my dish that was salty, but it was same for the appetizers that my friends and I got (the Japanese fried chicken), and their own meals that they got. 
Overall, the texture of the ingredients were good, but they used way too much salt for their foods.

This place is horrible! If you don't have reservation, you are not allowed to wait inside the restaurant for your spot. You leave them your contact info and you are supposed to walk around the block to find a bar or some place till they call you to come back. They literally kick you out of the restaurant and won't let you wait inside for your spot. We won't be coming back. If I could give a zero star, that would be my review. Totally unsatisfied with their customer service.
Service was great. Vibes were good. The ramen + pork buns were great. It was all around a good experience, it just didn't wow me. It's worth going to, but not worth waiting for.

This place is delicious! The staff were so pumped on a Sunday. Also everything on the menu looked veeeery delicious. We ordered de Curry Flower - you just can't go wrong with this dish. The curry koji butter is simply divine. Also ordered the Brussels sprouts and it was very flavorful. To be honest it wasn't the best ramen I ever had (I got the Shoyu), but the appetizers were the main thing for sure!

I really like the food at Ivan Ramen. And our server was prompt and friendly. However I did feel rushed once we paid. We were only there for an hour. The hostesses are extremely rude here, and I won't be back because of it. I feel like it's not difficult to find a friendly host to hire in this city. Love the food,
but there are amazing ramen places in nyc where you won't be rushed or greeted at the door by hosts who would obviously rather be at home.

Got the spicy ramen and it was delicious!!! The service was quick, and all the servers were friendly and happy to help with questions about the menu/give suggestions. Pork buns were pretty good but nothing to write home about. Awesome beer selection too. Would definitely go back!

(3.5 stars) As someone who infrequently gets ramen, I really enjoyed the spicy red chili one I got here. It wasn't my favorite I've ever had by any means, but it had some kick to it which I loved and it was hearty. The noodles were on the thinner side and more resembled thin pasta like angelhair than they did ramen noodles. I wasn't a huge fan of the pork being minced since it got lost in the broth, but I still ate all of it happily. 

The highlight of the meal though was the Japanese Fried Chicken. That nudged my rating up to 3.5-4 stars. Super savory, snack-size bites with a deep flavor profile, which was gently battled by the mellow, sweet flavor of the accompanying sauce. The two played off each other well, and every bite of this chicken was a joy.

This place is worth the hype! We got there around 1:30pm on New Year's Day and they told us it was a 45 minute to an hour wait. We were seated 40 minutes later. I went to Ivan Ramen after seeing it on Mikey Chen's YouTube channel Strictly Ramen. He did a ramen tour in NY and the bowl that stood out to me the most was the triple pork triple garlic mazemen so I HAD to try it. The pork buns were exquisite! They tasted as awesome as they looked. Aside from the food quality, the service was great! We tipped our server extra because she was super friendly and helpful. Zero complaints! I only wish I lived closer so I can go eat there more often. SIX STARS FOR IVAN RAMEN! :)

After watching the episode of Chef's Table and hearing all about Ivan's life and adventure learning to cook in Japan, naturally we were drawn to actually try out this wheat pasta that was so proudly introduced on the show.

First impressions, not the biggest restaurant, but that's part of what makes it so charming - with the Japanese fast food style atmosphere. 

Food was delicious and did not disappoint in the slightest, found myself carefully trying to observe the "umami" that he so adamantly proclaimed in the show. Although we were told this is one of the cheapest Chef's Table restaurants we'll find, I still found myself feeling it to be a little more expensive than I would've expected.

Overall, still highly recommend the triple garlic pork ramen and the fried chicken. You won't regret it!

This is kinda overrated.
We tried Chicken Paitan, triple pork triple garlic, and the classic shoyu.
The taste is Ok, it was different, but wasn't really worth the wait.
Further, all the dishes We tried was too salty. This is the major point why I rated this as 2-star only.
Overall, it was ok, but not something we will visit again.

Not worth the hype at all...I had the pork buns and the shoyu ramen. The pork buns were good but the shoyu ramen was absolutely disgusting I barely had a bite. Our server Stella never came by to ask us how the ramen was (clearly not good I didn't even eat it) or refilled our water (I was parched) so I couldn't even tell her it was terrible. We will not be returning or recommending this place.

The place was packed and we were seated after all parties arrived (we had made reservations). 

Stated off with the Pickled Daikon XO-dried shrimp + scallop chili oil which was quite intetesting. It had a crispy but sour taste. Not my cup of tea.

For the main meal, we had the following ramen, ranking from most favorite to least favorite:
-spicy red chilli ramen (with no pork/pork broth)
-vegetarian ramen (with no egg)
-tokyo shio ramen 

Our waiter was able to meet our request of having the ramen without any pork broth or pork. The ramen were great; just wished it was a bit spicy 

We were seated in the patio (which I definitely preferred over the main seating area). There were heaters in the patio to make you feel warm so it definitely felt cozy (and much needed) on a cold, wintery night. 

I definitely liked this ramen spot over Mu Ramen located in LIC. Next spot to try: Ramen Mafia in BK.

When the bf and I arrived the wait was 1 hour, but we got seated about 15 minutes in (thank you because we were hungry) We ordered the pork bun and 2 red spicy chili ramens. The pork bun was pretty good and was unique because it had pickled daikons instead of a regular piece of lettuce, but the portion is small for the price. The ramen we had came with rye noodles and it was very springy and thin which I liked. It also came with a crush egg, bok choy and some meat that was hidden at the bottom!! Lol I don't know the bf and I just didnt mix well enough or it was meant to be hidden but it was just a surprising way to end the ramen. Overall the meal was satisfying and had definitely stood out from other ramen places I've tried. Definitely worth a visit!
P.S. Service was excellent. Very fast and water cup was always filled.

Nowhere ever lives up to the hype. This does.
Miraculous rye noodles and the flavors....holy sh*t.
Plus our waitress was friendly, steered us in good directions, and timed things personally. My husband loved the extensive and unique beer list, and I had some excellent sake. This is the best food I've eaten in a long time.
Ramen and apps were amazing!!!! Highly recommend a reservation ahead of time  great beer selection and you need to reserve to enjoy ramen even Naruto would love!!!

We saw Ivan Ramen on Chef's Table and knew we had to check it out on our trip to NYC. It absolutely lives up to the hype. The food is phenomenal (highly recommend the chicken paitan) and the service was great. Our waitress was very friendly and helpful. She knew it was our first time there so she kindly explained what the dishes were like so we knew what to get. Everything was absolutely delicious. I definitely recommend checking it out!

Like many patrons of Ivan Ramen over the past year and a half, I was drawn to the ramen shop after watching Ivan Orkin's episode of 'Chef's Table'. I would consider myself to be an average ramen fan, and I figured it would be worth trying out. 

To start, we ordered the steamed pork buns and coney island tofu. The pork buns were good (not amazing), but the coney island tofu was inventive and tasty - lightly fried blocks of silky tofu smothered with chili and topped with chopped onion and yellow mustard. 

Had we stopped eating after our appetizers, I wouldn't have felt the need to write this review. What makes Ivan Ramen a 5-star restaurant for me was the chicken paitan with roasted tomato. The ramen was every bit as delicious as the food artists on Netflix filmed it to be. The broth was savory and rich, and the egg yolk elevated the broth. We were given wedges of lime to squeeze in our broths which added another dimension to the soup. The real treat was the roasted tomato, which added much-appreciated acidic & savory layers to the experience. 

The only negative aspect of our experience was the seating; even though the outdoor area was covered and had some heating we were very chilly and kept our heavy winter coats on during the entire meal. Overall, it was a small price to pay for one of the most delicious bowls of ramen in Manhattan.

This is my favorite ramen place in all over New York City!! I have been going here once a week since I moved to lower east side and I couldn't be happier. If you are looking to have your tastebuds rocked or go to the best restaurant in all of LES. This is the place.
First Ramen Noodle restaurant experience.  Cool back room dining area.  Server great in helping us decide what to order.  Chicken appetizer was delicious.  Flavorful and filling noodle dishes!

On our most recent trip to the city my husband had the idea of trying this ramen after seeing the episode on Chefs table. We made a reservation for 2 on a Saturday night and eventually made our way down to this location. It is very nondescript but the line out the door let's you know you're in the right place. Despite the line we were seated very quickly. Our server came over immediately and was so helpful. She helped us pick a sake and also had some great menu recommendations. For appetizers we tried the pork buns and Japanese fried chicken. Both were super awesome especially the chicken which was just the right blend of flavors. Then came the much anticipated ramen. My husband tried the red pepper and I ordered the shio. The stand out for me was the noodles which were very strong compared to normal ramen noodles which tend to be squishy. Every part of both dishes was truly delicious. We would definitely return in the future and it's definitely worth a try even if you don't love ramen.

Ohhh Ivan. He's got a Netflix special, you know that? Correct me if I'm wrong, I'm pretty sure it's the same Ivan. 

Ivan Ramen was an interesting experience. Not exactly a hole in the wall spot, but a different place when you enter. It's crowded, narrow, and dim lights make me think of a secret club. I mean the vibe you get is "cool" and hip  but causal and millennial. I swear, I recall jungle like music in the background. 

Unfortunately they didn't accept reservations when I called even though they asked if I had a reservation when I got there. So, either I got wrong information or I misheard. Considering that it was crowded the day and time we went, they said it was would be a 30-45 min wait, unless we could eat within an hour or less, they could find us seats. Weird, right? I know some kbbq places have a two hour time limit but that's a policy. Here, I was being told you don't want a wait? Better eat within an hour or less. We accepted. That's when we find out there's like a red lit room all the way in the back of the restaurant, I think for special guests, parties or reservations. It felt pretty mvp. 

Our server was incredibly nice, funny, and made the dining experience more enjoyable. 
I ordered the Tokyo shoyu ramen. It's a soy sauce base broth but boy was it saallty. You really notice the oil in the soup too. Honestly I went with one of the original soups because it's OG and it comes with an egg. But the egg was cold and there was only one slice of pork belly. I wanted to try the roasted tomato but considering the price already, I was fine. Conclusively, good flavor, but salty. 

My friends tried the chicken paitan, which they finished whole bowl and liked. I also tried some of their broth: salty, briny, kind of creamy chicken broth. Complex but quiiite salty.

I think it's a unique place to try but the prices, saltiness and comparison to another ramen place I had in NY left me with 3-3.5/5 stars. 

Do give this place a try!

If you are vegterian, dont come here！Even if you like drinking soy sauce, you can enjoy it at home other than this place. I can't believe some one went to chef table make something like that in his menu. I mean as a chef have you ever tried your own food. the noodle is really good but the soup is just soy sauce. don't tell me I don't know ramen. I am Asian chef and I have a vegan ramen shop in Beijing.  Huge disappointment. :(

So. YUM. 
The Chicken Paitan is what you expect from ramen - soupy, noodley, salty, warm. But OH MY, I have never tasted  t r u e  chicken until this bowl. So unctuous and savory and balanced. 
The Triple Garlic Triple Pork was equally delicious. A lovely light garlic, not sour or pungent. But, herbal? And for someone who is not partial to pork belly, it was AMAZING. Tender, meaty, soo sooo good. Note: no typical broth with this dish. 
Will be back.

Overhyped and overpriced. There are so many better ramens out there in nyc e.g., hide chan, ippudo, misoya etc. This particular ramen pales in comparison-soup is average, small portions, little garnishes, and too little meat. To top it off, the ramen is not cheap either. Do your a favour and go elsewhere
Ordered the pork buns, shoyu ramen, and the red chili ramen. The pork buns were good. But the ramens weren't as flavorful.

The ramen at Ivan Ramen is so incredibly flavorful. The broth has so many layers of complexity - truly a unique bowl of ramen in NYC. However, I think you could skip the pork buns (not even in the same ballpark as the buns at Momofuku in my opinion). The ambience is very bare-bones and contemporary, and the service is quick - you can be in and out in 30 minutes!

My work team had heard about Ivan Ramen on Chef's Table and booked a table here during a recent work trip. I have never particularly gone out of my way to go to a ramen restaurant, but I really enjoyed this place. 

Admittedly, my options were pretty limited by my seafood allergy, but they delivered on the Tofu Coney Island. I have never had tofu that was anywhere near this flavorful. The miso mushroom chili with mustard--not a combination I would have ever thought of--was AWESOME! I nearly ordered a second plate because it was so good. 

Sadly, I was only NOT allergic to one entree, the chicken paitan, but I really enjoyed it. Pretty sure I have never been able to finish an entire bowl of ramen, but I did this time. The thin cut noodles were refreshing, and it was just what was needed on a cold night. They had only a few wine selections, but the Riesling was nice, and no one comes to a ramen restaurant looking for an expansive wine menu anyway. 

Note for the restaurant: It doesn't make any sense to have a "vegetarian" ramen if it contains seafood products--although if I was warned against that dish because of a possible cross-contamination, then I'm very grateful!

Good ramen, great service, but VERY expensive. There are definitely better ramen spots with cheaper, more flavorful ramen but Ivan is pretty good. The service is really what sets this place apart from other ramen spots; the waiters are extremely attentive and friendly.

The karaage was so salty it hurt. 0/5

The chicken paitan was pretty good. Broth was still too salty to drink but good for the noodles. Was worried it'd be as bad as the karaage bc of some of the reviews here but thankfully wasn't. 3.5 or 4/5

Very tasty ramen and other dishes. Came here after watching chef's table and was very pleased. Ordered shio ramen and really enjoyed it. Roasted tomato and rye noodles definitely enhance the flavor and make it unique. Ordered Coney Island tofu and tongue-katsu as appetizers and they did not dissapoint. The ambiance was very hipster. The service was nice and friendly. They also have nice beer selection

Exaggerated food, not helped by the notoriety from Netflix and an 1-1/2 hour wait. To be transparent, our group got some comp'ed pork buns for waiting though - nice.

The spicy red chili ramen is like a Shin ramyun made with cream and too much water: decidedly whelming, and definitely not $17-worth. I will say that the grilled tomato is an inventive addition though, and worth considering.

If you're ever lucky enough to have friends who work in the restaurant or hospitality industry, take them up when they invite you to new places. Ivan Ramen had been on my radar for years as it's near so many inventive spots in LES that I like to frequent, so I am very glad I got to visit recently.

We sat at the bar, which is arguably the best part of the restaurant as you get lots of face time with the staff and chefs in the kitchen, who peek through the window behind the bar. 

From the kitchen came the following appetizers:
-- Crispy Eggplant; so delicious with a garlicky flavor and also topped with creamy tahini
-- Japanese Fried Chicken; perfect umami crunch with the garlic caramel kind of sauce that coated these beauties
-- Pickled Daikon XO; I really enjoyed these little radish ribbons which came topped with extra crunch from dried shrimp

As for ramen, I had the Spicy Chili Ivan Ramen, which was extremely rich for a chicken broth. I was so full after the many appetizers, but this was easily one of the most interesting, off-beat ramen I have had. As a classic tonkatsu ramen fan, this was a nice surprise.

If you're a fan of unique flavor combinations, come here.

Probably my favorite ramen place! The vegetarian ramen is hearty and flavorful. Had some vegetarian appetizers I really liked (e.g the Coney Island). Noodles are tasty and I definitely appreciated the texture and culinary creativity that went into the ramen. I loved the atmosphere. Highly recommend making a reservation!
Delicious ramen!! Very flavourful broth (we had the vegetarian). I've had vegetarian ramen before and I'm not always impressed but this one was amazing! Will be returning for sure!

Seriously this place has to have the best Ramen in New York City, we discovered this place about three weeks ago and we have been back thrice.

The staff is very friendly and they are knowledgeable, they create a killer environment. But come on... the absolute best part of Ivan Ramen is the food. I have no words to describe it but MAN IS IT GOOD. My mouth is watering at the thought of it now... my favorite dish is the roasted cauliflower appetizer. Go get it now!

We cant wait to come back and try more.

I would say that this is a great restaurant, their prices are extremely reasonable and they serve very very nice food. The waiting was a little bit annoying but that's not really the restaurant's problem. It can get a little bit crowded in there. The staff is extremely friendly, and that's always a great addition to an experience. I personally felt that the portions were a little bit small, though. I had 2 starters and a main and was still a little hungry afterwards. I must say, though, that their Japanese Fried Chicken is A+. Very very tasty. Their noodles are unique and good, too!

Long lines of white people waiting for Japanese food, which is telling of how authentic the food is. I kid. But really. There was only one gluten free option on the menu for my fiance, which was non-spicy and basically tasted like chicken noodles (remniscient of ), which is fine if you want chicken noodles, not ramen. Can see why it's attractive though and it would be good to come here with a friend who's never tried ramen before and wanted to try it for the first time. Line is pretty long for a overpriced restaurant that's quite confused about it's identiy as a ramen place. Two stars for the wait and mediocre food and crowded tables. Staff are super friendly though and bathroom is clean.

This place did not live up to the hype. 
We made a reservation midday on Saturday and still had to wait to be seated. 
Apps: Tofu Coney Island & fried chicken were great! 
Ramen: Shio & Tsukeman were subpar. The dipping broth for Tsukeman was cold before I even got to half the noodles.

Another trip and I've tried the Tsukemen Ramen.  I was a little hesitant, because I am such a huge fan of the rye noodles, but I went for it with the wheat noodles.  DELICIOUS!! Also it is served with an AMAZING Shoyu glazed pork belly and picked collard greens!  We also ordered the Japanese fried chicken and the pickled daikon.  Both were really flavorful and delicious, especially when eaten together.  I'm never disappointed here.  And a stand out is the Vegan Ramen bowl...which you can add protein to if you need to...

I'm a big chefs table fan so this was a must do for me. Service was quick - waiter explained all the most popular options and gave good advice. 

I got the chicken Paitan. I've had a lot of ramen over the years and this was a really solid bowl. I think I may have overhyped it in my head and had set me expectations a little too high. Don't get me wrong it was good ramen, but I think I just expected my mind to be blown. 

I definitely recommend checking it out!

Seriously SO delicious! Definitely make a reservation if you don't want to wait. Got the pork ramen and it was perfect. I've tried a few of the ramens and they are all so yummy it's hard to choose which one to get. We also got the pork buns which were tender and well seasoned. Will be coming back soon!

Heard about this place have good reviews and history and finally we try today evening with my family. So when we walked in without reservations and We seated promptly. We try pork bun for appetizer is soo good the pork is so tasty and tender is melted in your mouth wowww . And my kid try shoyu ramen and my wife try tonkatsu tsukemen and I try spicy red chilly ramen so overall I like the shoyu and tonkatsu tzukemen is the best because tzukemen is pork is the star plus u got salty vegetables is so good is really good combination and also the egg and broth is good too and shoyu the broth is light and not to salty but spicy chilly it's ok but the broth is like spicy  miso ramen but they don't put any pork so it's ok overall this the best ramen and must try and definitely we will back

If I could give this place less stars I would. Absolutely vile. Simply cannot understand the hype about unseasoned chicken broth with a tomato in it. If I wanted a take on terrible spaghetti I would have gone to the Times Square Olive Garden. Do not waste your time here.

A must visit again for me.

Preferred chicken paitan to triple garlic mazemen but both are really really good. But keep in mind, they both have heavier taste than ramen you had at other ramen places.

They also have lots of beer choices. I'm so satisfied.

I don't usually enjoy ramen, but this is definitely the best ramen I've ever had; everyone with me got something different and really liked it. I was a big fan of the vegetarian offering, but you should all try some of the appetizers (the eggplant was excellent). We also had a great waiter. 

Four stars instead of five because we had a reservation and got there on time, but not only did we have to wait ten minutes past our reservation time for our table, the location is so small that they made us wait outside in the cold.

I got the chicken paitan ramen and its really tasty.
But the broth is little bit too salty for me.
But overall is a good ramen.

Pork bun was good. Chicken wings were salty. I did not like the Chicken paitan.

I came from SF for this and I'm very disappointed. 
I have tasted orenchi ramen and ramen dojo in San Francisco.  Ivan is not even close to that.

We didn't have the greatest experience, maybe just a bad bowl or something. We definitely both got food poisoning from the ramen. My friend got the Tokyo Shoyu and I got the Vegetarian Shoyu. We both were nauseous and hr later and threw up  several hrs later (sorry tmi).

But I will say, service was very good. Cute little Ramen shop, but expect lines w/o reservations. For 2 of us, we waited about an hour, so it wasn't that bad. For me, the Vegetarian Should was very salty but my friend said hers taste good.  Good size proportions. Can't say I would recommend this place due to taste alone.

I had a great experience here. I watched chefs table and decided this was a must try. I'm glad I tried it! I had the chicken paitan based on servers suggestion. They were very quick and attentive, as soon as I closed the menu the waiter went right up to us. The chicken paitan was yummy and had so many unexpected flavors, the egg yolk melted right into the broth and the noodles were perfectly cooked. I will say this is not a traditional ramen, I would say this is more of an innovative approach to ramen. The price isn't that bad for ramen in the lower east side but some of the menu items were pricey. I will definitely be going back.

I really wanted to like this place, because I really respect Ivan's story. But unfortunately, I found my spicy chili ramen to be solidly middling. I could barely find any ground pork in my bowl and my soft boiled egg was quite cold. I will go back again to try the chicken paitan, since that seems to be a highly praised bowl, and will update my rating.

Tsukemen here is one of my favorites in nyc! It's got one giant piece of pork, chewy noods, and delicious mustard greens. Broth is super flavorful with pieces of shrimp in there. Also got the pork musubi with complimentary sake -- you can eat it in one bite so it's small, but super tasty.

Ivan Ramen was featured on Netflix, and well I guess this was on the list of one of my friends. They just got back from a wedding, and they were hung over. I mean, I probably would be as well if I had to wake up at 5 after a night long of binge drinking. Not to say that I had a long night the night before as well. Anyways, onto the food.

We shared a couple of appetizers, the Japanese fried chicken and the tongue-katsu and for the entrée I got the Triple Pork Ramen which was a wet noodle type of ramen. There was no broth in it, however it was really flavorful. You would think that it would be dry, but there is sauce towards the bottom of the ramen. 

I thought Ivan's was tasty. It was different, and I do believe I've had better. I know, but it's my opinion. There are better ramen spots around NY, but this place wasn't bad at all. I do think it's catered to a certain group of people, so it's not somewhere you would find me going back to. However, if you're new to ramen and you want to keep it safe, this is the place you should go first. 

TLDR; 
Ivan's not bad, but safe. The Triple Pork Ramen is a wet noodle and flavorful.

So like everyone else, we had watched Chef's Table and were really intrigued by this Jewish guy's bromance with Japanese ramen. It took us a long time to come here because the Yelp rating is only average. We bit the bullet on this trip and decided to see for ourselves if it was actually worth it. 

We arrived 10 min before closing time on a Thursday night. I used to be a waitress so I know how frustrating it can be to have last min customers when you're just about ready to go home, but the staff was super welcoming and didn't make us feel bad at all. We ordered the chicken paitan and spicy ramen. I am usually obsessed with spicy food but this bowl wasn't all that great. I'd definitely recommend the chicken paitan though- every spoonful of broth and bite of al dente ramen triggered tiny flavour bombs in my mouth. The roasted tomato is a weird but great addition to the bowl.  

I admit we were skeptical going in but Ivan Ramen did exceed our expectations.

The two times I've elected to spend my lunchtime at the counter of Ivan Ramen, an employee has initiated my repast with a snide comment on my attire. Neither men were candidates for Ford modeling contracts, but they unduly saw fit to immediately judge and air their opinions of my physical state. I'm usually up for witty banter, but this was not that. The food itself was fine, albeit dulled by my sudden loss in appetite. Both times the spicy pork ramen curdled in my stomach and made a hasty exit, presumably from whatever gutter oil they're using in the broth and the employee training.

Ive gone twice now and both times have been delicious. Their rotating beer list is amazing and has items I haven't seen anywhere else in the city. The Tokyo shio ramen is absolutely delectable and after building this place up in my head for about three years since first seeing it on chefs table I was not at all disappointed. The texture of the noodles in the ramen is perfect and they have a very satisfying bite to them. We also got the pork buns and they were yummy but pretty standard and a spicy pickle thing that was absolutely delicious! Can't wait to go again!!

Originally this wasn't on my list of "must-try" restaurants because I had heard from a friend that it was so-so, but of course I had to come after watching Chef's Table. 

We started with the daikon and fried chicken. 
Personally I love both pickled daikon and XO sauce so it was a great pairing. It's pretty oily though! 

Fried chicken was a miss. The name is misleading because it's not crispy at all and over seasoned. You almost have to have the ranch it comes with. We didn't finish this dish.

As for ramen, I had the chicken paitan, boyfriend had the one with spicy broth. The paitan was good! Really rich with depth, full of chicken and ginger flavors. The latter lacked the depth and really just tasted spicy.

Service was solid throughout. 

This place is a 3-star... because it's hit and miss on the menu. Worth the try and could be 4-stars if you order the right things.

OMG! No words!

I came to visit a friend and he took me here. I'm a fanatic of ramen and let me just say...best ramen ever. I ordered the Tokyo Shio Ramen with sea salt and he ordered the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen with soy sauce. You can really tell the difference between the two and the salty ness of each; though not too salty to where you can't eat it. I loved it and I am definitely coming back :)

This place is really just A-OK, nothing special, I've had WAY better ramen in NYC and surrounding areas. I first heard of this place when I was shown the Ivan Ramen episode of Chef's Table. It just seemed so interesting and amazing the fact that Ivan used to be one of the best ramen chefs in Japan and now has his own spot in LES. 

The appetizers we got were the pork buns and the Japanese fried chicken. The pork buns weren't really anything special, there are way better ones at specialized bun places in the city and at other ramen places. The fried chicken were pretty tender and it came with this great shiso ranch. 

As for my main ramen dish I got the vegetarian one and although it was good, I was expecting amazing. The broth, although normally salty as it is ramen, was just too soy saucey for me to fully enjoy. The ingredients in general were pretty standard with tofu and enoki mushrooms with a tomato as well. It was definitely a cozy meal, but all ramen is. Again, just not super wowed, definitely good ramen, but not as mouthwatering as the show depicts it as. 

As a plus though the backdrop of the wall is pretty cool! There is a doraemon stuck on the wall!

I came here on a Friday evening with a reservation for 2 and was seated right away. 

I had wanted to come here for a while after watching the Chef's Table episode and had high expectations. It was great ramen and I would definitely like to go again in the future!

We also got the pork buns which were amazing.
My experience was a standard restaurant of Ramen. Nothing that blow my mind. I had very high expectations and I thought the Ramen broth was missing flavor

My friend recommended I eat here and said this was the "best food (she's) ever eaten". After a long trek my husband and I finally made it here; Cute little hole in the wall it looks like we may not make our way back out. Once we got in it was nicely decorated and cute. The table next to us was eating some crispy looking chicken which I asked them what it was and they said it was the Chinese fried chicken it looked too good to pass up so we ordered that as an appetizer along with the chicken paitan which is what the waiter said he would order if he had only one chance to eat there.

That appetizer was the best chicken I've had. SOoooo good!!! The ramen was also quite flavorful. Perhaps not the best food I've ever eaten but it was really good!!!!

Would definitely go back!

no words for this place!! the chicken paitan is the best ramen dish I've ever had. the fried chicken is insane, staff is so friendly. this is the spot I always take out of town friends to. definitely recommend!

I went two days in a row.. on the train thinking abt heading back tomorrow. 

1. Triple Pork Triple Garlic
Delicious - great flavors and ingredients. No broth aka dry style saves room for more food. Little lighter on the palette as well. 

2. Chicken Paitan


3. Spicy Lamb Dan Dan  

If you're a ramen fanatic and haven't tried it, go wild. 

Spicy Chili seems to be a restaurant/server favorite. Have to go back and try it.
So so broth. Had a bad exp with a rude waitress. Not worth the wait and the hype to be honest

Came here on a cloudy and somewhat rainy day.
Place looked all filled up but I guess I got lucky and my group of 3 were able to get a seat.
Service was friendly and attentive. We had a little but of confusion when ordering an appetizer, the pork musubi, but I got it figured out with the help of the waiter.
I had ordered one of the ivan specials, triple pork, which was really good but I thought there'd be more meat in the dish with the name "triple pork"
I also had some of one of my friends tsukemen, which was also really good! We also got complimentary shots of saki, which was nice even though we barely drink.
All in all this place lives up to its name/hype.

So it is with some sadness that I come today to deliver this three star review. This place has been on my do list for quite some time, and I was completely underwhelmed. As of today, this place stands at a 3.5 star rating. I feel that is completely accurate. I'm going three stars just because I don't want to contribute to bumping that up to 4.

On the plus side, they did have some cool appetizer choices that you won't find in most Ramen spots. The crispy eggplant was quite delicious, and their pork buns were loaded with deliciously seasoned pork. Our server, Chris, was aces as well. Very upbeat, made some good beverage and appetizer suggestions, and was generally pleasant. He was rewarded with a generous tip.

So what was the problem you ask? Well it's a big one. Their tonkotsu broth was awful. This is simply unforgivable in any Ramen spot worthy of the title.
My wife ordered it with the cold dipping noodles, and I could see her face immediately dropped when she tasted it. She said it tasted "fishy". Tonkotsu broth should be silky salty, and umami. There should not not be any hint of fish! Also, it was lukewarm. So I asked our server for a small bowl so that my son and I could both donate some broth to my wife so that she could continue to enjoy her noodles. He was just about to give us a bowl of actual broth so that we wouldn't have to waste ours, but a rude nosy manager butted in and said "just get them an empty bowl." So that was pretty shitty.  

The other two Ramen choices we got at the table were the Shoyu and the Seitan. Both were simply OK.

The beer list, impressive as it was, was way overpriced. Cans of beer for $12 and $16... And 5 ounce pours of draft for $8 to $12. Really? Not on my watch...

So there you have it, an accurate summary of my first and last visit to Ivan Ramen. If you're looking for me, I'll be at Ippudo!

I was here way back when the restaurant first opened (as in, first day or couple days of opening). Everything from the service to the food was rough (wrong orders, missing food, food that came was meh), but all new restaurants have rough starts and I thought not much of it. So when a friend and I figured we'd try going there for lunch recently, I figured everything would be much better than things were then.

This time I went during sake week. They gave us a menu but didn't really advertise specials for sake week or anything; in fairness I didn't ask and didn't think to ask until I got the bill and remembered the reason why we'd chosen the place. We got the brussel sprouts and vegetarian ramen. The brussel sprouts were good and my friend and I ate them up really fast; the veggie ramen was super salty and took a little more time to get through (the salt could probably have worked with a bit more fat somewhere in the bowl, but didn't work as well with what was basically a bowl of noodles and salad greens). As soon as we got the ramen, servers would come over literally every five minutes asking us if we were done--even when I had a spoon or chopsticks still in my hand.

Overall not the most pleasant experience. There are definitely much better Ramen places in the city and I'll stick with those.

I've never had restaurant ramen before but wanted to try this place after seeing it on chefs table. I had the chicken ramen and my fiancé had the dipping ramen. What I loved about my soup, was that the chicken sausage had great seasoning, it was a blend between great chicken noodle and amazing ramen, the lime helped bring out the umami and the egg was the perfect touch. The noodles have a good bite to it. The boa buns are also good! A must try.

This is a must visit for me every time I come to New York with friends and family. All the starters are great, but my personal favorites are the curry cauliflower and fried chicken. My favorite bowl of ramen here is the Chicken Paitan. It's very different from your typical bowls of pork broth based ramen as it uses chicken based broth and has minced chicken in it. Very delicious and very nice combination of texture from the noodles and minced meat. It's best to come about 10-15 minutes before they open to get in line to get a table and get seated promptly.

My boyfriend and I, like Many other reviewers, sought out this ramen shop after seeing the Ivan Orkin special on Chef's Table. We were interested to see how this roasted tomato and special noodle would taste, especially given all the hype around it. 

Ivan specializes in being different, and it definitely was. You can't compare it to other ramen shops, because from its core it is different. Unfortunately it fell a little flat in my expectations. I got the Tokyo Shio ramen, and the noodles were definitely a standout as was the roasted tomato Ivan is known for. It's a unique addition that deserves the praise it has received. Sadly the broth and egg were the parts I was most disappointed in. The broth was oily and bland, and the egg was just a simple soft boiled egg with no added flavor. 

While the ramen was so-so, I did enjoy the beef tongue. It was soft and moist, and a good appetizer. My only complaint with this was the mustard they added to it, seemed out of place. 

Overall, I was disappointed but glad I tried it because of the noodles and tomato because those were standouts.

In a word--- delicious! I enjoyed the Chicken Paitan and everything (and I mean everything) I saw come out of the kitchen looked amazing. The place was packed and all the tables were filled. I highly recommend making a reservation. It was easy enough to carry on a conversation but buzzing.  I will surely by back to order the ten other items that caught my eye in the menu.

I was super excited to visit this branch. After reading that this was the original outlet I had such high hopes. We started with the pork buns, fried chicken and tofu to share. The buns were just ok. The fried chicken was super salty, the whole table agreed and we didn't even finish the small portion. 
The shio ramen was nothing special, the shoyu was salty as I know it's with soy sauce but it had way too much. I would skip this place unfortunately.

Chef's Table Fan?
Like many other people, I learned about Ivan Ramen from Netflix's Chef's Table show, so there were certain expectations on my first visit. I was not let down. Although the menu is not very extensive, every dish that makes it on the menu is unique and delicious. For starters the Japanese Fried Chicken and Steamed Pork Bun are a must, but if you want to try something new, give the Pork Musubi Bites a try. If you're struggling to pick a ramen, I would recommend the Shoyu Tonkotsu Tsukemen but there are other great choices as well. Seeing that the restaurant is very popular and not too spacious, there is always a line but if you don't have a reservation it's worth the wait.

I have wanted to try this ramen spot for the longest after hearing so many good things about and how the chef is so great.. but this turned into a huge disappointment. I ordered the tonkotsu. It comes with a side of cold ramen with their hot broth. Youre suppose to dip the noodles into the broth.. the noodles were still cold even after putting it in the broth! Not sure if thats how its suppose to be but if you like cold noodles, definitely try it. The meat that it came with was just sooooo salty.. I'm so glad I did not order extra.. 

My boyfriend got the spicy ramen.. he can take spicy but this was just super spicy so if youre into that, order it!

Overrall, 3 stars because we got our table right away and the customer service was great but sadly, I'm not sure about giving it a second chance. There are definitely better ramen spots in NYC and trust me, I have tried a lot.

I give this place four stars for the service and three stars for the food. We are from Setagaya, Tokyo, and live near his original shop near Karasuyama. We knew of his place but never stepped foot inside because, well, it's Japan, and authentic places are all over the place(and of course there is a famous Tsukemen place near Kanpachi, also near our home). But since we live here now in NYC and needed to satisfy our ramen cravings, we ventured all the way to Clinton street. First off, when you say Japanese style chicken we expect simple fried chicken coated with starch with a side of salt. What we got was more Korean/Chinese style marinated chicken. It was tasty, however, and we washed it down with cold beer(they have a lengthy list of various beers and sake). The ramen was good, not great(we had three different types), but still good. Having said that, I would revisit when I get another craving for ramen. But after I've tried the other ramen-yas in the city.

I was really excited about coming here as there has been a lot of hype of this place and I do have to say I was pretty Let Down and I will explain why...

I have traveled the world eating ramen, so I do believe that I have a great source of contrast and comparison. This is definitely not a traditional feeling ramen place where are you are entering and everyone says hello, more of a city-modern and hip type of place which is cool and what drew me here. 

FOOD: Long story short "UMAMI" was missing.
I tried both the Shoyu-Raman & the Spicy-Raman. The best part are the noodles which are thin and have a wonderful crisp bite to them. The Shoyu soup base tasted like it maybe was just from one of those cloth base starter bags w/too much Memmi flavor. I am quite a spicy lover, but the spicy broth was just spicy and not flavorful and enjoyable. The karrage chicken looked wonderful on the menu, but when it arrived it was soaked in a sauce which makes it loose all of its crispiness; it was also sweet not savory FYI. Pork buns are very average and can be found at your local food truck.

STAFF: Our server was wonderful and saved the day for us as was the very nice woman hostess. The manager woman had a very sharp tongue and was snitty and rude. 

Our reservation time had come up and someone from our party was not there so they would not seat us. Then three other people who were not with their party at different times past us to be seated when we were told that it was against the policy to seat the table without everyone being there. When I inquired about this the manger got upset which in turn made me and my wife upset, so we just stood their at the counter waiting. Then the manager said "I guess we will violate our policy, even though they had already done so three times before us, and seat you instead of having you stand there looking like that all upset in front of all the customers" WoW 

***All in all should have gone to Ippudo's Ramen instead!

I really like Ivan Ramen! The pork buns are a great appetizer, enough for three people. The ramen itself never disappoints and the noodles are clearly homemade. The drink list is also very extensive which I appreciate. The staff is always super friendly and knowledgeable and willing to help you decide which ramen to order.

Contrary to popular belief, Ivan is more than a ramen shop.  This is a great place to order a bunch of starters and try all these unique flavor pairings!  (Note: the owner, Ivan, spent years in Japan to learn about the cuisine and puts his own unique spin in his starters)

Starters:

-Pickled daikon XO: If you're not a fan of daikon, this dish will CHANGE your mind.  It is sweet and crunchy with a strong vinegar punch.  I couldn't stop eating this!

-Crispy eggplant: Highly recommend this twist on eggplant!  It came perfectly crispy on the outside and the tahini added a unique flavor.

-Japanese fried chicken: It was sweet and tender, but I was let down by the lack of crispiness.

-Kyuri pickles: if you can't handle spice, stay away from these bad boys!!

-Curry flower: Please do yourself a favor and order this.  You can thank me later.  The crispy exterior!  The flavor!  My mouth still waters at the thought.

Noods:

- I was recommended the Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen.  It's not your traditional ramen with broth, but the fragrant garlic and strong flavors carried the dish.  I wish there was more pork- they skimped on meat! :(

Ivan ramen's chicken paitan is my favorite ramen dish in NYC.

I know I'm in the minority on this one, but I love my ramen with chicken broth- and it's hard to find one comparable to the melt in your mouth overwhelming goodness of a bold pork broth. Noodles are just the right amount of firm, the minced chicken is flavorful, and the toppings are fresh. 

Some non-food details. This place is always super busy, and bar seating is the same as dining at a table. I've gone on weekday odd times and still waited for 30-45 mins, because, well, there is never a wrong time for ramen.

Try it out and throw it into your wintry mix of comforting soupy noodle bowls. 

*Will update review if I ever get something that's not the chicken paitan

In my recent trip to NY one of my friends recommended to come to Ivan Ramen to have some ramen. Definitely not disappointed!! I made reservations for 2 at 7PM and it was a great time.  After a long day of exploring the city, the quick service and a condense menu with different options was delightful. 

I ordered the Tokyo shoyu Ramen which wasn't overpowered by the soy sauce and the pork buns were tasty even though I'm not a big fan of eating pork. Took some awesome shots of the plates. Will be coming back next time I'm in town!

I really wanted to like Ivan Ramen, but it keeps disappointing.  

As someone who works in a ramen restaurant as well, I have been on a quest to find best ramen in NYC. Ivan is usually listed as one of the best in a variety of food publications, so I was surprised when I found the Shio Ramen at the "Slurp Shop" location in the Gotham Westside Market underwhelming. The buckwheat noodles were indeed different than typical ramen.... but it wasn't Better. Furthermore, the soup and topping, while edible, didn't really leave any impression at all. It was just forgettable. 

Fast forward a few years, my co-worker convinces me to give the Clinton Street location a try. It's much better than the Slurp Shop location, he heard. When we stopped by around 7pm on a weeknight, there was already a 45 minute wait - no problem, I do not mind waiting for good food. 

We finally got seated, and ordered the pork buns and Japanese fried chicken to start. My friend got the Triple Pork Garlic Mazemen, and I went for the Tonkotsu Tsukemen. 

Maybe we should have gotten the soup ramen instead of mazemen (mix ramen, less broth) or tsukemen (dipping ramen), but neither of us thought  the ramen was particularly outstanding. While I loved the pickled collard greens, I'm not sure it was an ingredient that really tied the whole dish together. I can see how pickled greens would go well with a heavy tonkotsu broth, but the rate at which the soup cooled down very quickly, didn't enhance the deliciousness of the rich tonkotsu. My friend said there really was not a lot of pork in the mazemen... 

As for the buns and fried chicken, I've definitely had much much better. I wish I didn't order the pork buns... at $5 a piece, it really did not deliver.
The best thing was the charred eggplant appetizer in tahini. A delicious blend of tastes. Somewhat sweet. I was very surprised by the result. The ramen is ok
Every single dish we had was amazing from the Japanese chicken and also the squid as appetizers to the two ramens! I don't understand why the average rating on yelp isn't higher! It should be!

I enjoy the ramen at Ivan Ramen. I have had the Tokyo Shoyu ramen. The standout quality are the rye noodles which give them an interesting mouthfeel and flavor that you don't get at other ramen shops. I don't think the chicken broth holds up to the stiff competition in the area. Kyuri Pickles were tasty. Would love to see if they have ago-dashi or other fish based broths on the menu.

Due to Ivan Ramen's episode on Chef's Table, there is much hype around his restaurants, and ramen. I'd been wanting to come here for sometime, but after being quoted with a long wait one evening, we planned ahead and obtained a reservation easily via Opentable. 
When we came in around 6pm on a Sunday evening, the restaurant was about half or three quarters full, with people also lining up and waiting already. We were seated immediately at the bar stools with our reservation. The staff behind the bar greeted us immediately, giving us water and menus right away. 
We ordered quickly after being seated, with our fried chicken appetizer being served perhaps 20 minutes after we'd ordered. It was titled 'Japanese fried chicken', but I couldn't really identify anything that tasted obviously Japanese. The menu stated that it included togarashi, which added a nice kick, but really could have been any other pepper. The chicken was served with a ranch sauce and was absolutely delicious- crisp on the outside and moist on the inside. 
Our noodles were served shortly after. My husband got the Tokyo shoyu ramen. He finished his noodles but then said they were average. On the other hand, I relished every bite of my lamb dan dan noodles. They were spicy and full of flavor, that being said, they were also very, very salty. 
Was very happy with the food, though my husband was not- would recommend and return.

I think the hype far outstrips the quality of the ramen, which is very good by the way, but not the mind blowing, awe inspiring way that I had expected. I suppose the restaurant is a victim of its own popularity. If you've ever been to Japan, you would consider Ivan's ramen to be quite standard.

The hostesses here are eager to discourage and turn away guests by lying about wait times. We had called ahead to ask if there was any way to reserve a table for two. The hostess told us we had to walk in to get our name on the wait list and wouldn't tell us how long the wait was, nor did she mention we could reserve online. Upon arrival, we were quoted a ONE HOUR wait time while the restaurant was half empty. We checked Open Table to see if they did reservations and there was a spot open in a few minutes, so we booked that and walked back in to get seated at one of those we saw open earlier. The hostesses continued to quote an hour wait to all walk ins throughout our dinner when this was clearly not the case on a Tuesday evening. All of the walk in guests were turned away/decided to leave. They neglected to mention the option of booking online as they did earlier to us. Lying about wait times is unacceptable as it cheats your servers out of tips and the restaurant out of business. Get your host stand in line.

Great ramen, but in no way worth waiting an hour for. The service was poor and they do not have chilled glasses for their canned beers. Two of the six draft beer selections were no longer stocked. Best thing about the evening was consistent water refills.

Really great ramen and if you don't mind dark meat chicken get the fried chicken appetizer. We got the fried chicken appetizer to start and I really liked the sauce that it came in and it was crispy, but I didn't like that it was mainly dark meat chicken. I also got the chili oil ramen soup and it was very good. It wasn't too spicy, but I wish the noodles were a little softer. I also tasted the one with chicken broth and it was very good so I would recommend both.

This review is for 4.5 stars. 

Excellent ramen. Might not be the best I've ever tried but worth a stop for its variety and specialties. Ivan is a little different in that they have a few low broth or no broth options for dipping rather than traditional noodle and broth. I went with the chili ramen and asked for extra spicy - they delivered. Really great taste where the broth is so hot but you're not overtaken with chili taste. Added enoki mushroom and egg. Came with some smashed egg but gotta upgrade for the regular egg if you're a fan of traditional ramen. Solid egg where it runs a bit. Minced pork was just average and I think this dish needs a little pork belly to make it work. Enoki good unique addition but coming raw it's kinda like a shabby shabu thing that's weird. Noodles very thin but cooked right and al dents. Small bowl but because of the spice level I was full. Beer menu actually quite good with tons of IPA and about 6 on draft overall. Expensive beers for sure at $10 average from draft and a little more for cans, but also have some sake if you're into that. I really liked Ivan and think it's a very nice option and great that it takes reservations on OpenTable because that line can get heavy. Service was absolutely fantastic from the bar. And I'm still feeling the heat a day later so thumbs up for that.

Absolutely amazing! I've made ramen quite a lot, and I know for a fact I could never make ramen this great. I had the spicy ramen with chicken.
