I'm a huge fan of spices and explore with ghost pepper, Carolina reaper, and the spices around that range.  This ramen gave me an immensely enjoyable experience, and I would recommend it to anyone who enjoyed spices. It's not overwhelming and I definitely recommend it.
Pretty good ramen. My friend and I tried of the apps and they were all very flavorful / different. Would eat here again.

Owned by Ivan Orkin, a Long Island native who grew famous cooking ramen in Tokyo. For a decade this Long Island native was the ramen king in Tokyo when he finally returned home and opened his ramen shop in the LES. I have seen him on tv a couple times and was excited to finally be able to try those famous ramen.

I went to the "slurp shop" soon after it opened a few years ago (yeah, never wrote a review for it!) but just in case you are wondering, yes was pretty good!!

 Believe it or not it wasn't till a few months ago that I finally went to Ivan Ramen. I made a reservation for 7:30pm but we ended up getting there earlier and the hostess was able to sit us after a 10min wait. We ordered a few things and loved it all!

Appetizer-
* HAMU KATSU SANDO
smoked ham, bulldog sauce, pickles, redeye kewpie mayo, cheddar-dashi dip
* JAPANESE FRIED CHICKEN
toasted garlic caramel, togarashi, shiso ranch

Main Course-

Mazemen (thick whole wheat noodles with sauce):
* TRIPLE PORK TRIPLE GARLIC
tonkotsu broth, pork belly two ways

Ramen (thin rye noodles with broth):
* TOKYO SHOYU
soy sauce, dashi + chicken broth, pork belly, soft egg, toasted nori

I will definitely go back and try other dishes!

I had the Chicken Paitan (ramen) and softshell crab appetizer (the special of the day). The ramen was great, very flavorful and creamy but the star of the day was the softshell crab sandwich. Would go back for the appetizer but I prefer other restaurants closer to my apartment for ramen.

Umami has been mastered at Ivan Ramen. I really enjoyed eating here and would recommend the brothless lamb ramen (the one with the egg yolk) which is creamy and tangy , if ramen were a pasta this would be the most similar to the Italian carbonara.

I came to this ramen bar for late night dinner with my boyfriend. The venue is a very nice small space with a lively crowd. The ramen bowl I had purchased was delicious but they only give you one small piece of pork belly. I highly recommend you ask for an additional add on or select another ramen bar for the price you pay
Good service. Super busy. Food quite overly salty for me. But, maybe that is what "umami" is?
The hamu katsu sando and calamari appetizers were mediocre but the noodles were definitely something different. The ramens had a delicate flavor to them. Would definitely return!

I would say I am not a traditionalist when it comes to ramen flavors so if you enjoy bold flavors, definitely the place to go. I ordered the Chicken Paitan with roasted tomatoes and it hit the spot and the tofu appetizer was cooked perfectly. Also watched the Chef's Table episode about Ivan Orkin beforehand - made the experience much more memorable!

The noodles were great, but the broth uses katsuoboshi (dehydrated and fermented bonito fish) as a base, which isn't my favorite when it's used so generously.  I like that seasoning more sparingly.  It's an OG ramen move to use it in the dashi (soup base) but it was overwhelming for me-it may be because I have a sensitivity to the fishy/seafood taste, so if you like that then go for it!
Great ramen! Really enjoyed the triple pork triple garlic! I finished my meal within minutes

Nasty!!! Veg broth tastes like burnt coffee. And dipping ramen dish is covered in a pile of pickled color greens which has a very strong taste. It ruins the whole dish if you dont like it. Noodles were just pathetic. Get some authentic ramen with a cool atmosphere at Ippudo Ny on 65th ave! Best ramen ever. Ive never gone to a restaurant and paid for a dish I didnt eat. This was insanely bad! Felt bad I waisted one of my NY dinners on this!

I've eaten at Ivan twice, with one year between each visit. The ramen was really salty, both times. It's so salty that it overpowers every other flavor. Overall, Ivan is not mind-blowing. The menu is interesting, but ultimately underwhelming. Better ramen spots exist in the city with less wait time and more flavor.

We walked into Ivans Ramen on a Friday night around 6ish. There were a lot of people but we were seates immediately at the bar! Bar was nice because you get to see the chefs making other people's dishes which made us know what we want to orderz 
We ordered japanese chicken, onigiri, Tokyo Shio ramen, and one of the cold dipping ramens. 

Ramen noodles texture was amazing, both hot and cold ones and portion

As for the crafted beers, it was on the pricy side. We got one of the recommended beers and it was 10  each. Total bill was around 110 for 2. I would def come here again because of the ramen and the vibe.

Service was excellent,bartender and manager kept refilling our water glasses; asked us how the food was; and recommended the most popular dishes. 
We had the fried chicken and pork dumpling appetizer and were great. The Chicken Ramen was also very good. We went on Fathers Day and before the restaurant opened it had a line! 
The place is small so it's better to be there early

This place has the best two appetizers I've ever had in my life! The Japanese fried chicken and the eggplant are delicious and so unique. This was a nice surprise because I actually came here to try to the ramen. The chicken paitan ramen is good. The broth is rich. They put ground chicken in it (not a big fan) but overall the ramen is bursting with flavor.

Very good ramen. Flavorful and fresh. 
The staff is ok. The place is quite tiny though.
It's very non traditional in a non superior way... pictured below is comparable to dan dan noodle... mehhh

This place is definitely not worth trying.  I had the chicken patine and it was salty.  It just taste like the only ingredient in the broth is soy sauce. My friend had the spicy chicken and she said the same thing.  I gave this place a 2 star because of the service,  the rating for the ramen broth is 0 star.  Complete miss for us.  So disappointed.  Need to go to an authentic Japanese ramen shop.

Finally made it to the Ivan ramen that became tourist attraction after he was aired on Netflix. The restaurant was sort of out of nowhere in LES. We had to walk so much from the train station. If it wasn't for the tv show, I don't think I would've made it out here.. the restaurant was actually bigger than it looked on TV but narraw and long.

The menu looked decent but expensive. I think we basically paid over $20 per ramen with taxes and tips.. the portions weren't too big and the ramens were very salty. The noodles were unique though. A lot thinner than usual ramen shops. Also, they specialize in chicken broth so try the paitan. To me, it had that chicken smell and I didn't like the grounded chicken meat.. I'd rather get the spicy one. Spicy ramen was good but again, too spicy though. I mean, overall experience wasn't too bad but I don't know if I want to make this trip for an overpriced ramen again.
Best ramen I've had of all time. I recommend the Chicken Paitan. Service was fast and appetizers were great. If you're in NYC definitely check this place out.

Great food here. But we can see why it's 3.5 stars for the amount of food vs the price. What we loved best about ivan ramen was the beer selection. They have an extensive beer menu for a ramen restaurant that would all go well with the appetizers. I wouldn't mind coming back here just to try the beers and rest of the appetizers. 
We started with one musubi for $5. It's literally a one biter. It was delicious. The pork was well balanced out by the plum, but we couldn't justify one bite being $5. If you ordered three, it would've the price of one bowl of ramen lol. 
We also ordered the fried eggplant and grilled corn. The eggplant was amazing. Good sauce and perfect temperature and texture. The grilled corn was ok. It was overloaded with herbs and spices in my opinion and half the corn was cold while the other half was warm-ish. 
We got the shio ramen and paitan. My husband and I each liked the other ramen. I liked how the paitan was heavier, thicker, and saltier. The shio was great but I preferred mine more. The noodles here were wonderful. Def made the ramen better.

I tried the spicy miso Ramen and I also tried the Tsukemen My daughter had, EVERYTHING was delicious and full of umami. I also tried the Japanese fried chicken and that was a bit too sweet for my liking and the breading was a bit thick ( I prefer a Karagee light and crispy coating). I am definitely going back to taste more.
This place is the ramen equivalent of general tso's chicken, but worse. In fact this food shouldn't even be called ramen. Please rename the restaurant to "Ivan soup noodle."  Thanks.
Wow! This place was so good. Please give it a try. It's a great place to get good ramen.

Super disappointed, came to NY for the weekend and saw Strictly Dumpling's raving review of this shop and the store flaunts it's Michelin Guide status. 

Ordered the pork buns and then two shoyu ramen bowls. Everything was extremely salty, it was as if everything was marinating in soy sauce over multiple days. I'll most likely never come here again because it's overhyped, the food is way too salty and everything is overpriced.

You're better off going to other ramen shops in NY, there are plenty better ones out there, especially if you dont want to spend $50 on a disgusting meal after waiting almost an hour.

My friend and I came here at 6 pm, and it was just starting to get busy but the two of us got seated right away. We both ordered the shoyu ramen, and I also got a draft beer to pair. This place is right next to a Boba Guys, and there are cafes super close by as well, so the location is great. The food itself was pretty overpriced for what it was. It was a good bowl of ramen and the soft boiled egg was perfection, but besides that it was nothing too special. The broth was a little too salty, and the chashu pork was good but a little tough in spots. I wouldn't say it's the best place to spend your money, but it's decent ramen if it's what you're craving.

Ivan Ramen had some great appetizers, but the ramen was just okay. Since we came as a large group, we had preset appetizers and then each ordered our own ramen bowl.

- Kyuri Pickles: pretty tasty! A little sour in a good way and mildly spicy; it was a refreshing way to start our meal
- Japanese Fried Chicken: really yummy! Definitely tasted fried but was still somehow delicate. Also, it came with a tasty white dipping sauce :)
- Pork Belly Steamed Buns: super flavorful with a plush bun and a good proportion of meat and sauce
- Pickled Daikon XO: a sort of fermented vegetable with chili garlic on top--this was good, but I probably wouldn't buy it
- Tofu Coney Island: I'd pass on this one because it was kind of strange; as the name suggests, all of the toppings (like mustard) could have been on a hotdog instead of fried tofu

I ordered the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen with enoki mushrooms as an add-on. The noodles were springy, the egg was perfectly cooked, and there was a generous amount of vegetables. However, I wasn't a fan of the broth, which didn't really have a distinct flavor of soy sauce and was mostly just salty tasting. I also tried a bite of my friend's chicken paitan noodles and probably liked them a little more than my ramen. I thought that the flavor profile did not really taste Asian at all, oddly enough, and my friend agreed. Three people in my party ordered the red spicy chili ramen and said it was not very spicy at all, which was kind of disappointing.

Ivan Ramen is a cute place to eat (we ate outside in the garden which was kept quite cool by a sort of vortex of three fans), and the waitress who helped us was super nice. If I came here again, though, I'd probably prefer to stick to appetizers--the pork buns and Japanese fried chicken are where it's at!

Unbelievable food and service!

Get the fried eggplant it is beyond wonderful. The barley iced tea is delightful too.

Sigh... I had really high hopes for Ivan Ramen after watching Chef's Table and just hearing all the hype. For all you ramen fanatics thinking about going to Ivan Ramen, trust me: the ramen here is nothing special.

I booked a res for two on a Wednesday night and was quickly seated @ the bar. The space is cozy and packed with Japanese decor -- that was a plus. Another plus was the robust beer selection; they had specialty beers on tap & in cans, along with a respectable array of ciders. So far so good.

Onto the food, we started with the Pork Buns and Japanese Chicken. The pork buns were meh... pork did not melt in your mouth and have had far superior buns elsewhere. The chicken was pretty good and if you're with a group I would suggest putting in an order.

OK OK OK... now for the important part: the ramen! They offer standard shio, shoyu, tonkotsu etc broths but also have a special chicken paitan broth. IF YOU EAT HERE, GET THE CHICKEN PAITAN. It has a solid flavor, but again have had much more dimensional and better broths elsewhere. We also tried the shoyu ramen and wow.... flavor was so flat.

Again, if you are a ramen fanatic, don't waste your time. So many better options in NYC.

Worth the wait. My friend & I visited New York in December & we walked from our Airbnb in the lower east side to ind dinner one night. This place looked so good but was very crowded & had a 30 minute wait or so. We decided to wait because ramen sounded so good. When we finally were seated, our food got to us in a timely manner & it was DELICIOUS. Some of the best ramen I've had. I highly suggest this place!

I've always liked this place even though it does lack the authenticity so many tout as their reason for going. The roasted tomato is amazing. It's delicious and fast. 

I usually eat in but I decided to order once. The broth container had spilled during their speedy delivery. Called them up, full refund, no problem. Thanks!

The food is outstanding. We sat at a small table outdoors that was really cramped. I wish that we could have had a bigger table or more space, especially once we got all of our drinks and food on the table. Service was good. Would come back for the ramen definitely. Best I've had so far!

Pretty solid chicken-based broth ramen. The restaurant has hype which comes with high expectations. Good ramen, overall - the egg is just yolk (I ordered the Chicken Paitan, does not come with traditional Ajitama). The Japanese fried chicken comes drenched in a sauce not unlike general Tso's - it is not your traditional chicken karaage. Good sake selection. Trendy atmosphere/crowd if you're into that - not a bad ramen bar to bring a date.

Ivan Ramen was always on my bucket list. So I had to go. I made a reservation 8:30pm. I got there hour late so I understood what the situation would be like. It wasn't extremely busy but it had traffic. I approached the front and the hostess said it would be 10-15 min wait. So I thought that's cool. But then another host person came up to me with a very snarky rude tone. And said " because u came extremely late and u missed ur reservation you have to wait 10-15 min wait". First of all I was already told that. And second of all there's no reason to be rude. Anyways I waited. Started off with a bad taste in my mouth. We finally got a table. The ambience is decent. Very small cramped. I'm ok with that because I love small Japanese ramen spots. But it wasn't comfortable. Sat on the wall table. The server we had was extremely great bless him. But the other workers around him were too casual at moments. We ordered the fried chicken, tsukemen and shoyu ramen. The fried chicken was in a sauce that was good but it was too strong. It had a very vinegar salt taste. I understood what they tried to do but as a app before ramen not sure if this good. Because ramen is salty. So just for the fried chicken alone, my tongue was over stimulated with salt and vinegar. It was cool for the first couple bites but after that it got too much. The tsukemen noodles and pork were dope. The chewy texture of the noodles were great. The pork was tender and flavorful. The pickled greens on the side was also too strong. Didn't care for the them and the dipping broth needed more broth and came out almost cold. The thing for me about tsukemen, because the noodles and other components are cold, when u dip, it makes the broth cold. I hate that. But now the dipping broth was not hot and filled 2/5 of the bowls. It was a downer. The shoyu ramen had a smoky flavor to it. It was good. But not amazing. Overall everything was overpriced for the experience and taste. Nothing special. If I'm paying ramen in the 16$ and up price range I'm expecting something bomb. A bowl that puts me into another dimension. Even if the host was rude, even if some staff members are this or that. Food is the most important thing and I didn't feel impressed. I will give Ivan another try. Hopefully my thoughts change.

Went for dinner 8/19/19

I am not a Ramen guy. Sorry my Son was celebrating his 21 Birthday for a few days in NYC so he got to pick food spots. I was not supposed to like this place and I planned not to like it. I did not want to pay for Ramen so I got the only thing on the small menu that sounded slightly American which was the fried chicken. I loved it because it was spicy and also just about as tender as I have ever had. 

My son and my wife loved the Ramen they picked and I did actually taste the broth and thought it was very good. I hate to admit it but I was wrong again this place Rocked.
Prices seem a bit steep for the portions received and my ramen was luke warm not hot which was not ideal, overall it was just okay.
The service was nice and helpful. The food was better. The sour beer was tasty. I loved it all. Thank you.

Had a bit of an odd experience here because I planned to give Ivan Ramen five stars up until we got the ramen itself. The appetizers were AWESOME. We got pork buns, crispy eggplant and the fried chicken - each one was perfect. 

I can't quite put my finger on what was wrong with the ramen, but none of us loved it. The broth wasn't as rich or creamy as I'm used to and it just lacked some flavor. We all added roasted tomato to the ramen at our server's recommendation and when we tried it we decided it really had no place in the ramen - just an odd addition. 

Overall I would definitely come back; the outdoor porch area was really cute and the service was friendly. But if you have "ramen" in the name of your restaurant, the ramen should be a total show stopper, and unfortunately it just wasn't.

Not what I had expected from a ramen shop at all when I first walked in. The decorations were good and hip but didn't set the right tone for ramen. I was still hopeful initially, as the menu seemed pretty standard for a ramen restaurant, but what stood out to me were the whole wheat noodles. No one eats whole wheat ramen. That's just wrong.

I ordered the shio ramen but was very underwhelmed. I got that the owners were attempting to add a bit of flair to their ramen but it was a miss for me because the broth didn't have the richness of taste that I've come to expect.

My boyfriend usually prefers phó over ramen, but made reservations for 7pm on a Saturday after seeing Jimmy Fallon day this was his favorite ramen spot in NYC. We arrived at the restaurant at about 7:05 and were promptly seated with no wait. We reviewed the menu and decided on the Japanese fried chicken as an appetizer and chicken paitan and tonkotsu ramen for entrees. As I ordered the tonkotsu ramen, the waitress advised me that the ramen was cold, dry noodles with a separate bowl of dipping broth, so I decided to change to mine to the chicken paitan as well and add the shoyu glazed pork belly. 
As we waited for our appetizer, our waters were promptly refilled. Although the restaurant was not as packed as expected it to be, the kitchen seemed to be backed up. It took about 10-15 minutes for our appetizer to arrive at our table. 
I was excited to try the Japanese fried chicken because I read lots of great reviews, however it fell short of my expectations. The chicken was very sweet and more sticky than crispy, but the ranch dipping sauce was good. About 10 minutes after our plates were collected, a waitress came by to apologize to us and the table next to ours for the wait and said that our ramen would be right out. It was another 10 minutes before our ramen arrived, but it looked delicious and was served with a lime and optional chili oil. The pork belly was sliced thick and very delicious, but was a little overpriced at $6 for one piece. I love rich broth, but this broth was almost too salty to bear. I had a drink of water after almost every bite and couldn't finish the broth. Overall it was good, but not worth the hype.

Good ramen. I had the Spicy Red Chili Ramen. I went around 8 pm on a Sunday night. I ended up paying $20 including tax and tip for the one bowl. The seating is a little cramped. I sat at the bar between two couples, and it was super loud. The music was a little loud and there were a bunch of people yelling at each other trying to speak over the noise. Service was good though. The waitress was very attentive and refilled my water whenever it was low.

As for the taste, it's good ramen. My first thought when it was served was "Wow, this looks kinda small for $16", but that was not a problem at all. I felt full afterwards since they put plenty of noodles in the bowl. The noodles were interesting; I think they were rye instead of the usual wheat. The initial taste was a little funky, but I soon got used to it. The noodles soak up the broth quite well. The broth was quite spicy. Don't recommend for people who can barely handle spicy food. The egg was somehow broken into pieces and not whole, but personally I didn't mind. All the condiments were a nice touch to the overall flavor. I rate 4/5 because the ramen was great, but the price was on the high side for me. And the seating is cramped.

Love the ramen noodles. I had the triple pork ramen with thick brothy sauce. Excellent fatter noodles perfectly cooked. I found the flavor a bit too smoky but otherwise good. The chicken broth for ramen soups is creamy and good with balanced flavors.
The fried chicken app was too greasy and heavy. Eggplant app was fantastic, and the eggplant was creamy and soft inside each piece.
Service is friendly and excellent.

TLDR: Ok ramen, but mediocre at best. I'd probably go somewhere else for ramen. But if you're a chef's table fan, it's pretty cool knowing the story behind the restaurant! I'd opt for Ichiran instead.

Food: 5/10
In a word: underwhelming. The broth wasn't as rich as I expected and was heavily under salted, in my opinion. The ramen egg (which is usually my absolute favorite part of this dish) was also pretty bland. On the bright side, the noodles were cooked to perfection! 

I got the Shio ramen and my friend got the Shoyu ramen. Both were bland, but the Shoyu ramen had a slightly tastier broth.

Price & Portion: 6/10
Pretty standard prices for ramen in New York (~$20). However, I really wouldn't pay that much for mediocre ramen when there's better food for the same price like 5 minutes away.

Service: 8/10
Our server was very friendly and helpful when we asked him for recommendations! Very quick service and kind workers.

Ambience: 8/10
The decor is very modern and pretty casual! It's a lot of fun looking around at the set up after seeing it on Chef's Table!
Tasty ramen and cool atmosphere! A little different than traditional ramen but in a good way. Pretty standard price but considering all that they put in your bowl, it's worth it.

Tried the vegetarian ramen with shoyu base. The broth was bitter but ramen consistency was good. Will not get it again.  Thumbs up to the Ivan Palmer though -- combination of Yuzu lemonade and barley tea.

Really enjoyed the food and experience here. Made reservations beforehand for lunchtime on a Sunday and the lunch crowd was still there with the place packed. We sat at the bar which I enjoyed since you can see the kitchen and there is also cool artwork behind the bar. Bartender was chatty and made great recommendations.

We got the pork buns and Tokyo Shoyu. Pork buns were excellent with a soft bun and tender, saucy pork. I really enjoyed this ramen and it was a wake up call for my taste buds compared to other traditional ramens out there. Perfect ratio of broth to noodles (I find most places have too much broth). I really loved the rye noodles. So much different flavor in a great way. The combination of everything in the ramen went well together. Not too salty at all in my opinion. Good portion sizes and price.

The wait was a little long when we first got here but I have to say the food was worth the long wait!!! We found out after that in the future we can call to make a reservation which is super convenient.  I got the barley Tea it was interesting but very tasty, we started out with the pork buns which were super flavorful and fresh. Both dishes that we got were super filling and super tasty. I would highly recommend coming here if you are looking for a good ramen place.

I've always been a fan of food shows like chefs table. And when Ivan ramen was shown in one of the episodes, I was determined to check it out. Now going on 3 years, I've been visiting the restaurant on a bi-monthly basis.. & I live in Ohio. 

The new Spicy Red Chili Ramen packs a good amount of heat in comparison to the other traditional Ramen they offer. With a rich and flavorful broth, well prepared vegetables and a spicy aroma which is definitely present. It's definitely a must try if you're a fan of spicy food.

For the price you expect at least the same size of bowl as other ramen places but not here, here is smaller with a little of meat. The flavor was just Okay. I was still hungry at the end, went to a bodega for a small bite to feel complete.

Great ramen! They offer some vegetarian options.
We also got the eggplant appetizer and it was amazing! I loved it and I don't even like eggplant. They also offer a bunch of sake and we got a super
Cute one that came in a panda glass we were able
To keep.

I love the atmosphere here and even more the FOOD!! This is one of my favorite noodle
Spots in the Lowe east side. I would recommend this place to anyone. This is my definite goto especially when it's a rainy day.
Just a wonderful story.  An American goes to japan and learns the timeless craft of ramen.  Brings it back to the heart of the LES.  A modern day "Marco Polo," for real.  The flavors are so memorable

I was in the area to get Boba Guys & decided to stop by here for a quick lunch with a friend. My friend had told me that this spot was featured on Chef's Table so I had pretty high expectations.

Pork musubi bites (2/5): Super super tiny at $5 per bite so I was very disappointed. The sweetness of the plum also threw me off a little bit...

Gyukotsu (4/5): First time trying tsukemen. They give a good amount of noodles so that was reassuring. The short rib was sooo soft and chewy. The beef dipping broth was also pretty good - very hearty. 

Was not particularly blown away by this place. Would definitely hit up other ramen spots before this spot.

This place had been on my to-try list for a few years so I was absolutely stoked when my friend made a reservation for this place. She said this was her favorite ramen spot and *she is a vegetarian*. So it's dope that this place is veggie-friendly!

Little did I know this restaurant was also featured on Netflix's Chef Table - which I promptly went home and watched after dining in.

I had high expectations walking in but was blown away by the flavors. We ordered the Triple Garlic Triple pork, Vegetarian Ramen, Chicken Paitan, and the Short Rib Tsukemen. Friend had said the short rib tsukemen was almost always sold out when he was there so when we found out they still had it that night, we had to order it of course.

Absolutely adored the Triple Garlic Triple Pork. Packed with flavor, excellent texture throughout. Short Rib was fall apart tender and the broth on the side was incredibly rich and delicious. Chicken Paitan was not my favorite but certainly not a bad dish. Vegetarian ramen was also not bad, but IMO, was not as stand out as the other dishes. 

Episode was a great complement to the meal and really happy I got to try :)

The ramen itself didn't particularly live up to the hype, but appetizers were delicious! The Japanese fried chicken was my favorite thing on the menu. You also really can't go wrong with pork buns, but Ivan Ramen did an exceptional job. The ramen noodles are rye noodles, so it's not your expected ramen which is maybe why I didn't love it too much. There are plenty of vegan and vegetarian options on the menu!

The restaurant itself has a great covered patio with heaters so you can still enjoy sitting outside even in the cold NY winter! Inside the restaurant is narrow and probably not great for groups. We sat outside with a group of 6 and it was pretty tight. 

I really liked that they sold swag. You can get glassware for super cheap which is a great idea for tourists wanting to remember their trip and show off the fact they went to a restaurant featured of Chef's Table!
The best Ramen place in town by far !after tried so many places in New York! Great food, great service and cool place !

After watching Chef's Table about Ivan Ramen I had been wanting to check out when I come to NYC. I was pretty easily able to get a reservation though it is a pretty small restaurant. 

I started with the spicy pickles and pickled daikon. I was a huge fan of the pickled daikon. The saltiness of the dried shrimp with the tart vinegar was a wonderful combo. 

The fried chicken was highly recommended and I'm so glad I tried it. The chicken was perfectly cooked and juicy. The shiso ranch was the perfect dipping sauce. 

I had the tonkatsu ramen which they serve cold. Which means the ingredients were precooked and cold to room temperature but they provide a dish of warm broth to dip in before you eat. I'd never had ramen served like this and I'm not the biggest fan. It's hard to eat and pretty messy. Though the dish was still delicious.

It was a crisp fall day and my friend and I were in the mood for some ramen. This spot has been on our list ever since we saw Chef's Table. We called ahead since we knew there was probably a wait for this place at all times and Grace was very kind on the phone and took care of us to come in later that afternoon. 

Once we got there we were seated immediately. We ordered some apps -- and oh my heavens the eggplant app will essentially dominate your experience at Ivan. To be honest maybe just order that. Their new fall menu items - are questionable to say the least -- not sure if they actually got the Ivan stamp of approval or what because the crunchy kale otashi app is a funny attempt at making an appetizer. I too could put soy sauce on cold kale...

Our kind waiter Elmer soon brought us our Ramen. I realize I am not the targeted clientele at a Ramen spot but I've had some incredibly excellent vegetarian Ramen in the great big city of New York. Chuko, Ippudo, Momofuku, goodness even Wagamama kills it which isn't saying much. Trust me even with the city tap water and the limited supply of ingredients, excellent vegetarian ramen can be achieved. Unfortunately my first taste of Ivan's Vegetarian Ramen I laughed thinking it was a prank! No way would the great chef's table Ivan serve me a vegetarian broth made out of muddy street water and coffee grinds. But alas he did. Either the man has never tried it himself, or his tastebuds are questionable. And if it's based on some tradition then heavens please just add another veggie broth to the menu for the vegetarians that like good flavor and umami. Doesn't seem like too much to ask for but what do I know.

All in all the service was excellent, the food was questionable to say the least. My return to this establishment is still up in the air but leaning towards a big ole no. Vegetarians beware!

There was a list of ramen spots I wanted to try during my stay in NYC and this place wasn't on the list but decided to give Ivan Ramen a try since they were Michelin Starred last year and the years before that plus I was in the area. Regrettably I wished I had walked to Nakamura rather than going here for dinner. The ramen wasn't as flavorful as I expected and read. The starters were pretty good,  come back soley for the starters but that's about it. The service is awesome, my server was really informative and friendly. There are tons of ramen spots in NYC so I would highly suggest you go elsewhere especially if you're going to be paying that much for it. Does not live up to the hype it's not bad but definitely not good either. There are other places I would have choose but choose this place because of the Michelin starred. 

Tokyo Shio Ramen:
It was very light but not much flavor after the initial sip. Even though there was only just one piece of chashu it was pretty good. 

Gyokotsu Tsukemen:
Meat was really good other than that nothing else. Broth feels like it's definitely salty but doesn't have much depth besides that. You're left with a feeling of wanting more ...

Spicy Red Chili Ramen: 
Its spicy and has a kick but after that the flavor is non-existent. Has no meat.

Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen:
Has some flavor but not as much as I would think triple pork and triple a garlic to have. I ended up getting a slightly bitter taste after each bite. I didn't enjoy it as much but out of the line up it had the most flavor.

Came here on my trip from the UK and trekked especially out to try the famous 'Ivan Ramen Noodles'. Sat at the bar as I was on my own, which meant I could make conversation with the chap next to me and read my book - i really enjoyed this! The speciality Ivan Ramen Mikkeller lager was a gentle IPA. Service was fast, had the Tonkotsu Tsukemen - probably one of my favorite dishes of all time. And was disappointed with what i got after much anticipation. Thick udon noodles (OK fine, broth wasn't hot enough (IMO should be scolding hot if you're dipping and dripping) and had to ask them to heat it up for me. Pork belly was thick sliced, not intricate thin slices - which allows the broth to heat the pork properly. For the price - and bare in mind i'm from the UK were we can get incredible ramen for half the price - i just wasn't super feeling it. Sad as i had such high hopes!

Got the tsukemen. The broth isn't as rich as I'd like but it's still my go to order when i go here. Steamed pork buns are good. Japanese fried chicken (karaage) was different. It had a semi sweet coating. Their spicy ramen is really spicy. I've had friends who like spicy food, dying from the hotness level of the spicy ramen so get it if you know you can handle it. It gets busy for dinner so make a reservation in case.

Ivan ramen (3.5)
I was super stoked to go to this place and I was not disappointed. I got the Tokyo shoyu, chicken paitan and the spicy lamb dan dan. The shoyu had a wonderful deep soy flavor that has a complex seafood profile that accented the thin and tender noodles. The eggs were also soft boiled to perfection and the pork belly gave an extra meat flavor to the overall ramen. The chicken paitan was also very delicious. The chicken broth was very very thick and creamy and it worked so well with the thin noodles. The ground chicken was cooked to perfection and all of its flavors infused into the soup and noodles. In my opinion, if I was to come here again, I would definitely get chicken paitan. As for the spicy lamb dan dan, I was a bit underwhelmed. I love spicy food but this dish got too overwhelmingly spicy for me to a point that I wasn't able to taste the other components of this ramen. I would recommend asking the servers to tone down on the spice if possible so that the lamb and sesame flavor profiles come out more. Overall this is a great place and would come here again from time to time. FYI- They do reservations so you wouldn't have to wait in a line and can go to the local bars nearby when you're waiting for a seat.

Went on busy Friday night. Bar tender was still quick and attentive. Food came quickly and was tasty. a few beers on tap and a decent list of bottle/can options available. A little pricey for what it is, but positive experience overall.

Googled Ramen places in the lower Manhattan area.  I Immediately recognized 
Ivan Ramen as the place I saw the segment on TV. That's where I wanted to go for my birthday lunch. There was a long line of people waiting outside, that was not a problem as it was a beautiful day out.
The young lady who took my name was very pleasant and friendly. She took my number and texted me about 20 minutes later when space at the counter was available. We had the great fortune to have Jam as our server. What a nice guy!!
Friendly and personable & made great suggestions. He even threw in a special side of the Curried Cauliflower as a birthday treat. Amazing!!! As was the Steamed pork buns, Japanese fried Chicken & Chicken Paiten Ramen. My partner had the Spicy Red Chili glazed Chashu. Loved it!
Along with a glass of Yuzu and red wine we were set! Thanks Ivan Ramen & Jam for a memorable 57th birthday lunch!!
We will definitely be back!!

I lived in Japan for close to half a decade and have sampled lots of ramen and the Shio Ramen at Ivan Ramen really does live up to it's reputation.  The ajitama were perfect with custard-y yolks, the chashu melted in my mouth, and the noodles had just the right amount of bite.  However as expected, the broth was the star of the show and met, if not exceeded expectations.  Appetizers were good, but but not great.  Still strongly recommend!

I eat ramen all the time and I highly recommend this place. Ivan Ramen was on chef's table on Netflix, so we had to stop by for our NY trip. My boyfriend and I had split a bowl of the chicken paitan and it was packing in flavor and great for a lighter lunch. The waiters were super nice and Ivan even came out to talk to all of the customers. Great food and great customer service. Only thing is the restaurant is pretty poppin and a little small, so I don't recommend large groups.

I had very high hopes after watching a chef's table episode. However, it didnt live up to my expectations at all. Japanese fried chicken was okay, it had an unexpected sour kick which caught me by surprise. Having Tokyo Shio ramen after the JFC was not a good decision. JFC had a strong flavor and the shio ramen was really mild. So, I couldnt taste much of the broth. Maybe I just had bad decisions on that day.

I have wanted to try this place for a while. Went there last night and it was great. The flavors were awesome. Tried a few of the appetizers, the curry cauliflower was crazy good. I had the garlic garlic ramen in the flavor was very good. Love his story and enjoyed the food immensely. Ramen is not the same everywhere!
Hello! Great job! That eggplant the Count and I had on Friday was wonderful!!! The Yuzu lemonade is out of this world! Keep it up!

I visited Ivan Ramen for the first time over the weekend, and it was also my first time trying ramen. I started off with the japanese fried chicken which was delicious ! Packed with flavor & it also came with an awesome dipping sauce which completely switched up the original flavor lf the chicken (in a good way). For ramen I ordered the chicken paitan and added in bok choy + mushrooms. The broth was very good, had great flavor and the dish was light but filling. I wasnt too crazy about the ground chicken in it, i'd probly order it without that next time. Other than that the ingredients balanced eachother out very well.


Service was fast & friendly; the hostesses were welcoming and my server was very helpful explaining the menu and helping me make a choice on what to order. I most certainly will be returning !

Wow what a great find. We didn't know we needed to book on a Monday night but the wait wasn't too bad. Great ramen and we loved all the appetizers too. It's a small narrow restaurant- like many in NYC - but it's funky and cool. The service is really fast too so the tables can be turned over but we didn't feel like they were pushing us out the door. Just wish they had a larger drink selection.

As far as ramen places go this is definitely my top 3! The wait was around an hour, but we grabbed drinks at a bar nearby to kill the time. We started off with the crispy eggplant and Japanese fried chicken. The crispy eggplant come with a tahini sauce that was absolutely delicious. We had to ask for another side of it because it was made to perfection. For the main, I ended up going with the spicy red chilli and I replaced the pork with the minced garlic chicken. It was the perfect combination of ramen ingredients on a cold day. I love how amenable they were to vegetarians but also replacing different items in the dish. Most ramen places are unwilling to ever accomodate. Will be visiting again in the future.

After watching the video about the furikake Gohan and the gf raving about this place, this was the first stop after we got off the flight, didn't even check in at the hotel. I decided with the tsukemen since that's my favorite style of ramen and I couldn't pass up a seasonal dish where the ingredients are at its peak. Chicken Paitan was the recommended and most popular and it was really good but I personally not a fan of ground chicken. The gf wouldn't stop saying how good it was every bite though. The beef broth for the short rib tsukemen was immensely flavorful with beef flavor and well seasoned. Noodles were perfect, not soggy at all and at the thickness I prefer. It's definitely comparable to the ramen shops in Japan and will definitely be back everytime I visit NY!!

Came here to celebrate a friend's birthday with a group of 6. We made a reservation about a week prior as they were a very small restaurant. We were seated in the back section were there was room for that big of a party size.

We ordered a variety of appetizers to share. The Crispy Eggplants were pretty tasty. The Pork Croquettes looked exactly like Takoyaki which had me fooled once I bit into it. The best one was the Japanese Fried Chicken. I had more than my fair share of the chicken.

For the ramen, I got the Chicken Paitan which the staff stated that that was their best seller. This contained rich chicken broth, minced chicken, egg yolk, and shio kombu. I asked it to be spicy in which they gave me a mini squirt bottle filled with spicy sauce, which I ended up emptying the entire bottle. The noodles I finished pretty quickly which left me thinking this isn't a lot for a meal. That's when they hit me with the kae-dama and I now realize their tactics to get a few extra bucks off of you.

They also have a very big, exotic, and unique beer selections. It will cost you a pretty penny though. I got their Pirate Bomb! and it was as dark as my soul.

In conclusion, they have some pretty good appetizers, pretty damn cool beer you probably won't find anywhere else, and pretty decent ramen. The pricing is on the premium side and for what it's worth, I don't think it's worth what they're asking for, most likely from the publicity they got from the media (just going off other Yelp reviews). I wouldn't go out of my way to come here, but would not mind stopping by again when the opportunity presents itself.

I had pretty high expectations for this place after hearing from friends and reading reviews, but the group I ate with was all somewhat disappointed with the quality of our meal. The broth was only meh and I honestly prefer some types of ramen I make myself at home over this meal.

A friend suggested coming here, so I came down to meet a friend for Saturday night dinner. We got there at 7pm and it was an hour long wait. The waitress came to take our order pretty quickly and answered our questions about the differences between the noodle options. She said the chicken paitan was one of the most popular choices and has a rich broth, so I went with that option. The noodles were thinner than I thought they would be (like a miswa texture) but chewy. The chicken was shredded and there wasn't a lot, but there was a good amount of broth. My friend ordered the spicy ramen, which the waitress cautioned was spicy, but it wasn't actually spicy according to my friend. They do take credit cards and there's no WiFi. The wall decor was splattered with art and it looked pretty cool. Overall it's a decent ramen place, but there are other good options in NYC.

My absolute favorite NYC ramen place.
A couple things to know before you go:
1: The ramen isn't traditional style. The two Tokyo ramen dishes are very subtly flavored, if your looking for heavier flavor profiles try the Triple Garlic Triple pork Mazeman, or the Red Chili Ramen (which has charsui pork in it, contrary to other reviews).
2: Reservations are a must, unless you're solo. With the exposure, it's busy all of the time. If your walking in without reservations post-lunch / pre-dinner is the best bet for getting seated without a wait.
3: The appetizers change often. Consistent winners are the Japanese Fried Chicken and the XO Daikon salad. Others come and go, so if you're feeling adventurous don't wait to order a particular dish. I made that mistake on one of the delicious Japanese Sando dishes ;)
4: The noodle portions are a perfect size, unless you've a gluttonous appetite. Just eyeballing it I think its around 4 oz of noodles. If you've broth left over, the staff is always quick to give you another side of noodles, at a small surcharge, since they are all made in house.
An absolute original NYC gem!

3 to 3.5 I'd say. Compatriot and I stopped in for a spell on a rainy day hoping to get something to ease the cold and fill our bellies. I had heard from a friend that I needed to stop in here. I'll have to stop by again though since he had mentioned to get the chicken paitan, and well... I forgot so next time here I have to try that out. The service was pretty attentive for how busy it was at the bar, and the selection of beer is certainly worth checking out.

I had gotten the vegan shoyu with an extra egg, and we had gotten the curry cauliflower and spicy kyuri pickles to share. Vegetarian ramen is always kind of funny money to me but I eat vegetarian a lot due to dietary restrictions. That and I was drinking a lot during the trip and had to offset it a bit. It was decent but I wanted the broth to be hotter for sure. The size of it was quite tiny for the price honestly. Noodles had a decent bite, but not very springy. The curry cauliflower felt the same as the ramen, a little underwhelming with the spices to me. The pickles were delish tho, I'll definitely have to get those again the next time through.

I'll have to give it another shot next time I'm in the area. Certainly for some dishes, and definitely for the beer.

Came here for a second dinner after a work outing. I had only 2 nights in NY and I had to try Ivan's after watching his episode on Netflix. 

Great food and extremely friendly staff. 10/10 would come back here when in New York.

May favorite ramen bar in the city. Appetizer and ramen both have great flavors and quite different from usual ramen places in the city. Chicken Paitan is highly recommended. They don't take reservations over the weekend but we generally get a table within 30 mins or so even when they tell you a longer wait time.

Walked into Ivan wo reservations around 2pm surprised that the place was packed. Seated right away. Tight spaces and tables packed closely. Went with the waitstaff's recommendation on the menu the triple garlic and triple pork. Came out to be noodles/ramen without broth and 1 slice of belly.
Seasoned well and quite salty at that. Service was attentive. $17 for a bowl of ramen. Pricey at that.

Can't say that I was impressed. The broth, after so much hype, was about average, if not a bit saltier than I've had at other places. I realize it's all a matter of preference, but NYC has better (and less expensive) ramen spots (Ramen Misoya on 2nd ave being one of them). $17 for a bowl of broth and noodles is excessive.

Made a reservation a week in advance and glad we did. It was freezing rain and almost fell down on the sidewalk. Everyone in the area was wanting to get some Ramen.

Server was so on the ball and knew all details about every item. It was fun, ordered pork buns, potato caviar (interesting name), fried chicken, the house special chicken Paitan ramen, and the tonkotsu beef Tsukemen.

Everything was prepared and cooked beautifully. It was a high energy place was excellent tasting food.

Had to take most of it to-go and made a nice late afternoon snack.

It's really good. Make a reservation and eat in house. Friendly staff who don't seem stressed with the packed tiny area and tiny table. Table for 2 is the sweet spot, or 1 and simple chow down. I went classic flavor selections and it was a light, less fatty broth then what I had in Japan. I loved it.

We got there right when it opened. Was seated right away. 
While there, Our water glasses were never empty. Was checked on several times. They even asked if we have any food allergies or shellfish allergies. Loved the artwork on the walls.
Some of the best ramen in NYC, perfect contrast between salty and sweet, pork buns are amazing as well.

Food was great, not a question.
My wife and I come here every few months for some good food and to try some beers, my wife ordered a beer off the menu she thought she might like. When the waitress brought over the bottle she asked if we still wanted it because it was bigger than a normal pint. We said yes not thinking about it, when the bill came the bottle was $70!

When I asked her why she didn't mention it was $70 when she asked us if we were ok with it being a pint and a half she said she doesn't want to risk offending anyone. 

This beer is around $25-30 a bottle online, unbelievable rip off. Very disappointed they would not only mark this up at a crazy rate, but not make the prices clear on the menu, of course it was a mistake to order this, but maybe separate out your overpriced beers from the reasonably priced craft beers? Unreal

The beer menu conveniently lacks any dollar signs

A chilly evening in NYC is a perfect excuse to have a hot bowl of ramen and that is what led us to this restaurant yesterday. We started with the crispy eggplant and Japanese fried chicken for appetizers. Both were delicious and I would gladly go back just to eat those again. We also had their fall seasonal sake (don't remember the name) which had the perfect fall flavours but was not too sweet. Finally it was time for the main event, the RAMEN!! And it did not disappoint. I had the chicken paitan which was rich and flavourful but not too spicy. The waitress gave us a bottle of chilly paste and I ended up using it generously. The noodles were also on point. My husband had the vegetarian ramen which he enjoyed immensely. All in all, it was an extremely satisfying ramen evening for us and given the chance, I would definitely eat here again.

Meh - was not impressed and not worth the hype.  SKIP THIS JOINT!!!  Luckily we had resos - the walk in wait time for a Friday lunch was 1.5hrs, would have been seriously upset if I waited that long for this place.  Had the vegan shoyu and Tokyo shoyu - both were underwhelming at best.  

Service was great and the staff working was very nice.  A lot of other/better ramen spots out there.  When you walk by and see the line up to get in - KEEP WALKING.
I got the chicken paitan and it was delicious!  This, super flavorful broth and his noodles are excellent. This is my favorite ramen place in NYC.

I'm sitting at the bar and have been watching them working in the open kitchen. They pay attention to every detail of their food. I see someone cleaning up the split on the bowl before it's served to customers. They want their food not only taste perfect but also look perfect. 
Zack who works inside the bar recommends Tokyo Shio to me since I mentioned I want something light. This is actually my second time here. I forgot what I ordered last time but it was great. I didn't expect this Tokyo Shio to be so good as well. Oh you can add Bok Choy, mushroom, tomatoes if you want more veggies.
I will definitely come back even though there is a long wait sometimes. But it's worthy.

Love this place!!!!  Our third time here.   Chicken paitan rules.  Super rich broth, great noodles.   The other dishes are great too.   We got triple garlic pork and the tokyo shoyu.  The last one is the most "typical" but still yum.  The appetizers were great.   The crispy eggplant was abig hit and i really liked the salad with its slightly sweet dressing.   The fried chicken is good,  but not the rock star as the others. The fried potatoes were good,  with some roe and sauce.   We will be back!!!
Ramen was deLISH. It was packed on New Years Day at 9pm. The pork belly buns were also amazing and one of the best ones I've tried.

This is one of my favorite ramen spots in the city. I love how different the ramen is from other traditional locations and there is always something new and exciting to try. My favorite is the Toykyo Shoyu. Definitely check out this spot if you want to try something new!

Food is expensive and very salty. If you have any issue with your kidney you should walk pass this place at speed.  We asked for a hot green tea, yep they did get us a green tea in a "Can" which you could get one in any Chinese food market for a fraction of price. For the price we expected a genuine green tea or at least brew from a green tea bag.  uhhh ! 

The place decor is not bad. 

If you are looking for modern Fusion food then yes this place may be a place for you.
This review is only for their chicken broth ramen.  Really flavorful.  We also got a pork-based broth, which was OK but not as good as the chicken.  Good beer.

Overall: super delicious share plates, mediocre ramen (only tried one)

The fried chicken and cauliflower appetizers were INCREDIBLE. Chicken is so tender and flavorful and the shiso leaf works so well. The dipping sauce that comes with the chicken is addicting. Cauliflower also comes in an amazing light curry sauce. Both dishes are BIG portions. Good to share.

Ramen: the spicy red chili ramen .... broth was WAY OVERLY SALTY. I am a huge broth person and usually love having the broth at the end and I couldn't have this one. It's super decadent and salty and heavy feeling. On the other hand the ramen noodles were cooked very deliciously and the egg as well. But the broth is 1/2 of it and I wasn't loving it. Maybe need to try the shoyu one instead?

It was 2 of us and we had the chicken cauliflower and shared a ramen and we were so full !!!


3.5/5
I went in here because it was a cold day in the cIty and  was craving some ramen. Honestly the ramen was okay nothing wow about it.

Great appetizers and the ramen was great. They have a awesome beer selection, I definitely recommend the pineapple whip beer. The service was quick even though it was packed and the server had great recommendations. The beer was a little expensive but I will totally be back.
Not so so special ramen at a special ramen price. Not going back.i might as well have instant noodles at home

I learned about Ivan Ramen from a beer discussion, saved it to Maps and then forgot about it for awhile. One night we stumbled upon it, remembered we had been meaning to try it, and stopped in.

Try to get a reservation if you can, because our first time there we did not have one and it was a pretty long wait, even towards the end of the night. Learned our lesson and the next time reserved a table. 

The food we've had here has been great. I recommend the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen, and my new favorite, the Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen. As for the beer list, they get some pretty great stuff, with a lot of local options. Only 5 or so beers on tap, but they have a nice can and bottle list. My only complaint is that I think the beer is expensive, even by NYC standards. But that's OK, because ironically I now come here for the food and not the beer.

This is hands down my favorite ramen place in NYC! The atmosphere is really interesting and they have a really friendly and attentive staff. The ramen is amazing! It's really hard for me to find good vegetarian ramen with good flavor, but this place always delivers. I highly recommend everyone to come try this place and you will not be disappointed.
Worth the price paid, came all over from Dominican Republic to try it after seeing it on Netflix - Chef's Table. Nice crew, food great, good music, free wifi  and best of all, smiles everywhere.

Arrived at 8:30 pm for a 8:45 pm reservation and was promptly seated, which is great. However, the whole meal felt rushed with plates being removed as soon as the last bite was taken and the check being placed on the table without being asked. 
Food wise, Ivan Ramen is just ok. The vegan ramen was pretty lack luster in appearance but the tofu was definitely the most interesting thing in that bowl. The shoyu ramen had too much of a chicken stock flavor (not surprising given that it was made with chicken stock) and lacked the shoyu flavor I was looking for. The fried shrimp buns were good but the proportion between filling and bun felt off and the japanese fried chicken was interesting but the breading was too thick.
For the price and passive aggressive service I would not be back BUT the food isn't bad and the atmosphere is very trendy.

Basic Americanized ramen. I actually flew to NYC with the primary intention of visiting this place. I was truly hoping that since this dude got his start in Japan that the ramen would actually reflect that. It did not. The broth lacked umami and just wasn't anything to write home about. They didn't even have  condiments to add to the ramen. The curry cauliflower, pork belly buns, and pickles weeds fantastic however. The prices were a little high for what you get, especially $50 for a carafe of sake. I would probably go back for a different dish but I i was sad the ramen didn't deliver.

I had this place bookmarked in my maps for the longest time and I'm so glad I stopped in. Definitely worth the wait!
Japanese fried chicken and the ramen were  amazing and super flavorful. I can't wait to go back next time I'm in the city.

I showed up at lunchtime without a reservation and there was already a line of people outside so try to get there early or reserve a spot. The staff was friendly and efficient. The bowl of ramen is unlike any other bowl I've had. I had the chicken ramen and it was RICH and all kinds of umami yumminness. I loved the salad and the appetizers were all pretty simple yet tasty.  Tip* Read the descriptions of what you are ordering carefully because they are not all Ramen dishes. My husband almost made that mistake.

I've been here a few times and it never fails to disappoint. I personally think it's a very authentic menu, albeit a bit small. The ramen is amazing, definitely a must have. The Paitan is probably my favourite as it's the most flavourful broth.
The shrimp heads are really interesting, definitely not for everyone and prepare to eat the shell and some little legs. But if you're looking for something unique then they're a must. 
Curry flower, pork buns, and mazemen are definitely our other faves.

Highly recommend! Some of the best ramen in the city. Especially the chicken paitan. Not many places offer a good chicken ramen and this place does it right. The bowl offers a savory broth with minced chicken, scallions, shio kombu and egg yolk to mix in. I personally recommended added a marinated egg as well, very delicious! 

In addition to ramen, we ordered the spicy kyuri pickles and the curry flower which were delicious. Great selection of beers as well, although some were pricey. 

Tucked away in a small but trendy area of lower east side, this is a must visit if you love ramen! The restaurant has limited seating (roughly 10 tables and 10 bar seats) so I recommend making a reservation in advance through either OpenTable or by calling - they are often able to squeeze you in if you call.  As a bonus, check out the Chefs Table episode on it before you go!

I didn't like ramen, until I came to Ivan Ramen. The Japanese Fried Chicken was an amazing appetizer to the Chicken Paitan. I loved how rich the broth tasted, while still tasting fresh. Be sure to add the roasted tomatoes as a garnish!
Food was good but not excellent. I enjoyed the atmosphere and tables in the patio are really nice.

The service and noodles were super nice but the broth itself was not good. 

The portions are small and the flavor is lacking. Ingredients are incredibly basic, the egg is not marinated and adds no flavor to the ramen. Usually I look forward to the egg - but this was just an uncooked wet mess. The way they add spice to the ramen is simply by giving you a tube of chipotle mayo.. maybe it used to be good before the hype. Plenty of random places in NYC you could try with much better flavor. 

The mazemen was also very weak in flavor. Everything was brown and bland.

I have been wanting to try Ivan Ramen for quite a while but didn't have a chance to since I always come for work and it's quite far from East village. 

Nevertheless, I went at 2pm so no crowd at all. I believe I was in and out within 15mins. 

I only ordered the Tokyo Shio Ramen only because I have never had tomatoes in my ramen. 

Overall, it's definitely a very interesting take on Ramen and I have had funky ramen but what made me shake my head while eating was the noodles. It felt uncooked and  were stuck together most of the time. 

The saving graces were the pork belly and the rich chicken broth. I'm not one who waste a single drop. So I slurped up every drop.
Lived up to the hype!!! The minced chicken Ramen was amazing! Really cool atmosphere and great Ramen. Make sure to make a reservation before hand

Came last week on a Sunday and got the Tokyo Shio Ramen, Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen, and the Japanese Fried Chicken. I want to start by saying that the Japanese Fried Chicken not only tasted nothing like karaage but it came out lukewarm, which makes me think that it was sitting out for a while. The sauce they use to coat the chicken is very, very salty (and I love salty foods) and reminded me of a wannabe, albeit very inferior, Korean fried chicken. 
Next comes the ramen, and I don't even know where to start. The noodles for both the dishes were great! However, the shio broth tasted kind of dirty. I'm not exactly sure how to describe it but there was a very strong, unclean taste about it that didn't taste anything like bone/meat broth. I would highly recommend staying away from that one in particular. Next comes the Mazemen, which was quite tasty but it tasted overwhelmingly of bacon. There was no garlic flavor whatsoever. 
I think the biggest disappointment is the fact that both dishes barely had any food in it and were very salty in a bad way. The portions are tiny! I would say if you don't eat that much, it'll be good enough, but if you have a big appetite don't even bother! Also, I don't know if it's because of the time we came, but all of the tables got a complimentary appetizer but us.
Overall, I would say the Ramen here is more suited for an American-palate and is very very mediocre. The service isn't bad, but I would rather spend my money to get a more satisfactory meal elsewhere.

I've heard so much about Ivan Ramen that I was really excited to try it out when I was in New York. It was pretty good, but at the same time, it was about as good as the ramen places back home in Austin and I was just hoping that it might blow me away? Maybe an unfair request, but it was decent ramen and the environment was quiet and calm.

Don't understand the reviews under 4-5 stars on here. The place was amazing. The service was friendly and efficient, the ramen was delicious and the music they had in the background was on point. Started off with the Tongue-katsu sando, never thought I'd enjoy eating beef tongue. We ordered the Tokyo Shio and the chicken paitan ramen. My bf couldn't stop talking about the chicken Paitan after leaving. The broth was very flavorful. This place set the bar for ramen pretty high. I'd move to this neighborhood just so I could become a regular at this place. 

Also, this chef (Ivan) was featured on an ep of Chef's Table; it was pretty cool learning his background before coming. He makes his noodles from scratch and puts his own spin on it which is why they aren't stereotypical ramen noodles.

The fact that this isn't a 5 star Yelp restaurant is mind boggling. Music is great, Noodles are fantastic and the Broth? MYYYY GODDD it's delicious. I ordered the Chicken Paitan by the way, and every part of the dish works together in a great way for most flavorful ramen I've ever had. Service was efficient, and knowledgeable of the dishes. 
Within 30min you could easily crush 2 asahi beers and a bowl of ramen. 

Cannot recommend this place enough.

Holy shit this was actually the WORST ramen i've tasted in my life. The Shoyu broth is bitter and disgusting unlike any other ramen i've had. Very small portions, only came with ONE piece of pork for $17. DO NOT GO HERE, if you want ramen go to TATSU RAMEN instead. Very very disappointed will never come here again

Ordered takeout, when we got home we realized they forgot half the order. Delivery of the last two ramen bowls took 45 minutes and was cold -- our dinner experience was terrible since we didn't get to eat together and it was all cold. When I called to check in on the delivery time the manager was unnecessarily rude and made me feel bad for checking in on food that we had paid for.
I found this restaurant by chance and I am very happy about my choice. They serve very tasty ramen and have a good selection of beers.

Wanted to try this ramen shop since I saw it on Chef's Table.  It was really good but I'm from Toronto and there are a few ramen restaurants that are a lot better there.  The service was friendly and quick and had a great fun vibe.  The spicy ramen was about an 8 on the heat meter and totally addictive but be prepared to sweat a little.  Overall, I enjoyed it and would consider going back.

*REVIEW FOR VEGANS AND VEGETARIANS* 
This was my first time to this restaurant and could have been great, the staff was very welcoming and helpful but something very inconvenient happened. 
I'm VEGETARIAN for 16 year now and NEVER ATE PORK and some other meats in my life (until tonight), long story short: I ordered a "vegetarian" dish and came full of bacon (there was no option with bacon or add on).  it took me a while to realize it was meat because I never had it before. I asked the waitress if there was any meat or if it could have happened a mistake that they added it and she kept saying no, so I had 4 people on my table to try it and all of them was convinced that was bacon and then I had to take my napkin with the pieces of it and show her so they could tell me what I was eating. Finally they brought my plate to the kitchen, and CONFIRMED WAS BACON! Was very frustrating and spent a few minutes vomiting in their bathroom because I refused to let my stomach digest a dead animal. 
They wanted to make something to repair their mistake but honestly I don't trust this place anymore. Also a guy from the other table said that it happened the same to him so it was clear that they messed up in the kitchen and all the vegetarians that night ate bacon Lol
Wooooooooow. The Chicken Paitan was one of the best soups I've ever eaten. The broth was *chefs kiss* perfection.

This is my second time here. This time, I ordered the Duck Tsukemen. Omg!,the broth tasted so good. It came with grilled oyster mushrooms, napa cabbage, soft eggs and duck. I'm definitely coming back again with my family. Thanks to the team at ivan ramen.

Ramen is delicious--we had one wet one dry LMAO ima look up them names in a bit. 

Even though they are super savory & wonderful, toward the end, the dishes were suuuuuper salty at the end. Not 100% my cup of tea, but still great :) 

Edit: the super garlicky pork thing lacked.....garlic lmao no garlic taste bros! Would amp it up a bit

I think my issue here may be that this place was overhyped. I came here with a friend of mine on a trip to NYC and ended up leaving a little disappointed. The signature shio ramen just didn't live up to the hype for me. Maybe I'm missing the point of shio ramen, but I wanted something rich and flavorful and unforgettable. However, what I got was pretty darn good chicken noodle soup. To be clear, this was still a good dish, but definitely not what I expected coming in. My friend ordered the mazeman and it was really something. The broth was thick and concentrated and completely coated our mouth with savory goodness, if I end up coming back, I would definitely opt for that.

Called in for pick up and the guy on the phone was extremely helpful. He was explaining to me what to expect from the Ramen that I ordered and he gave me some recommendations and suggestions. They gave me some very generous servings! 
I didn't expect to enjoy the pickled daikon xo, but it sure is a good appetizer to start with. The steamed pork buns were sumptuous, and juicy! Thinking about it is making my mouth water again lol Lastly, the Chicken Paitan Ramen, wasn't the best that I had, but a very decent Ramen, as far as Ramens go. What I like about it is the generous serving that they gave me. Overall, I'd say I'd order from them again.

Our waiter was extremely friendly and conversational. She even offered to help charge my dying cellphone in at the counter while we ate our food. I'm giving it three stars due to the quality of the ramen. It wasn't as flavorful or tasty compared to the hundreds of ramen shops all around New York.
I love their spicy ramen. It is flavorful and rich. I always get it. I am a ramen noodle fanatic but enjoyed their noodles which looks different but their texture is good.

Best Ramen I've ever had. Every time I go there I notice how nice and friendly the staff is, and the food is really amazing. My favorite place to go by myself for a bowl of Ramen, and I love bringing friends there, too.
Great spicy ramen with fantastic duck buns as appetizer and great beer selection. Book ahead or be prepared for a long wait. Tables are a bit tight together but not terrible.

Of course this would be my first sit down stop in the city post quarantine. I'm truly obsessed with this place, like I'm going to turn into a ramen noodle with the amount that I eat it; that, and gain 50 lbs. Ok onto the stuff you actually wanna hear... their patio is open for outside dining! It's super clean and a small space so you will only be eating with max 2 other groups at a time, which is good if you're worried about being around a lot of people, but probably not so good for their business :/ utensils are prepacked beforehand so there's no contact as they're wrapped up. Service was excellent as always. I feel like I'm coming home when I walk into this place! Ramen was amazing, spicy red chili never disappoints me. We also got the eggplant appetizer which was delicious. The only downside is it's sorta intense eating ramen in the heat, BUT so worth it! Or order takeout! Please support Ivan ramen during this crazy time!

First time in since COVID , loved it. Food as always was great , service excellent but the setup was impressive. A 1:00 Sat & I had my own corner of the rear patio with privacy divider and a big table of six for myself. They couldn't have been any nicer as well ! All good 
Pork buns never miss & spicy red chili had some kick !

So good! I recently went here and enjoyed their outdoor dining in the front of the restaurant when I was walking down Clinton with a friend and noticed they had availability! The texture of the cold sesame noodles was awesome pickled daikon salad was refreshing and the sauce was *chef's kiss*... Ramen wise i went with the spicy red chili option and it was just right... Can't wait to come back and try more items now that I can get a seat. Haha. Our waitress was over the top nice and super helpful with her suggestions I love that I could feel her smile through her mask and hoop earrings. I would definitely recommend this spot to treat yourself during these crazy times.
BEST RAMEN IN NYC! Period. Service is always on point and their spicy ramen is to die for!! No where else will have my business for Ramen! Must check it out! :)

Great outdoor seating available for quarantine eats. 

I tried the curry cauliflower, vegetarian ramen, and cold sesame noodles and loved the unique flavors of each. Tied for the best dish is the curry cauliflower and cold sesame noodles. The noodles usually come with chicken but I requested it without as I'm a vegetarian and it was amazing (a little spicy too so if you're not into that, ask for it to be removed). The curry cauliflower appetizer was nothing like I've ever had before. They were so crunchy and perfectly fried like popcorn chicken. The flavors of the butter sauce was incredible. 

Lastly, our server (a tall, skinny woman) was incredibly nice and friendly, we had the best time dining here. Before I could even ask, she asked if I'd like some spice and I was so excited when she brought out a delicious spicy sauce I added to my noodles. Thank you so much for a great dining experience!

Great spot! Came here on a ramen date adventure. Trying different ramen around the city and they were the nicest! Very friendly staff and the food was good. Also, loved the child of zombie beer! Made our casual date night feel very special! Will come back if in the mood for ramen again!  Thank you!

Honestly was excited to try this place for a long time. Unfortunately, we thought the food wasn't great :(  The buns were okay, the fried chicken was soggy and the ramen we ordered were not good. We love ramen and we usually slurp it all til the last drop but we left half of ours. Wouldn't recommend and won't be going back. The only positive was the staff, they were wonderful.
Fantastic ramen shop. Every bowl is very interesting and has lots of depth. I had the spicy red chili with a chicken substitute. My personal favorite. Their outdoor seating is wonderful too.

Absolutely Disgusting! 

This spot I heard a lot of good things about but it tastes like greasy overcooked lard... Not trying to be mean or rude. We came and heard great things from friends so gave it a try. I ordered an app- crispy eggplant, and for mains: tokyo shoyu and my bf ordered a Tokyo shio. For drinks we had the "Homemade" Yuzu lemonade which did not taste homemade. It tastes a bit powdered or too granulated. At least add a straw or a stirrer because most of the "Yuzu" which is "homemade" sinks to the bottom so within 5 minutes of sitting down you just get water- no flavor. The Yuzu has no pulp / kind of sus.  Meal looks very aesthetic but does not taste good. We had other food coming but when the waitress collected our plates she put our chopsticks on the dirty outdoor table (yes you wipe the table but that's really dirty still, at least put it on the napkins we used or something not directly on an OUTDOOR table)... Lastly the ramen was just extremely greasy. I go to japan every year. It should never taste like that much grease. For 17$ a bowl I could have gone someplace  else. I did not want to tell the waitress directly how the ramen and her chopstick manners made us feel but it was a bit uncomfortable and gross? We still tipped but my boyfriend was very uncomfortable. The ramen tasted a little bit burnt- but not charred* just had a slight off flavour. Chashu texture was okay. The half boiled egg was good.

Ramen broth- 2/10
Ramen noodles- 4/10
Egg-9/10
Chashu 7/10

Eggplant appetizer- 8/10
Drink 5/10.... 


Covid Cleanliness- 0/10 

That waitress was extremely polite and nice but... kind of not hygienic at all... 

We got there around 1pm. Table already had some long brown black hairs on it. My hair is rainbow  so I knew that definitely ain't me. It was kind of gross. 


not worth it. I was expecting a bit more from this place :/

First, let me start by saying that everything we ordered was outstanding. They have a good amount of out-door dining -- we ate on the back patio, which is pretty sheltered such that you could mistake the tables as still being inside. 

Back to the food: we enjoyed some of the best ramen we've ever had. The chicken paitan was out of this world; the spicy red chili ramen was bursting with flavor. The fried cauliflower and Japanese Fried Chicken apps were also top notch. We finished of the night with a delicious graham cracker ice cream sundae, which is made in partnership with Morganstern's.

I have seen Ivan's story on Chef's Table so did have some high expectations.  I have had a lot of ramen off over the place, including in this city.  It's one of my favorite things to try in a city that I visit when I can find it.

I sat at the bar, as I was eating on my own.  Unlike some reviews that I read, I have good personalized service and wasn't rushed.  Chatted with the bartender/server and some other patrons.  The place is super busy and has a cool and fun atmosphere.  

The real issue I had was that the ramen did not live up to my expectations.  I have had better in NYC and worse in NYC and elsewhere.  Much too salty, as I have seen in other reviews.  The broth was not as flavorful as I was expecting, which might be diminished by the salt.  The options were interesting, but did not wow me in any way.  I would go back, but only if others I was with wanted to go.  I have another preferred place in this city and others to still try.

I had a bad experience ordering takeout. This was my first time visiting Ivan Ramen and I've heard so many great things about this place but I was not impressed whatsoever. I rarely ever leave reviews but I was ticked off this time. I have stomach problems and I asked one of the lady's how spicy the spicy red chili is. She said it was mild. I told her please let me know if it's really spicy because this is my first time here and if it's too spicy I'll order something else so I order it and it's a literal hell fire. Like why lie about it? 2 bites in and I threw it out, my stomach is on fire. I also tried the chicken sandwich don't bother it tastes literally like nothing. I'm gonna go back and try the regular ramen and give it one more chance but jeez service was awful.

The best spicy ramen in the city. Very sad I haven't been able to find something that compares since I moved to Brooklyn. I guess i'll have to go into the LES a couple of times a month to enjoy Ivan Ramen's ramen! I repeat -- THE. BEST. SPICY. RAMEN. Have been coming here for two years and nothing compares.

Great spot for outdoor dining and inter covid. Went with my coworkers for a weekend lunch. Food looked amazing on paper and it didn't disappoint.

We ordered the pork buns and crispy eggplant. Both were amazing and had fantastic flavor. I think the tahini sauce with the eggplant has some chicken broth in it.

The spicy ramen wasn't too spicy. It doesn't burn the tip of your tongue and burns just the back of your mouth. 

Definitely recommend the black sesame. It packs tons of flavor, not too sweet and was very smooth.
