Service was great & the ramen was very yummy! We got 2 different bowls to try & the spicy one was my favorite of the two- if you can handle spice I definately recommend!!
Not many vegetarian options. The only vegetarian ramen they had was ok, but it was a taste I could only have so much of.

The fact that this place has less than a 4.5 star rating is absolutely absurd. Out of all of the ramen places that I have been to in NYC nothing compares to Ivan Ramen. Even though it may not be as authentic as Ichiran, I believe the ramen is better. The chopped pork (instead of 6 inch strips of dried pork you would normally find in a ramen bowl), the scrambled egg (instead of the dense brown hard boiled egg typically in a ramen bowl) provide an interesting twist that I believe make the dish easier and better to eat.

If you want tasty, authentic ramen, please don't come here.

I stumbled on this ramen place while in the neighborhood. Ordered delivery/pickup for Vegetarian Ramen since it seemed interesting.

Broth was overly salty and was diluted with soy sauce. Received four cold pieces of tofu, a small tomato, some enoki mushrooms, and a few pieces of spinach.

To be honest, it just didn't taste good. Portion size was also incredibly small.

For $16, I'd look elsewhere. It'd be hard to even consider this meal for $5.

This restaurant's speciality might be ramen, but I'd say, nah man, it's just not good. Americanized. Overly salty. Small portion size.

Look elsewhere. It's NYC.

We made a reservation and the outdoor seating in the back of the restaurant was really nice and well spaced out. I got the vegan ramen and eggplant appetizer, which was absolute heaven and probably my favorite of the night- really recommend. Overall had a great time!

Been here multiple times with friends and family. Their ramen is really good and always consistent. I always order the chicken paitan with is minced chicken in a bowl of ramen. The touch of dried tomatoes is simply amazing! Love this place!

Chanced upon this place while exploring the neighborhood and decided to give it a try because it seemed popular. Ordered the Tokyo Shio Ramen for takeout and was surprised by the small portion - food only filled up 1/3 of the takeout container as pictured and a pitifully tiny slice of pork was given. Food came cold, broth was flavorless and overly salty. Genuinely offended by how blatantly the restaurant butchered a food as heavenly as ramen. Overall disappointing experience and definitely not worth the price.
Very good ramen, need to visit at least 1 time if your a ramen lover. There triple garlic pork was amazing. Very low key but cozy.

Considering the fact that I love pho I figured I'd give ramen a try. Myself and a few friends went here over Halloween weekend and we were originally sat outside on their little patio but then asked to move inside when we saw a table leaving. They were accommodating and had no problem with us moving. We decided to start with the fried chicken, cauliflower, eggplant and Bao buns for appetizers. Personally the chicken and bao buns were my favorite but everything else was very good. I had ordered the chicken ramen and it was better then I expected. I feel like it does require a certain taste in order for you to enjoy it but I would definitely recommend getting the chicken option if you've never had ramen before. Over all I would return but I definitely think I would try other places as well.
The ramen is good but the broth can be stronger. Size is alittle small for the price.
Rye noodles are everything. A great example of a chef putting his everything into a concept and it being executed perfectly. If you haven't had Ivan Ramen, you need to order ASAP!

What a meal. The food was next level for ramen lovers and I made an account just to review it. When you go, ask for Will. He gave us great recommendations and had us covered the whole way through. Overall great experience. Shoutout Will.

This winter storm had me craving soup delivery so I happened upon this classic joint. (Soup during a snow storm, I know, HOW ORIGINAL haha.)

I went with the spicy red ramen and it did not disappoint. This bowl was the perfect amount of creamy and spicy. I definitely found myself having a few breaks to fan my mouth down! It was so good.

I also got the steamed pork buns, these weren't my favorite and I'm not quite sure why. I think I would have preferred the plum sauce to be more evenly applied to the pork. I also found the pork extremely fatty (pretty sure this was pork belly, so it was possibly supposed to be super fatty). 

Regardless, I was super happy with the spicy ramen, the takeout packaging and directions to heat up were great and the delivery was seamless. I will definitely order from here again.

4.4/5

I use to live in Japan for a number of years. I would always have my ramen there for lunch and on the weekend. That was wonderful no matter where you went in the neighborhood. When I came back to the US I would look for my ramen here in New York, Chicago, LA, Boston and even in Tampa. It was good. So when compared to Ivan Ramen -- I have had better. This stuff is fine. It is fresch. Tasty. A bit too salty. And a long line outside with a concept inside. Also it is expensive for a bowl. To think it is $16 here, and if I bout this in Tokyo it was about $3 for the same size bowl. Even in Beijing (where it comes from originally) had large bowls for about $5 at most. Ivan Ramen is not a bad bowl of a favorite meal. But nothing unique.
Spicy red chili ramen...best in New York, hands down! Really bold spice with elegantly thin noodles topped w the perfect egg, ground chicken (substitute) and crunchy greens. LOVE IT

Got takeout ramen and crispy eggplant with tahini sauce and it was so good!! The food was still hot when it was delivered which is always a plus. The spicy ramen was amazing! Sometimes places do spicy and it's not that spicy, but my mouth was on fire with this one (in a good way!). Also the crispy eggplant was a last minute addition to our order and I'm so glad we decided to get it. The tahini sauce and charred garlic was sooo good. I bet it would be even better if you ordered it at the restaurant and got it fresh. 10/10 recommend this place!

Spicy chili Raman and pork buns are delicious! Nice beer selection. Outdoor seating in both the front and back of restaurant. We were seated as walk ins in the front area but if you want the back patio, make a reservation:)

Rainy cold winter night, let's go get ramen!! we had seen Ivan featured on chefs table and was super excited. We were able to snag one of the last seats out front, woo hoo here we go. We ordered the curry cauliflower. I got the Tokyo shio and hubby got triple pork triple garlic. The curry flower was interesting and good. My Tokyo shio was pretty disappointing, the broth was so light and tasteless, it truly didn't feel like ramen. I've had chicken noodle soup from Whole Foods with more flavor!!! The triple pork was much better and flavorful. I also wasn't a big fan of the super thin ramen noodles. Overall pretty disappointing. Maybe I should've gone with the recommendation and gotten chicken taipan? I'm still in shock that they would serve such a tasteless bowl of ramen here. The people working here also rubbed me the wrong way, none were friendly or welcoming. They were impatient and going through the motions robotically. It was like they were doing us a favor by letting us spend $70 on some ramen here lol. Don't waste your time, plenty of other delicious ramen places around.

The environment and workers were nice but the ramen was not that great. Ordered the spicy ramen and it was way too spicy that I couldn't even eat it.. I was surprised that they don't serve hot matcha tea for free.. So we got those hot canned green tea. Won't be going anymore.

This place is the best! The food is so delicious and I love coming here. We went yesterday and I got the spicy chili ramen and it was so good. We also got the pork dumplings, but my favorite thing on their menu is their Korean bbq chicken with the sauce!

When a restaurant gets a lot of hype I am immediately skeptical, but to me Ivan Ramen lived up to my expectations. The rye noodles added such an interesting toasty flavor to the dishes and really stand out. The pork is almost pastrami-like, and very demonstrative of Ivan's New Yorkness. The soy (shoyu) broth is one of the most flavorful I've had. Also, the karaage (fried chicken) was delicious. I loved Ivan's less traditional take on ramen and I'll surely go back to try more of the menu. 

Added bonus was the back patio was the warmest outdoor dining I have experienced! Heaters all around and lots of distance from other tables. The hot sake was a great pairing for outdoors, plus we got to keep the cute panda glasses!

WOW! The hype is real. I can honestly say I have never tasty such a flavorful and well balanced broth. Before ordered I was worried it would be overwhelming...nope! It was perfect. The level of culinary skill here is noticed and appreciated. Thank you Ivan Ramen!

It was all because my Japanese coworkers wouldn't shut up about this place. Wondered what the hype is about and stopped wondering. Got the triple dish and a bite of shio ramen both so smoky just like walking in a forest in front of a fire. Reminds of Afuri ramen in Tokyo.

I like this place, I really do. I don't agree with the very mixed overall ratings from other reviews, though I think I get why the reviews are very much "some people REALLY like it" vs. "others can't understand the hype". ~ I think this place suffers from its notoriety and people's expectations of ramen going in. 

As for the ramen offerings that I've ordered, I've had the TONKOTSU, SHIO, and SPICY RED CHILI. First of all, the spicy red chili bowl does indeed produce quite a kick and so order this if you truly can handle the heat. (Yet, to its credit, it truly is a delicious bowl of ramen; the heat doesn't take away from the overall taste). As mentioned earlier, I think the division over Ivan's reviews is due to not only its notoriety from its Chef's Table fame but also people's expectations of what high-level ramen should be. Ivan Ramen definitely is not what purists/traditionalists might be looking for as especially their shio and tonkotsu may not taste or look exactly the way their counterparts at many other ramen joints taste or look. However, to me it's clear that the good folks at Ivan, while adept and knowledgeable at techniques and flavors of more "traditional" ramen, kind of want to play and color outside of the edges, which I'm fine with. I'd say that as long as you know what you're getting into when you go to Ivan Ramen, you'll be fine.

Price-wise, all of the bowls, while a little more expensive than other comparable ramen joints in the area (LES/East Village), are very rich and so they fill you up quite nicely. Also, they do their soft boiled eggs so well at Ivan. Nice marinade but the runny-ness/solidness of the yolk is just perfect... not too runny, not too hard, just right.

I also love the KYURI PICKLE appetizer; when you order a rich bowl of ramen like what Ivan makes, the pickles accompany it so nicely (they're also a little spicy, which I like).

I enjoyed this place a lot! Some of the best ramen I've had since I moved here to America, the staff was friendly and my daughter thought the waiter was charming hahah! Over all, the food was very good. The pork buns were absolutely delicious and the tonkotsu ramen was just amazing! The broth was extremely rich and just slightly spicy in the best way possible, and the meat was soft and basically falling apart in your mouth. Definitely recommend.

Not sure why this place has such low reviews - I loved it! I saw Ivan's episode on Chef's Table and his story was really touching (I recommend watching the episode before you go). His ramen is not overly salty like everyone says and has a special distinctive taste that is definitely unforgettable and much different than your typical ramen taste. The pork was also really juicy and tender. 

I only tried the ramen so definitely coming back in the future to try other things. If you're put off by some of the reviews, give Ivan a chance and definitely watch his Chef's table episode. His story as a gaijin in Japan is amazing.

Not sure why this place has negative reviews. It was amazing! We got our ramen to go and it was packed perfectly (broth was packed separate from the noodles so nothing was soggy when we went to eat it). I watched Ivan's episode of Chef's Table and had to go. His story is inspiring and the ramen lives up to the hype. Thank you!

So I'll start off by saying i love this little gem. I tried to support them during the start of the pandemic and they were always so gracious and nice to me. Anytime i would pick up food the staff would thank me for placing my order, they would throw in a free app. Their noodles are bomb. I love their stuff. I feel like the ramen is good and not watery like other spots. The chicken app is soooooo darn good. I feel like their variety and choices on the menu are good. I enjoy their ramen and will definitely be back.
Tried 2 out of the 3 Ramen options on the menu and loved it!! Spicy one is a must try.

I just want to give a shout-out to the staff and management at this spot for being amazing, creative and SUPER helpful! You guys win across the board for your dedication to the food and to making it happen. 

The story: I placed an order for pickup for two Tokyo Shio Ramen dishes. My harebrained scheme was to transport the food with me on the train to Philly, as I was going to visit my best friend. She been planning to come visit me in the city today, but our plans changed last-minute when her mother had to get an emergency surgery and landed in the hospital. I decided I'd come down to Philly instead! Ivan is her favorite ramen joint in the city, and we originally had plans to get dinner at Ivan tonight, so I decided I'd bring some WITH me so that she could still have that delicious ramen after a long, emotionally draining day. The challenge: how to keep the ramen fresh after a 2 hour train ride and additional driving?  
I came equipped with only a cooler that I had just bought at Target, and a vision for delicious, heavenly noodles for my friend. When I explained the situation, it was GAME ON. Everyone from the incredibly sweet hostess to the kitchen staff to the manager pitched in to make sure the components of the dishes were all separated out according to design, and fit like puzzle pieces in the cooler. They even gave me instructions for how to reheat the broth so that it tasted as good as fresh, and how long to cook the noodles. 

5/5 stars, Ivan Ramen staff: you win the day for your enthusiasm, helpfulness and all-around amazing energy!

Amazing Ramen and appetizers!
Our server William was right on everything.  Watched the episode of Chefs Table that features Ivan and it all made sense and was delicious!

I got this ramen via delivery and didn't expect much. I normally HATE chicken ramen because it's not flavorful and the chicken is always so bland but THIS CHICKEN PAITAN IS IT. The broth is rich and salty and creamy and delicious. The chili oil was ACTUALLY spicy AND flavorful (which I feel like never happens). The eggs were perfectly cooked. And the ground chicken was SOOO good. It was cooked in spices and was SO flavorful - none of that grilled or boiled business. Clearly a thoughtful approach to non-red meat options!! And it was warm and filling and packaged great! 

Eat here if you can't eat red meat!! So worth.
Chicken Paitan was amazing  noodle texture was delicious. We sat in a cute back room area. Will be back!
Ramen is just ok. I don't know what the hype is about. Won't go back for the $20 bowl of ramen for sure.

Ivan Ramen is open with indoor and outdoor seating! This is my favorite ramen place in New York City! I love how chewy the noodles are and how savory the broth is. I always get the chicken paitan and it's always super filling. I also recommend getting the curry flower! The best cauliflower you'll ever eat.

I love ramen and eating ramen from Ivan Ramen was like falling in love again. I have tried so many bowls of ramen and this ramen simply blew me away. The restaurant is small and hip and has the coolest decor like their magazine collage wall. 

Our group ordered a bunch of appetizers like:
-Tobanjan Green Beans
-Japanese Fried Chicken 
-Steamed Pork Buns

They were all so good and the buns in the steamed pork buns was like eating a fluffy cloud. The green beans are tossed in such a delicious spicy sauce and I would recommend you order them. 

In terms of ramen, I ordered the Tonkotsu Ramen which brings a rich pork broth, shoyu-glazed chashu, woodear mushrooms, mustard greens, and a soft boiled egg and my goodness. This bowl was the definition of "umami". They were so many depths of flavor and the broth has this "smokiness" to it that I cannot describe. 

If you like ramen, you need to try ramen at Ivan Ramen.
I ordered Japanese fried chicken and tonkotsu ramen. Both were way too salty.  Should have stayed alert when the menus got completely Americanized.

Ordered:
- Karaage with shiso ranch
- Tsukemen with shrimp toast on the side
- Shoyu ramen
- Yuzu lemonade

The karaage is delicious. I love the shiso ranch.
The star of the meal is shrimp toast. When it's warm and crispy, we dip it into the sauce omg it's beyond words.
I prefer tsukemen over shoyu ramen. The ramen in other bowls is thin noodle and somehow it's thinner than normal. Shoyu ramen is good but not outstanding good.
The yuzu lemonade is so refreshing. It helps wash down the richness from the ramen.
I will definitely go back for the tsukemen.

Despite the mediocre reviews this place is actually really good. I tried the tonkotsu ramen and the seafood tsukemen.
The tonkotsu broth was very flavorful and the noodles were great. The egg was good and the chashu was okay (was tender but felt subdued by the broth). (4/5)
The seafood tsukemen dipping sauce was amazing, it was super creamy and not too salty. It came with a really nice shrimp toast that went with the sauce really well. The noodles it came with were thick and carried the sauce well. (4.3/5)
The service was pleasant, the waiter explained the dishes and suggested ways to eat them, which was a cool touch. Overall, surprisingly good.

I first heard about Ivan Ramen after watching Ivan Orkin's episode on Chef's Table. As someone who loves ramen, I knew I had to try Ivan Ramen during my time in NYC.

Visiting during the tail end of the NYC pandemic restrictions, Ivan Ramen had set up a few tables outside for outdoor seating with very vibrant colors. The menu is accessed the a QR code, but the waiters will still take your orders manually and deliver your order.

I tried the chicken paitan, which, according to my waiter, was Ivan's favorite ramen. I accompanied my dish with a yuzu lemonade.

The chicken paitan is definitely a unique dish in that it is very rich in flavor, but it is based on a chicken broth as opposed to a pork broth that ramen is typically made from. While it's not super uncommon to encounter a chicken-based broth in ramen restaurants, it is rare for me to see a chicken-based broth ramen as the spotlight ramen. Overall, the dish was very flavorful, lean, and definitely high quality.

The yuzu lemonade was also something unique in that it has a prominent yuzu flavor as opposed to a hint of yuzu, which most yuzu-flavored drinks have. I definitely think the yuzu lemonade is something people should try it if piques their interest.

Overall, I give Ivan Ramen four stars because it is very excellent, high quality ramen, but it is definitely on the pricier range when I compare against other ramen shops that I've been to.
First time trying. It was pretty good! Got the pork broth and egg and woodear mushrooms. Super tasty and fast delivery ! Can't wait to try more food from there

There's a lot of hype around Ivan Ramen, which I think might've built it up to be more than what it turned out to be, which is a solid ramen place with A+ service. 

I definitely recommend the pork chashu bao appetizer and their ramen eggs were beautifully gooey. The tonkotsu ramen though, while rich with a very generous helping of pork, was just OK, maybe a little too salty, though it is beautifully presented. 

I wouldn't go out of my way if you are a big ramen snob, but if you live in the area and have a craving for Ramen, it's a great place to go, with a fun informal ambiance.

Me and Ramen go hand and hand on my best days and on my worst days lol. Tried out IVAN Ramen with a group of friends last weekend and off the bat I loved how unique their space was. They have a few different seating options, including a covered outdoor patio at the back of the restaurant! I ordered the Tonkotsu Ramen and it tasted appropriately but definitely not filling. For $18 I truly thought the portion size would've been bigger. Nonetheless its a cool spot to check out if you're in the mood for some ramen and are willing to supplement with some appetizers.
Awesome food and service! Waiter was extremely kind and helpful and the ramen and apps were fantastic - Especially loved the Japanese Fried Chicken which may be the best fried chicken I've ever had!

Ivan Ramen has been bookmarked on my list ever since watching Chef's Table but sadly it was overhyped. I enjoyed the meal enough - wasn't bad but did not wow me. The chicken karaage was oversauced (this is coming from someone that loves sauce) and tasted more like Orange Chicken/General Tso's chicken. The sauce made the chicken soggy which defeats the purpose of eating fried food. The shiso ranch as solid and inventive though. Chicken paitan was just OK. The menu is fusion oriented and creative but this is definitely curated for the Western palate.

How does this place have such low ratings?? If you're looking for an authentic ramen place, this isn't the place for you but if you're looking for Japanese fusion with really good food, check it out! We got the steamed pork buns, crispy eggplant, and triple garlic pork ramen. We got pork buns because virtually every table near us had ordered them. The pork is super soft and flavorful but it's nothing out of the ordinary. The crispy eggplant on the other hand, is SUPER good and unique. I've never had a dish like it. The ramen was good too, just a tad salty. The wait staff is super friendly as well, which added to the experience :)

We had a reservation and when we reach there they said our reservation was cancelled and we checked and we hadn't cancelled our reservation, the email said they had cancelled it which they'd sent when we reached.  She offered no apology and no table, instead she was really rude and was like sorry we have other reservations you guys have to leave in an hour and sit outside in the heat if we want. Who wants to eat hot ramen in 82 degrees heat?? Anyway very unprofessional restraunt and very rude service for something that was their fault and not ours! The woman also cut us off while speaking instead of accommodating us.

I was so excited to try the food here as a fan of Ivan Orkin and the chefs table episode that chronicled his life, but was so rudely turned off by the staff that I decided to go somewhere where I could maintain my self respect. I had made a reservation for 6:30 pm at this location a day in advance and had it confirmed. I was on my way to the restaurant and at 5:22 pm the restaurant cancelled my reservation for an indoor table and when I arrived they said there was a mixup so the only table they could give me was in the backyard which was ridiculously hot and humid (82 degrees outside). I politely asked once, "why was my reservation cancelled for someone else's" and as I was speaking the lady server at the reception rudely cut me off and gestured out front like you would point out a destination for a dog "you guys can go outside and just take that table". Feeling insulted and disrespected I am sad to say I won't be trying the food at this place. I remain a huge fan of Ivan orkin and his life's story, but I can't say I'm a fan of the service. Take out is probably the way to go

New to the neighborhood and looking for my go-to ramen spot. This place is GREAT! I got the Tonkotsu Ramen and Crispy Eggplant - the ramen was tasty and the broth was really silky. The eggplant is addictive!! Other reviewers said that the broth was too salty, it was definitely on the saltier side but it didn't bother me. And the portions were great too!

OMG. I cannot believe this place does not have 10 stars! I am not a ramen fan but my daughter is and when I read about Ivan I thought I have to try this. Well it did not disappoint, it was AMAZING!! First of all Chad with my order was an angel and so helpful. I did pick up to take to my daughter in NJ and Chad was waiting at the door and knew my name like we were old pals. But the food was so flavorful and yummy. We got two ramens: one veggie and one regular. They were both a treat for your tastebuds. I am now a ramen fan! We also got some apps and the pork bun which was so delicious and the fried chicken went to my son in law who never likes anything and he loved it. Ivan Ramen, you rock!!

I heard about Ivan Ramen from Mike Chen, as he placed it as one of his top ramen places. I had been dying to try out this place for a while and I finally went with my mom. First impression, the service was great, a server held the door for us as she was heading back in the restaurant, and another server took his time taking our order patiently despite seeming busy. Our food didn't take long to come which was a relief. Now for the reason of three stars, I ordered the tonkotsu and my mom ordered the shoyu. We both agreed that the broth was salty. The tonkotsu broth was quite thick and looked like it took time to make. The rye noodles were interesting, since I'm used to eating the ramen from a package. I actually like the rye noodles. Every few bites, we had to drink the lemonade and palmer (barley + lemonade.) I got the palmer, at first I was a bit confused of how it wasn't as sweet as I intended it to be, but when you pair it with the ramen, it kinda makes sense. The lemonade part tasted homemade, not something you'd buy from a deli/market. It's more on the sour side, but there's also a taste of sweetness. The steamed pork buns were not too bad, also quite salty as well. For somebody who only eats lean meat and can't handle animal fat texture, the flavors were pretty good. The fat LITERALLY melts in your mouth. Overall, it's quite mediocre. I rarely eat ramen, but maybe I should give it a second chance and order something else next time.

As a ramen lover, after watching the Chef's Table episode about this place I just knew I had to give it a try. So, months later on my next trip to New York, we added Ivan Ramen to our packed food itinerary and prepared to be amazed.

We visited to New York over the summer in the scalding heat, so maybe a huge bowl of steaming ramen wasn't the best idea timing wise, but lucky for us we got there when it was raining. 
My group and I were some of the first customers to arrive for dinner after putting our names down for a reservation earlier that same day. Our waiter led us to our table in the back where he warned us that if we put our bags against the wall, water might leak onto them since we were really only covered by a roof of plastic and the rain was really coming down. He was very friendly about it though, and it didn't turn out to be a problem.

We already knew what we were going to order. My mom and I both got the tonkotsu ramen, my aunt got the spicy red chili ramen, and my uncle got the Ivan Ramen classic, Tokyo shio. For appetizers, we ordered the crispy eggplant and tobanjan green beans (which our waiter said were about a 5 on the mild to spicy scale). 
Our food came out very quickly, which was perfect because we were in a hurry that day and only had 40 minutes to eat.

~Appetizers~
The crispy eggplant was delicious, it came out piping hot from the kitchen and the amount of crisp was just right. The flavor was subtle, not so overpowering that it would take away from the ramen.
I only had a few of the tobanjan green beans because I have a very low spice tolerance. They were really good, and very crispy but even my aunt and uncle, who love spice, admitted that this dish was a bit of a jolt.

~The Ramen~

I had known this before coming here, but when the ramen arrived I was still shocked at how truly unique it was. The broth in my tonkotsu ramen was extremely thick, it was almost like a sauce yet it coated the noodles perfectly. The noodles themselves were the perfect texture, firm yet chewy in the way that all ramen noodles should be. They for sure tasted house-made. The soft boiled egg was cooked for just the right amount of time to get the perfect jammy center, but other than that there wasn't anything special about it. 
The chashu pork was also slightly underwhelming, as it didn't have much flavor and just kind of sat there. The highlight of the ramen was most definitely the broth and the noodles, and despite my few gripes, I managed to finish the entire bowl, savoring even the last dregs.

My aunt with the spicy red chili ramen however, had trouble with the spice. She said that her bowl was extremely delicious, but she just couldn't finish due to the spice level. She had sweat dripping down her face while eating it! So, if you aren't a hardcore spice fan, maybe avoid ordering that.

~Quick Summary~

Service: Friendly staff, food came out quick

Appetizers: Just the right amount before a big meal, would order the same things again and would like to try more

Ramen: Untraditional ramen, so don't come here if you're a purist! It was very good though.
Portion size was just the right amount for one person. Flavor was on point

Would I come back here?: 
The short answer, yes. Although I'd only return once I've tried every other ramen place in New York and wanted a taste of unconventional ramen. 

Definitely come here if you're visiting, the quick service and good food is worth it, however I'm sure there are other ramen places that haven't been spoken about by everyone and their mother that I would rate higher than Ivan Ramen.

A fun meal - particularly with a group of 4 (or more).  Visiting with a group will allow you to share multiple starters. We particularly enjoyed the Spicy Kyuri Pickles, Crispy Eggplant and Japanese Fried Chicken.  The Ramen is distinctive. Eating with a group will allow you to sample several of the Ramen varieties.  All are delicious!  The service is friendly and attentive.

Like some other reviewers here, I discovered Ivan Ramen through Chef's table on Netflix, so I was curious to try it out. My friend and I came here on a Thurs early evening (my friend has also seen Chef's table), no wait time without a reservation, and the staff was friendly. For further context, my friend and I have had our fair share of ramen bowls in nyc; we have also been to Japan and had ramen there as well.

My friend had the Tokyo Shio ramen with the unique roasted tomato (not a typical ingredient in ramen) and I had the tonkotsu. I generally prefer the richer broth of tonkotsu ramen vs shio or shoyu ramen.

Tonkotsu: Rating 7/10
I thought this was a solid bowl of ramen, but not anything particularly special. The broth was rich and flavorful. The noodles were unique; relatively thin and quite firm. I saw on Chef's table that Ivan likes to use rye flour in his ramen, and I'm assuming that there was rye flour in these noodles, though I didn't confirm. Personally, I would prefer a bit thicker noodle with a bit more of a springy chew. The pickled mustard greens added some strong flavor, though I'm not sure if they really enhanced the overall bowl. The chashu pork I actually thought was a bit subpar; not particularly flavorful, and there some parts that actually tasted a bit dry.

Tokyo Shio: Rating 7/10 per my friend
My friend thought his bowl was just ok, not bad, but not great. 


Overall, I think Ivan Ramen is a perfectly fine ramen spot, but not anything special. If I happened to be in the area again, I would be willing to try one of the other types of ramen on the menu, but I would not go out of my way to come here again. The pricing even for nyc is a tad high; $18 for the tonkotsu, $17 for the tokyo shio. NYC has a lot of good ramen spots, and in my opinion there are better ones out there, e.g. Ichiran and Ippudo to name a couple. I would rate 3.5 stars if I could; at the time of this review, the overall rating average is 3.5 stars, which I think is appropriate.
Absolutely delicious ramen I ever ate was the Tokyo Shoyu! The appetizers were pretty good. I definitely recommend you eating it and I also look forward to eating there next time! :)

Love me some ramen!! I got the chicken paitan and the broth was delicious! They recommend to break the yolk fast so that the yolk doesn't harden at the bottom. It gave the broth a nice creamy flavor! I love the minced chicken and felt like they give a good amount of it!

I got a delivery from this place. Ramen had very little flavor and portion was very small for the price. Curry was tasteless. Worst curry sauce ever. This is a restaurant which does not take any care or pride in its offerings.

Went for a family member's early evening birthday dinner. We got seated outside right away when we arrived on time. We started with some uniquely delicious appetizers, crispy eggplants and deep fried cauliflowers. 

We each had a different mostly noodle/ramen dish. I ordered the cold noodles and found it delicious if the flavorful tahini sauce was what I liked. One of us had spicy ramen, which was particularly amazing for me as far as al dente noodle and broth! It was legitimately spicy and also flavorful, but not overly salty.

Service was prompt although we didn't feel rushed at all. Great experience!

I really liked this place!

Got seated on the patio in back and ordered a yuzu lemonade and seafood tsukeman. Orders came out relatively quickly by a lovely waiter. The yuzu lemonade, not gonna lie, was tart! One of the rare few times I was glad there was plenty of ice in the drink to dilute the taste a bit. 

The seafood tsukeman however was *chefs kiss*. It came with these very thick noodles with a good chew. The broth itself was like lobster bisque in the best sense. Creamy, savory and full of seafood flavor, you could drink it alone without the noodles. The shrimp toast it was served with was crunchy and tender in the middle, filled with shrimp. I will say, I do feel like both together was a bit too much richness. But if you're looking for a cheat day treat, totally worth it!
I am not a huge fan of the minced chicken.  The raw egg enhanced the creaminess of the soup though. I wish I got a different entre.
Love this place. Never disappoints. Was there 2 weeks ago and met Ivan who was super nice. Sat in the back. Shio ramen and the chicken ramen. Excellent.

An excellent ramen place. We ordered the cauliflower and the green beans appetizers. The cauliflower was perfectly crispy, the curry sauce was fine. The green beans were ina delicious garlic-chili-peanut sauce, very tasty, not spicy. The spicy ramen was spoon good. The broth was hearty but not too heavy, perfect spice level, the egg tasted rich, the noodles and the pork were good. The triple pork was very filling.

First time at Ivan Ramen and I have to say everything was pretty much on point. Mainly to the staff, who were super accommodating and on top of their game. Something you can't even say of 3 Michelin starred restaurants post pandemic. From the gentleman that changed our tables to avoid to the rain and climbed on the table to turn off our heating lamps to William who suggested everything amazing. 

The spicy daikon dish was a sleeper hit so definitely order that. I went with the spicy ramen, and although not every spicy, was every bit delicious. 

If there was one negative about the entire night, it was the hostess that seemed slightly overwhelmed and lost at times. But between the food and the rest of the service, this place is popular for a reason.

I eat a lot of ramen. At a lot of different places around the country. I'm not a ramen snob, or wanna be poseur, or someone who leaves a 1-star review because they didn't get the table they wanted. If the food and service is good, I say so. If it's not, I say so. 

Ivan Ramen is the best ramen I've ever had. Hands down. I know food can be very subjective, so take it how you want. But the chicken paitan, Tokyo shio, spicy red chili, as well as the mazemen triple pork triple garlic, Japanese fried chicken, and curry cauliflower are all sublime. 

Now let's talk service. Every time I've been here the people are friendly, attentive, and accommodating. The food is always delivered quickly and at the right temperature. 

The service is as good as the food, and that's saying a lot. 

Thank you, Ivan Ramen, for a perfect experience every time.

No pictures because I can't get over how salty the Tokyo Shoyu was. The Tokyo Shoyu was wayyyyyyy too salty. Usually, I love drinking my ramen broth but I really could not this time. I get that there's soy sauce in this but it's really salty. The ramen and meat were great but damn still cannot get over how salty the broth was. Please calm down here chefs.

First off how this place only has 3.5 stars on this app is crazy. This place is defiantly a 5 star place. I first was turned onto this place by the Netflix series where Ivan's story was explained and this was when I found out about him. 

I arrived at the restaurant right when they opened at 12pm. There was surprisingly a lot of people there already but I was greeted warmly by the front of the house and seated right away. I came knowing what I wanted but the waiter asked if I needed any suggestions or if he can answer any question. 

I stated out with their take on an Arnold Palmer, its called an Ivan Palmer. Its their Yuzu Lemonade and barley ice tea. This was amazing. It wasn't overly sweet, tart from the Yuzu and the strong tea with a little bit of barley taste to it. It gives this drink a very unique taste. 

I started with the steamed pork buns. Probably one of the best steamed buns I have had. The pork belly was very tender and it was rich, the plum sauce that was on it was sweet a little salty and had a very umami flavor. they had shredded pickled daikon on top that really cut through the fatty richness of the pork belly. The actual steamed bun was soft, warm, and very tender. This was an amazing start to the meal.

I opted for the Tonkotsu Ramen. My first impression looking at the bowl was that the broth was thick, there was a thin amount of fat on the top of the broth, the egg was perfectly soft boiled and it was very inviting. The Broth itself was rich with flavor. It coated your mouth and you could really taste the elements that went into making it. the pork flavor was there, it was slightly sweet and did have a little heat on it. to me the broth and the noodles are what make ramen special. The noodles in this dish were fantastic. They are either made in house or by someone in the city because you could tell these were hand made. They were a good thickness, they gripped onto the broth well, they were tender but chewy at the same time and had a great flavor to them. This was a very special bowl of ramen. Best I have ever had in the United States and maybe even in the World, and that counts my ramen expeditions in Japan. 

The rest of the toppings in the ramen were great. the Egg was perfect, the mushrooms complimented the soup well with taste and a nice texture change. The Chashu was tender and melted in your mouth when ate it. The pickled greens in the ramen cut the fattiness of the broth while adding a layer of flavor. 

Please go out of your way to go to this ramen shop. You will not be sorry. best ramen in the United States and maybe even in the world. He has really honed his craft.

First time coming across Ivan was via Chef's Table on Netflix. Thought it was super interesting as the owner, Ivan Orkin, comes from a non-Japanese background, albeit lived in Japan for a bit of time. As many ramen bowls are typically pork-based, Ivan was known for his chicken-broth and popularizing that style in NYC.
 
I walked in on an early Saturday evening as the restaurant was starting to fill up. Luckily, my friend and I did not have to wait as we were able to grab one of the seats at the "bar" (single-seated areas).
 
I ordered the Japanese Fried Chicken and Triple Pork Triple Garlic Mazemen (tonkotsu broth / pork belly two ways / garlic shallots). Admittedly,  I was going back & forth with the mazemen and tonkotsu ramen despite my above note about the chicken broth as I was craving a pork-based meal. Notably, mazemen is essentially broth-less ramen and it is my favorite type of ramen; however, this was not the best that I have had and wish the portion size was a bit larger. Still on the search for my favorite in the city! For the Japanese Fried Chicken, this was cooked in toasted garlic caramel, togarashi (Japanese mixed chili pepper), and a side of shisho ranch. I was totally expecting this to be karaage, but to my surprise was nothing like it. Contained more sauce, thus saucier and was overall a bit mid. Next time, I'd probably order another appetizer.
S'aight-not my favourite ramen I've ever had, trends towards upscale without really justifying it imo. Broth wasn't as flavourful as I'd have liked.
Disappointing. Everything was meh. From food to ambiance to service. And to think I thought it was a must-try. Pass.

Tasty food. Enjoyable twist to the traditional Japanese ramen. The crispy eggplant app is very light & tasty. Chicken paitan broth is very flavorful & satisfying without being too heavy. The rye noodles are not quite al dente but have enough chewiness to them. The Ivan Palmer is very refreshing & a perfect complement to the hearty broth.  Just a bit on the pricey side for ramen.

Very happy to see Ivan ramen still open and thriving, we stopped for lunch on a Monday and almost every table was full so lucky we didn't have to wait. We sat on the high top tables which I liked as you can see the chefs at work. Ordered Cucumber Pickles and Japanese Fried Chicken, the pickles are very understated absolutely delicious for something so simple. The fried chicken was the perfect crisp and juicy mouthfuls, dunked in the flavourful ranch. We had the Chicken Katsu Curry and Spicy Miso Ramen for mains, one comment I would make about the Katsu as you can see from the picture they need to put it on a bigger plate as the chicken was hanging off the edge. Great tasting curry and crispy chicken. The spicy miso ramen was lovely, noodles had the right chew and broth have great flavours. Perfect spice to warm you up in this cold weather we've got.

As a home ramen chef, I've been there twice, and enjoyed the food each time. My favorite bowl was the shoyu, which has a really nice smoky and oceany umami. My partner had the chili ramen and liked it too.

I enjoyed my spicy pork ramen! They checked vaccine cards and gave us the option of indoor, outdoor, and patio seating. We sat on the heated back patio which was entirely enclosed; good for heat but not functionally different from indoors if you're looking for open air. They seemed to have a nice beer list alongside some wine and sake options, but I didn't get the chance to try anything out this time.  The ramen-themed mosaic on the patio wall was charming and the service was a little slow but friendly.

I didn't know this place was famous from being on Netflix, but I came because of Seated and I was going to Koneko right after. 

I arrived at 1pm and 70% was full. I was seated right away at this bar table that faces the wall. While staring at the wall the whole time, I noticed how the paint was chipping and cracking. 
Heat inside was a bit too strong and stuffy especially when you're going to get hot from eating the ramen. 

Crispy eggplant caught my eye the most out of the whole menu. It seemed a bit extra if I was going to order a ramen on top of this but I insisted. 
I like how it came fast and really hot and crispy. The batter is tempura but not too thick or rough or hard. The eggplant was tender and soft without seeds inside. Even though this was fried, it didn't feel oily. 
I didn't like how they paired this with tahini sauce. It felt too heavy. It would be nice to get a vinaigrette or citrus sauce option. 

Ramen. I have a whole thought process for how I chose shio. 
Didn't want tonkotsu for the mustard greens and looks like it wasn't part of the original menu. 
Didn't want chicken paitan because of the minced treatment of chicken and how it comes with egg yolk. 
Between shoyu and shio, I chose shio because of the tomato it comes with. I can't tell if I like or dislike how each soup base has different toppings. 
Shio. The dashi chicken broth was too weak for me. I didn't like how it was grainy not just at the bottom of the bowl. 
Chashu was tender in some parts but rough in others. 
Soft boiled egg was overcooked as you can see from the edges of the yolk
Good they gave so much scallion. 
The deciding factor tomato was a great decision because it was so juicy and sweet. Too bad they only gave one piece rather than two in the menu. 
Noodles. Other ppl are saying how it's made from rye flour. There is a chew to it but I'd prefer bouncier and eggier type of noodle. 

The server checked in on me multiple times but it felt weird whenever he came up cuz it feels surprising each time. The music was (not too) loud and facing the wall made it hard to detect surrounding movements. I was afraid to look around too hard in case I triggered someone to check in on me. Maybe it's a good idea to have some decor on the wall such as a photo frame or brushed metal items to give some soft reflections.

Overall the food had nice aspects but too many small details that irked me. I wouldn't say I had a bad experience but I'm not eager to come back.

Family of 4 came here when visiting NYC after seeing the Chef's table show. It was great ramen and lived up to all expectations. We all ordered a different ramen bowls and we all loved our dishes.  My Spicy Chili was just a bit of a challenge, but not too much, which is the way I like it.   Pork bun appetizers were excellent.  Waitress was friendly and responsive, and we were in and out rather quickly (as we expect with ramen.)  Ramen noodles are unique.  Everything I expected!

Ramen was great, but the whole staff was amazing. They seated us properly, we never had to ask for anything, water was never empty, and the check was promptly. Really not sure why this place has 3.5 stars. This is one of the best ramen and the service was even more amazing. I can't wait to visit again when I am back in the city.

I really enjoyed Ivan Ramen. I made a reservation, which I recommend. The staff was super friendly and service was excellent. Portions are big. Their appetizer menu is interesting and I had a tough time deciding, but went with the crispy eggplant with tahini, which was fantastic. I went with the Tokyo shio ramen and added bok choy. The ramen was rich and delicious. I was excited for Ivan Ramen and it did not disappoint.

It's like they did everything different, but in no way better. 

Instead of classic wheat noodles, it's buckwheat that tastes worse. Instead of pork broth, it's chicken broth that tastes like overly salty matzo ball soup. Instead of steaming hot, it's lukewarm and uncomforting. 

It's one of those places you see food critics rave cause it's "different", but honestly you just feel disappointed and want actual ramen instead.

When first arriving at the restaurant during lunchtime,  we were told there would be a 45 minute wait for 2 people. I wasn't surprised considering the place was a full house. However, it turned out to be about a 15 minute wait (not saying this will be the same experience for everyone, but it was a pleasant surprise). We were seated at the bar, which was fun since we got to see the cooks in the kitchen. There are other seats lined along the whole restaurant though, both indoors and outdoors. The whole time we were tended to by very friendly staff and an amazing, personable waitress.

We started of pork buns that offered a burst of flavor. Then we got our main course, Tokyo Shio ramen. This dish looks simple off first glance but it's everything but. The chicken broth was like a warm hug, eggs were perfectly soft boiled and runny, pork was so tender it was falling apart, the famous roasted tomato was truly ~umami, and the buckwheat noodles had a great snap when biting into it. Additionally, it was surprisingly very filling considering I showed up starving. Loved getting to experience this restaurant after watching it on Chef's table.

Blithe incompetence is the general rule at this place. I ordered a delivery of their spicy ramen and they failed to include the broth. Fine - mistakes happen. But they made sure to block any possible way of getting the mistake corrected. Their phone number drops immediately. When I then went the indirect way through DoorDash, they refused to do a re-delivery, but were perfectly fine with taking a fresh order (DoorDash was willing to offer credits for this). By the time they haggled their way into this position, it was too late to place the re-order. The evening was ruined for an out of town guest who had heard amazing things about this place and decided to burn a night in a town with so much to offer on these guys. What a sh**show of an operation.

Fabulous ramen place. That every seat is filled and the turnover is quick says a lot. What speaks the most is the quality of the food. Spicy Kyuri pickles the perfect blend of cold, sour, and hot red-flake chili spice! The pork bun was constructed so every bite had the bao, pork and sauce. Every bite!! The rich pork broth of the Tokyo Shoyu ramen was so flavorful - it was as if the broth had subtle tones of flavor. Every slurp was smooth with flavors. Id happily travel the 40 min from uptown to eat here!

I was super hyped for this restaurant since I got the Ivan Ramen cookbook for Christmas and wanted to taste the real deal while I was in town. We made a reservation weeks in advance but when we got there still had to wait outside in the cold for 15 minutes. Doesn't a reservation mean your table is physically reserved until you arrive?! Anyways, we eventually got seated but the tables are crammed super close together, like maybe 1 ft apart) so you have to push the table to the side to let someone sit down. This also means you can hear and participate in everyone's conversation if you wanted. Our server at least was friendly and responsive to our needs, he checked on our meal regularly and never rushed us.

Food-wise we started with some fried chicken and pork buns which were both a little weird. The pork bun i had still had some connective tissue and stuff in it, not the melty smooth pork belly I'm used to at other restaurants. It was also served with some cold vegetable slaw that was discordant with the otherwise warm and steamy bun. The fried chicken was mushy like some orange chicken dishes although the flavor was unique with a citrusy/yuzu sauce that was refreshing. For the main course I got the Shio ramen which is the dish that made him a success in Japan while my wife got the spicy ramen. In both, the noodles were definitely the star of the dish as they were texturally perfect with a toothy bite expected of fresh ramen and the toasted rye he adds definitely adds more dimension. The broths were only OK though and nothing mind blowing. 

Overall I was glad I got to try Ivan ramen but probably won't come back because there are just much better options in New York such as Ippudo.

I can't believe I haven't reviewed this place already. Ivan is one of my favorite NYC ramen shops. It's a hike to get to it as it's located in an out of the way area of Manhattan but it's well worth the trip. I get the Shio or Spicy whenever I eat here. Both are delicious.

A little ramen shop that I have now fallen in love with.

Although it's a little on the pricier end of the spectrum, it really didn't stop me from going back and introducing it to friends and family. 

I like to order their tonkatsu ramen while I would order their shoyu ramen for my husband. 

At first glance, I'd hope the portion to be bigger because I've got a big appetite. But because the broth is sooooooo overwhelmingly rich, it feels perfect.

Never been here since the initial hype. It was easy to make a reservation and there was no wait. The indoor dining area is fairly small (very narrow and tables were pretty close together).

Appetizers were great! We ordered the crispy eggplant and XO daikon. Both were super flavorful and had interesting spices.

Ramen (I ordered the tonkotsu) was decent but nothing out of the ordinary. The onsen egg was perfect. I found the broth to be too salty. My friend had the vegan ramen and also thought it was too salty.

Decent ramen for given price

Food: This was my second trip here. My first time I ordered the Tokyo Shio ramen, was absolutely blown away. Loved the flavors and each ingredients complemented the main star: the noodles and soup. Ordered the Chicken Paitan this time, was not as satisfied. The taste wasn't where I wanted it to be, will likely go back to getting my shio ramen next time. Broth felt a little heavy without the lime. With the lime, it was definitely lighter, but it didn't feel like ramen anymore. I highly recommend the shoyu or shio ramen, those are the original dishes that really shine. Never heard of sun dried tomatoes in ramen, but it works in this case. Would have tried the tsukamen ramen, but with a lobster ingredient in there, it was going to cost a pretty penny to order.

Environment: with COVID barriers set up, it feels more cramped than usual. They have hooks for your jackets under the tables and bar stools for seats. Not entirely comfortable, but it's doable. They have outdoor and indoor dining. The bathroom is pretty clean. Very cramped, but it's supposed to be a ramen shop. I wouldn't mind waiting or reserving a spot if it means I have a more comfortable experience. 

Staff: relatively friendly staff and checked in on us occasionally. We didn't stay too long, so I can't really judge this aspect too harshly.

Takeaway notes: plan to eat in and out. Probably not a spot you want to dine in and chat for a while. Pretty much an in and out type of place, nothing wrong with that however. Great food, but depends on what you like and your flavor preferences. They have a little bit for everyone. Prices on the higher end, but nothing crazy.

Came here for lunch and were told the wait would be around 20min, but we ended up being seated within 5min.

We ordered the fried chicken, pork buns and eggplant as appetizers. The chicken was good, but a bit sweet for me and not as crispy as we would have liked. The pork buns were enjoyable and the eggplant was tasty but strange. Definitely an odd combination of flavor and texture. The outside of the eggplant was crispy but the inside was almost liquid.

Tried the spicy chili ramen, vegan ramen and tonkatsu. The vegan ramen was not great and we would not order it again. The spicy chili was good, nice spice level and the tonkatsu was very good. I would definitely recommend the tonkatsu.

The portions and prices are what you would expect. The service is fast, the only complaint is the restaurant is very narrow, so there is not alot of space.

This is, hands down, one of the best bowls of ramen I have ever tried. It's rich and well balanced, with every single ingredient being a star of its own. The noodles are silky and have a bite, without being rubbery. 
The spicy pickles are incredible and the pork belly buns are to die for. This was my first time here and I'll return every time I am in the city. What a treat!

I can here with family for dinner. My sister and cousin ordered the Tonkatsu. They share that it had dynamic flavors that separates it from similar ramen they have had. I ordered the spicy ramen, and the heat level was on-point! Typically when I order spicy ramen, the heat is off. 

The steamed pork buns have room for improvement. The Coney Island fried tofu was a new items for me, and it was delicious; as a non-mushroom fan, this was delicious.

Lives up to the hype. We were able to sit at the bar for a weekday dinner. Good vibes and service. Our waitress was extremely attentive and professional yet also chill. The ramen itself was oily af-- making it delicious and flavorful. The homemade noodles are so chewy and perfectly cooked. Solid ramen, on par with neighbors Mr.Taka and Ishida... will definitely go back!

Garden seating available for those who prefer a super safe dining experience!
Before I begin writing about their ramen, I have to mention their yuzu cheesecake with gooey center. 
It's splendind. I can't detect any yuzu flavor, but no matter. 
Order it. And the dessert pricing is fabulous. I mean, aren't we're all tired on paying $14 for some mediocre diner quality cakes? They're only charging $7-8 for a marvelously made cheesecake. 

Ramen: Broth is unforgettable. The noodle itself is OK. They should give customers the choice of noodle hardness for "koshi" コシ.  

The Appetizers we ordered were delicious. We ordered Coney Island fried tofu and fried chicken. 

The staffs are super friendly and informative
It was certainly a little busy, but so overwhelmingly delicious. The aroma and the food just made everything amazing. Great service and excellent food menu.

This place was amazing- from food all the way to staff. The food was flavorful and fulfilling! We had multiple appetizers, the vegan ramen, the spicy ramen and even a free steamed pork bun on the house bc they heard I wanted to try it but I thought I've order too much food already. Will return and would definitely recommend.
Been here half a dozen times now. Fast, friendly, and delicious. Noodles have excellent mouth feel, broth is fatty and delicious. Steamed pork bao is unparalleled.

Years ago I read about Ivan Orkin, a New Yorker who took Japan over by storm with his interpretation of ramen. When Ivan Ramen opened in the Gotham West Market, my son and I rushed to be one of the first to try his famed ramen.

Fast Forward 2022, I see a show on Orkin. How he started in Japan, his personal loss  and how he came back to the US. I have to say it was touching. I told my son let's hit up this place on the weekend. 

We walk in before noon and I'm asked if we have reservations. I replied we do not but we eat very quickly! The hostess laughed and sat us at an open table. 

We're easy: two beers and two Tokyo Shio Ramen bowls. No sides, we're on a mission to slurp.

The ramen comes out pretty quickly. I'd like to say I taste rye in the noodles, I will say it's a very different spin on what I've been enjoying at other ramen spots in the city. 

Ivan Ramen, I thank you for the elegant and well crafted ramen bowl my son enjoyed at both of your locations. I wish you great success in all your endeavors. You're a testimony to why you should never give up and keep trying.

My experience was perfect. The servers were out of this world kind and attentive, the noodles in my Chicken Paitan were al dente and was the best partner for the broth, and the Ivan Palmer was refreshing and comforting at the same time. My partner got the Triple Pork which was also amazing. I can't wait to go back!
Very few places that have chicken paitan and it's soooo yummy. I add spicy chili oil every time. I love the minced chicken. So yummy. Not like other places with dry chicken breast.

Simply some of the best ramen in the country. It also helped that our waitress had some great recommendations with regards to the appetizers (the eggplant was incredible, and I'm saying this as someone who isn't an eggplant fan). Can't wait to go back!

CHICKEN PAITAN @ivan_ramen lower east side, NEW YORK

Booked this cute spot on OpenTable after reading raving reviews online. Ivan learned and built his ramen businesses first in Tokyo and later started this flagship shop in lower east side 

Ramen noodles are thinner and chewy, with the star of the show being the chicken paitan ramen that comes with rich chicken broth, minced chicken, egg yolk, and shio kombu. Light and simple with the sweet and umami taste from a chicken broth made for hours . 

At anytime , you can squeeze in lime juice, which uniquely changes the flavor profile of the broth. 

We also ordered the classic tonkotsu, that comes with rich pork broth, shoyu-glazed chashu, woodear mushrooms, pickled mustard greens, soft egg, and mayu. Tonkotsu was definitely richer and fattier. The pork want as smoked or charred as I liked but still pretty good, especially with the thinner hand made noodles

Would love to try the mazemen next time. Thicker more concentrated broth for dipping and thicker rye  noodles with lots of garlic 

@midwestmunching
The Michelin starred restaurant training comes through in these tasty, inven, and well composed ramens. Don't miss eggplant appy.
The best ramen restaurant I know of in NYC.  Their pork buns are also exceptional. Please open other locations!

Delicious ramen! And the steamed buns were some of the best I've ever had. The place was pretty packed when we went, but everything still came out pretty quick. If you like ramen, you should check this place out!

Update to the below review. Ivan Ramen called me after I sent an email to their website portal. They 1. apologized that that happened and 2. explained the situation.

Sounds like the server was a newer server and didn't realize the policy. Hope he doesn't get punished or anything. They said it was their fault for not giving him the proper information/training, which is the right thing to call out - don't blame, take responsibility. They also said that this is not their policy. Apparently, sometimes they have like an uncorking fee, but they usually wave it. I'll leave the review below untouched, but I'm incredibly glad to have this happen. The person who talked to me seemed really considerate and sad that I had a bad experience. They also essentially said they were glad to receive this kind of accountability, etc. After this, def willing to recommend - they might have even convinced me that chicken-based ramen can stand up to pork-based.

Food was great, huge issue with service. I'll talk about both.

Food: Food was great. I liked the ramen. I had fried chicken and chicken paitan ramen. Both were good. I prefer pork-based ramen, but I figured I'd get the chicken since they specialize in that. I would have rated this 4-5 stars if I were planning to write a review on just the food

Service: Waiter was nice and all, but there was exactly one thing that made me really angry. It was my friend's birthday and we were all having an excellent time. We were respectful and ordered a cheesecake for dessert. We also had brought some cupcakes, which - yes - you sometimes aren't allowed to bring. Seriously, though, we all ordered food and even ordered dessert. They weren't trying to rush us out either. Anyway, we open it up and are about to dig in, but the waiter came over and said, "hey all, as much as I'd love for this to happen, my manager would kill me if I did." We respectfully put the cupcakes away, finished the cheesecake, continued our conversation, and eventually left.

Ok, this was super frustrating. I have no idea if it's a restaurant policy, a manager policy, or if the waiter just made it up. I don't really care. It was my friend's birthday and making us put our cupcakes away was ridiculous. If none of us had ordered food, whatever, I get it, but we all ordered plenty of food, had some sake, and dessert. He literally ruined the experience and for what? If he had said "hey guys, it's our policy to not let food in from outdoor places, but I know it's your birthday, so just don't do it next time," I'd come back. Quite frankly the manager shouldn't be making his workers feel bad for accommodating customers. Not only did it not make us leave faster (since we still were enjoying the after dinner chat), but it also ruined the experience for two of us. Maybe there's some law or something, and if so, I'll consider amending this review, but there's no good reason to make customers feel bad, so that they're forced to buy your dessert. Look, you can even have a no outside food policy, but if the customers are already there and about to dig into dessert, don't make them put it away. I didn't buy dessert and won't recommend Ivan to people. Again, unless there's a legal issue with us bringing food, this is poor, poor management. I know customers can be super annoying and entitled and stuff, but this made me mad.

So, if you want good ramen, by all means go. I'm not writing this review so that people don't go. I'm writing it so that whoever made the policy will see this. I'm guessing Ivan, whoever he is, just really wanted people to enjoy ramen. I doubt that what the restaurant did is in that spirit.

For the record, I'm planning on contacting management and telling them about this. If they respond there or here, I will probably come back and edit this.

Everything I've eaten has been amazing, but my standouts are all the appetizers and especially the Seafood Tsukemen (shrimp toasts with rye noodles and a bisque-like sauce)--OMG. All the ramen is great, too--incredibly flavorful broths, amazing rye noodles.

I love this place because there is no mystery! What you see on the menu is exactly what you get! Very rarely does the food actually come out looking like the menu photo, but it does here and I totally appreciate it...especially with food that I don't know too much about! There's no missing ingredients, no surprises...exactly what you order is what will come out. The flavors are amazing, service is great and I really enjoyed every dish that came out! I highly recommend

Huge fan of this place. Have been several times and the food is consistently tasty. Service is fast but not rushed, waiters/staff are attentive but not overly so. Tonkotsu ramen is heavenly, japanese fried chicken and eggplant dishes are both delightful as well. Getting takeout from this place is awesome, called during peak hours on a Friday night and food was ready in 10minutes.

The vibes were right with this one! We went around open and the place was already jumping! I ordered the steamed pork buns to start. They were scrumptious! Our party ordered 2 orders (4 total). I went to reach for a bun and my friend DeAndre reached for one at the same time. We touched hands!! My heart started racing and I got the butterflies. Would this be the day we kissed? I snapped out of it when I remembered I was heterosexual. I needed to order a drink and get my mind off what just happened. I got Bellwoods, "JELLY KING". I am not normally a fan of sours, but this was a fruit forward sour. 1 word, delicious. It was perfect to put the questionable event that just occured behind me. For the main course I got the Tokyo Shio Ramen. It was other worldly! It was the umami bomb I didn't know I needed in my life. I took a big slurp of the broth. When I look up from slurping the broth I lock eyes with my other friend Ryan. Simultaneously a dribble of broth rolls down my lips to my chin. The butterflies were back. I needed to remind myself "Cian you are heterosexual". Things were getting tense. I was getting hot, starting to sweat. I needed an ice cold drink to wash these thoughts away. I ordered a Asahi, "SUPER DRY" a Japanese Rice Lager. It was the cold refreshing beverage I needed to get through this meal. All in all a great family friendly environment that serves great Ramen! I will be back!

It was quite packed on a Thursday night! I ate a giant pile of spicy pickles as an appetizer and ordered the classic tonkotsu for my entrée. 

I would definitely come back cause the food was great and the staff was really attentive and nice. I'm deducting a star because I wish the ramen portions were slightly larger.

It was just okay. My Japanese partner had warned me that they didn't think it was great but when my cousin visited and had it on their list I decided to see for myself. I am not sure why it's appeared on so many lists of must try Ramen when I feel that the price and quality are just about average. Also I think the owner/founder is a white guy? Maybe that's why the taste just doesn't live up to quality, authentic ramen.

The spicy chili ramen is sooooooo mf good omg. I crave it every day of my life. The cauliflower appetizer is also really really good. At first I was like "hmmm do I really want cauliflower?" But the answer is yes, you do.

Overall, I'd say I was pretty happy with my meal here. Staff were super nice and our waiter took the time to explain some of his favorite dishes. Ordered several appetizers and wasn't the greatest fan of the green beans but I liked the eggplant and fried chicken. Wished the chicken was a bit more crispy but flavor was good and really liked the sauce it came with. Ordered the chicken paitan ramen and was pleasantly surprised by the depth of flavor to it. Noodles had good texture, broth was rich without being oily, and the crispy chicken bits added some nice texture. Had the yuzu cheesecake for dessert-- thought the yuzu flavor was really mild and could've been stronger. Also while I'm familiar with the concept of a burnt top/basque cheesecake, I think they overdid it here because I was left with a fully charred top layer to scrape off and the inside wasn't gooey at all.
Really disappointed. Instagram sent me and turns out it was overhyped. The ramen taste was off and the prices were high. Wouldn't do it again.

Some of you might be aware of Ivan's backstory, some not. In short, Ivan has two locations in Tokyo that have a strong following, and he spent like two decades in Japan trying to perfect his version of a shio ramen. 

Quick primer for new ramen heads:
-Shio ramen: chicken stock, dashi (a kelp and fish-based stock), salt
-Shoyu ramen: soy sauce-based flavor 
-Tonkotsu: pork bone broth that's very creamy, rich and cloudy (it's a lot more nuanced than that but trying to keep this short)

Ivan's specialty is in shio ramen, although there is also shoyu and some other styles of ramen on his menu.

This is a very caveated 4/5 rating. I'm a big tonkotsu guy; that's my favorite ramen. So naturally, my favorite ramen shops in New York are Ichiran and Tonchin, where they specialize in tonkotsu. My palate prefers very strong flavor, salty af, rich, fatty, creamy, etc. So this review will be most relevant to those who have a similar palate as mine.

Shio ramen (4/5):
-I'd describe the flavor/saltiness/richness level as fairly mild and subtle. I can pick up some of the creamy subtleties but to me it was a bit too subtle. 
-Overall, the dish is decently good and satisfying, although I will note that as you drink more of the broth, more dashi (the sweet-ish kelp/fish stock) is concentrated towards the bottom so it will taste sweeter as you go. You can mitigate this by gently stirring the broth as you eat. 
-A+ job on the egg. Perfectly executed. Major points here
-A+ job on the pork chashu as well. I personally prefer pork shoulder chashu (the lean cut of pork, which is rare in New York), but I can appreciate a really good pork belly chashu (the one that is fatty and melts in your mouth)
-The noodles were good; chewy and starchy
-I appreciated the fact it was a simple bowl without nuking it with toppings, which I view as a sign of covering up for mediocre taste of the broth
-I admire Ivan's dedication to his craft, but this wasn't to my palate. Didn't knock my socks off, but you may really love it

Spicy ramen (3/5):
-This is basically a tantanmen. I think I've had better tantanmen elsewhere. This is decent, but not at the same level as the shio ramen. I'm glad I ordered both
-I find that the flavor is more than adequately flavorful/salty, but one-dimensionally so. It lacks something else, whether it's fat to cut through the acid or some other nuance for this to really be A-tier or unique versus a run of the mill ramen shop

Conclusion: definitely worth a visit just for the fact that Ivan is an important figure in ramen culture; tonkotsu lovers or people with salty palates like me should temper their expectations, otherwise you may really enjoy it

Other than that, the service we received was really exceptional, to a point worth mentioning and complimenting.

More like 4.5/5 because the eggplant was outta this world. Crispy garlic crust with soft juicy eggplant once you bite in, and the sesame purée is the sauce of my dreams I would carry around with me in my purse if I could. 

Featured on Chef's Table s3, this small restaurant specializes in thin noodle ramen. They have bar seats and also several tables for which I was able to make a reservation for on resy. 

Portions were a bit smaller than usual and the chasiu for tonkotsu was more lean/firm than preferred. We were still satisfied after especially with the rich broths. The different textures in my chicken paitan from the minced chicken and crispy chicken were more unique if you want to try something different!

We had the spicy ramen, japanese fried chicken, pork buns and yuzu cheesecake.  From head to toe it was a fabulous experience, my son really enjoyed his first ramen! He said it was his favorite meal in NYC, the only thing better than the ramen was seeing Hamilton.

My husband and I started out with the spicy kyuri pickles, which were out of this world! I had the Tokyo Shoyu. It was so delicious, and very flavorful! Last but not least, we had the Yuzu Cheesecake, which was also delightful! Jonathan was wonderful! We had a great experience, and really enjoyed all of our food! Thank you!
Very pleasant staff, good atmosphere,. great vibe
I stopped by this location for drinks and they were so refreshing! The yuzu lemonade was perfection and their outdoor eating area is so nice.

Some of my friends are addicted to this place and some of them say they don't enjoy it. There's a huge love - hate relationship with this place so I've been on the fence in coming here - however they have amazing GF options which made me fled here when my lover needed to be treated with her candida. All of their ramen could be made with tofu noodles and I am so grateful a place like this exists because we love ramen!

For appetizer we got the Kyuri pickles which came in a huge portion to start and was very nice and fermented tasting. We also got the Coney Island tofu which had no wheat in it and had a lot of mushrooms on top with a lot of flavor. The tofu was lightly fried which was a great added flavor. Already my taste buds were hit with a western flavor. Super American. We said that it tasted like an American fast food hot dog with onions and mustard except in tofu. 

The tofu ramen was still nice and springy - although like most vegetarian ramen it's more on the cleaner and healthier side versus their tonkotsu. For a gluten free option this can't really be beat. My tsukemen was so thick and yummy. The dip is made of lobster and shrimp dipping broth and it was super creamy and flavorful. Sort of reminded me of seafood/lobster bisque. It came with a "shrimp toast" that reminded me of cantonese fish balls on top of a really nicely toasted bread. I was really freaked out about the toast because I've never had anything like it and I was taken aback and couldn't really eat it together in comfort because it was so bizarre. But it had a great flavor to it. I can see why this place has a love-hate relationship for sure. It's very Americanized and non traditional and I guess for some people a more traditional taste would be optimal. It definitely was the first time I tasted anything like this. 

I would come back again because of the amazing options they have for GF and to try another ramen for myself! The tsukemen noodles are amazing alone and I would just come back for that dip and the noodle.

*pro tip- they have unlimited unsweetened barley tea

My boyfriend and I we're super excited to try the food here at Ivan Ramen. However, we were super disappointed at the quality of the food.
We started off our dinner with the pork bao buns and it was strong starter with no complaints 
Next we had the Tokyo Shio Ramen and it was super subpar with the noodles being super firm and the broth having a super fishy taste. 
We also had the Tonkotsu Ramen which was a bit better but had a bit too much seasoning than i'm used to for a classic tonkotsu ramen:
I think this place is fun if you want to experiment with out of the ordinary ramen flavors BUT my stomach didn't agree with the food and had me soooo sick
I haven't gotten food poisoning in sooo long and have forgotten the pain it brings. 
Come here if you want to spend your whole night in the toilet

Okay so to start off, I ate here about a month ago and completely forgot to leave a review! I just had to because of how often I have been daydreaming about the next time I get to eat here again! I am from CA and would take it to the extent to fly out to NY just for their food!! Lol. Their pork belly buns are delicious!! Ramen-outstanding. This spot was definitely everyone's favorite part about the entire trip & we could not stop talking about it on our way back home. Thank you for the amazing experience.
It is ok/decent ramen, the place is a bit overrated. The cucumber   appetizer was great! The atmosphere and service are good!

Since first seeing the Chef's Table on Ivan, I have not gone to New York without making the trek to have a bowl of absolute heaven. On several
Occasions, Ivan has been in the kitchen making what I can only describe as one of my favorite bowls of food I have ever had. We always have great service and plenty of sake. Full disclosure, I have only had the Chicken Paitan (add the roasted tomatoes) because I can't imagine having anything else. If you like ramen, It's worth the trip from wherever you are.
Delicious! Tried the ramen and a few of their appetizers. Everything was very tasty and the service was fast. Wasn't able to get a table so we sat at the bar. Definitely will come back!

Ivan Ramen has an informational and educational menu that is so fun to go through. If you know very little about ramen, Ivan will take away all the enigma with their TikTok-like video loops and captioned explanations.

I got the shio ramen, which I really enjoyed because of the surprisingly fishy taste. However, you might not expect fish flavor when you order a shio broth. The noodles were buckwheat or whole wheat, and had a brown color and a toothier texture which I liked.

I still wished the ramen had menma and seaweed and other topics instead of the excess of scallions and roasted tomato.

They do have a broad menu for non traditionalists, so it could be worth a return visit just to catch 'em all.

About a 1-1.5: I made reservations in advance to try Ivan Ramen out, and the super friendly host made sure we had great center seats at the counter, in front of the kitchen. That was so nice!

The menu included various starters, ramen, mazemn, tsukemen, rich dishes, desserts, and beverages.

We came here for an early lunch, and ordered:
+a Chicken Paitan - chicken broth with minced chicken, egg yolk, and chicken skin
+a Seafood Tsukemen - this came with a bowl of lobster & shrimp dipping broth, roasted cabbage, and slices of shrimp toast
+a glass of Housemade Yuzu Lemonade
