At first, we wanted to try the Shio, but we got suckered in in ordering the Paitan, as that was stated to be the most favorite out of the ramen choices.  Unfortunately, both bowls were just not good.  The ramen noodles were slightly overcooked for our taste, and there were several noodles that were clumped together.  Both of the broths in the Paitan and the Tsukemen had an unpleasant taste to them.  

I thought I liked the shrimp toast, but after the 2nd bite, it just tasted super greasy.  The tuskemen broth was on the thicker end, which I appreciated, but it had a fishy taste to it.

The housemade yuzu lemonade was fizzy, but could have been more chilled or served with more ice.

Service was welcoming and friendly, but our server enjoyed rambling on and on about the menu, and without sporting a mask, I noticed that the counter was continuously sprayed. Eeks.

The place definitely became packed with both those who had reservations and those who were walk-ins.

I'm glad I was able to try this place out, but wouldn't return.

+fishy tsukemen
+clumpy noodles
+reservations accepted
Pretty good vegan option for ramen! Albeit a bit pricey around $17-18 for a veggie bowl. Tight seating.
I tried their Italian sweet cream soft serve and it was delicious! Can be purchased quickly at the window as you're walking by

Not sure why this place is rated 3.5 stars, ramen was pretty good here. I've seen Ivan on various shows and I was interested in trying out this place for a while. The broth's here are definitely lighter than other ramen shops. I think I enjoyed the tonkotsu ramen the most, chashu was good and the broth was fatty but light. The noodles here were pretty good too. The qr scanned menu takes you to their website which gives you videos explaining the ramens. Got the Ivan Palmer too which was refreshing (yuzu instead of lemonade). Overall, a pretty solid ramen shop.

Stopped by this spot after a comedy show next door and my experience was... alright! Nothing crazy, neither good or bad. 

If you're an avid ramen eater, I don't think you would like this place. First off when a ramen place is owned by a non-asian person it's already heavily discredited in my opinion. I can appreciate it and their love for ramen but I guess I'm biased. 

The restaurant itself looks like any other ramen restaurant. Super long. (Anyone else notice this? Why are so many ramen restaurants long?) There's a bar section and also dining tables. We sat at the high top section. The decor is cute, not too obnoxious but definitely Asian-centered which again, a little weird since it's owned by a non-Asian person... lol. 

We ordered off the online menu that everyone seems to be so entertained by but when you're in the city with slow service due to high traffic/crowds, it's just annoying lol.

We got the Tokyo Shoyu, Tokyo Shio, pork buns, curry flower, tofu Coney Island. 

The ramens were good but not great. Nothing special or out of the ordinary. Broth was subpar and not deep and rich. Also the portion was pretty small... The pork buns were great. Super soft and delicious buns and the pork was cooked and seasoned well. The curry flower was delicious! Such an interesting flavor and texture combo and it just worked. The tofu was also pretty good but a little salty. 

Overall, I would say the apps stole the show. It was good to finally try this spot but prob won't be craving this spot by any means.

After spending countless years living in Japan, where he studied all things Japanese, and graduating from the famed Culinary Institute of America, Ivan Orkin opened up Ivan Ramen in the Lower East Side. As this spot has quickly become famous through countless features of it on television, blogs, and magazines, I expected a lot when I tried it. Happily, it did not disappoint.

The Restaurant itself feels like an alternate reality 1950s diner with mid-century pop funk music playing in the background, a massive collage of 20th century Japanese culture in the foreground, and a classic diner counter located at the back of the establishment.

This heavily marinated and sauced appetizer of Japanese Fried Chicken was solid. The batter remained crispy despite being heavily drenched with a mildly spicy, fruity, and rich sauce. The chives on top provided needed brightness to an otherwise heavy dish. Finally, the white sauce (which strongly reminded me of the white sauce found at Halal carts throughout NYC) added a refreshing creamy end to the bite. After finishing the dish, I had the pleasant surprise of the mild spice and yuzu flavor that coated the chicken lingering on my taste buds.

Hiding just under the broth laid perfect noodles that despite their narrow width were still quite adept at picking up loads of broth. The added soft-boiled egg was perfectly cooked, and the pork (aka chashu), although uniquely thick, surprisingly stayed tender and juicy. Like a real high-quality tonkotsu should, this broth coated my mouth with a mildly creamy and extremely porky flavor that was deep with a black pepper kick.

The second main dish I tried was the Chicken Katsu. Although quite good, this was the weakest dish that I tried. The chicken cutlet was crispy and moist but unfortunately too thin which made the chicken go cold fast. While the Japanese curry was very good, I wish it had that home made flavor. Instead, it was definitely the generic, out of the box Golden Curry type. Similarly, the rice was good but not special. The surprising highlight of the dish was the different forms of pickled vegetables as they added a much needed vinegary kick that cut through the rich flavor.

Check out the rest of my review on my blog here:

https://www.freshbite.org/articles/ivan-ramen-review

THE BEST RAMEN AND FRIED CHICKEN. 

I've heard about Ivan for years but finally made reservations. I got the Japanese fried chicken for an appetizer and it was perfectly juicy with a light and crunchy batter. I couldn't stop eating them and almost ordered another portion to take to go lol! It came with a garlic aoili mixed with herbs and the balance between the two made it one of the best things I've eaten. 

For ramen, I got the pork ramen and the broth had a depth of flavor that was unmatched. The umami and creaminess of the broth mixed with all of the toppings made me eat every last drop. 

DO NOT SKIP THIS PLACE!

It was a rainy day and I was feeling under the weather and what better way to feel better than eating a bowl of hot ramen. I decided to try out Ivan's ramen since it's very popular. I walked inside and the restaurant is very narrow and service was friendly and they also have outdoor seating. I tried the fried chicken and it was very soggy but flavorful. The ramen I chose was tonkotsu pork base broth with eggs. It was overly salty but the broth was milky and creamy like the other ramen spots. The noodles did have a good texture and was bouncy. It was around $20. Portions were good and kept me feeling full for a few hours. Not crazy about the eggs. It wasn't creamy on the inside. It was over cooked.
The best Ramen I have ever eaten. Comes out quick. Everyone who works there are very nice. I eat here 1-2 times a week and will continue to do so.

Normally my go to ramen is Ippudo or Momofuku but lately my top spot is Ivan Ramen. The dishes are very good, even if you get delivery. Flavor is plentiful and you will not be disappointed with portion size. If you have not tried, I highly suggest that you do.

I got the tokyo shio. 

This is a super dashi forward ramen and the first thing I smelled when they put it down was the familiar dashi smell. However, the broth is more concentrated and opaque than I expected. It is very salty and features a layer of chicken fat on top which coats the palette. The pork here is very tender and has great fall apart texture. The egg is less seasoned than most ramen eggs, but with the intense saltiness of the broth, it's probably just as seasoned as it needs to be. The roasted tomato is a unique topping and definitely a good pairing with the broth. The sweet, juicy bite of tomato mingled with the salty fish soup in a really interesting way. The noodles here are unique as well; they have a strong rye flavor. They were maybe a bit over cooked for my taste.

A unique, less traditional bowl of ramen with some interesting additions. The flavors all make sense together and pair really cohesively. It probably shouldn't be the first bowl of ramen you ever try, but this place is definitely worth a visit for ramen fans. The service is great and I like the chopsticks they have with textured tips to help grip the noodles.

So good! Walked into this place around 7:30 on a Monday night and luckily was able to snag two seats at one of their counters. It's very popular and I recommend making a reservation (even for a Monday!). I had the Ivan Palmer to drink, homemade yuzu lemonade mixed with iced barley tea. It was so refreshing. We tried the crispy eggplant appetizer - highly recommend it. It's served with a tahini-like sauce. The eggplant is perfectly fried in a crispy and flavorful, light batter. It's topped with chopped scallions. As an entree, I had the pork mazumen. The waiter said it was his personal favorite on the menu and I totally understand why. It is served in a brothy sauce rather than in actual soup broth. Delicious, chewy noodles with melt-in-your-mouth pork and tons of garlic. Highly recommend. This place was great.

Chef Ivan was nice enough to meet with us in person to thank us for our patronage. Very impressed by level of hospitality from all wait staff. Fried green tomatoes and shrimp were the highlight for me!  Ramen was amazing. Eggplant app and cauliflour apps were dope, id do eggplant over cauliflour.  Will 1000% return here during fall to enjoy the cozy atmosphere, quick service and quality eats.

Came here because I watch chef's table really excited to try the Ramen. Unfortunately the broth was the most salty I've ever had and the cauliflower side was extremely oily. Nothing special about this Ramen and probably would not come back.

I ate this for lunch on a Saturday afternoon with my girlfriend to celebrate her birthday. The servers were really attentive and great overall. We looked at the menu via QR code and ordered from the servers. We had the steamed pork buns, tofu Coney Island, Tonkotsu Ramen, and Chicken Paitan ramen. Food actually came out really quick to our surprise. The pork buns were kind of salty x the tofu Coney Island was crispy and good but also a bit on the salty side. Both ramens were rich and extravagant in broth. I would definitely get the ramen, but maybe because they cater to many tourists some of the food are a bit salty. However service was great and this restaurant is definitely a good place to grab some quick food.

Food was ok but the service was so poor, it deters us from ever coming back here. When I got there, I was told by the hostess I wouldn't be seated until my friend arrived. As I was waiting, I saw someone else walk in and be seated right in front of me even though his whole party wasn't there. When I mentioned it to the hostess, she said it was a mistake and sat me at my table. Bad attitude and rudeness all around. Food was not good enough to deal with this kind of service. Also cramped tables and outdoor seating looks really dingy. Wouldn't recommend.

They had a nice outdoor patio area, which was a great vibe for a dinner with a group of friends. I got the vegan shoyu but added a soft-boiled egg. This was one of the better ramen places I've been to in NYC, as they did not skimp on any ingredients.

Firstly, I would like to state that there is certainly a lot of thought behind the ingredients chosen. 

I am sure for some people, it's quite different and delicious.

My girlfriend and I ordered the Vegan Ramen, Spicy Ramen, Tofu Appetizer, and Cauliflower Appetizer

Tofu - thought it was interesting how yellow mustard was used. couldn't finish the dish.

Cauliflower - a little more appetizing to myself as I like ginger and fried vegetables. flavor mix still kind of odd for myself

Veggie Ramen - noodles used here are different than what I'm used to but broth and overall flavor were truly lacking any flavor other than salt. My gf's main source of protein is tofu and the fact that she thought the tofu was off definitely means something 

Overall it's not horrible and I'm sure there's people who enjoy a less traditional/umami approach to ramen but as someone who frequently eats ramen this was just ok. I may have had high expectations given all the reviews.
Even better than everyone says! Ivan is the king of ramen and we loved everything we ate. Best spot! Thank you Ivan. You are the man!

I went to this spot with a friend for lunch. We stopped at this location because it was one on our restaurant bucket list places. Upon entering the restaurant looks small but it is long and has outdoor seating in the front and the back. The staff inside was so friendly and helpful and willing to answer any questions that we had about the food. 
We ordered the Triple pork triple garlic mazemen ehich has a tender pork and a combination of wheat and rice noodles. It was a fun surprise to see mung beans which are my favorite in ramen. It was delicious especially with the sauce underneath. It was recommended to mix the noodles with the souce to get the full experience. The food had such an umami taste that i could still taste it after i had finished it. It was delicious. 
The second dish we got was the chicken paitan which was such an interesting dish. I have heard of ramens with a egg before but had never tried it before. What made it even more of an interesting dish was that it was recommended to mix the egg in and then do a squeeze of lime! I've never had lime in any ramen dish before which made it so interesting. Upon tasting it the broth was do good but with the lime it gave it such a nice acidic afterwards. I didn't think a squeeze of lime would make a big difference but it did!
The last item we tried was the steamed pork buns! I ways enjoy a good steamed bun and this one was especially good. Upon bitting it there was a sweet aftertaste and once we asked we were told it was a plum sauce! This was also such a good dish because I'm not much of a mushroom person but I had not known that this  bun had mushroom until after I had finished it!!! 
This place was so good I recommend for anyone to come by and if you don't know what to get to ask for any recommendations from the staff as they seem to really know a lot about their food.

This is my favorite local ramen spot!! My boyfriend and I come here whenever we are able to get a reservation. I've tried so many dishes of theirs over the dozen times I've been. Every single one has been incredibly flavorful. I really enjoy the options they have for their noodles as well, especially the gluten-free. The food comes out super fast, the staff is so friendly and helpful. 10 out of 10 every single visit.
Best Ramen I have ever eaten, love love love it!! Hands down, the best. Please come to Brooklyn!!!

Vegetarian option 
Soft serve yogurt

Icy soft serve

A bit Overrated. We were excited to visit this place after watching the Netflix special. The service wasn't great, our food took a long time, a table near us ordered the same stuff as us after we did, they got it before us. We ordered the Kyuri pickles which was good. The Chicken Paitan was very salty, after 3 sips of the broth, I couldn't eat it at all. My husband ordered the Tsukemen, that didn't have any salt at all. 
Finally within 10 mins of eating our food, we asked for takeout, never touched it later on. Very disappointed.

This is a delayed review: I came here in April and had reservations for 4. To be honest the ramen wasn't too memorable now that three months has passed, but that means that the noodles and soup were of good quality since bad noodles are the worst when you eat at a ramen joint!

THE BEST HOWEVER was the CRISPY EGGPLANT.
Oh my lord.
I smelled it from the bathroom. The texture is excellent. I would 1000% come back for this plus a beer on the regular.

Definitely worth a try!

Will preface with I visited in the mid afternoon when the restaurant was not crowded at all. Ordered the steamed pork buns and the Tokyo Shio bowl

Everything was freshly cooked to order and the ingredients were all delicious. Steamed pork buns had good flavor but the buns were a bit chewy and there wasn't a ton of fat on the pork to balance out the pickled vegetable on top, in addition to it being a bit salty for my taste. Would skip this app 

The ramen was the highlight. In contrast to the app, not too salty at all, and amazing flavors and broth. Noodles and eggs were cooked to perfection, and the sliced green onion was just enough to balance out the fat in the broth and the rolled pork belly. 20/10 - it's not a traditional ramen but it's delicious! Will come back for this, 100%

Wow this place is full of gems on the menu. I had the fried eggplant, curryflower, fried chicken, house made pickles and chicken paitain (ramen), all items were amazingly delicious and perfectly paired with suntory and a special Lime cilantro gose (beers). Our server Minori was incredibly informative and so sweet. Had a blast and would totally return 10/10.

New York City has no shortage of amazing ramen restaurants, and Ivan Ramen is no exception. Every dish is absolutely gorgeous, and the flavors definitely live up to the Instagram-worthy presentation. For my plant-based friends, they have an absolutely amazing vegan shoyu ramen, or you can always go for one of their vegetarian starters. 

I'm, personally, a huge fan of crispy eggplant, which has a delightful breadcrumb layer that is fried to golden perfection and offers the best contrast against the soft, succulent eggplant. This goes beautifully with the rich, nutty sesame paste and the smoky, fragrant charred garlic. If you're a fan of eggplant, I definitely recommend giving this dish a shot...and, honestly, I'd still give it a try if you aren't a huge fan of eggplant -- this dish might be the one to convert you! 

They also have a lovely yuzu cheesecake with a burnt top; while the cake was rich and lovely, I didn't find it particularly special. The yuzu flavor wasn't particularly strong, and it honestly just tasted like a slightly lemon-y, vanilla-y New York slice. The burnt topping was a nice contrast, but I think that there was a bit too much of it for my taste. All in all, though, I loved my experience at Ivan Ramen. The service was phenomenal, the prices were reasonable, and the outdoor patio was wonderful. I can't wait to visit again!

Found this place on tik tok and it looked good on videos, but it wasn't that amazing when we got there the service was amazing and the food was good - but I wouldn't go out of way to go back here again. I got the vegetarian ramen and felt like it lacked spice and flavor but the chicken bits were good.
Wonderful service!! Food is also excellent and flavor combinations are worth the visit.

So this is the second time I came here. Found out about this because the Chef here was featured on a Netflix show. Hands down one of the best ramen places I have been too. I ordered the Tokyo Shio Ramen which is a stable chicken based broth dish. There was a also a special on the menu that is a must try if you like mala (if you know you know) spiciness. I just kept thinking about how netflix interpreted the Chefs love of ramen and I really did feel that from the menu.
A simple place with good ramen. The rest of the food is not nearly as good, at least everything we tried. So, just get the ramen and you're good.

Came here on 8/28/22 by myself for lunch and got the spicy pickled cucumber appetizer and the "Triple Pork Triple Garlic" mazemen. The appetizer and mazemen came out to $34 after tax and tip - a touch expensive, but I suppose Chef Ivan has the credentials and fame to back it up, and you gotta try it for yourself to see what it's like, right?

I came right at open and was seated at a counter. This place is FANTASTIC to come to alone - lots of small tables and the counter as solo spaces (of course, it'd be fine in a group too - maybe would struggle in a 6+ but when I went the restaurant was fairly empty and I think they could have accommodated that too, plus what NYC spot comfortable fits 6?). Service was awesome too, I had my water and menu instructions (really great digital menu experience with videos and pictures!) immediately.

The pickles were awesome - maybe a little expensive ($6) for the size, but it was the right size for a solo diner so I was happy with them. Not too salty, not too liquid-y, not too vinegar-y. For the noodles, I came in with the intention of trying a classic ramen, but there's so many options that I've never seen elsewhere in the US, I had to try one... ended up picking mazemen, which is ramen noodles but with a sauce instead of broth, I got instructions to mix it all up after I got my bowl. Admittedly, having no other comparison for mazemen, I only have my own senses to judge it by, but I thought that the sauce was a bit salty - not to the point that it was inedible by any means - and the char siu and egg were cold, which was a lot more unnerving. I'm sure those two ingredients are mass prepared since they're used in multiple dishes, but I found the temperature differential really extreme and felt like it couldn't possibly be intentional seeing as I had one of the first bowls served that day.

Big points for providing some unique options, and I'm willing to chalk the temperature situation up as an honest mistake. I'd come back for sure and try something else, luckily there's no shortage of new choices!
This is my favorite ramen spot in New York City. It has some really great noodle options and appetizers worth trying. I also appreciate their great beer selection! Pairs perfectly with umami ramen.
Tonkotsu Ramen   Best ramen these taste  buds have ever tasted. I'm a picky eater and this place is definitely worth visiting again and again.

Heard good things, but honestly wasn't impressed by the food. We ordered the curry cauliflower and the tonkotsu ramen. The cauliflower was ok, but overwhelmed by some red things on top - wish there was more cauliflower. The tonkotsu I understand is supposed to be non-traditional, but I wish the broth was more flavorful, and overall it fell a little flat for me.

This ramen spot smelled good from outside!
The menu shows videos of how each item is made and what it looks like finished, which is a pretty cool touch. 

I went with my friend and we got the tonkatsu ramen, Japanese fried chicken, and drinks (I had a glass of sake and he had a beer).

The Japanese fried chicken was excellent. It's listed as an appetizer but it's a pretty big portion. Very flavorful and comes with a sauce that is perfect. 

The tonkatsu ramen was pretty good-- the noodles were a little different than most ramen noodles I've had and it was a bit saltier. The pork belly was fall apart tender. The Woodward mushrooms were sweet, which was an interesting (but very tasty) change up. 

Drinks here are small, just a heads up. If you order a specialty beer it's like a typical wine pour. The sake was delicious and smooth.

Service was very friendly up front, but the server that we had seemed very rushed.

I came here on Monday for my birthday brunch this past week. We came with a group of 7 and were seated in the backyard patio. We made a reservation ahead of time and I'm glad we did because the place filled up even on a Monday afternoon. 

We came here on a suggestion of my friend who saw this place from Chef's Table and from strong recommendations from other friends.

Here is what we ordered:
For the table
- Crispy Eggplant
- Coney Island Tofu
- Pork Buns
- Spicy Kyuri Pickles
- XO Daikon
Myself
- Tokyo Shio

All the appetizers were really savory and delicious. I must admit I did not have high expectations but they well exceeded what I'd expected. The Crispy Eggplant had such a good crisp and the spices to it meshed so well. The Coney Island Tofu was soft but packed a good punch. I was surprised at how good the XO Daikon was. XO sauce usually gives a strong savory front, and it worked well with the daikon neutral flavoring. Pork Buns and the Spicy Pickles were both very tasty. I must say this was quite a lineup of good tasting appetizers. I got the Tokyo Shio which is their signature dish. The broth and noodle were on point and not too salty. The roasted tomato they add in gives it that well placed umami taste in every bite. My friends who got their Chicken paitan really enjoyed it as well. 

Our service was attentive and on point. Our server Zack was knowledgable and courteous. He gave us a thorough rundown of the differences between the different types of ramen, which I am sure is a common query. Definite big props to him for making our experience that much better! 

In summary: great food and service; I would be returning here!

Made a reservation for early dinner on a Sunday and given sidewalk tables, which I was fine with, but was not told there was a time limit. when we got there, we were told we had 1 hour and 15 minutes max. the wait staff then proceeded to rush us the entire meal. The food was good, not great. Overall, a disappointing experience.

Very tasty food; atmosphere - okay; overall I enjoyed my dinner but think that this place is overrated. 

If you ask me, it's hard to mess up ramen. By default - it's delicious, and sure, I greatly enjoyed my bowl of Chicken Paitan, but did it blow my mind? No. I also found the ramen portion a little smaller than I'm used to - not necessarily a bad thing, but FYI.

Was also unimpressed by the appetizers: Japanese Fried Chicken, Tobanjan Green Beans, Spicy Kyuri Pickles. 

So why 4 stars for what reads like such an underwhelming experience? Well, if you're looking for a yummy meal in the area - definitely go, you'll have some good food. BUT if you are on a mission to find NYC's best ramen - don't go out of your way to eat at Ivan's: I think there are plenty of similar or better options throughout the city.

Tip: definitely make a reservation and get a table in the room in the back if you can. And for those who prefer outdoor seating - that option is available as well!

Greatest ramen dish (get the chicken paitan, egg plant, and Katy's curry!) but the service is what really contributed to the 5 stars. Diana is the nicest/most helpful server I have ever had in NYC. So fortunate to have her serve us tonight. Will be coming again!!

So I went to this lovely location about a week ago and was greatly by the owner of this establishment. I was greeted with the outmost professionalism and had an amazing waitress. She was very informative and I asked her opinion about what type of ramen I would love she suggested this one and I was truly happy with her choice. The only thing I was upset was my lunch wasn't longer because I definitely would like to try their desserts but I highly recommend this place and I will be back to enjoy some more food. The pork buns and ramen AMAZING good food good service and I will be back.

As being Japanese who was raised and grew up with Ramen culture, I am very particular with ramen noodles.

But honestly I enjoyed food here. I loved the appetizer, the fried cauliflowers a lot. Very crunchy and tasty.

Tonkotsu was good as well. The soup was bit thick and salty for me though, the noodles hardness and the temperature of the soup were right. I really enjoyed them.


The server was very nice as well. I would come back!

Second time going to Ivan! We are from Cleveland and made sure to visit twice! The ramen was probably my favorite meal in NYC the entire weekend. The fried eggplant is almost better than the ramen! Love Ivan!

The service here is impeccable the perfect combination of friendly and professional - the kind of people you both want to eat dinner with and trust with a recommendation. If the service wasn't enough to come back, the food will make your taste buds dance. If you can get your hands on the house made chili oil sauce you're in for a good time. The ambience is fun and quirky, adding to the appeal of the restaurant.
Totally lives up to the "Chef's Table" hype. It is by far the best ramen I have ever had!

GO TO IVAN RAMEN! We just had a fabulous meal with wonderful service and really friendly staff. Ramen was just so good and the appetizers were incredible. It surpassed my expectations. Go to Ivan's; you will not be disappointed.
This is the best ramen I've ever had! Everything is perfect from the rich broth to the soft boiled egg.

I was super disappointed by Ivan Ramen. I have had a lot of people recommend it but it really fell flat for me. I got the vegetarian ramen and felt like the broth was just soy sauce. The tofu also had a really bizarre taste and was nearly inedible. My friend had the Chicken Paitan and said that my ramen tasted better than his so I can only imagine what the one was like. My last friend had the Tonkotsu and she said it was good but nothing compared to Tonchin or Ippudo. Overall I would definitely save 2 hours and $20 and just go somewhere else.
This was the first ramen "restaurant " that I ever tried. It started a love of ramen that has carried forward.

Horrendous service! They didn't put the main component in my order and then when I asked for a solution the employee was very rude. I asked her if I was just supposed to have broth for lunch which she stated "yes". I then spoke to the manager who was also dismissive. I can understand mistakes happening I also work in the service industry but to completely dismiss someone was incredibly wrong. Would not recommend.

Ivan Ramen, we'll done you guys are doing it right in the lower Eastside. I have never experienced anything as good as what me and my wife shared. I could have eaten way more than I did, keep up the great work

Came in with a ramen craving and this place was not it. The service was nice and refilled out drinks frequently.
My friends and I ordered the tonkotsu ramen and the second we tasted the broth, we were extremely disappointed. There was so much pepper that it kicked the back of our throats on every slurp and the broth was extremely salty. The only thing we liked was the pork and egg but that's it. Another thing was the extremely small portion size for $19-20? If you're looking for an authentic bowl of ramen I wouldn't recommend this place.

Had great ramen here (and also spotted some celebrities!). We shared the cripsy eggplant appetizer on recommendation from other Yelp reviews and you really can't miss it! The food came out quickly. I had the chicken paitan ramen and loved the touch of crispy chicken skin. The food was solid and our server was incredibly friendly and happy to offer her suggestions.

Was pretty excited to try this Tsukemen and was pretty disappointed. The dipping broth was VERY thin almost like an au jous which is sad cause I saw an amazing video of the thickest broth I thought they had. Noodles were also kinda just ok, had a soba noodle feel to them but thicker. Meat was really good just kinda heavy for an already heavy Tsukemen. Brussels sprouts were probably the highlight of the meal. Probably wouldn't go back

my friend wanted to stop by for a quick eats, i was a bit worried bc we didn't have a reservation and of the popularity, despite that the hostess was super nice and squeezed us in !! the food came out super fast and the waitress was super friendly and extremely attentive. we sat at the back with the nice heaters, super nice bc it's been pretty cold in NYC, the food was great and not too expensive, i scarfed down the noodles so fast because i came out of work lol but so delicious ! :) also the punk lemonade draught beer is also a must try hehe

I mean - come on! This place certainly lives up to its reputation. You've probably watched the Chef's Table episode on Netflix about Ivan Ramen. The chef behind this restaurant really immersed himself in Japanese culture and now is known for amazing ramen that he has made both in Japan and in the US. The chicken paitan is full of flavor with an amazing rich developed broth. Best broth I have had in awhile. The tomato umami bombs are honestly brilliant. The noodles have a great bite. I love that a bowl of ramen comes with most of the staple toppings already. The vibe of the restaurant is modern, urban, and fun - not to mention - we had great service. But the main draw of this restaurant is that this ramen has soul, and I'm here for it!

Simply Amazing!  The staff was welcoming and warm the place feels casual and laid back while serving what is a culinary delight of epic proportions!
We started with the curry cauliflower appetizer.  It was one of the most interesting ways I have ever had cauliflower prepared.  Every bite was an adventure there was so much going on.  Solid crunch, acidity and sweetness and lots of umami all coming together highly recommend!
For the mains we had the Tokutso Ramen as well as the Triple Pork Triple Garlic.
The Triple Pork Triple Garlic was so rich and creamy and had really nice chew of what was the thicker version of noodles.
The Tokutso Ramen also was nicely executed.  The pork belly was extremely tender and flavorful in both dishes!
This place also maintains what is one of the most amazing and unique beer selections I have ever seen!  If you are into various very special, rare craft beers from all over the world this is your place!
I can not recommend this place enough it did not disappoint despite somewhat elevated expectations after seeing Chef Ivan on Chef's Table.
One of the best ramens I've had so far. Rivals Ichiran--maybe better. Food also came out really fast. Would highly recommend if in the area.

When you step into Ivan Ramen, you're transported into a new continent full of fun and exciting flavors. 

Comic-lined walls and invite you into a cozy, quick-to-serve slurp shop, where, spoiler alert, the best thing on the menu isn't the ramen but the fried chicken. 

Service is quick as staff tries to keep up with the demand Netflix created with their hit show Chef's Table. 

If I were more of a ramen fan, I might give this 5 stars, but my ceiling for ramen just isn't high enough!

We had a lovely dinner at Ivan Ramen yesterday. The bartender (brunette with bleached eyebrows) at the counter was a delight, she gave us recommendations and provided great service. 

We ordered:
* Crispy Eggplant ($13)
* Yuzu Lemonade ($4)
* Ivan Palmer ($4)
* Tonkotsu Ramen ($19)
* Tokyo Shio Ramen (18)

We spent a total of $63.16 - a little pricy but the food was delicious. The fried eggplants had a delicate crispy breading on the outside and had a silk like consistency on the inside. The drinks were tart and refreshing -- some might say they're not sweet at all compared to traditional lemonade and Arnold Palmers. The unsweetened barley tea is very prominent in the Ivan Palmer even when you mix it together but it was very good. It was a nice palate cleanser to cut through the richness of the ramen. 

I LOVED the broth of the Tonkotsu ramen. It is jam packed flavorful with tender pork and bits of mushroom. Tokyo Shio ramen had a very deep yet "clean" tasting broth. The tomato was a nice umami bomb which is an unusual topping but totally worked. Both bowls didn't look like a lot of food but we left feeling stuffed. The only thing we weren't too crazy about was their noodles. They were a bit lackluster and wished they were wavier for texture. Also they only have one dessert on their menu which is their Yuzu Cheesecake. But overall we had satisfying dinner.

Argh, almost 5 stars for the savory umami broth and quick service. Fun vibes with the waitstaff both taking their jobs seriously and not taking themselves too seriously while selecting different Christmas songs and dancing along. The wall art was unique resembling graffiti/comic book art. We sat at the bar and had a direct view of where the magic happens.

Would recommend getting a beer to go with your ramen. We got the tonkatsu (garlic, umami, rich) and chicken paitan (Ivan's favorite, clean, homey) ramen. Definitely hit the spot given the paucity of thoughtfully created ramen dishes in our area (please feel free to prove me wrong).

Came here on a Friday night and the interior was really chic, especially for being in an outdoors area. I really liked the broth and the texture of the noodles. 

Service was good. The ramen was great but didn't blow me away.

Is this RAMEN....? I don't know... it's a copy of a copy of a copy of a copy for sure tho. I love how traditions gets destroyed to the point you see a new thing but oh boy.... Very plane depth of taste, it is almost... bland. It's like Umami what's that? Their ramen tries too hard to be new and different, I don't think any essence of ramen exists. That's the choice of dashi, noodle's koshi, and the quality of umami. Noodle quality is... okay. You don't expect any Koshi from these noods tho. It's like fancy version of Ramen that has lost its grace. There's so much of something that is missing I am not sure what is missing but maybe they've lost something while trying to reinvent something... . Otherwise great store design and ambiance. Service is standard, like a normal restaurant with service. But true ramen place has bad service that's the tradition lol jk but for real. All in all, if you're Japanese, I can't recommend this one. You will be heart broken. I did go with another Japanese n his review is harsher than mine. I think Ivan Ramen is just a creative store that serves something that tries to be unique.

Amazing apps... fried cauliflower, fried chicken, pork buns and roasted Brussel sprouts; excellent ramen; very good service; tables in back "tent" are the best (spacious and it noisy); very good service

Great ramen
Great service
Sake was solid
Nice table
Good flavors
Easy to enjoy with a group
The chicken appetizer was awesome 
Pork buns rock

I would say this place is similar to Toto Ramen in midtown. Ivan is decent but it doesn't come close to Ippudo. We ordered the steamed pork buns, brussel sprouts, chicken paitan, and tonkotsu ramen. It was good, super quick (like most ramen spots) but the broth for both ramens was not as flavorful or didn't have as much depth as Ippudo. 

If you don't want to wait for Ippudo and you're downtown and you can snag a reservation at Ivan, it's a decent alternative.

Ivan is a decent Ramen place but what helps it greatly is how friendly and welcoming the entire staff is. I'm not influenced by Netflix so the ramen options were not mind blowing but still very good. The atmosphere is one of casual and nothing exceptionally ground breaking. Expect a good Ramen and great service, recommend if you're down in this area.

we (my Dad, brother, and I) arrived to find they had reservations indoors but none outdoors. we happily sat outside but it rained lightly. In an act of kindness, our server Kiss hooked us up and they seated us inside immediately. Shouts out to Kiss and Ivan Ramen.

We saw this restaurant featured on Netflix's Chef's Table and put it on our list for a future New York trip. It did not disappoint! The pork buns were incredible, the curry flower was so unique and yummy, and both Ramens were delicious. Our waitress was very attentive and engaged and kind. It was worth the wait. Can't wait to come back!

There's 2 places I frequent in NYC. Ivan Ramen happens to be one of them. I typically eat here for a pre race meal before running the NYC Marathon or NYC Half. This time around I decided to just go for the heck of it. I love the idea of a little hole in the wall ramen shop. It's very reminiscent of my short short time in Tokyo. I like the idea that everything is made in house. The flavors of cold sesame noodle dish, I can close my eyes and still taste it. I learned how to make these noodles however nothing will ever compare. The ramen was well balanced and not overly salty. The pork buns were just so so but still 5 stars to me.

I've always been satisfied with my experience at Ivan Ramen. The Pork Buns have great flavor and melt in your mouth. I always get the Chicken Paitan, and I find it to be delicious. Great spot to go on a cool/cold day! Only thing is they fill up quickly. I advise making a reservation ahead of time.

The only thing that can be annoying is their online ordering service sometimes shuts off during peak hours. Which I understand if they want to service the restaurant primarily over online orders, but I wish it was more clear on the website.
Incredible on all fronts! Good food, lovely service, and quaint but fun ambiance. Looking forward to the next visit!

One of my new favorite spots. The Chicken Paitan was truly one of the best things I've eaten, and the Tokyo Shyo was really excellent as well. One of the best things there was the service, though. We sat at the bar, and the bartender/server was incredibly friendly, and informative with helping us pick the items that matched our style. He also was kind enough to let us taste various sakes, and was overall a blast to have as part of our experience.

Will for sure be back!

I traveled all the way to New York just to try Ivan's ramen, and I was not disappointed. The noodles were incredible, and the broth was even more so. I had the pork belly buns, which were fantastic! I wish Florida had a ramen business as good as this one. If you ever visit New York, this is a must-visit.

My fiancé and I came to try out Ivan Ramen by recommendation of my sister during our recent visit to New York.  

First let's start with how awesome and hip the interior was. I loved the wall pattern covered in what looked like images that were classic to Japanese pop culture. So cool!

Now the food: On first bite, wow we were speechless.  The egg plant and chicken karate appetizers were so bomb. The ramen, wow. And the yuzu cheesecake, chef's kiss!!!  This was the best ramen that we had on our trip, and we went to four places total. Just written this review is making my mouth water lol!

Lastly, the service was amazing. Our waitress was so attentive and friendly!! 

I definitely plan to go back the next time we visit NYC! Thank you Ivan Ramen for a memorable dining experience!!
Great food and "Kiss" our server was awesome!!! We ordered the triple pork triple garlic Mazaman, Chicken Paiten, and Tokuo Shoyu Ramen.
Food was amazing. Diane was great. The experience is one of the best in NYC. I go here everytime I visit the city.

There's a lot of hype around Ivan, and if you compare it to Gorin, Ippudo, or Miso Ramen, this leaves a lot to be desired.  The buckwheat noodles are way too overpowering against the soup. This basic problem moots the bowl itself.

The pork buns are spectacular though...

This was a one of a kind experience. The staff was friendly and knowledgeable, very happy to navigate the guest through the menu. The service was prompt and well executed. The food...omg, the FOOD! We started with the cold sesame noodles which were way beyond our expectations. We then ordered ramen, which our waitress patiently explained the different options. It was so off the charts good. Highly, highly recommend! We will be back!

Having seen chefs table, had to try out Ivan's ramen. You could look at it through different lens if you compare it to ramen there's definitely betters ones in the area based on noodle texture, meat flavor and temperature of soup. If you see it as a noodle shop it's somewhat special and unique but the only downside was the broth was not hot enough, but great vibes. Call to make a res!

Easy weeknight reservation. Good place for a comforting meal after work. I came with my partner but the bar tables make it solo dining friendly. There's an outdoor dining area that would be great for warm days. The inside looks a lot like an elevated diner with fun murals covering the walls. I loved how our server started with recommendations and popular dishes. We took her advice and ordered the Chicken Paitan, Tonkotsu Ramen and Crispy Eggplant. They were all some of the best food we've had. You can ask for chili oil if you'd like added spice. Portion is generous and filling. Had to try the yuzu cheesecake. On the surface it looks pretty ordinary- no toppings. But it is a rich and solid slice of a classic desert with an understated taste of citrus.

I came here after seeing the Chef's Table episode about Ivan, the restaurant's founder. He has a really interesting story, and his restaurant makes really delicious food. Unfortunately, he wasn't in the kitchen on the day I went. 

I had a reservation for 1pm on a Sunday, but arrived early. They were able to seat me where I wanted on the counter, even though the restaurant was quite busy. And it was busy for a good reason. 

The ambience is Japanese-style comic book (not Manga, the western-style comic book). It's a fun and unpretentious vibe, but with a lot of thought behind the decor, and the flatware/silverware. 

I started my meal with the Kyuri (cucumber pickles). They were well-made, but beware, they're quite spicy. Consider yourself warned. 

My friend had the pork buns. He really liked them, but s not as good at describing food as I am. The buns were not spicy, but he said one of the garnishes inside it was. He did not consider the dish itself to be spicy, and he said he thought it tasted really good. 

The crispy eggplant was incredible - probably my favorite dish of the meal. The coating on the eggplant was crispy, but the eggplant itself was tender - perfectly cooked. It came on top of a delicious sesame sauce. It felt reminiscent of the Japanese "goma nasubi" dish, but with a New York twist. I loved the dish and would order it again. That said, (suggestion based on personal preference - not a criticism) it would be cool if the sauce came inside the eggplant instead of underneath. Cutting the eggplant would let it cool down faster, and the sauce being on the inside would make eating it a different experience. 

The ramen itself is not your traditional Japanese ramen - but I really enjoyed it nonetheless. The chef mixes rye flour into the noodles, giving it an interesting texture. The noodles come firm at first, but soften up as they sit in the broth. They don't feel particularly springy, but are still a delight to eat. The broth itself was probably the best ramen broth I have tasted in my life - the umami was strong, but the broth did not leave you dying of thirst after having it. I also really appreciated the grilled tomato - it was something different - it tasted almost Italian. 

It's apparent that although this restaurant is a ramen spot, and celebrates the 20 years Ivan spent living in Japan, the restaurant does not purport to be 100% traditionally Japanese. Instead, while being firmly rooted in proper Japanese cuisine, I appreciate how each dish also brings in an element of Ivan's New York heritage. For example, while the Kyuri is a traditional Japanese appetizer, the pickles were more akin to NY deli pickles, and while the ramen looks traditional to the ye, the noodles contain rye flour - a testament to Ivan's background (I learned the rye part from the Chef's table episode). 

The food is delicious, and each dish tells a story. It's creative and delicious, and I plan on coming back. 

I docked a star because although the service was good, it did feel a bit rushed at times. That said, the restaurant was quite busy on the day I went.

There were some parts of this restaurant that I loved and other parts that were okay. This place isn't bad at all, but I wouldn't put it at my top recommendations for ramen in NYC.  If you do like ramen that packs a punch, then I think this place would be good for you. 

My loves for the restaurant:
- Great service and attentive staff. They explain the menu very well and provide excellent recommendations based on your preferences. They don't hover too much and they're there when you need them 
- The buckwheat noodle style. I preferred this with the punchy flavors of the ramen because it's not as thick and heavy as the other noodle styles 

The part that left me hanging might just have been the broth itself. Does it taste different from other restaurants? Absolutely. But, it just felt like too much for me. It's a very stimulating experience, so if you're wanting a homier style of ramen, I would try another place.

Packed on a nice Sat at 1 but what do you expect?  Friendly services fair prices (i mean there are no bargains anymore) hip crowd and music.  The ramen was solid if not spectacular (a bit salty).  The crispy eggplant app is worth the trip downtown alone.

Ivan Ramen's QR code menu was SUPER pretentious, all but forcing you to watch a video on each dish's origins before it gave you any information on, I don't know, what was in it. This level of self-importance would have been easily forgiven if the bowl had been great, but it was barely edible, and the reason why is...

... salt. I don't know what happened in the kitchen that day, whether this was an aberration, or whether every Ivan-celebrator just reallllly likes salt. But I reallllly like salt most of the time, and it was about a thousand times too much for me. When they pickled the mustard greens and the wood ear mushrooms, is it possible they just poured the pickling water into my soup? It was medicinally salty, chemically so. I could smell it when they put the bowl down - I picked the bowl up to sniff it curiously before I even lifted a spoon to my mouth.

If ratings were an average of how well each ingredient was prepared, Ivan would have done okay, actually. The pork was a perfect melt-in-your-mouth ring, the noodles firm and chewy, the egg delightfully orange and runny. But none of those things mattered because they all sat in the Great Salt Lake of Ramen.

SOOOOOO delicious. 10/10, highly recommend. I went on a Friday night without a reservation and got in right away. Had the chicken ramen and it was absolutely amazing. The fried eggplant was to die for as well. Will be back!

The savory umami broth was absolutely delicious and paired perfectly with the chicken paitan. The waitstaff were professional and attentive. The place was small and packed but that added to the atmosphere.  The chicken paitan was absolutely delicious. Would recommend if you are in the neighborhood and are craving ramen.

Very hip decor and music made
it fun. Service was great, answered all our questions, had pickles, cauliflower and fried chicken appetizers, ramen and some drinks.

Love the story behind this place, watch the Chef's Table episode! Not your traditional ramen place, if you're looking for the classics this isn't it. Was able to book a resy a few days out. 

Nomz: Shared a couple of starters before having a bowl of ramen. 
Lemon Brussels sprouts: really tasty in terms of flavor, felt healthy, unlike most of the times I order it at restaurants 
Japanese fried chicken: came out a bit cold, a little sticky but good flavor, probably wouldn't order again 
Steamed pork buns: my favorite starter, delicious and flavorful
Tokyo Shio Ramen: I'm a tonkotsu girl at heart but tried something different this time. For me lacked flavor, the tomato bites made it better but I only had one piece so couldn't make it last for the entire bowl. I did try the tonkotsu from someone's bowl, a lot lighter in flavor and density than your average, not for me. 

Drinks: Had two sakes bottles, didn't have much price spectrum, on the more expensive side. Unfiltered was my fav, on the sweeter side of sake but not overly sweet generally speaking. 

Service: Waitress was prompt and helpful.

Ambiance: Small/cozy long setup of the place, hip art and outdoor back area. 

Nope or Dope: Nope, the pork buns were winners in my book but the ramen should be stealing the show and it didn't for me.

Ok this place for some reason gets a very hard shake that it doesn't deserve. 3.5 stars????!! What are we doing here Yelp family. This is a five star establishment. The ramen isn't super traditional but it is super delicious. I love the tonkotsu ramen. The apps are also money specifically pork buns and fried chicken. They have a great beer menu, wonderful sake selection, and lots of other good looking drinks. The vibe inside is really cool, lots of playful comics above the bar that I love. Also there is solid outdoor seating in the garden. My one qualm is that the service is a bit too fast. I like a well timed service that gives you ample time for apps, chit chat, and dinner. They rushed through everything a bit too quickly for my liking.

I got the Chicken Paitan and it was just delicious. Loved the entire thing. Perfect texture for the ramen for me. We also got the steamed pork buns which were fantastic. Also special callout to their menu which had videos for every item which was super cool. Loved the entire experience.

Likes
- great s service 
- good appetizers
- close to citibike

Dislike
- vegetarian ramen broth 
 Just salty bitter soy sauce. Boring !!!!
Attentive staff. Great ramen, would definitely recommend. Good use of surprising ingredients that make it unique and tasty.

Came here for lunch, no reservation, was seated immediately. Host was very kind although I did not get her name, we decided to get the Japanese fried chicken , crispy Eggplant, and the Chicken Paitan ramen. 

Crispy Eggplant: really enjoyed this! Texture was on point, very crispy on the outside, inside was nice and soft. It comes plated on a sesame sauce, which paired nicely. Overall a pretty mild flavored dish, but done well.

Japanese fried chicken: unfortunately I didn't like this as much as I was expecting to. Unlike a traditional Karaage, it has a wet garlic caramel sauce on it and comes w a shisho ranch sauce on the side. We ended up sending this dish back because it was too acidic for us, I felt the wet sauce took away from it. They very kindly comped it off our bill which was greatly appreciated. That being said the shisho ranch sauce was really good! Just wish I liked the actual chicken more. 

Chicken Paitan Ramen: enjoyed this! Comes w a soft egg yolk on top that you mix into the broth and ground chicken. Pretty light but flavorful, pretty heavy on the black pepper so if you don't like that, I'd get another dish, but I enjoyed the peppery flavor. Noodles were thin and cooked well.

Also want to note service was very good and fast here! Shoutout to our server Aimee, she was very kind and helpful. Ambience was nice as well.

Absolutely fantastic ramen meal.  Our 17 year old son actually handed an additional $20 tip (from his own money) to our server, telling her how fantastic the meal was.  He's never done something like that previously.

Get on Netflix and check out the episode on Ivan Ramen on 'Chefs Table' (believe it was season 3).  It will make you appreciate the meal that much more.

We all loved this meal so much.

Amazing food. I got shio ramen. It had great taste and good texture and temperature. I ate it so fast I couldn't believe it. The service was amazing and I appreciated it. The people serving us were enthusiastic and kind. The place has good background music that isn't too loud or annoying. Overall, I loved eating here and would love to visit again!

To be fair, I didn't eat ramen here, so I definitely need to return and update my review based on that. 

Ivan Ramen is a really cute restaurant between LES and EV that serves ramen and a few appetizers. The menu is small, but everything I tasted was delicious. We started with the cauliflower appetizer, which included fried cauliflower, a delicious curry sauce, and shaved (maybe fried?) ginger on the top. Everything came together beautifully, and I thought the curry sauce was absolutely delicious. The cauliflower also did not get soggy throughout our meal and tasted as crisp as when it came out. I ordered some of the pickles, which were spicy and salty and delicious. My friend ordered the chicken ramen and added spicy sauce to it. It was definitely spicy, but the broth had a  really deep and tasty flavor. 

Overall, I really liked this place. The staff and service was amazing, and the food was stellar. Now to return and actually try the ramen!

Ivan had the best food, I actually liked the appetizers more than the ramen (but the ramen was still great). We ordered the special Pastrami Bao Buns, the fried chicken, and ramen. The food was amazing. 

I did feel a bit rushed by the staff, it was a busy night, so I understand, but I felt that I was being subtly directed to leave before I finished my drink.

Incredible, personable service. Jam and azza both had the time to chat and make an amazing tasty meal a great & enjoyable experience. We've had ramen all over the US and Japan and thoroughly enjoyed the food. Would definitely be a regular spot if we lived here but will absolutely be back next trip!!! Thanks you guys!!

After watching Chef's table my husband and I knew we needed to have one dinner from our vacation dedicated here. I hate to admit it - we were incredibly underwhelmed by the food. The service was attentive and very kind. The only thing worth noting was the fluffiness of the pork buns. We tried the fried chicken appetizer and it was covered in so much sauce we couldn't finish it and it was very salty. I ordered the Tonkotsu ramen and my husband ate the chicken Paitan - both tasted flat. I've had many types of Ramen, in Japan and many other places, this had absolutely no flavor. The vegetables inside seemed soggy and not fresh. If I could have a do-over, I would not go back here.
Holy hell. If you don't go, you missed some serious enjoyment of life. Just be sure to make reservations, and have some of the best treats in the country. Try everything.

Yo.  The hype is real! Excellent service, mouth watering ramen (OG chicken) but the kicker was the pastrami/sauerkraut steamed buns. WTF.  I had to hold onto the back of my head to keep it from blowing off.  Will be back, Ivan.  Love your story and love this food!
The workers are very cool and knowledgable on the menu. They also have the best ramen I ever ate. I recommend 10 out of 10!!

Every time I come here, the servers are always overly friendly and knowledgeable. The space is lively and casual, as it's pretty popular! The food comes out so fast, and you can get extra noodles as well :) I will say, sometime the ramen/noodles tend to be a bit salty.
With the hype this place gets I was super whatever on the quality of the dish. Not bad or anything, but definitely not amazing or memorable kind of ramen.

I enjoyed this place! The apps were out of this world - we started with the crispy eggplant and the curry flower which are a must try! Such a creative combo of flavors! For ramen I got chicken paitan which was different than any other ramen I've had. It was rich, flavorful and cozy. My friends had bao buns and said we're good. They're feedback to Ivan Ramen was that there are better places, I really liked it nevertheless. The service was really quick.
Great food. Amazing beer list. Great service.  This was well worth the trip and the space was clean and cozy.  Will be coming back
Lots of hype, but it wasn't too special. High prices for ramen that I found very mediocre at best. There's also constantly a line for the bathroom, which is terrible in such a small space.
Excellent vegan options, got the food really fast which was great, restroom for customers which is always needed in city. Would recommend to friends
This place has fantastic ramen , service was great , ambiance was fantastic. Make a reservation
This place has to one of my favorite places in Manhattan. The food, drinks, service and atmosphere are all amazing!! Go here when you're in the neighborhood. It's incredible.

If you find yourself in the LES craving ramen, head on over Ivan Ramen for a special treat. Although, don't be too spontaneous because you'll need an online reservation! 

I very much enjoyed the chicken paitan ramen. I added a soft boiled egg and bok choy to add to the fun! The crispy togarashi chicken skins added an extra something-something to the dish. I also enjoyed the Ivan Palmer - half-tea and half-yuzu lemonade. We also liked the yuzu cheesecake. 

Last, but not least; our server was attentive and lovely.

While having high expectations this place exceeded our expectations and served us amazing food with great flavor. Everything we tried was absolutely delicious and I strongly recommend this place to anyone in Manhattan. The service was amazing and food came really fast.
Probably my favorite Ramen spot. I love food that's outside of the box, and this one most definitely is. The whole menu is a winner to me. Great wall art here. Great people take of you here.

The ramen was so salty. I came here on a recommendation, but really I wouldn't come back again. Had me wanting to chug water after the meal. I'd recommend looking for other options unless you like your food pretty salty!

We had to sample Ivan's famous ramen after seeing him on Netflix's Chef's Table, and we're definitely glad we got to try it! Ivan incorporates rye into his noodles, and they are noticeably chewier than others I've had before. It gives a bit more of a "glutinous" feel to your bowl. 

We got the tonkotsu ramen, and the broth was rich, flavorful, and the other ingredients were super fresh. 

We shared the kyuri pickles - which seemed like northern chinese pickles with a spicy kick, the fried chicken, and the crispy eggplant. All 3 were a hit. The fried chicken was cooked well - wouldn't be surprised if it was twice fried, and had some spice to it. The crispy eggplant was in a bed of miso based sauce, and while very crispy, I was slightly disappointed that there still didn't seem to be much flavor unless you loaded them with sauce. This was a surprise because other reviewers loved the dish. The pickles were more of a bar food item - not something to fill you up, whereas the chicken was a fairly large portion.

While the ramen was great, we're on a mission to find new places to try and the food wasn't memorable enough to try twice. 

Overall,
Food 4.5/5
Ambiance 4/5
Service 4/5
We sat in the outdoor courtyard in the back, which was nice. Three craft beer portions were small and the ramen was decent. The appetizers were the best.

My friends and I enjoyed our ramen dinner after a looong day. After the reviews, I was a bit worried, but without reservations we were immediately seated (at the bar). I enjoyed the bar because we were given excellent service!  The bartender/server was really friendly. My boyfriend and I tried the shochu cocktails (grape or plum flavored). The grape one was tasty but the plum didn't have a strong taste. Both of them were pretty mild in terms of tasting the alcohol! 

For ramen, I ordered the Tokyo Shio which hit the spot. I enjoyed the signature roasted tomato. The dinner wasn't anything mind blowing, but it was an enjoyable experience with great service.

Very rich, depth broth flavor, definitely exceeded my expectations. I loved the chicken paitan the most as it was the least salty, the other broth were good but it is salty after a couple sips. I also enjoyed the crispy eggplant.

My friend and I decided to try Ivan Ramen after seeing that it was featured on Chef's Table and is also super close to her apartment. We didn't have any issues getting a reservation for dinner on a Thursday, but we thought the food was overhyped. 

Our favorite thing we ordered was the yuzu lemonade; very refreshing and not too sweet. I would definitely skip the Japanese fried chicken next time. I was expecting it to be more of a traditional karaage style fried chicken, but it didn't have much crisp to it as it was essentially drenched in a very strong soy glaze. The ramen was ok, maybe slightly above average, but nothing to write home about.

Service was very quick which was nice, but it didn't really make up for the mediocre food. The restaurant itself was kind of loud and dim but there was a cool wall with a bunch of pop art.

Overall, definitely overhyped

This place was recommended to me by a few friends. The vegetarian ramen here was pretty mediocre and was more expensive than I would have liked. It's hard to recommend this place over other ramen shops in the neighborhood.

Came here around 6PM on a Friday and it got pretty busy but never was completely full. It was rainy, humid, and hot so having cold noodles on the menu really made me happy since I was slightly dreading hot ramen. There were larger tables in the back and small parties at the front which was unfortunate since the air conditioning was running more in the back so I was slightly uncomfortably warm. I got the hiyashi chuka and it wasn't bad but the two shrimp was over cooked and the ham was way too salty. I also added bok choy ($3 extra) and it was literally 4 small pieces which was not worth it at all. I also tried the lemon-miso Brussel sprouts which were the highlight of my meal. They were crispy and refreshing. Overall I don't think off of my one dish this place was worth the price but maybe their warm ramen would've wine me over.

This place is a known quantity, so it's probably silly to add yet another review. But, I wanted to at least mention that while my most recent visit was delicious this place can be a little uneven. I think that may always be the case when the owner is, more or less, the reason a place exists; the restaurant will sort of ebb and flow with their influence and participation as the "energy source" of the place--as opposed to some restaurant group monolith that changes very little from season to season. Knowing that going in may be useful.

This place is smaaaalll (read: "cozy"), and I encourage a reservation regardless of the day or time. In the summer, you're going to be warm. It's LES, it's an old building, and AC can't always do miracles.

On our previous trip, I just did not care for what I ordered at all. On this trip, the wagyu brisket buns were delicious and sort of whimsical, like the Coney Island Tofu used to be. (Alas, RIP.) The ramen I ordered was equally tasty and essentially textbook perfection. I added nothing and nothing was needed. 

The servers here are really good, by the way. Our most recent was so pleasant, and ready to answer questions and make recommendations--but not in an obnoxious way. She kept the meal rolling along without making it feel hurried. I mention this because it's getting harder and harder to find this, even at places where it shouldn't be. 

You should go if you're in Manhattan, bearing in mind that it's a bit of an adventure. Part of the charm is the variances from visit to visit. It's as close as most of us will get to meeting Ivan Orkin himself.

I came here with my son who lives in the neighborhood. 
It's a minimalist lower east side ramen joint.

 We started with the crispy eggplant which was new to me. Very good. Crispy outside, moist inside. Great sauce.

I had the gound chicken ramen (it has a better name but I forgot it) and my son and the tonkonsu (pork).
The broth was very nice. The noodles were good. They were thin and dark like soba but did not taste like soba. The toppings were interesting. Ground chicken with a little crunch.
Prices are very reasonable. The server was very nice and helpful.
Verdict: minimalist, high quality, tasty.
Go for it.

Oh yeah, totally worth the 30 min train ride. My husband and I had this on our must try list when visiting. It lived up to our expectations. The seating was limited, glad we arrived early (around 5pm)and the place was packed within 20 minutes of our arrival. Everything came up quickly, which was great because we were hungry. Staff was accommodating and friendly. The flavors were so thoughtfully balanced and delicious.

Ivan ramen is an incredibly cool spot in the Lower East Side. They have a great front and back patio and the inside is very hip as well! The staff were super helpful in providing recommendations for our first time there and we were not disappointed.

We got the cold noodles and the chicken ramen and both were awesome. The chicken ramen almost tasted like thanksgiving dinner with an asian flare but was a 10/10. The cold noodles were super refreshing for a summer night but if you have a low spicy tolerance definitely asks!

Damn this place is so fire. I had heard this place was gas, and it definitely did not disappoint. Started with the Ebi Lemon Mayo, per our server's recommendation, and it was seriously so good. Lots of great spicy lemon flavor. For ramen, I went with the Spicy Red Chili and DAMN SO FIRE. Our server said it was a 7/10 on the spicy scale which was pretty accurate. Incredible flavor.

Service was 10/10 and the vibe was 11/10. I also think this would be a great solo dining spot. A bit pricy, but absolutely worth it.

Do not go here. I wanted to try this place out and I got a Tonkotsu Ramen. It was so salty I had the noodles only (I never send the food back bc you never know) and the girl (curly hair, was working at the bar making drinks too)  asked me if I wanted more noodles I told her it was super salty and she just smiled and walked away with the soup, came back and asked me if I wanted desert and I said no and she slapped the check on my table and walked away. She had the worst attitude. Of course never coming back here they don't care if you like the food or not just pay the bill and go kind of thing.
Amazing food and great service! This is one of the few restaurants which I visit frequently. Good place to chat with friends and I would recommend the Triple Pork Triple Garlic ramen!

Planned a day out based on hitting this place for lunch. Website, Yelp all listed open 12-9p. Called to make sure they'd be open before we took the subway, but was too early and they don't have an answering machine. Arrived a few minutes before opening and waited outside. While we stood outside, some moron hung this sign in the window and never bothered to speak to us like humans. Don't waste your time and don't believe the hype- clearly they do not care about their customers or reputation.

The staff was really nice and the sitting area was cute! Unfortunately the food was not that good. Both me and my friend didn't finish our bowls because they were kind of tasteless. Not vibrant flavors.

A favorite once in Japan and now seated in the East Village, Ivan Ramen is the spot for authentic ramen. I have visited twice now and was impressed both times with the food, service, and overall vibe of the restaurant. 

I have tried the karaage, shoyu ramen, and chicken ramen. My favorite is the chicken ramen but I opted for the shoyu at this visit because I thought the broth would be more fitting for a hot summer day than the richer broth of the chicken ramen. 

Although Ivan Ramen is a slightly higher price point than other ramen joints in the city, I think it is a great spot for a chilly night. Note that they have a fairly spacious patio for when you want to dine outdoors.

I wasn't sure about what to expect from this place given the middling reviews, but I actually quite enjoyed the meal I got takeout. 

I typically favour pork-based ramens, but when I saw how popular the chicken paitan is here, I opted for that instead. My friend got the tonkotsu. While it was good, it wasn't stand-out, and I'm very glad I tried the chicken paitan. I would highly recommend it, with its rich and flavourful chicken broth (a tad on the salty side) and minced chicken. It might be because I ordered takeout, but it's worth mentioning that I got a regular ramen egg instead of egg yolk, as is listed on the menu. The ramen egg was strangely cold compared to the rest of the soup (it had probably come right out of the fridge) but the flavour was great. 

Overall, this is a decent spot to order from and I'd order/visit again for the chicken paitan!

Exceptional vegan ramen. The broth was as rich as any I've tasted anywhere. The noodles were incredibly filling. The veggies were standout in food quality and taste. My colleague could not finish hers it was so filling! But the best part was sitting out on the best day of the summer on the outdoor patio with beautiful mosaic artwork and the kindest, friendliest wait staff I've encountered in NYC in ages. I cannot wait to return.

Ordered delivery from this place and it was one of the best delivery meals we've had since living in NYC. Ordered the fried chicken, pork buns and spicy ramen. Chicken was very tender and the glaze was delicious - probably my favorite of the three. Buns and ramen were wonderful as well, the chicken is just something I've been craving ever since. This place was recommended to us by a friend and I'm glad we listened!
Excellent service, divine ramen, LOVED IT! Price was on point, waiting time was reasonable(20 minutes for a table of 5)

Excellent ramen with a reputation that speaks for itself. I love the creative spin on traditional dishes. Deviations like this polarize many, but I found this take to favor my palate. I can never choose between the chicken paitan and the tonkotsu. It's always a pleasure when there's a specialty tsukemen on the menu. The karage and eggplant appetizers are always good. I've been many times and will continue to return.

Came here at 12pm for lunch. There was a short line outside before they opened but they still had many tables available.

We ordered the eggplant to share. I'm not usually a fan of eggplant but this one was cooked really well and very tasty! I ordered the tonkotsu ramen and enjoyed it as well. The broth chashu was very tender but the star was definitely the noodles. They were very thin and had a unique texture.
Busy, small restaurant. Very consistent in its high quality ramen. I don't love sitting at a high top/ bar, but it gets you in and out, which is kinda the idea. Make a reservation.

Amazing, amazing, amazing experience. We took a guest here that was visiting us from out of town, and needless to say it lived up to the hype. Our server went above and beyond to explain items on their interactive virtual menu to us, gave us great suggestions, and even modified the ramen to fit our exact needs. Since I was between two, she somehow found a way to combine the both of them into one, and I was extremely satisfied. 

The place is always busy, on any given night there is a line out the door -- BUT this is the perfect excuse to put your name in and head around the corner to have a drink at Donnybrook (which we did) or the cute wine bar two doors down. We were seated in less than 20 minutes. Overall, I'd recommend this restaurant to anyone who loves great ramen.... This will not disappoint. I live in the area and will be returning ASAP.

Food here is amazing. It was a bit loud in the evening around 7:45 pm but it is a small spot so it is to be expected. Tables are quite close to each other. We come here for the food and don't mind the crowd. Everything on the menu is delicious. You literally can't go wrong with anything you choose.

This was the best food I have ever eaten in my life. I got the Chicken Paitan ramen and Yuzu lemonade and it was an emotional experience, seriously I teared up for a moment. You have to try it. 
Great service and a cool private patio in the back with an awesome mosaic mural.

Made a reservation for two at 1:30pm on a Sunday and it was packed. Service was friendly and quick.

I got the Shoyu Ramen and we had the Picked Cucumbers to share. While it doesn't look like a lot, the bowl ended up being super filling and tasty.

I'm glad I tried out Ivan Ramen while visiting the city, but I don't think I'd go out of my way to come back.

Three stars? Really? Yes, really.

The service is what gives it the extra oomph. I found all of the servers genuine, attractive, and intelligent, especially the one who helped me out at the bar. I expected less out of her and instead got more, which is why I gave her more when my meal was over (I sadly could not get her name, oh dear).

As for the rest of the meal, it is pretty par for the course. Like really par. Not mediocre, but not outstanding. The prices are eye popping for such a small bowl and plate of food. Two pastrami bao for $13 is killer. Thankfully they are tasty, and it feels like I am getting a vintage Lower East Side twist with a modern take on the neighborhood. Only reason I will not judge these too harshly.

The ramen is tasty too, albeit the portion is on the smaller side. Not a lot of noodle, one piece of chashu pork, but a lot of soft boiled eggs. Never turn down extra eggs. Everybody could use more protein.

You will need kadima, or a noodle refill. Otherwise you will still be hungry. For some reason I almost always need it at every ramen restaurant I have been to. Thankfully I got the lighter ramen compared to my usual Tonkotsu one. The latter ramen you should only order when it is 30 degrees outside and blustery.

The pretty staff will have you seeing double and ordering more, but the high prices and small portions will have you seeing stars and ordering less.

Think about all of that before you make your move.

Stopped into Ivan Ramen on a Thursday evening for dinner with a reservation. They require your whole party to be present before seating you, but we were seated immediately when everyone was there. They seemed to have plenty of availability for walk ins at the time as well. 

As a big fan of spicy food, I decided to go with the spicy ramen. In addition to a warning on the menu, the waitress cautioned me that it would be extremely spicy. The food came out very quickly. However, to my disappointment, it was not very spicy at all. It still had a very good flavor though and the toppings were fresh. 

We also decided to try their made in-house yuzu lemonade. The flavor packed a punch with strong sweet notes and a sour aftertaste. The two paired together really well making it quite tasty. I would recommend giving it a try. 

All in all, this is a pretty good ramen spot, but I probably would only come back if I was already in the area.

Wow! I'm a big ramen fan from the San Francisco Bay Area and was excited to try Ivan Ramen . The noodles are soooo good. I had the vegetarian shoyu which had a fantastic soy sauce + vegetable broth that had incredible depth. Did I already write about how amazing the noodles were?  writing a review weeks later as I sit on the other side of the continent wanting more.

Where else can you get a comfy filling lunch at this price? Also this is excellent ramen.

At the spur of the moment we decided to head over and fortunately caught an open table. Service is excellent and VERY fast.

We had the chicken paitan and Tokyo Shio ramens - both winners. Our other diner got the lemon-miso Brussel sprouts with a side of rice and was quite happy.

Add a few beverages and tip and damages for 3 was $85.

Recommended!

Just a great bowl of ramen. This place has a really cool, flavorful spin on the dish - the broths are not as rich as most but so so good. Appetizers were fantastic as well, really liked the chicken which wasn't overly fried and so juicy. The service was also awesome - we had the sweetest waiter who answered all our questions and was super attentive. Wish I lived nearby and could get this all the time!

Came in for a bowl of ramen on a freezing day. One of the ramen places in the area that still had a few seats. It is a bigger place than I imaged it to be. Menus are on QR codes, and the staff are very friendly. 

The chicken paitan was richer than any chicken paitan I've had. It was very similar to what I would think of as a tonkotsu broth. It is on the saltier side.
