The lime that came with it helped to add a bit of acidity. The minced togarashi chicken was okay. It didn't seem to add to much to the dish nor did the raw egg. I would've preferred actual slices of meat and a soft boiled egg. I did think the ramen was lacking compared to ramen at other places in the sense that there weren't a lot of toppings. The noodle portion also seemed like a smaller amount than most places. 

While I was there, I heard the waiters discouraging guests from ordering anything other than the chicken paitan or tsukemen if it was their first time, stating that those two were the best.

Wow, I really enjoyed my time here. Walked in on a Sunday evening and got counter seating-aka they take walk ins! 
We got the curry cauliflower and it was yummy! I'm not a vegetables for appetizer type of girl but really enjoyed it. The moving stuff on top gives it an amazing umami flavor. 
I chose the chicken pastian? Sorry if I am misspelling it and CLEARED MY BOWL. I never finish my food so that's telling you how good it is. The egg on top adds a richness to the broth. And the noodles are to die for. Thin and not too chewy. And our waiter was amazing, I wish I got his name but everyone in the shop is happy to work there and all around good vibes. Will come back

It was a cold rainy Sunday afternoon and we were walking without care of where we would go although we knew a bowl of Ramen was what we each wanted to enjoy.
We had considered Mexican & Italian food as we journeyed along sparklingly the narrow lower Eastside sidewalks avoiding the basement access grilles that were everywhere but nowhere it seemed. All the usual places had perished with the pandemic, and then suddenly there it was Ivan Ramen. From where did he come? We both looked inside, it was packed but comfortable, rule #1 passed. (If a lot of people are inside, the food must be good)
We were enthusiastically greeted upon peering through the vestibule, cool, a pleasant hostess and waitress, escorted us to our seats next to a happy couple already enjoying appetizers. My mouth was beginning to water and we quickly placed our orders. We didn't get drinks just water. Soon the waiter brought our plate of this crunchy eggplant dish. I had the adventurous spirit for something I never had before. I can't say it was delicious because it was so outside the box for me. Like trying on your first space suit, no comparison, I usually skip appetizers anyway. However, this was like the first gear of a mustang, I was already accelerating past 1969. It was hot! As for the rain outside, it was now delightfully left behind in the dust. Yes, I'm ready for my ramen Now! My jokes were as bad as ever, thinking my wife is from Venus and I'm from Mars, of course mine will taste better than hers. If she complained about losing on choosing, it was expected, women are from Venus. Ivan's Ramen was out of this world..."I'll be baak"

I had the CHICKEN PAITAN in October and I'm still obsessing over this dish to this day! I loved it so much! The flavors were incredible and it was definitely an experience while devouring it.

I will absolutely return!

Horrible...I brought my then-boyfriend here to try ramen for the FIRST time after seeing this place in a documentary. The apps were ok, but the ramen broth and noodles were served to us nowhere near hot. The fatty broth was starting to congeal and was extremely viscous and lukewarm, but we ate anyway because they were extremely busy. We both felt nauseous and disgusting after we left. Since then, he refuses to have ramen with me anywhere else. Thanks IVAN for ruining the idea of ramen for my now-husband!

Came here after seeing that episode of Chef's Table.

Made sure to book a table in advance, and so glad I did because people were non-stop clambering to get in without reservations. The restaurant is small and kinda loud, but the service is quick. 

We started with the Japanese Fried Chicken, which was uniquely fried and had a delicious dipping sauce. We also had the Brussels sprouts, which were a highlight of the meal, and I loved all of the garlic chunks in it. 

We each had a different entree: tokyo shoyu with minced chicken, chicken paitan, and triple pork triple garlic mazemen.  Everyone left happy and full. 

Def try the house-made Yuzu Lemonade!! So yummy and has bubbles :)
Great ramen, great friendly service. Highly recommend their Chicken Paitan ramen, super flavorful broth with a great textured noodle. Came out nice and hot

Date: Thursday, January 11th, 2024
Time: around 3pm
Party of: 4
What: late Lunch 

*CURRY FLOWER: cauliflower, curry koji-butter, pickled ginger, katsuobushi ($13)
*JAPANESE FRIED CHICKEN: toasted garlic caramel, togarashi, shiso ranch ($13)
*TOKYO SHIO: sea salts, dashi + chicken broth, pork belly, soft egg, roasted tomato ($19)
*TONKOTSU RAMEN: rich pork broth, shoyu-glazed chashu, woodear mushrooms, pickled mustard greens, soft egg, and mayu ($19) x2
*MAZEMEN: concentrated sauce (no broth), thick flat rye noodle - TRIPLE PORK TRIPLE GARLIC: tonkotsu broth, pork belly two ways ($19)
*Coke ($3) x2
*DFT Wild East Brewing Co "Funhaus" ($9) x2

I was craving noodle soup and decided on ramen! Since Ivan was around our hotel, we decided to drop by for a late lunch. We walked in and were immediately seated at a table in the back.

The cauliflower was good. Had a nice crunch / snap and I adore curry. I didn't read the description for the chicken, so I was surprised it was sweet. (Completely my fault.) I'm not a huge fan of sweet and salty so this wasn't my jam. I got the tonkotsu ramen since I love rich broths. The soup was meaty, creamy, and flavorful. The egg nicely soft boiled. I like my noodles thick and chewy, so these were not my fav. Ivan's ramen has thin rye noodles. But I honestly don't eat much of the noodles in general, so it was fine.

Since it was between lunch and dinner time, it was very chill. Our server was attentive and friendly. Suggested the beer I got since I wanted something light.

Nice spot to grab a bowl of ramen. If you prefer thin noodles, definitely check this place out.
Ivan Ramen is still incredible! So much flavor, care, and excellent customer service.

After watching Chef's Table, I was intrigued to try chef Ivan's take on ramen. The interior of the restaurant is narrow and almost cramped but very lively. There is also ramen art of cartoon characters enjoying ramen above the back wall of the bar creating a laid back atmosphere. For the ramen, I was intrigued to try both the Tokyo Shio and the Chicken Paitan but only had room for one bowl. On this visit, I opted for the Tokyo Shio and was satisfied. The Ramen bowl was crafted well and the use of his signature ingredient of the roasted tomato added excellent flavor. Simply put, the ramen was good but not exceptional. If you're looking for a casual spot to enjoy a unique flare on ramen, make sure to check out Ivan Ramen.

Made reservations for weeknight dinner and was glad I did because it was packed! My friend was running late but the staff were friendly and flexible. The restaurant is small and can get a bit crammed, but that's ny I guess. 

Got the Japanese fried chicken for starters which was good but nothing really special. The spicy red chili ramen was great and actually pretty spicy! Some reviews say it wasn't so maybe they kicked it up a notch? Good portion size as well.
Absolutely amazing, this is my 3rd time coming back. Has such amazing ramen that I really don't want to go anywhere else

service was great, the staff were all super friendly and seemed to have great energy. i got the shoyu ramen which was too salty, but the pork was really tender and the eggs were just the right degree of runny. i thought the curry flower was pretty tasty. the restaurant itself had some cool decor, i liked the cartoons they had on the wall in the back and overall seems like a casual, laid back place. id come back here and try some of their other noodles

My boyfriend and I came here on a Wednesday during lunch time and surprisingly it was not too busy and we were seated right away. We both had the classic tonkotsu and added roasted tomato. I was skeptical about the tomato at first but it's honestly a game changer! It brings out so much flavor and ties the entire dish together. There were also a good number of apps but since the ramen was heavy we decided to pass this tike round.

It has been on my list for a very long time. I finally made there this week. The ramen here is exceptional. Deep, deep broth that you hope never ends. For starters we had the pickles and roasted carrots. Both are very good. The pickles have just the right amount of balance between sour and sweet. Service is casual, friendly, and prompt. As for ambiance, it's a ramen shop.
Finally tried Ivan Ramen after seeing it years ago on Chef's Table! Had the crispy eggplant and chicken paitan - both were good! Would go back to try the tonkatsu. Really friendly staff too!

Anyone who doesn't rate this 5 stars is a clown and doesn't know anything about ramen. Every item I ordered was a home run. The attention to detail exceeds all competition. I'm pretty confident the lower star reviews are people rating the ambiance and not the food quality, but in my opinion, ramen is best served in hole-the-wall locations. My only reservation with this place is that the lighting could be a little dimmer to make it feel a little more intimate and grimy.
Love this place. Hole in the wall on Clinton street dishing out phenomenal ramen for years. Relaxed atmosphere serving up knockout food. What more do you want?

First time at the mother ship after they closed Gotham West. The Katz's pastrami bun was a great start. The Yuzu Lemonade was delicious.  The Vegetarian Ramen kept hot longer and was rich tasting with lots of aldente noodles. The tofu was even good. Service is friendly and efficient.  We will return.

AMBIENCE: (5/5)
- Very narrow entryway with tables down the hall that leads into another outdoor area. The narrow & close seating reminds me of actual ramen shops in Japan
- The wall is decorated with images & drawings plastered on the brick in a street-style graffiti fashion 

SERVICE: (5/5)
- Came as a walk-in with my cousin on a rainy day & was able to be seated right away
- Waiter was great, greeted us with a smile & checked in on us when appropriate
- Food came at a good time, didn't have to wait too long

FOOD/DRINKS: (3/5)
- Crispy Eggplant (5/5): Came out piping hot & breaded lightly to give that perfect crispiness on each side. The white sesame puree was very unique, acted almost like hummus in a way. Quite an interesting dish & well worth ordering again
- Brussel Sprouts (2/5): I love brussel sprouts and these are cooked nicely but they were drenched in the oily chilly sauce. The sauce itself wasn't bad, a bit spicy to kick off the taste buds but the entire dish was just completely soaked in a layer of oil that has separated from the sauce
- Tonkotsu Ramen (3.5/5): noodles were cooked to perfection & the perfect texture. Where it fell short was the broth, wish it was a bit more rich as it had promised & more layered in flavor. It felt like it just needed... something. Felt a bit flat. The chashu was tender & the rest of the toppings were fresh. 

OVERVIEW: (3/5)
- Wish I liked it more than I did. I think the place is good but it must've been overhyped & so the expectations were high
- Gave it an overall 3 since the ramen is weighted heavier than the other components given this is a ramen restaurant
- Would be open to giving it anther try but I wouldn't say it's worth all the buzz & it's definitely not one of the best ramen I've ever had

Went here on a weekend date, and I'd say getting a reservation definitely helped as it was almost completely packed as we came in. Tables seemed to be turned pretty quickly as we saw many people come in and out during our short dinner.  
Menu was definitely a but much. We got a little QR code menu which as others mentioned, makes you click through a instagram story-esque video about each dish when you select. It made looking through the menu cumbersome, but (at least?) the waiters were still taking orders down manually so we were able to sort it all out. 
Food came quick, and with a good amount of time between to finish the apps. The curry cauliflower was delicious and definitely worth it: each flower was still crispy and the sauce was so indulgent and buttery. We got the Tokyo Shio & Chicken Paitan, the ramen itself was pretty good, but felt a bit separated as a whole. Each component individually was great, but I felt as though it was a bit difficult to get most of the components in one bite. We both agreed that it was filling nonetheless, but will say the meat (pork belly & minced chicken) got a bit grainy by the end and that was where we felt the dishes fell the most flat.

I came here with my friends the other night. We had a reservation but one friend was about 20 minutes late. Luckily they were accommodating and still sat us. We dined on the patio which was roomy and private.

We started with the gyoza and curry flower. I had the triple pork triple garlic mazemen. The gyoza was good, pretty standard. The curry ramen was amazing. The sauce was delicious. It tasted cheesy but there was no cheese. 

My friends had the chicken paitan, Tokyo shoyu ramen and the Tokyo shio ramen. My dish was a hearty dish, similar to a pasta dish. It was heavy but I enjoyed it. My one friend said her ramen was a little salty but everyone liked their meals.

We shared a slice of yuzu cheesecake which was light and tasty. Our server gave it to us on the house since the    curry flower app came out later - what a nice suprise! 

Our server was great the entire time. From suggesting things on the menu, to continually checking in and always making sure our water glasses were filled, he didn't miss a step.

food was subpar. broth was too salty to drink. service was good, ambiance was nice. nice for a fast sit down dinner i suppose. but the food was too expensive for how disappointing it was

wouldn't risk it. go next

1 star for the food. 4 for the service. too bad good service doesn't make food taste better

Let me start off by saying the food and service is great. My favorite dish is the chicken paitan and their beer selection is always great. I have been here a few times and have never had any complaints.

This is where my 2 star review comes in. This past Saturday I stopped by for dinner and I noticed a manager being very rude and belittling one of their staff. I have been here a few times, I believe it may have been a manager or supervisor by the way they were talking down to their staff. I have seen this manager here before and she always seems to be in a bad mood or angry. As someone who has worked in the service industry in the past, this was very unprofessional and made me very uncomfortable to say the least. Not sure if I will be coming back to dine in any time soon.

It's been a while since I first ate here on my trip to NY but I loved their ramen , very rich in flavor . Can't recall if what I ordered was the chicken paitan or ?? Just risk it all and order any , it's worth it !

Ivan Ramen is one of my top 3 ramen spots in NYC. Their food never misses and their constantly changing menu keeps it interesting. I don't usually write reviews but the service was so stellar it required one. Diana is truly a gem.  Amazing place.

Was on my son's bucket list and it was spectacular.  He had a savory ramen dish and mine was vegetarian.  Both were excellent, but I liked his more than mine.  Excellent service and they brought more ramen. Definitely going back.
Delicious and the food came super fast! It was a very cute New York style restaurant! The servers were al very friendly and helpful.

I recently visited Ivan Ramen, the well-known restaurant featured on Netflix's Chef's Table. I arrived right as they opened and was immediately impressed by the super nice servers. Their warm welcome made it feel like a classic diner experience.

I started with the Wagyu Pastrami Bun, which was hands down the best bun I've ever tasted. The flavors were like a symphony in my mouth, melting with every bite. Absolutely delicious!

Next, I tried the Chicken Paitan Ramen. The rich, creamy chicken broth was smooth and flavorful, and the addition of a raw egg added a velvety texture that enhanced the overall taste. While it was good, I didn't find it particularly special compared to the bun.

I also ordered a half-and-half iced tea and yuzu lemonade. Not sure why I did this because I don't even like iced tea, but the yuzu lemonade was refreshing and tasty.

The aesthetic of the place is super cute, like stepping into a comic book diner. It's such a fun and unique vibe that adds to the dining experience.

All in all, I'd definitely go back just for that Wagyu Bun and can't wait to explore more of their ramen offerings!

Went here to celebrate a birthday and found the ramen to be delicious and super unique! Note that it is definitely very very RICH and HEAVY so you'll be leaving feeling like you definitely ate a big meal. I got the Chicken Paitan which I was so curious about, seeing as I usually opt for pork belly/cha shu for my ramen, but it was such a unique and delicious flavor that I loved it!

Not pictured, but I also got the karaage (pretty standard and good) as well as the soy garlic chicken appetizer (reminiscent of Bonchon so if you like that go ahead). Solid place!

It's been way too long for me to finally make it here, but so glad we did. This is one of the best and possibly the best ramen I've ever had in my life. I tried the Jiro and it was fantastic! Everything about it was so thoughtfully created and added to the dish. The egg was perfectly jammy and loved all the flavors like the garlic and even the wood ear. The soup was so flavorful and the rye noodles were perfect!

We also tried the Chicken Paitan which had an even more flavorful broth, so concentrated. We started with the tuna tartare which came with nice rice chips which was also great.

As a bonus, we also saw Ivan there and was able to say hello and meet him. He was very friendly and gracious, such a treat!
We had the eggplant appetizer and it was very good.  The vegan option ramen and the Tokyo Shoyu ramen  was good but  unfortunately overly salty.   Nice staff, good service

Awesome, welcoming and friendly service. Beautiful restaurant with funky wall design. Ramen is the best in the world!!! From broth, to each ingredients to presentation is out of this world. The taste and the aroma touch your senses. 100 % recommended!

Service and vibe were fantastic. Explained everything. Everybody did. Felt like the whole waitstaff were serving me. Ramen was really tasty but I loved the various veggie starters, like the pickle dishes, eggplant.

This was 4.5 stars, really. The triple pork, triple garlic ramen was incredible, as was the spicy ramen. My kiddo loved their tonkotsu as well. It was nice that the server offered extra noodles, which we happily took him up on.The yuzu lemonade was good, too. We thought it was better than Momofuku and would come back in a heartbeat.

I got there shortly after an exam and I'd been having a day. Someone recommended it to me. I got there at 1:47. I sat down at the bar and Jam the guy behind the bar was kind enough to measure my mood and ask me how I was doing and I let him know it was my first time there. He kindly recommended the cold sesame noodles and by 1:53 I was eating. It was so great. I'd love to return. The space was very calming and lifted my mood. The staff were attentive and kind. Very pleased.

Incredible! The absolute perfect bowl of ramen. I've had hundreds of ramen that were attempting to reach this pinnacle. The flavors and textures are in perfect harmony, rich and full and varied. Unforgettable experience.

Ivan Ramen wasn't on my radar at all before our New York City trip, but when I learned how acclaimed the place is, I found myself becoming very excited about our visit.

We showed up at around 6:00 on a Thursday and the place was already quite busy. We snagged a couple of spots at the bar, and even though we weren't planning on getting an appetizer, we certainly couldn't say no to the special: the "Lamb Shawarma" Gyoza ("Shwarma-seasoned lamb gyoza, "red sauce", "white sauce", shredded lettuce, cilantro and tomatoes").

It's amazing. We ate a lot of terrific stuff on our trip but this ranks very close to the top. It really did remind me of a shawarma, but a shawarma that's been elevated to incredible levels. Everything just worked so well together.

For my main, I went with the Spicy Red Chili ramen ("dashi + chicken broth, red chili tare, shoyu-braised pork chashu, smashed egg, yu choy"). Though perhaps not quite as exquisite as that appetizer, I heartily enjoyed this ramen. At first I thought maybe there was nothing going on but heat, and yeah it's extremely hot, but the more I ate the more flavors began coming to the forefront. It doesn't hurt, either, that all the other components work really well and also elevate it.

(Our server congratulated me after I finished, so I guess perhaps it's just a tad too hot for most people.)

I also tried their house beer and it was great. I can tell Ivan Ramen would be a regular spot if I lived nearby. It's awesome.

I was surprised to see the lower rating for this place given the acclaim but now that I've been there, I get it . The restaurant was pretty busy for a Monday night but I got a seat at the bar.

It's a pretty decent sized restaurant for NY and has a modern feel with the manga art across the walls. The waitstaff is really friendly and quick with their service. 

I ordered the shawarma gyoza, the maguro, and the shoyu ramen. The maguro came first. It has a nice balance of citrus, salt and a little sweetness. I wished it had more of a spice but otherwise not bad. The crackers held up well to the fish and there was a nice balance between fish and cracker. 

The gyoza came next and the description was spot on. It was like eating chicken rice from a cart but in a gyoza wrapper. Pretty tasty. 

The ramen came next and unfortunately it was a disappointment. Maybe I should have ordered one of their more unique noodle dishes but given how I read Ivan had studied authentic ramen, I wanted to try something traditional. The broth tasted a little like udon broth and not really very flavorful. I was pretty disappointed. The noodles were slightly over cooked as well. For a place that prides itself on ramen, this was not great. The egg was cooked well and the pork was delicious. But the basics of the ramen, broth and noodle, didn't stand up to some of the better places in LA, let alone Japan.

Really cute ambiance and decor obviously but it gets really loud. The girls next to us were having a conversation they felt comfortable with having in public but I didn't really want to be privy too haha but can't close my ears.

My friend and I had a reservation for 8:30PM on a Saturday but were early so we walked in. They couldn't seat us but I think they treated us as a walk in and there happened to be counter space. The service felt mixed - it was busy and they were sweet but not as attentive. 

We got the pickles which were pretty good - super vinegary with a little kick. My friend got the vegetarian option that came with a soy broth and tons of mushrooms and also a random tomato. She did need to jazz it up with a bit and they brought us their house spicy sauce which she said helped. 

I got the same thing I got the last time I came haha the triple pork and garlic and I had forgotten it was a mazemen! I had been craving some ramen broth. It was still super delicious and hearty, the ramen was thick and chewy and really great flavor with thick cuts of the chashu. We also got a light beer, super cute beer glass hehe. 

Not bad for the area, it's just so loud lol.
Good but not Impressed.  I would not wait in line.  Got early reservation.  Ramen was decent and bao was ok.  Nothing really stands out from other ramen joints. Had better.

I'm still thinking about the pastrami bun, which did outshine my mazemen a bit.

I appreciate the brothless and tsukemen options. Service is fast. The restaurant gets busy on even weekday nights and can be a little loud. QR code menus on the table, you can also pay that way but they can bring you the bill if you prefer.

FOOD
- Pastrami Buns are 5 Stars, I would return for these alone
- Ramen wasn't very memorable, but sitting outside on a chilly evening it hit the spot

SERVICE
- Good! 

MISC
- This place is CROWDED every time I've gone or tried to go, try and sit outside
- The small backyard area has a small section with heaters and one section without heaters (at least when I was there)
- Beers are overpriced but around what you pay in the neighborhood at a restaurant
I love this ramen spot. Always delicious and not pretentious. Often I can come without a pre-made reservation. 10/10!

Maybe it was because  we were wearing our aloha shirts, but we had fun and enjoyed our meal at this highly rated ramen spot. Both the pork and wagyu bao buns were excellent. I love wagyu anything but this was pastrami!!!  The ramen was picture perfect and delicious to the last drop. The drink menu was eclectic for me. The manager was very helpful with this part. I would head to the back patio if you don't need A/C.

Phenomenal ramen spot! Really enjoyed the vegan ramen and my partner couldn't stop raving about the spicy red chili ramen. Also...Don't miss out on the crispy eggplant appetizer. Unlike anything I've had before and an insane burst of flavor!
cool ambiance and the ramen was okay. a good neighborhood ramen and good service. worth a shot if you're around LES.

Jose and the team are outstanding! We had the triple pork triple garlic ramen and chicken paitan. It was just spectacular. The staff are engaging and passionate about the food and service. Get a reservation... it gets busy very fast! Highly highly recommend!

I already want to go back! 

Making a reservation online is easy. We ended up running a little late for ours, but called the restaurant and were informed they would hold our spot for 15 minutes! There were several people waiting at the door, so a reservation is definitely recommended. 

Inside it was packed! A little loud, but not too distracting. I loved the comic-esque art over the bar where we were seated.

We had a fantastic bartender/server! He was extremely friendly and conversational, but it didn't detract from anyone's service at all. He recommended the crispy eggplant instead of the pickles and I'm so glad he did. The eggplant was phenomenal - I would put that miso tahini on anything. 

I ordered the Chicken Paitan for my entree. I would recommend it to anyone! It was as rich as a tonkotsu (which is my usual ramen go-to), but it definitely wasn't as heavy. And the crispy chicken skin added a nice crunch.

The best Ramen in NYC hands down!
If Ramen is not your thing, they have some amazing other options. 
I always order the whole menu!
Best service 
Best ambiance 
Best Ramen

They should consider being a bit kinder to their patrons. 

I had a table at 6:45pm. I got there at 6:55pm. The host made me wait inside right in front of her as she had a conversation. When she was finished, I approached her and asked to be seated. She literally clicked onto her screen in front of my face and said "I already marked you no show". I told her I thought the reservation was at 6:45pm and that they have a 15 minute grace period. She said "And now it is 7:01."

Don't get me wrong - I understand if they have a very strict policy on this. I of course don't want to get anyone in trouble. But 
1) I was INSIDE the restaurant in front of the host desk waiting for them to wrap up a conversation. 
2) There was nothing apologetic about the way I was shooed away. It felt like they were almost satisfied, the way this person stared at me annoyed and said "And now it is 7:01". 

I am baffled. I have never received such disrespectful treatment in even the highest end restaurants. I come here often, and had invited a friend who was visiting from out of town that day too. I'm sorry but I frankly do not understand who they think they are.

Tbh I was hesitant to come because the name doesn't scream authenticity and we're very picky with ramen. When we arrived, my friend whispered "it's all non-Asian people here, this can't be good" but we'd come so let's just try it! 

We ordered three noodle dishes to share between us. The jiro stood out - it's got a unique flavour and unusual topping. However we thought half way through it's a little too salty.

The tsukemen with katsu was nice, but again the broth (this one is a dipping broth) was very heavy and salty. I guess that's why they also give you vinegar on the side. The noodles were bouncy and good. The katsu's very different from regular Japanese katsu, it's kind of like sous vide then deep fried. The texture's interesting.

We also ordered shoryu ramen and it was just okay.

Service was excellent and attentive, there's only one bathroom but it's pretty clean when we visited.

we all know & love Ivan Ramen flavor - but why do they allow everyone waiting for a table and or pickup to congregate inside by the door? I have never experienced this in NYC and always expect to wait outside myself... this is kinda crazy also because the amount of tourists waiting the spatial awareness is horrid, my poor bf got sat on a few times while eating his ramen .... Did get a complimentary Diet Coke though ?

For years, I've been wanting to go to this ramen shop ever since I watched the chefs table episode for Ivan, AND I FINALLY GOT TO TRY IT. First off, thank you to the staff for being able to squeeze us in without a reservation. They were fully booked, but they told us if we could finish our food within 45 mins, we could go. Ivan has always said, ramen should be eaten fast, and boy, did I LMAO. I ate it fast not because I had to, but because I wanted to. Beat shio ramen I've had. The infamous roasted tomato was one of the best bites in the bowl. Will go back next time I'm in NY

I LOVED the eggplant appetizer but I thought my spicy miso ramen was just ok. The spice overpowered the miso flavor and because the noodles were on the thinner side I felt like I couldn't really taste the noodles that much either. The appetizer on the other hand I was trying to lick the extra sauce that was on the plate. It was so good. If I were to come back I would get the Tsukamen instead. My friend ordered this and let me try it, and I thought it had more well rounded flavor and the noodles were thicker so it picked up the broth better without being overpowered. The service is pretty good though and the vibe is nice.

I came here with the Ramen Meetup group and it was fantastic!  I had the Jiro and it was awesome with a mountain of vegetables, but still flavorful with pork and mustard greens.  They were kind enough to honor my request of noodles Al dente on the side.  Great noodles!

Ambiance (5/5): It is tight and bustling on the inside with some high top seating facing the open kitchen. There are some also floor seating as well as covered backyard outdoor seating with heated lamps. We dined outside and the heat lamps were sufficient in keeping us toasty.
Service (5/5): The servicing staff were stellar with cool/approachable attitude and swift help to our needs. The waiter was able to remember almost 10+ orders without taking down a single note!? The food came out fairly quickly!
Crispy Eggplant (5/5): It was a unique spin to eggplant! The inside was soft but the exterior had a light breading that soaked up the mayo-based sauce that gave it richness to each bite!
Karaage (4/5): The breading was tasty but a little too breaded for me. The inside chicken pieces were juicy. With the dipping sauce, the chicken was perfect.
Tonkotsu Ramen (3.5/5): Although the ramen portions felt generous, I thought that the broth was wayyy too salty (as did other patrons of their ramen). The noodles had a great bounce. Their sliced pork is a bit different and sliced more thin, tender, but still good. Ramen had a whole soft boiled egg.
Sadly how salty the broth was and something missing in the broth overall let me down.

We walked in on a Saturday evening around 7pm. I suggest making a reservation ahead of time and the wait time can range from 30 minutes to 2 hours during this time. The servers were kind and seated us after my party was complete. 

We enjoyed the Tokyo shio and the chicken paitan that was recommended by the waiter. Both were delicious. I enjoyed how the Tokyo Shio broth was rich yet not overwhelmingly oily. The roasted tomato was a nice touch to the ramen. The noodles were chewy and cooked al dente. 

The cozy atmosphere is great for a meal with family and friends. I would recommend for those who enjoy Japanese fusion ramen as it does not seem to be traditional style.
Excellent!  Best ramen in NYC!! Chicken ramen so many layers of flavors!  Spicy miso is very spicy- be prepared.  Great service.
Fun ambience with a killer collage mural. Food was very tasty, delicious, and original. Service was attentive to detail.
We got a cute booth towards the back. I highly recommend making a reservation so you can get seated right away. Smooth broth that didn't make you feel too bloated after eating!

I really used to enjoy Ivan Ramen but I cant say the same any more.

It takes over 20-25 minutes for a bowl of ramen to be made even when it's barely less than 50% occupied.  Sure there might be takeout orders but in the 50 minutes I sat there no one was picking up takeout.  I just don't know what gives.

The server I had was mediocre at best and I probably should have left less of a tip for him to be honest.  It was just an annoying experience.  He tried to convince me to order the chicken paitan.  Hello dude.  If i wanted it I would have ordered it.  Certainly I would have asked for your help if I needed it.  Needless to say this was a distraction for this guy and he could not get my order right with a minor adjustment I'd asked for.

Communication is a difficult skill I guess.  I'd say the best communicator was the hostess who made it clear to me she needed the table back by 5:30pm.  I got there at 4:40 and was out the door by 5:29 due to some unforseen delays.

I was so excited to try the different dishes here and they did not disappoint! The restaurant serves Japanese food and it seems to also have some Jewish influence as well which brings forth new and unique flavors in my opinion. 
I came with my partner and while we definitely ate with our eyes more than our stomachs could handle, we enjoyed our meal thoroughly. 

1. SEASONAL SQUASH WITH STRACCIATELLA
This wasn't my favorite but I did enjoy the sauce with the squash. It seemed to have some sort of wasabi flavor in it. 

2. CRISPY EGGPLANT

This was so fun and tasty! I loved the crispiness of the eggplants paired with the sauce. The sauce was pretty addicting too in my opinion. The eggplants were nicely seasoned as well and I almost wish I got some to go. 

3. MAGURO BUTSU

This reminded me of ceviches and was enjoyable. I don't think I needed to get it but I was happy to try it. It was nice with the seaweed crisp however the crisps are rather large and so it's hard to eat them together in a clean manner. 

4. SCHMALTZ-FRIED GYOZA
I was interested in these as I've never heard of such gyozas and I thought they were soupy which was a nice surprise! They felt like tasty small surprises and I loved how much flavor it packed. 

5. WAGYU PASTRAMI BUNS

Its flavor reminded me of McDonalds but in a good way! It was quite tasty. I thought this was a smart idea to use buns for. 

6. TONKOTSU TSUKEMEN

I do love a good Tsukemen and I thought this was quite good. It was quite salty which is expected and it came with an anchovy sauce that you could add in if you wanted. I didn't think it was really necessary but try a drop or two before adding in more. The pork katsu was nicely cooked and so tender. Since it's a salty dish, I think it would've been nice to have also ordered a drink! 

7. "JIRO"-STYLE TONKOTSU

Like the description mentions, this ramen was very garlic forward and had a lot of small bits in the bowl. I think having all those bits makes it a bit cumbersome to have to chew through although it was good. With noodles I like to be able to slurp them and taste the broth on its own, but it was so packed with bits and pieces of many ingredients that it sort of got in the way. 
8. YUZU CHEESECAKE

This was my favorite dessert here! What a great way to end a delicious meal! The yuzu was punchy but so addicting. 

9. YUZU KAKIGORI
If you think you are going to finish this on your own, you may want to reconsider. You will be presented with this large talk bowl of shaved ice and in the center and in the bowl, is all of the yuzu extract. It's like hidden treasure! I loved the cream they had on the top and wish they actually used more of it! Unfortunately I was not able to finish this but if I could , I would've! 


Overall, I had so much fun tasting different flavors and textures and would love to come back again!

I came to Ivan Ramen on a Thursday early afternoon. I made reservations - there were plenty although I'm glad I did because the restaurant was pretty busy. The staff are, as mentioned in previous reviews, very friendly. The place is small and space is tight. I can imagine it becoming cramped. The bar isn't for eating - so don't ask to sit at the bar if you want to eat. As most know Ivan worked in Japan and perfected Ramen , specifically his chicken umami broth and rye noodles. I went the vegan route and had the Vegan Ramen and the Crispy eggplant. Both were excellent. The broth for the ramen was very flavorful and the noodles were lovely. I also loved the tofu, mushrooms and tomato. The crispy eggplant was really good - crisp on the outside juicy on the inside and super flavorful. I really enjoyed

brought my husband as our first date night of 2025 and he fell in love with the Gyoza and Chicken Paitan Ramen, and he's very picky with food. I was surprised he mentioned how good it was all the way til he finished. Afterwards the team surprised us with the shaved ice desert which was the most kind and sweetest experience. 100/100"

Wait time was a little long after having scheduled reservation 
Ambiance is nice 
Service spectacular 
Eggplant appetizer really good 
Chicken paitan ramen had very tasty broth, but noodles had a strange texture and overall more to be desired

Loved this unique ramen spot! Highly recommend making a reservation - it was packed on a cold Friday night in Jan. 

Loved the squash appetizer, lamb gyoza, and both the tonkatsu and shoyu ramens. The basque cheesecake and Japanese shaved ice was a perfect way to end the meal!

Ivan Ramen is a true gem, and you can taste the passion and innovation in every bowl. Ivan's journey from Japan to New York shines through, blending authentic ramen techniques with a unique New York-Jewish twist. The use of dehydrated tomato in the broth is genius--it adds a depth of flavor you won't find anywhere else. The ramen is hands-down the best I've had, with perfectly balanced flavors and textures. To top it off, it's surprisingly affordable for the quality.

For a deeper appreciation of Ivan's story, his episode on Netflix's Chef's Table is absolutely worth a watch. A must-visit for ramen lovers and foodies alike!
Literally so good!! Ordered the chicken paitan with a tomato and it was THE BEST THING!! The vibe is so great in there and our server was amazing, shoutout to Johnathan!

OUTSTANDING!!! My husband and I were in NYC for Christmas and we had time to kill before heading to the airport. A friend of ours recommended this spot for great ramen.  We decided what the heck let's give it a go and my only regret is that we didn't try it sooner, as we would have been repeat customers for sure.  The restaurant itself is very well lit, clean and cozy. It was freezing outside, but this space has an enclosed patio with heaters so we decided to sit there.  Their menu is very attractive with lots of options for everyone and prices that will not break the bank.  We had the spicy pickles to start (drool worthy) and for our mains, I chose the Spicy Miso Ramen and my husband chose the Vegan Shoyu.  The spicy ramen is NOT for the faint of heart when it comes to spice. I love spicy food so it was right up my alley. The spice was perfectly balanced with the other flavors in the dish which created a very flavorful broth with a kick.  Exactly what I was looking for when I needed a hug on a cold winter day. Just perfect! My husband's Vegan Shoyu was INCREDIBLE.  The depth of flavor in that bowl was mind blowing. I don't know what the base of that broth was, but the silky texture, next to that beautiful tofu was so dang good. We have been home now for a month and I am still thinking about this spot. The highlight of our dining experiences for sure. The owner has his back story on their website and as a woman who grew up with a Japanese grandmother in the kitchen, I can taste his love for Japan through his food.  I live in Orlando and sadly we do not have anything that even comes close to this place.  This is a MUST not a maybe and when I am back in the city this will be my first stop.

I made a yelp account just to give this place a review because of how awesome my experience was tonight. Killer food -- we got the tonkotsu and chicken paitan, which our awesome server Britton recommended. She was super knowledgeable about the menu and totally steered us in the right direction. Major shoutout to Nat as well, who couldn't have been friendlier. She was very helpful, answering all of our questions and making us feel welcome. Can't wait to come back !! Amazing service at this spot !!

Went here with a bigger group of friends back in January!! I was truly impressed with the service, for such a big group they really stayed on top of our orders and timing! 

They have nice selection of drinks! I got Yuzu Barley tea something that was so good that I got it twice. My friends kept getting peach soju-kinda drink and they were repeating that one too!! 

I got Paitan that had a great flavor. It was on a thicker/heavier side but I enjoyed it a lot! My friend got the spicy ramen, it was so flavorful and I saw why that was their signature thing!! I wished I could eat spicy food more.
Amazing Ramen, flavorful broth and worth every dollar you spend here. Staff is also incredibly friendly. I had a solo date in the LES and decided to hit up my favorite ramen place.

Ivan Ramen is a must-visit for anyone looking to experience ramen like never before! Thanks to a friend for bringing us here and encouraging us to watch the Chef's Table episode featuring Chef Ivan Orkin--a moving story that resonates deeply and is worth watching (grab a tissue and watch before you go!)

We went on a night when the Blackbird special was going on, and the ramen was half-price through the app. We ran into some issues with the app, but luckily a representative was there to help. Even though we couldn't get the app working correctly, Ivan Ramen still honored the deal. Great service!

Ivan Orkin's dedication to creating a unique culinary experience distinctly shines through in the food. The ramen I enjoyed was absolutely the best I've ever had, even compared to my time in Japan. I savored the chicken ramen, enhanced by roasted tomato, and it was nothing short of spectacular.

Accompanying the ramen, we had a delightful serving of the Ivan Karaage, which was beautifully crispy and flavorful--a true highlight of the meal. On our plates but not pictured were the scrumptious miso Caesar salad and a refreshing daikon salad, both of which complemented the meal perfectly.

Everything about our dining experience was exceptional, and I can't recommend Ivan Ramen enough for anyone looking to enjoy an authentic yet innovative take on ramen!

Update: had to go back again, added some more photos.
The food and the service were both fantastic. The chicken paitan was wonderful. Highly recommended.

My review is not bases on the food but my experience at the restaurant. 

We bad such a terrible experience here. We didn't even get a chance to eat. We had come as a group of 8 and we were told that for 8 people they only do a prix fixe menu. It would cost $60/person and includes 1 ramen per person and 5 shared appetizers for the group. We're all vegetarian and they didn't even have 5 veggie appetizers so they would repeat one of them. 
When we did the math, it didn't made sense. On the menu, it's $20 for ramen and each appetizer was less than $20. So if we all got a ramen and shared 5 appetizers our total would have been much lower than being charged $60/person plus tax and tip. 

We asked if it would be possible to do 2 groups of 4 and not get the prix fixe menu and the hostess said that's fine. But even though there were tables next to each other, she said she would split us and we couldn't sit together. 

The hostess was very rude and kept giving attitude even when we first came in. 

It's really disappointing as I've been wanting to try out this ramen place for a long time and this is not what I was expecting.

I'm a die hard ramen fan, the ramen here fell a bit short for me. Having sampled 4 different ones I'd say the chicken was the best (chicken the best? Something I thought would never come out of my mouth). The triple pork, triple garlic is a soupless ramen that was second best. The spicy miso was ok and at least lives up to its spicy name. The tonkotsu was flat and watery, especially if you've ever been to Japan. The apps however were extremely solid, the sashimi, the fried chicken, and the curry cauliflower were all very tasty. Service was great, reservations easy to snag, and for those into vibes, this place has it.
I tried the spicy ramen and it was great. They're not lying when they say it is very spicy.
